playstyle.suited: Players who wield randomness as pressure on the opponent — presence over precision.

synergy.reason: Enables safe positioning and damage output through mobility buffs and silence skills.
Boosts the survivability of low-mobility marksmen through movement speed buffs and healing.

counters.reason: Uses high mobility and burst damage to instantly delete the squishy Sun Bin.
Excels at poke and mobility, constantly applying pressure while easily dodging Sun Bin's skills.

passive.description: Whenever Sun Bin uses a skill, he gains 65-130 Movement Speed for 2s.
passive.name: Passive Skill: Hourglass of Time

skill1.description:
Sun Bin throws a bomb in the target direction that deals 200 (200 + 20% magical attack) magical damage to the first enemy it hits and latches onto them.
The bomb explodes 3s later or when the target dies, dealing 575 (575 + 60% magical attack) magical damage to enemies within range and slowing them by 15% for 2s.
Cleansing the bomb will cause it to detonate immediately.
skill1.name: Skill 1: Time Bomb

skill2.description:
Sun Bin manipulates time, increasing the Movement Speed of himself and nearby teammates by 130 for 2s. After the 2s, he recovers Health equal to 25% of the damage taken during this period.
Passive: He gains 7.5% Cooldown Reduction.
skill2.name: Skill 2: Time Flux

skill3.description:
Sun Bin throws an enhanced bomb in the target direction. Upon hitting an enemy or reaching its max range, the bomb unfurls an energy field, dealing 500 (500 + 45% magical attack) magical damage to enemies within range and slowing them immensely for 1s. The field interrupts the enemy's skill and silences them for 1s.
The energy field explodes 5s later, dealing 1,500 (1,500 + 135% magical attack) magical damage to enemies within range.
skill3.name: Skill 3: Time Lapse

strategy.earlyGame: Sun Bin is a roaming support built around time manipulation. Start by shadowing your marksman and holding the farm lane bushes; when the enemy commits, Skill 2's team-wide speed boost gets everyone out. The boost heals 25% of damage taken during its duration when it ends, so cast it just before enemy skills connect — not after you've started running — and the HP difference is plain to see. Skill 1's bomb is all about the 3-second detonation, so in skirmishes, sandwich the tagged target with an ally and chase until it pops.
strategy.midGame: From level 4, ganks built around your Ultimate start connecting at a much higher rate. The field applies a heavy 1-second slow on hit and even silences enemies caught mid-cast, making it the answer to targets holding escape skills. At the 4-minute Tyrant and mid-game rotations, ferrying your whole team with Skill 2's +130 move speed is a job only Sun Bin does. Walking speed converts directly into numbers advantages — arrive at objectives five-strong one beat before the enemy, over and over, and the map tilts your way.
strategy.lateGame: Late game, placing your Ultimate is map control in itself. The field detonates 5 seconds after deployment, so drop it in the narrow entrance to Shadow Tyrant or Overlord and the enemy must either fight inside the blast zone or concede the spawn. When fights break out, stick Skill 1 on their key hero and play for the detonation; when your team needs to reset, Skill 2's speed and refund heal rebuild the line. Your personal damage is modest, so operate from behind your team, out of enemy reach, and keep pulling the strings.
strategy.teamfight: Open teamfights by placing your Ultimate on the enemy's escape path, not at their feet. The 1-second slow lets your team's follow-up land, and the 5-second delayed blast catches them on the retreat. Attach Skill 1 to a frontliner and the 3-second fuse plus AoE slow completes the trap. Skill 2 works as an engage tool too, but its best use is covering the exact moment enemy burst lands — with 25% of damage taken coming back a few seconds later, it feels like haggling the enemy mage's full combo down to three-quarters price.

combos.title: Close the Three Seconds
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (attach the bomb) → Skill 2 (+130 Movement Speed for Sun Bin and allies) → chase with your team
combos.description: The bomb's real payload is the blast 3 seconds later. Skill 2 is not an escape here — it is the speed that keeps your team on the target until the fuse ends. The blast damages an area and slows by 15% for 2s. It also detonates if the target dies first, so attach it to anyone you might finish off.

combos.title: Cut the Cast, Seal the Exit
combos.sequence: Skill 3 (field opens, immense 1s slow) → Skill 1 (bomb) → Skill 2 (speed)
combos.description: The field lands 500 (Lvl 1) and an immense 1s slow the moment it unfurls. Interrupt an enemy skill with it and a 1s silence comes along. The best targets are heroes holding an escape or casting something long. The 1,500 (Lvl 1) explosion arrives 5 seconds later, so place it on their exit rather than their feet.

strengths: Skill 2 speeds up the entire team, winning rotations and chases before they start
25% of damage taken during the boost returns as healing — a strong burst counter
Ultimate silences on interrupt, and its delayed blast dominates whole areas
weaknesses: No stuns or hard CC, so he can't lock down a kill by himself
Both Skill 1 and the Ultimate have delayed payoffs, lacking instant stopping power
Personal damage and durability are below average — a misused speed boost leaves nothing

playstyle.style: A time-keeper who accelerates allies and converts damage they took into healing. His silencing ultimate directly answers enemy channels — an understated kit that touches every critical moment.
playstyle.suited: Players who appreciate distributing the invisible resource of speed — governing the match's tempo itself.

synergy.reason: Uses durable tanks on the frontline to easily stack poison on enemies while keeping allies healed.
Soaks up enemy attacks, creating an ideal environment for dealing sustained damage and healing.

counters.reason: His missing-Health damage and true-damage burst outpace the healing, making it very hard to drag out fights.
Uses high mobility and burst damage to burst them down before they have a chance to heal.

passive.description:
Dr Bian's Basic Attacks and skills place a poison mark on enemies for 7s (up to 5 stacks), dealing 20 (20 + 5% magical attack) magical damage per second.
Healing skills place a healing mark on teammates and himself for 7s (up to 5 stacks), restoring 3 (3 + 2% magical attack) Health per second to teammates, and 3 (3 + 2% magical attack + 0.15% extra Health) Health per second to himself.
passive.name: Passive Skill: Malicious Practice

skill1.description:
Dr Bian throws a vial of lethal poison that shatters upon impact, releasing a pool of poison for 4s. Every second, it deals 65 (65 + 14% magical attack) magical damage to enemies within the area and slows them by 30% for 2s.
Dr Bian stocks 1 vial every 12.5s. Up to 3 vials can be stocked.
skill1.name: Skill 1: Deadly Panacea

skill2.description: Dr Bian throws a concoction, dealing 130 (130 +30% magical attack) magical damage to enemies hit and restoring 65 (65 +15% magical attack) Health to nearby teammates.
skill2.name: Skill 2: Fatal Diagnosis

skill3.description:
Dr Bian detonates all nearby marks, dealing 150 (150 + 40% magical attack) magical damage to enemies while restoring 70 (70 + 20% magical attack) Health to teammates. Each stack of mark increases damage and healing by 50%.
He also recovers 400 (400 + 30% magical attack + 5% extra Health) extra Health.
skill3.name: Skill 3: Master of Life

strategy.earlyGame: Dr Bian's early game is an exercise in patience. With no burst, mid lane trades are losing propositions until your first core item finishes, so clear waves with Skill 1's poison pools and manage your HP. Vials restock every 12.5 seconds up to a cap of three — always bank one for self-defense. Whenever the enemy jungler is off the map, dropping a pool at your feet before backing off cuts gank success rates dramatically. Basic attacks apply a poison stack through the Passive too, so keep tapping targets from safe range.
strategy.midGame: Around 8 minutes, with one or two items done, you can drag fights into your arena: long skirmishes. In Tyrant standoffs, throw Skill 1 at their feet from behind your frontline, cycle Skill 2 for chip damage and ally healing, and once poison marks build up, detonate them with your Ultimate. Each stack adds 50% to the blast's damage and healing, so holding for 5 stacks instead of panicking at 2 changes what the fight looks like. Past the 10-second mark of any brawl, the poison-versus-healing math starts sinking the enemy team.
strategy.lateGame: The later the game, the more Dr Bian wants to dodge coin-flip bursts and drag everyone into attrition. Line up three poison pools in front of Shadow Tyrant or Overlord and the enemy either fights while melting or gives up the spawn. In teamfights, stand near the center of your team and use the Ultimate's detonation for AoE damage and a team-wide heal in the same instant. Once enemies start buying anti-heal items, your edge shrinks — compensate with timing, detonating earlier, before allies drop below half HP.
strategy.teamfight: Skip the flashy opener — you're the fight's accountant, keeping the books on marks. Open with Skill 1 into their clump, throw Skill 2 at whoever is easiest to hit (usually the frontline) while healing allies around you, and once both teams tangle, detonate everything with the Ultimate. Blowing 5-stack poison across multiple enemies at once is the comeback button: AoE damage and a team recovery in the same moment. When an assassin jumps you, crack a pool at your own feet and walk them across the 30% slow toward your team — that alone changes your survival rate.

combos.title: Wait for Five Stacks
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (poison pool) → Skill 2 (damage + team heal) → Basic Attack → Basic Attack → Skill 3 (detonate every mark)
combos.description: Each basic attack or skill hit adds one poison mark, capped at 5 stacks. Every stack raises the detonation's damage and healing by 50%, so two stacks and five stacks are entirely different weapons. Don't rush it — fire when your team's health starts to drop.

combos.title: Crack a Pool and Walk
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (at your own feet) → Skill 2 → Skill 3 (extra self-heal)
combos.description: With no mobility skill, the answer to a dive is to make them stand in poison rather than to run. The pool lasts 4s and slows anything inside it by 30% for 2s. Skill 3 detonates the marks and restores an extra 400 (Lvl 1) Health to Dr Bian himself. That is the walk back to your team.

strengths: Poisons enemies and heals allies at the same time — long fights snowball his way
Five-stack Ultimate delivers big AoE damage and a team-wide heal in one cast
Three stocked vials make him excellent at zoning objective pits
weaknesses: No mobility skill — an assassin who reaches him rarely lets him leave
Needs time to stack marks, so instant-burst shootouts are not his game
Anti-heal items erase half of what he brings

playstyle.style: A dual-ledger mage who stacks poison marks on enemies and healing marks on allies, then detonates both at once. Every decision moves two scoreboards simultaneously.
playstyle.suited: Players who see offense and defense as one board — and love flipping a fight with a single well-timed detonation.

synergy.reason: Follows up on Bai Qi's taunt clump by dropping massive AoE and true damage directly onto the grouped enemies.
Provides shields and utility to greatly boost Bai Qi's survivability while he soaks damage in the middle of teamfights.

counters.reason: Deals massive damage by ignoring Bai Qi's high physical defense with true damage.
Kites and disrupts Bai Qi with long-range poke and CC, preventing him from getting close enough to taunt.

passive.description: Bai Qi gains Shadow Power when dealing or taking damage, which increases his Movement Speed by up to 70 and healing by up to 80%.
passive.name: Passive Skill: Reaper's Revenge

skill1.description:
Bai Qi swings his scythe, dealing 252 (180 + 40% physical attack) physical damage to enemies in range and recovering 90 (90 + 2% extra Health) Health.
Passive: Bai Qi has a 20% chance of automatically triggering this skill whenever he takes damage.
This skill can be charged up. The longer he charges for, the higher the damage and recovery effect, up to a maximum of 3 times the base damage and recovery. Effect is halved against non-hero units.
skill1.name: Skill 1: Blood Echo

skill2.description:
Bai Qi summons scythes which retract after 1.2s and pull enemies back, dealing 325 (325 + 120% extra magical attack) magical damage and slowing them by 25% for 2.5s.
Passive: He deals 30% extra damage to enemies below 30% Health.
skill2.name: Skill 2: Deathscythe

skill3.description: Bai Qi instantly gains maximum Shadow Power and jumps to the target location, dealing 481 (300 + 100% magical attack) magical damage and taunting enemies. Base taunt duration is 1-1.5s, and every 1,000 extra Health increases the duration by 0.2s, for a maximum duration of 2.5s.
skill3.name: Skill 3: Lay Waste

strategy.earlyGame: The lane badge at the top of this page reads Clash, following the official stats. The advice below assumes a roaming pick. Bai Qi roams from the opening minutes, but his taunt only comes online at level 4 and lasts barely a second while his bonus HP is low, so deep dives backfire. Hold the space between mid and farm lane and play interceptor: thread Skill 2's scythe through ganking enemies and drag them back. The scythe returns 1.2 seconds after the throw, so aim it across the target's walking path rather than at their feet and it connects far more often. Taking damage has a chance to auto-cast Skill 1's heal, so tanking minion aggro to hold ground is less painful than it looks.
strategy.midGame: Two HP items done around 10 minutes is Bai Qi's power spike. Every 1000 bonus HP adds 0.2 seconds of taunt, and by now you're holding enemies for close to 2 seconds. When setting up vision at Tyrant or Shadow Tyrant, the real play is your Ultimate from a bush: the taunt forces enemies to attack Bai Qi, instantly sealing away the enemy carry's skills and combos. After landing, drag retreating targets back with Skill 2 and charge Skill 1 to heal while your team arrives.
strategy.lateGame: Full-build Bai Qi taunts for up to 2.5 seconds, and late-game teamfights come down to who eats it. The ideal is dropping it on the enemy marksman or mage — if your team burns them during 2-plus seconds of lockdown, the fight becomes 5v4. Miss the Ultimate, though, and your gap closers are spent, leaving a walking target. Discipline yourself to hold it until you've seen the enemy's dashes. Skill 2 also deals bonus damage to enemies below 30% HP, so you can finish runners yourself more often than you'd expect.
strategy.teamfight: In teamfights, one thought is enough: land your Ultimate on the enemy's most dangerous hero. Catch several with the AoE taunt and their entire damage output points at Bai Qi for seconds while your team swings freely, essentially untouched. Every hit you take stacks Shadow Power through the Passive, boosting your healing, and Skill 1's auto-proc stacks on top — melting mid-taunt is rarer than it looks. As the taunt expires, scythe their squishiest survivor toward your team as a parting gift and the numbers advantage keeps rolling.

combos.title: Taunt, Then Trade
combos.sequence: Skill 3 (jump, taunt) → Skill 1 (charge and release) → Skill 2 (pull, 2.5s slow)
combos.description: The taunt runs 1-1.5s at base, plus 0.2s for every 1,000 extra Health, capped at 2.5s. Early on that is barely a second, so don't dive on it. Charge Skill 1 while they are locked and the release deals and heals up to three times as much. Anyone backing off as the taunt ends gets dragged back by the scythes.

combos.title: Peel Off the Backline
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (pull, 25% slow) → Skill 3 (taunt)
combos.description: Hook the diver off your carry with the scythes, then taunt to force their attacks onto Bai Qi. The scythes retract 1.2s after they are summoned, so lead the throw into where the enemy is heading. Targets below 30% Health take 30% extra damage, which sometimes ends the chase on the spot.

strengths: AoE taunt scaling to 2.5 seconds with bonus HP seals away entire enemy combos
Auto-proc Skill 1 and the healing-boost Passive make him tougher the deeper the brawl
Skill 2 hits harder below 30% HP, letting him finish fleeing targets himself
weaknesses: The scythe's 1.2-second return delay makes it dodgeable once the path is read
Missing the Ultimate leaves no gap closer — he becomes a walking target
Early taunts last about a second, so early dives tend to backfire

playstyle.style: The taunt tank: he forces enemies to attack him, embodying aggro control. His scythe pulls and self-healing sustain the frontline — rated easy, but the craft runs deep.
playstyle.suited: Players at peace with 'getting hit is the job,' quietly wasting the enemy's entire damage output with one taunt.

synergy.reason: Locks down enemies with CC, making it much easier to guarantee landing skill 2.
Draws enemy aggro on the frontline, allowing Mi Yue to safely engage, deal damage, and sustain.

counters.reason: Counters Mi Yue's lane pressure with high durability, burst damage, and fast farming.
Can kite and poke from a distance with high mobility, making it extremely difficult for Mi Yue to land her chain.

passive.description:
Mi Yue summons shadow servants when using skills, which automatically attack nearby enemies. Each strike deals 50 (50 + 7% magical attack) magical damage while restoring 20 (20 + 0.5% extra Health) Health to her. Strikes deal an extra 80 (80 + 14% magical attack) magical damage to minions and deal half damage against monsters.
She gains 30 Shadow Power when summoning shadow servants, which grants up to 30 Movement Speed and a 10% bonus to all healing.
She can have up to 6 shadow servants around her at a time. When Shadow Power reaches zero, the servants will disappear.
passive.name: Passive Skill: Eternal Youth

skill1.description:
Mi Yue unleashes shadow energy, dealing 200 (200 + 24% magical attack) magical damage to enemies in its path.
Upon using this skill again, she manifests herself at the shadow energy's location and deals 200 (200 + 24% magical attack) magical damage to nearby enemies.
She summons a shadow servant if she hits an enemy at the new location.
skill1.name: Skill 1: Dark Transfer

skill2.description:
Mi Yue sends out a tether forward, linking to the first enemy hit for up to 4s. Every 0.5s, she slows the linked target by 1.25%-2.5% (increases with skill level), steals 10 physical attack and 30 magical attack, deals 30 (30 + 7% magical attack) magical damage, and recovers 10 (10 + 0.25% extra Health) Health.
The tether will break if the distance between her and her target exceeds 1,000 units. If the tether remains intact for the full 4s, she will summon a shadow servant.
Passive: Her Basic Attack is enhanced, dealing 200 (40 + 100% physical attack + 20% magical attack) magical damage, slowing enemies by 10%, and granting 10 Shadow Power.
skill2.name: Skill 2: Ravenous Tether

skill3.description:
Mi Yue disappears into the shadows for 2s, removing all debuffs and gaining 30% Movement Speed and immunity to all effects.
Upon disappearing and returning, she deals 380 (380 + 70% magical attack) magical damage to nearby enemies.
If she lands a hit upon returning, she summons a shadow servant.
skill3.name: Skill 3: Umbral Moon

strategy.earlyGame: Mi Yue hits her stride at level 1 with Skill 2. In the clash lane, tether the enemy laner: while linked you siphon their physical and magical attack while your chip damage and healing tick together — a one-sided trade. Holding the link for the full 4 seconds spawns an extra shadow servant, so pick fights early and build toward the six-servant cap. The chain snaps at range, though, so when they back off, don't chase — use Skill 1's recast movement to return to the wave safely.
strategy.midGame: Mid-game Mi Yue rules the side of the map by forcing 1v1s. From around 8 minutes, push the clash lane wave and welcome whichever fighter comes to answer with a Skill 2-led war of attrition. Even when their jungler makes it 2v1, the Ultimate's 2-second shadow form negates everything — eat their burst, come back out, and the turnaround is more realistic than it looks. Train the reflex: enemy assassin commits, then you press Ultimate, and you stop dying. Skip coin-flip Tyrant fights and take the tower they left behind instead.
strategy.lateGame: A straight 5v5 is still not your arena, so keep the side pressure up through the late game. With four items done, no single enemy stops you, and two enemies coming means numbers advantages everywhere else. When you do join Overlord or Shadow Tyrant fights, work the edge: tether their frontline with Skill 2 to drain attack damage, indirectly cutting what your team takes. Treat the Ultimate as a reactive dodge, not an escape — hold it until you see the enemy's big cooldown, then make it whiff.
strategy.teamfight: Never enter from the front. Open from a flank by tethering their key fighter or marksman with Skill 2 — a drained enemy hits nowhere near their listed numbers, and 4 seconds of link restocks a servant. When heads turn your way, double-dash out with Skill 1; if they chase, answer with the Ultimate's immunity and let their skills hit nothing. With six servants up, Mi Yue heals back damage just by walking around, so dragging the fight out is itself the win condition.

combos.title: Win the Tether
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (link, steal attack) → enhanced Basic Attack → Skill 1 → Skill 1 (recast to descend)
combos.description: The tether lasts up to 4s. Every 0.5s it steals 10 Physical Attack and 30 Magical Attack while chipping and healing at the same time. Hold it the full 4s and a shadow servant joins her. It breaks past 1,000 units, so recast Skill 1 to close the gap the moment they back away.

combos.title: Hold the Immunity
combos.sequence: Skill 3 (2s in shadow, all debuffs removed) → Skill 1 → Skill 1 (recast)
combos.description: Two seconds in shadow nullify all effects and clear the debuffs already on Mi Yue. That makes it a reaction, not an opener — save it for the enemy's big move. Damage of 380 (Lvl 1) lands both when she vanishes and when she returns, and a hit on the return summons a servant. Recast Skill 1 afterwards to leave on your own terms.

strengths: Skill 2 drains enemy attack, and with shadow servant healing she's a top-tier duelist
Ultimate's 2 seconds of full immunity and cleanse make enemy ace cooldowns whiff
Shadow servants stack just from casting — longer fights mean more damage and more healing
weaknesses: Zero hard CC — no way to peel for allies or lock down fleeing enemies
Damage-over-time kit loses the healing race against instant burst
A skirmish specialist whose influence thins in full frontal teamfights

playstyle.style: A dark mage attended by auto-attacking shadow claws, weakening enemies through her draining link. Her ultimate phases her out of existence entirely, buying a reset near the frontline.
playstyle.suited: Players who like layering summon pressure over personal pressure — with an untouchable ultimate as the safety line.

synergy.reason: Can reset ultimate cooldowns, allowing for double jumps to completely dominate teamfights.
Groups enemies up, ensuring Lu Bu can land his massive AoE ultimate on multiple targets.

counters.reason: Uses high mobility to dodge Lu Bu's attacks while relentlessly poking him from a distance with true damage.
Can knock Lu Bu away the moment he lands from his ultimate, preventing him from disrupting the team's formation.

passive.description:
Lu Bu's Crescent Halberd becomes enchanted for 8s after striking an enemy hero. Basic Attacks and skills deal an equal amount of true damage while it is enchanted. When not enchanted, Basic Attacks and skills gain 35% Physical Pierce.
While his weapon is enchanted, Lu Bu recovers 80 (80 + 1.3% extra Health) Health on each Basic Attack hit.
passive.name: Passive Skill: Bloodthirsty Ancestry

skill1.description: Lu Bu slashes in the target direction with his Crescent Halberd, dealing 600 (600 + 200% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies within range. He loses his enhanced state if the slash does not hit an enemy hero. While enhanced, he recovers 130 (130 + 2.5% extra Health) Health whenever he hits an enemy with his Skill 1.
skill1.name: Skill 1: Impaling Thrust

skill2.description:
Lu Bu captures the souls of enemies in the target area, dealing 100 (100 + 35% extra physical attack) physical damage and reducing their Movement Speed by 15% for 3s.
Each captured soul grants him a shield, for up to 3 stacks. Each stack of shield negates 350 (350 + 7% extra Health) damage. He converts 25% of his remaining shield to Health every second, gaining 1 Health for every 2 points of shield.
skill2.name: Skill 2: Souleater

skill3.description:
Lu Bu leaps to the target location and creates a ring of slaughter, launching enemies within range for 1s. He gains crowd control immunity during the leap. Upon landing, he swings his Crescent Halberd, dealing 650 (650 + 240% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies within range. While his Halberd is enchanted, he recovers 130 (130 + 2.5% extra Health) Health for every enemy hero hit.
He gains 150 physical defense and 150 magical defense within the ring. Enemies that touch the edge of the ring take 150 (150 + 75% extra physical attack) physical damage and are slowed by 30% for 2s. He restores Health for every enemy hero who takes damage this way.
skill3.name: Skill 3: Tremble, Mortals

strategy.earlyGame: In the clash lane, Lu Bu lives and dies by landing Skill 1 on enemy heroes. A hit enchants his halberd for 8 seconds, adding true damage to basic attacks and skills plus healing per swing — but whiffing it on heroes removes the enchant entirely, so never burn it on a minion wave out of habit. Open trades with Skill 2: the more enemies it clips, the more shield stacks you bank (up to three), each ticking back into HP. Keep trades even until level 4, then hit the gas once your Ultimate unlocks.
strategy.midGame: From level 4, Lu Bu headlines the 4-minute Tyrant fight. The Ultimate is a descending 1-second knock-up with CC immunity until landing — a reliable counter-engage you can throw after seeing the enemy's first move. Inside the kill zone you gain 150 physical and 150 magical defense, so the iron rule is: fight inside the circle. Enchanted true damage ignores armor, so your damage doesn't fall off as the lane opponent stacks defense — build tanky yourself and let the true damage carry the numbers.
strategy.lateGame: Late game you play two roles: frontline and backline diver. Before fights, load three Skill 2 shields off minions or their frontline, then drop the Ultimate at the enemy marksman's feet. The zone's defensive bonus plus true damage means tanks and squishies both count as valid targets. Watch out for the mobility void after the Ultimate is spent — land at the edge of a fight and you're stuck walking back into relevance. Drop only when they clump and stop moving: the late-game mantra.
strategy.teamfight: The ideal script: bank shields with Skill 2, wait for their formation to lock in place, Ultimate into the center, then unload Skill 1 and basic attacks with true damage during the 1-second knock-up. Keep the 8-second enchant timer in mind — as long as you're hitting any enemy hero, the healing never stops. Getting shredded in the scrum? Re-cast Skill 2 into three enemies and a 1000-plus shield rebuilds you. The zone's rim slows anyone leaving, so land the Ultimate a half-step toward their escape route.

combos.title: Shield Up, Then Drop
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (one shield stack per enemy) → Skill 3 (1s launch, CC immune until landing) → Skill 1 → Basic Attack
combos.description: Skill 2 grants one shield stack for every unit caught, minions included — 350 (Lvl 1) per stack, 3 stacks maximum. The leap ignores crowd control until he lands, so you can answer an enemy stun with it. Stay inside the ring once you are down. It grants 150 physical defense and 150 magical defense.

combos.title: Keep the Halberd Enchanted
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (must hit an enemy hero) → Basic Attack → Basic Attack → Skill 2
combos.description: A Skill 1 that hits no enemy hero strips the enchant. Never spend it clearing the minion wave. A hit arms it for 8s, and each basic attack during that window restores 80 (Lvl 1) Health. Close with Skill 2 for the shield and a 15% slow for 3s before you disengage.

strengths: Enchanted true damage cuts through stacked armor — even tanks aren't safe
Ultimate descends CC-immune with a knock-up, so his engage rarely gets interrupted
Skill 2 shields plus healing basic attacks sustain him through long brawls
weaknesses: Whiffing Skill 1 on heroes drops the enchant — damage and healing die together
The Ultimate is his only movement; once it's spent, he walks everywhere
No lockdown beyond the Ultimate and slows, so kiting marksmen frustrate him

playstyle.style: A fighter whose enchanted halberd deals true damage that no armor answers. His ultimate descends with a knock-up and claims the ground — where he lands becomes the center of the fight.
playstyle.suited: Players who light up when the enemy stacks defense — wielding violence that ignores the rules of mitigation.

synergy.reason: Hooks enemies directly into Zhou Yu's fire zones, locking them down for heavy sustained damage.
Protects Zhou Yu from assassin dives with shields and teleports, ensuring he can keep dealing sustained damage.

counters.reason: Uses high mobility to bypass the fire zones and quickly burst Zhou Yu down.
Easily disrupts Zhou Yu's zone control with long-range poke and stuns.

passive.description:
Zhou Yu's Basic Attacks and skills place fire marks on enemies (including structures) for 4s. At 4 stacks, the marks ignite, dealing 125 (125 + 17% magical attack) magical damage per second for 4s and reducing the target's Movement Speed by 15% for 1s.
Targets cannot gain more marks while burning.
passive.name: Passive Skill: Blaze

skill1.description:
Zhou Yu invokes a wind domain. Teammates within the domain gain 5% Movement Speed (up to 5 heroes; effect doubled for Zhou Yu), while enemy heroes' Movement Speed are reduced by 10% for 3s. When the wind is invoked, enemies within range are knocked back in the target direction and take 200 (200 + 30% magical attack) magical damage.
If the wind domain overlaps with a fire domain for 1s, a new fire domain spreads in the target direction, dealing 100 (100 + 25% magical attack) magical damage every 0.5s. This damage stacks with any existing fire domains.
skill1.name: Skill 1: Wildfire

skill2.description:
Zhou Yu calls down a volley of flaming arrows at the target location, dealing 250 (250 + 40% magical attack) magical damage and leaving behind a fire domain that lasts for 6.5s. The fire domain deals 100 (100 + 30% magical attack) magical damage to enemies within range every 0.5s. There can be up to 6 fire domains present at any time, after which creating a new fire domain will extinguish the first one. Zhou Yu stocks 1 volley every 9s (affected by Cooldown Reduction), and up to 3 can be stocked.
Passive: While inside a fire domain, he recovers 35 (35 + 7% magical attack + 2% extra Health) Health every 0.5s.
skill2.name: Skill 2: Scorching Bolt

skill3.description: Zhou Yu unleashes a burst of flames in the target area, dealing 200 (200 + 40% magical attack) magical damage. If the flames travel through a fire domain, a firestorm is created, dealing an extra 200 (200 + 40% magical attack) magical damage to enemies within range and stunning them for 1s.
skill3.name: Skill 3: Flames of War

strategy.earlyGame: Zhou Yu's lane is a placement puzzle for Skill 2's fire arrows. They restock every 9 seconds up to three, and each burn zone lasts 6.5 seconds, so budget one for the wave and one for pressure. The core habit is placing flames where the enemy wants to retreat, shrinking their playable space. You heal while standing in your own fire thanks to the Passive, so trading on top of your flames is a fight you're happy to take. Your Ultimate only stuns when it passes through a burn zone, so even past level 4, everything starts with Skill 2.
strategy.midGame: The 4-minute Tyrant kicks off Zhou Yu's setup game. Thirty seconds before it spawns, push mid and reach the pit first, laying two arrows across the entrance. The enemy detouring around your flames is zoning working exactly as intended. When the fight starts, spread the burn with Skill 1's wind field, knock their formation loose, then send the Ultimate through the widened flames for a multi-man stun. The Passive's 4-stack ignition ticks hard too — in tight corridors, enemies sometimes sit at half HP off placement alone.
strategy.lateGame: Late-game Zhou Yu wins fights before they start. Carpet the approach to Overlord or Shadow Tyrant with burn zones: your team gets the wind field's speed while the enemy is forced through flames and slows. With items done, overlapped flames in a narrow path melt even tanks off pure damage over time. The weakness is self-defense — no dash means a read on your position is a death sentence. Stay behind your team, always within reach of your own fire, and keep shooting.
strategy.teamfight: Run the same teamfight script until it's muscle memory. Open with two Skill 2 arrows layered between the teams, push the flames enemy-ward with Skill 1's wind and knockback, then fire the Ultimate through the extended flame line for a clustered 1-second AoE stun. From there, keep feeding restocked arrows onto their escape paths and backline — the enemy is forever choosing between burning and backing off. New and old burn zones stack their damage, so deliberately doubling them on one spot builds a genuinely lethal firepit — a veteran's move.

combos.title: Lay the Fire Line
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (fire domain) → Skill 2 (stacked) → Skill 1 (knockback, spreads the fire) → Skill 3 (firestorm, 1s stun)
combos.description: Skill 3 only stuns when its flames travel through a fire domain, so the fire has to be down first. Once the wind domain covers a fire domain for 1s, a new one spreads in the direction you chose, and old and new domains stack their damage. You stock one volley every 9s up to 3, so spending two on the opener still leaves one in hand.

combos.title: Keep the Marks Alive
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (fire arrows + fire domain) → Basic Attack → Skill 1 (knockback) → Basic Attack
combos.description: Marks expire after 4s, so chain a Basic Attack and Skill 1 straight after the arrows. Reach four stacks and the target ignites, taking 125 (Lvl 1) magical damage per second for 4s. A burning target gains no new marks, so hold the follow-up until the fire runs out.

strengths: Overlapped burn zones melt even tanks with sustained damage in narrow terrain
Ultimate through flames becomes an AoE 1-second stun — real CC on a zone mage
Heals while standing in his own fire, making him stubborn on claimed ground
Skill 1's knockback doubles as self-peel and engage-breaking
weaknesses: Setup takes steps, so he reacts poorly to sudden skirmishes and flanks
The Ultimate only stuns through a burn zone — on its own it stops no one
No mobility skill; once his position is read and dived, there's no answer

playstyle.style: An area-denial mage who pre-burns the ground enemies want to stand on, stacking ignition marks until they catch fire. He wins not by aiming at enemies but by removing their real estate.
playstyle.suited: Players who design the board — restricting where the enemy may walk until there's nowhere left.

synergy.reason: Zhang Fei's Skill 3 wind knocks enemies back and stuns those at its far end for 1.5s. A pinned target makes it far easier for Yango to land both strings of Skill 3, and hitting with both adds physical damage equal to 13% of the target's lost Health. His 4 paper birds connect too.

counters.reason: Diaochan's Skill 3 circle damages when it opens and again when it closes, and Skill 2 scatters 3 petals, so area chip is constantly on the ground. The puppet takes 100% extra damage and breaks quickly under it. When it breaks, Yango is stunned for 2s and cannot resummon for 20-16s.

Gao Changgong's Skill 2 dagger places a mark on the enemy it hits. His attack on a marked target stuns for 1s and restores 350 (+10% extra Health) to him, so damage Yango deals gets paid back. His Skill 1 shadow copy also prioritizes heroes with low Health.

passive.name: Passive Skill: Occult Arts - Manipulation
passive.description:
When Yango and the puppet's Basic Attacks hit an enemy hero, they have a 30% chance of granting a Hero Shard and restoring 70 (70 + 1% extra Health) Health.
Yango's Recovery skill is replaced with Hero Shards. He can stock up to 150 Hero Shards, which can be used to turn his puppet into a copy of an enemy hero. He automatically stocks 1 Hero Shard every 10-5s, depending on his level.
Hero Puppet: Consumes 50 Hero Shards to transform the puppet into a copy of the selected hero for 10s. The hero puppet possesses all of the copied hero's skills, but only deals 50% damage and takes an extra 100% damage compared to them. The hero puppet becomes stronger with Yango, dealing 1% more damage for every 15 extra Physical Attack and taking 2% less damage for every 80 extra Health.

skill1.name: Skill 1: Occult Arts - Umbra / Occult Arts - Return

forms.description:
Yango throws the puppet, dealing 300 (300 + 100% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies in its path and launching them for 0.5s. He then starts controlling the puppet. The puppet's Basic Attacks deal 100% physical attack physical damage. When recalled, the puppet purifies crowd control effects from Yango and grants him 40% Movement Speed for 1s, as well as a shield that negates 420 (420 + 6% extra Health) damage.
When the puppet is destroyed, Yango is revealed and stunned for 2s. He is then unable to summon the puppet for 20-16s. If the puppet remains beyond a range of 2,500 from Yango for 5s, it is automatically destroyed.
Normal Puppet: Inherits all of Yango's equipment effects (excluding Revive, Blood Fury, Dark Curtain, and Mana Shield), inherits certain buff effects, and shares Gold and EXP with him.
Retrieves the puppet immediately, dealing 300 (300 + 100% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies along the path and launching them for 0.5s.

The puppet's Basic Attacks deal 100% physical attack physical damage. forms.skill_name: Skill 2: Occult Arts - Zhi Chu Luan
forms.description: Yango sends out 4 paper birds, dealing 435 (435 + 165% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies in their paths. When multiple paper birds hit the same target, the damage is reduced by 50% for subsequent hits.

The puppet swaps locations with Yango if it is within a range of 900 from him; otherwise, it will move to a location that is 900 from him, dealing 300 (300 + 100% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies in its path.
If the puppet's movements have been restricted, this skill pulls Yango to the puppet and returns control to him.

skill2.skill_name: Skill 2: Occult Arts - Zhi Chu Luan / Occult Arts - Substitution
skill2.description: Yango sends out 4 paper birds, dealing 435 (435 + 165% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies in their paths. When multiple paper birds hit the same target, the damage is reduced by 50% for subsequent hits.

The puppet deals 300 (300 + 100% extra physical attack) physical damage to nearby enemies and slows them by 250 for 2s.
If the skill is used again within 3s, it will enter its 2nd phase. After a brief delay, the puppet will stun enemies continuously, with each strike dealing 120 (120 + 40% extra physical attack) magical damage.

skill3.skill_name: Skill 3: Occult Arts - Shadow Crucifixion / Occult Arts - Binding
skill3.description: Yango releases two strings then pulls them back, each string dealing 180 (180 + 90% extra physical attack) physical damage. Enemies hit by both strings take extra physical damage equal to 13% of lost Health and are slowed by 30% for 2s.

skill4.name: Skill 4: Occult Arts - Dispersal / Occult Arts - Breakout

forms.description:
Yango instantly vanishes, cleansing all crowd control effects from himself, then reappears in the target location after a short delay.
Does not cleanse the stun effect from the puppet being destroyed.

The puppet charges in the target direction, dealing 300 (300 + 100% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies in its path.
If the puppet's movements have been restricted, then control is passed back to its master.

skill4.skill_name: Skill 4: Occult Arts - Dispersal / Occult Arts - Breakout
skill4.description:
Yango instantly vanishes, cleansing all crowd control effects from himself, then reappears in the target location after a short delay.
Does not cleanse the stun effect from the puppet being destroyed.

strategy.earlyGame: Yango's opening minutes are about collecting shards and getting comfortable on the puppet. Shards accrue passively over time, but basic attacks on enemy heroes have a chance to grant extras, so roam between lanes and harass from safe range. Skill 1's puppet doubles as a bush scout, but if it's destroyed, your real body is stunned for 2 seconds and locked out of resummoning for roughly 20 — don't toss it carelessly at enemies with skills still up. Without his puppet, Yango is just a squishy melee hero.
strategy.midGame: Once you bank 50 shards, the Passive's hero transformation widens your playbook. The copy matches the original's kit exactly, so the standard play is borrowing an enemy with CC or a dash as your engage tool. Ganks start with Skill 1's puppet launch: the 0.5-second knock-up on hit, whittling through puppet control, then the recall — its purify and shield transfer to your body as you finish with Skill 2's hidden weapons. Keep the real body behind walls and bushes, showing the enemy only the puppet. That habit separates Yango players.
strategy.lateGame: In late-game teamfights, the puppet is the perfect decoy. Walk it into the enemy's path before the fight; when they burn skills on it, that's your cue. It takes 100% extra damage and breaks easily, so recall early when threatened and convert the purify and shield into your own engage. For the finish, chain Skill 2's four paper birds into Skill 3's strings, which pull you back out as they land. The 13% of lost Health only applies to a target hit by both strings — land one and it's chip damage, nothing more. Line up the angle before you fire, especially on a target already low. Once your real body is caught, the fight is basically lost, so check your exit before anything else.
strategy.teamfight: The rule is simple: the real Yango doesn't fight. Send the puppet in from a flank to pressure their backline, and only move your body once you've confirmed their CC and big cooldowns have gone into the doll. The moment they spend a major skill on the puppet is the only window where you're allowed forward. Start with Skill 1's knock-up, and once a target is pinched between puppet and body — with 50 shards turning that puppet into a copy of an enemy hero — you are effectively more than two attackers. Skill 3's strings can cap a combo or buy your spacing back. When a collapse actually lands on you, the answer is Skill 4: it cleanses every crowd control effect and drops you somewhere else. Hold it for that, and remember it cannot clear the 2-second stun from a destroyed puppet.

combos.title: Bind With the Puppet, Finish in Person
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (launch the puppet, 0.5s launch) → Skill 3 in puppet form (250 slow) → recast within 3s (continuous stun) → Skill 1 in puppet form (recall) → Skill 2
combos.description: A clean launch buys 0.5s of hang time. Follow with puppet-form Skill 3, then recast inside 3 seconds to reach the second phase, which stuns continuously after a brief delay. Recalling purifies crowd control from Yango and hands him 40% Movement Speed for 1s plus a 420 (Lvl 1) shield to walk in behind. If the puppet is about to die, recall early — losing it stuns him for 2s.

combos.title: Swap Into Their Backline
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (launch the puppet) → Skill 4 in puppet form (charge deeper) → Skill 2 in puppet form (swap places) → Skill 1 in puppet form (recall) → Skill 3
combos.description: Within 900 units, puppet-form Skill 2 trades the puppet's position with Yango's outright. Charge the puppet past the enemy first and the swap plants him behind them. The recall itself launches anyone in its path for 0.5s, which is the window for the strings. Land both strings and the target takes an extra 13% of their lost Health.

strengths: The puppet leads, soaking enemy skills and attention while his body stays hidden
50 shards turn the puppet into a copy of an enemy hero, borrowing their ace card for 10 seconds
Skill 1's knock-up plus the recall's purify and shield cover offense and defense
Skill 3 adds 13% of lost Health when both strings connect, and creates distance as it lands
weaknesses: The puppet takes double damage, and its destruction stuns the real body for 2 seconds
Controlling the puppet leaves the real body exposed to a pincer
Extremely demanding to pilot — below mastery, you get half the hero

playstyle.style: A one-of-a-kind puppeteer who fights through his puppet while keeping his real body safe. You manage two positions at once, trading mind games with the enemy's vision.
playstyle.suited: Players who enjoy complexity for its own sake — mastery here creates an information gap most opponents can't answer.

synergy.reason: Li Bai's Skill 1 dashes twice, stunning enemies for 0.5s and building Sword Energy, and the third cast returns him to where he started. He can follow Dun's Skill 3 dive and its 1s stun into the fight and still get back out. Four stacks unlock Flickering Flurry.

Arli's Skill 1 blinks and leaves the parasol behind. For the 4s she is without it, she gains 30-60 Movement Speed and 10-20% Attack Speed. If Dun steps in first with his crowd-control-immune Skill 3, she can spend that window attacking instead of escaping, and Autumn Storm knocks back anyone who closes.

counters.reason: While Lu Bu's halberd is enchanted, his Basic Attacks and skills carry true damage; while it is not, they gain 35% Physical Pierce. Neither state cares that Dun stacks Health and defense. Inside his Skill 3 ring, Lu Bu gains 150 physical and 150 magical defense on top of that.

Diaochan's Skill 1 lotus damages on the way out and on the way back, so she stacks floral marks from range. Four marks detonate for true damage and a 50% slow for 1s, and that reaches Dun however much defense he buys. Her Skill 2 blink steps away from his chained blade.

passive.description: If Dun takes damage while his Health is below 50%, he becomes enhanced for 8s. While enhanced, whenever he hits an enemy with a Basic Attack or skill, he recovers 220 (220 +6% extra Health) Health. This passive effect can only be triggered once every 25s. (Decreases with hero level.)
passive.name: Passive Skill: Unyielding Might

skill1.description:
Dun swings his blade, creating a gust of wind in the target direction, dealing 400 (400 + 130% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies within range and slowing them by 25% for 2s.
If the wind hits any enemy, he can use the skill again within 5s in the target direction, dealing 400 (400 + 130% extra physical attack) physical damage and launching enemies for 1s.
skill1.name: Skill 1: Wind Slash

skill2.description: Dun deals 300 (300 + 100% extra physical attack) magical damage to nearby enemies and gains a shield that negates damage equal to 500 (500 + 12% extra Health) for 5s. His next 3 Basic Attacks are enhanced for 8s, dealing an extra 150 (150 + 45% extra physical attack) true damage each. Hitting enemies reduces the cooldown of his Ultimate by 1s.
skill2.name: Skill 2: Gale's Benediction

skill3.description:
Dun throws his chained blade in the target direction, which stops upon hitting an enemy or reaching its max range.
The blade stuns the first enemy it hits for 1s. Dun deals 400 (400 + 10% extra Health) physical damage to enemies near the blade and pulls himself to its location. Upon reaching the blade's location, he deals 400 (400 + 10% extra Health) physical damage to nearby enemies again.
Dun gains immunity to crowd control while using this skill.
skill3.name: Skill 3: Unruly Blade

strategy.earlyGame: Your Clash Lane game plan starts with landing Skill 1's shockwave. Connect the first hit and the second cast's knock-up follows, letting you clear the wave and harass your lane opponent in one motion — that is what makes Dun's laning so comfortable. Don't be afraid to take even trades below 50% HP, since your Passive kicks in and refunds the damage through on-hit healing. Just remember it only triggers once every 25 seconds; the moment it's spent, take a step back so you don't get run down. Once you hit level 4 and unlock your Ultimate, a coordinated dive with your jungler generates real kill pressure.
strategy.midGame: From the 4-minute Tyrant fight onward, your Ultimate's stun and pull is your team's engage button. The priority targets are the enemy jungler or mid laner — but the chain blade stops on the first thing it touches, so never throw it through a screen of minions or frontliners. In fights, cycle Skill 2's shield and your empowered basic attacks: every hit shaves a second off your Ultimate's cooldown, setting up your next catch. With one or two defensive items online, Dun doesn't fold to a bit of focus fire.
strategy.lateGame: By the time your third defensive item is finished, you're playing pure engage tank. Your single most important job is landing the one-second stun on the enemy carry and pulling your team in behind it. Decide your escape route before you throw, so a miss doesn't turn into a death. In standoffs before Overlord or Shadow Tyrant, an ambush from a bush lands far more often than a face-to-face throw. Even after dumping your full combo, the shield and Passive healing let you survive one more exchange — that's what makes late-game Dun so dependable.
strategy.teamfight: Open every teamfight with an Ultimate catch. On hit, the pull puts you point-blank, so stack Skill 1's two-part knock-up on top, throw up Skill 2's shield, and simply refuse to leave the enemy's side of the fight. You're immune to crowd control while the Ultimate is active, so nothing they do can stop your entry. Keep landing empowered basics and the Ultimate comes back faster than you'd expect — throwing it twice in one fight is common. Staying alive is priority one: cutting off the enemy carry's escape route beats chasing kills every time.

combos.title: Chained Catch
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (2s slow) → Skill 3 (1s stun, pulls Dun to the blade) → Skill 1 recast (1s launch) → Skill 2 (shield, 3 enhanced Basic Attacks)
combos.description: Open with the wind slash so their feet are stuck. The chained blade stops on the first enemy it touches, so do not throw it through a minion wave. Once the pull drops Dun on top of the target, the recast — available within 5s of the first hit — launches them for another second. Skill 3 also grants immunity to crowd control while it runs, so enemy peel will not stop the entry.

combos.title: Trade From Low Health
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (2s slow) → Skill 1 recast (1s launch) → Skill 2 (shield, 3 enhanced Basic Attacks) → 3 enhanced Basic Attacks
combos.description: Dun is at his best once his Health falls under 50%. Take damage there and the passive turns on for 8s, healing him every time a skill or Basic Attack connects. Land the Skill 1 recast on a slowed target, put up the shield, and swing all three enhanced Basic Attacks. Those three carry true damage, and every hit shaves 1s off Skill 3's cooldown.

strengths: Reliable pick potential with the Ultimate's one-second stun and pull
Excellent frontline staying power from stacking the shield with Passive healing
True damage on empowered basics punishes armor stackers
CC immunity during the Ultimate makes his engage unstoppable
weaknesses: Skill 3 stops on minions and rarely reaches its real target in messy fights
Passive healing has a 25-second cooldown, leaving him weak in back-to-back fights
His only mobility is Skill 3's pull — miss it and long-range kiting goes unanswered

playstyle.style: A defensive tank whose healing awakens below half Health — he wins by refusing to finish dying. A stunning chain-blade and area shield round out a kit built for weathering storms.
playstyle.suited: Players strongest in the defensive hour, laying the foundation for comebacks one refused death at a time.

synergy.reason: Locks down enemies in teamfights with knockbacks and stuns, allowing Lady Zhen to easily land her skills and ultimate on multiple targets.
Compensates for Lady Zhen's low mobility with speed buffs, and locks down enemies to easily proc her freezing passive.

counters.reason: Uses untargetability and high mobility to bypass Lady Zhen's CC and instantly burst her squishy down.
Bursts Lady Zhen down with long-range dives and silences before she can even cast a single skill.

passive.description: Every time Lady Zhen's skills deal damage, she places a frozen mark on the enemy for 7s, up to 3 stacks. At max stacks, the target takes 250 (250 + 30% magical attack) magical damage and is frozen for 0.75s. The duration of repeated freeze effects is reduced to 0.5s.
passive.name: Passive Skill: Frozen Touch

skill1.description: Lady Zhen conjures icicles at the target location, blocking heroes and dealing 500 (500 + 70% magical attack) magical damage to enemies within range and launching them for 1s. The icicles last 8s and continuously inflict 10% slow on nearby enemies. If Lady Zhen is within range when the icicles are conjured, she will be frozen in an invincible state for 3s. The icicles shatter violently when the skill ends or is canceled, dealing 150 (150 + 35% magical attack) magical damage to nearby enemies and inflicting 10% slow for 3s. Damage is doubled at the center.
skill1.name: Skill 1: Ocean of Tears

skill2.description:
Lady Zhen fires a water orb at the target which bounces between nearby enemy units up to 5-7 times (max number increases when skill level reaches 3 and 5). Each bounce deals 230 (230 + 40% magical attack) magical damage to enemies.
Icicles are considered targets. Once the orb is unable to continue bouncing, it will disappear at its current target's location after a 3s delay.
skill2.name: Skill 2: Flowing Sigh

skill3.description:
Lady Zhen unleashes a water spirit in the target direction, knocking back non-hero units. Upon hitting an enemy hero or reaching its maximum range, the water spirit forms a pool, dealing 300 (300 + 65% magical attack) magical damage to the first hero hit and reducing their Movement Speed by 90% for 1s.
The pool lasts for 5s, dealing 150 (150 + 32% magical attack) magical damage every second to enemies in its range and reducing their Movement Speed by 25% for 1.5s.
skill3.name: Skill 3: Destructive Deluge

strategy.earlyGame: Start your mid lane by clearing with Skill 2. The water current bounces between minions on its own, so firing it the moment the enemy laner steps near their wave turns clear and harass into one cast. Your Passive's frost marks last seven seconds, and three stacks trigger a 0.75-second freeze — land two or three bounces, follow with Skill 1, and you can freeze targets as early as level 2. That said, the ice pillar comes out slowly and gets sidestepped on its own, so treat it as a placement tool for the moment your opponent steps forward. Don't force plays before level 4; keeping your lane opponent at half HP is a job well done.
strategy.midGame: Once you learn your Ultimate, Lady Zhen becomes a gank-assist specialist. The water current slaps a 90% slow — a near-total stop — on the first hero it hits for a full second, so firing it as your jungler arrives all but guarantees the catch. Chain Skill 1 and Skill 2 behind it and you ride straight into a three-stack freeze. From the 4-minute mark, rotate toward the river about 30 seconds before Tyrant spawns and lay your Ultimate's flood zone across the narrow river paths to seal off the enemy's approach entirely. Anyone who steps in bleeds damage every second, forcing a choice between a long detour and walking through the pain.
strategy.lateGame: With three core items finished, chained freezes alone let you dictate teamfights — but your own body stays paper-thin, so always operate from behind your frontline. When an enemy assassin dives you, the trump card is self-freezing: cast Skill 1 on top of your Ultimate's flood zone to become invulnerable for three seconds and let their whole combo whiff. The pillar's collapse damage on exit even sets up your counterattack. You can't move while frozen and everyone knows exactly where you are, so save it for moments your teammates can collapse as you thaw. Narrow-corridor standoffs before Overlord are where Lady Zhen has no equal.
strategy.teamfight: Before the fight starts, fire your Ultimate down a narrow approach to break the enemy's formation with the flood zone. Pour Skill 2 into anyone caught standing still — the bouncing current farms frost marks across clumped enemies and can freeze several of them at once. A frozen target eats your team's entire damage output without answering back, so landing the chain effectively ends the fight. If you get dived, self-freeze with Skill 1 inside the zone and wait the three seconds for help. The one thing to respect: miss your Ultimate and you've lost your pick tool until it returns, so back off rather than gamble.

combos.title: Freeze Chain Setup
combos.sequence: Skill 3 (90% slow for 1s on the first hero hit, leaves a pool) → Skill 1 (1s launch) → Skill 2 (bouncing water orb)
combos.description: The water spirit all but roots the first hero it touches, which is what makes the slow-forming icicles reliable. Follow up with the orb, which bounces between nearby units. Every instance of skill damage applies one frost mark, so three connections reach the 0.75s freeze.

combos.title: Lane Mark Poke
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (bouncing water orb) → Skill 1 (1s launch, icicles last 8s)
combos.description: The orb hops between minions and hands out frost marks, so fire it when the enemy laner steps toward the wave. Icicles are slow to appear and get walked out of on their own. Even without the freeze, the launch plus eight seconds of slow around the pillars keeps the trade in your favor.

combos.title: Self-Freeze at Your Feet
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (conjure it so you are inside the range: 3s invulnerable) → cancel the freeze (icicles shatter for damage and a 3s slow) → Skill 2
combos.description: When a diver commits, drop the icicles so that Lady Zhen herself is inside their range. Being in range at the moment of casting freezes her into three seconds of invulnerability and the dive whiffs. The pillars also block heroes outright, and shattering them doubles the damage on anything at the center.

strengths: Every skill applies frost marks, chaining lockdown through three-stack freezes
Bouncing water damage that gets stronger the more enemies clump together
Elite zoning — the flood zone and ice pillar seal off narrow corridors
A self-freeze escape hatch worth three seconds of invulnerability
weaknesses: Skill 1 is slow to arm and hard to land without a slow set up first
Missing the Ultimate removes her pick threat almost entirely
No mobility skill — one positioning mistake is usually fatal
Enemies who time her thaw can delete her before the counterattack comes

playstyle.style: A lockdown mage who freezes enemies at three ice marks and reshapes the map with an impassable ice pillar. Her value is measured in seconds of stopped enemies, not damage.
playstyle.suited: Players who take pride in crowd-control uptime over kills — rewriting the fight's geography with one pillar.

synergy.reason: Donghuang's Skill 3 suppresses one enemy hero for 2s. Against a target that cannot act, Fatih can land all three slashes of Skill 1 plus Skill 2. Keep it short, though: damage the target takes during the suppression is shared with Donghuang.

Guiguzi's Skill 2 pulls enemies in and stuns them for 1s. The tighter the pack, the more max Health Fatih's Sacred Tree Blessing grants him, since it scales by 20% for every enemy hero nearby. If the pull hits a hero, teammates in range also get a shield.

counters.reason: Lu Bu's Skill 3 creates a ring of slaughter, and inside it he gains 150 physical and 150 magical defense, which blunts Fatih's physical output. The landing launches for 1s, and the ring's edge slows by 30%, so Lu Bu also dictates the spacing.

Mulan stacks Balance in dual-sword form, and at 5 stacks it detonates with a 1s silence that locks Fatih out of Sacred Tree Blessing exactly when he wants it. In heavy-sword form she also gains crowd control immunity and 45% damage reduction while casting.

passive.description: After using a skill, Fatih gains 1 enhanced Basic Attack (up to a maximum of 5) as well as 35% Attack Speed. Enhanced Basic Attacks become consecutive long range slashes that recover 100 (100 + 1.6% extra Health) Health (halved when hitting non-hero units).
passive.name: Passive Skill: Only the Strong

skill1.description:
Fatih charges forward and slashes, dealing 300 (300 + 90% extra physical attack) physical damage. This skill can be used up to 3 times. The third slash launches the enemy for 0.5s.
Every unused slash reduces Cooldown by 35%.
skill1.name: Skill 1: The King's Blade

skill2.description:
Fatih unleashes sword energy, dealing 320 (320 + 100% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies in its path and slowing them by 25% for 2s.
Recovers 200 (200 + 3% extra Health) Health for each hero hit (halved for non-hero units).
Hitting enemies with Basic Attacks reduces this skill's Cooldown by 5%.
While Sacred Tree Blessing is active, this skill unleashes 1 additional blast of sword energy.
skill2.name: Skill 2: The King's Return

skill3.description:
Fatih calls upon divine power to remove all crowd control effects on himself, dealing 230 (230 + 75% extra physical attack) physical damage to nearby enemies, as well as gaining 450 (450 + 7% extra Health) max Health (increases by 20% for every 1 enemy hero nearby) and 10% Resistance for 8s.
While this skill is active, Skill 2 and enhanced Basic Attacks unleash an extra wave of sword energy (50% damage) and continuously grant enhanced Basic Attacks.
Tap again to end the skill.
skill3.name: Skill 3: Sacred Tree Blessing

strategy.earlyGame: Fatih's Clash Lane edge is a healing trade: land Skill 2 on the enemy laner and 200 HP comes right back. Until level 4, the loop is simple — tag your opponent with the sword wave, win the sustain war, and reset with your Passive's empowered basic attacks whenever you get chipped. Skill 1 stores three casts, but burning all three every time is a mistake: stop at one or two and each unspent cast refunds 35% of the cooldown, letting you out-tempo your opponent on rotations. Bank the third cast's knock-up as self-defense for when the enemy jungler shows up — it visibly cuts down on early deaths.
strategy.midGame: The moment you learn your Ultimate at level 4 is your first real power spike. It grants CC immunity, raises your max HP, and — crucially — the HP bonus grows another 20% per nearby enemy hero, so you can win skirmishes even against two opponents. While it's active, Skill 2 and your empowered basics each fire an extra sword wave, and your effective damage jumps to roughly 1.5 times normal. Be the first one into the Tyrant-fight scrum and brawl while you heal. Basic attacks also shave Skill 2's cooldown on hit, so never stop swinging — that's the secret to his staying power.
strategy.lateGame: Late game you're a dual threat: side-lane pushing and teamfighting. Almost nobody stops a five-item Fatih head-on, so welcome anyone foolish enough to duel you. One catch: your healing only pays full value against heroes — it's halved on minions — so recovering HP by farming a lane takes longer than you'd think. Before a big fight, don't get greedy; recall and reset. You are at your absolute strongest during the Ultimate's 8-second window and noticeably softer once it drops, so commit to finishing fights inside it.
strategy.teamfight: The advanced play is holding your Ultimate instead of opening with it — pop it the instant enemy CC is aimed your way, and the immunity lets you walk straight through their lockdown into the middle of their team. From there, spray long-range empowered basics and bonus sword waves; there are stretches where your healing genuinely outpaces their damage. Any nearby squishy target is a fine focus, but don't chase deep — the second your Ultimate expires, focus fire melts you. When in doubt, just stand next to your frontline and keep swinging. The enemy formation cracks on its own.

combos.title: Sword-Wave Sustain Trade
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (2s slow, heals on hero hit) → enhanced Basic Attack → Skill 1 (stop after one slash)
combos.description: Skill 2 pays full healing only when it connects with a hero; against minions it is halved. Every skill cast banks an enhanced basic that heals as well, so wave-then-basic refills whatever the trade cost you. Stopping Skill 1 after a single slash leaves two unused casts, cutting its cooldown by 70%.

combos.title: Blessing All-In
combos.sequence: Skill 3 (removes crowd control on himself, raises max Health and Resistance) → Skill 2 (extra wave of sword energy) → enhanced Basic Attack → Skill 1 x3 (third slash launches for 0.5s)
combos.description: Hold Skill 3 until enemies have surrounded you rather than opening with it. The max Health bonus grows by 20% for every enemy hero nearby, so a two-on-one makes Fatih tougher instead of weaker. Inside the 8s window Skill 2 and enhanced basics each add one more wave of sword energy, and all three Skill 1 slashes go out last so the 0.5s launch cuts off the escape.

strengths: Every skill cast banks an empowered basic and 35% bonus attack speed
The Ultimate's HP bonus scales per nearby enemy — tankier when outnumbered
Outstanding sustain from Skill 2's on-hit healing plus empowered basics
Smart Skill 1 charge management massively compresses his cooldowns
weaknesses: Healing requires hitting heroes, so he slowly bleeds out in poke wars
Noticeably squishier whenever the Ultimate is down
Lacks a gap closer and has no answer to enemies who keep their distance

playstyle.style: A berserker who stacks empowered attacks by cycling skills, healing as he swings. His CC-immune ultimate plants him in the center of the fight, out-sustaining the damage aimed at him.
playstyle.suited: Players who want to be the last one standing in the middle of the brawl — staying and out-slugging, not weaving in and out.

synergy.reason: Movement Speed buffs and healing support make it easy for Dian Wei to quickly close the gap and burst down enemies.
Provides AoE CC cleanse in teamfights, allowing Dian Wei to continuously wreak havoc without worrying about getting peeled.

counters.reason: Her high mobility and sustain allow her to kite Dian Wei, chunking his health from a distance while denying his engage.
His suppress ultimate cannot be cleansed, completely shutting down Dian Wei's engage.

passive.description:
All of Dian Wei's skills can cleanse crowd controls. Each successful cleanse grants Mounting Rage for up to 6 stacks, each stack increasing his Physical Attack and Attack Range for 6s.
Mounting Rage: Each stack increases 15-29 physical attack and 35 Attack Range.
Cleansing hard crowd controls and soft crowd controls grants 2 and 1 stack(s) of Mounting Rage respectively.
passive.name: Passive Skill: Mounting Rage

skill1.description: Dian Wei gains 60% Movement Speed, which diminishes over 3s. His next Basic Attack is enhanced, granting an Attack Range equivalent to his max passive stacks, and dealing 220 (220 + 50% extra physical attack) extra physical damage to nearby enemies. When using the enhanced Basic Attack, he will charge toward a target that is beyond his normal Basic Attack range.
skill1.name: Skill 1: Holding On to Sanity

skill2.description:
Dian Wei tramples the ground, dealing 350 (350 + 110% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies within range while slowing them by 25% for 2s. Whenever his Skill 2 hits an enemy, it enhances him for 3s, during which he gains 200% Attack Speed and 20% Basic Attack Lifesteal. For 3s, each Basic Attack hit also restores 30 Health to him.
If he misses, he only gains half of the Attack Speed, Lifesteal, and extra Health recovery effects.
skill2.name: Skill 2: Outburst

skill3.description: Dian Wei launches a leaping slash at the target enemy, dealing 320 (320 + 90% extra physical attack) true damage while slowing them by 30% for 3s. Grants 1 stack of Mounting Rage for each enemy hero hit. If this skill lands a hit, he becomes enhanced for 5s, during which he deals extra true damage to enemies equal to 2% of their Health.
skill3.name: Skill 3: Leap of Fury

strategy.earlyGame: Jungle is the standard assignment. Skill 2's 200% attack speed steroid works on monsters too, putting his clear speed near the top of the jungler class. Open on your two buffs and the riverside camps and race to level 4. Before that, only take ganks that Skill 1's 60% move speed lets you reach for free — Dian Wei doesn't truly come online until his Ultimate, so an incident-free farming start matters more than anything. One thing worth knowing: in early buff scraps, if Skill 2 connects you win most straight slugfests, so you can afford to play those confidently.
strategy.midGame: Once the Ultimate's leaping strike is online, you become a gank machine. For five seconds after it lands, every instance of your damage adds true damage equal to 2% of the target's max HP — half-finished armor doesn't come close to absorbing it. The fun part: enemy CC actually feeds you. Every skill in your kit cleanses crowd control, and each cleanse stacks your Passive's Rage, growing your attack damage and attack range. See their stun come in, cleanse it with a skill, and hit back harder — master that rhythm and the players trying to catch Dian Wei are the ones who fall apart. Tyrant also melts quickly solo thanks to the attack speed buff.
strategy.lateGame: Past the 10-minute mark, camp the fights that break out around Shadow Tyrant and Shadow Overlord. That 2% max-HP true damage bites deepest into late-game tanks with inflated health bars, making you one of the rare fighters who can melt the enemy frontline first. The catch: your only gap closers are Skill 1's empowered basic and the Ultimate, and getting kited at range with both down is your nightmare scenario — time your dives with allied CC. But when six Rage stacks come online mid-brawl, the rampage that follows can flip an entire fight on its own.
strategy.teamfight: A chaotic brawl full of flying CC is exactly where Dian Wei belongs. Enter second, after your team commits, and drop the Ultimate on the squishiest target or a wounded frontliner. After landing, Skill 2 must connect — the difference between having and not having 200% attack speed plus 20% lifesteal decides every slugfest that follows. When enemy lockdown hits you, don't panic; cleanse it with a skill and convert it into Rage stacks. The only genuinely dangerous moment is when your cleanses run dry, so never stand in the middle of their team with every skill spent.

combos.title: Leap-Slash Gank
combos.sequence: Skill 3 (true damage, 3s slow) → Skill 2 (200% Attack Speed, lifesteal) → Basic Attack → Skill 1 (enhanced basic that charges in)
combos.description: For 5s after Skill 3 connects, every instance of damage adds true damage equal to 2% of the target's Health. The whole plan is to cram hits into that window, which is why Skill 2 has to land. Miss it and the Attack Speed, the lifesteal, and the extra recovery are all halved — the brawl swings the other way.

combos.title: Turning CC Into Rage
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (cleanses the crowd control, 200% Attack Speed) → Basic Attack → Skill 1 (enhanced basic charges to the target) → Skill 3 (adds true damage equal to 2% of max Health)
combos.description: All of Dian Wei's skills cleanse crowd control, and each successful cleanse grants Mounting Rage. Hard CC is worth two stacks and soft CC one, with every stack raising his physical attack and attack range for 6s. Cleansing with Skill 2 specifically hands him the 200% Attack Speed at the same moment, so the instant after being locked down is when he hits back hardest.

strengths: Comeback engine — every CC cleanse grows his attack damage and range
Skill 2's 200% attack speed and lifesteal make him a premier brawler
Percent-based true damage on the Ultimate shreds even late-game tanks
Fast jungle clear keeps him ahead on levels
weaknesses: Missing Skill 2 halves the steroid, gutting both damage and sustain
Few gap closers — nearly helpless against ranged kiting
Enemies who hold their CC deny him Rage stacks entirely

playstyle.style: A fighter whose every skill cleanses crowd control — and each cleanse raises his attack. The enemy's lockdown literally becomes his damage.
playstyle.suited: Players who relish being the hero that refuses to stop, turning the opponent's favorite tool into their own power source.

synergy.reason: Guiguzi's Skill 2 pulls enemies in range toward him and stuns them for 1s. Against a clumped group, Musashi's ultimate launches every enemy hero in range for another second as he lands. If it catches a hero, Guiguzi and nearby allies also gain a 600 shield.

After transforming, each skill Zhang Fei uses slows nearby enemies by 25% for 2s. The hero Musashi marks for the duel is left slowed, with recovery held back for the full 5s. Zhang Fei's Skill 1 also knocks back enemy heroes who come to the rescue.

counters.reason: While Diaochan stands in her Skill 3 circle, Skill 1 and Skill 2 come back faster, and every petal that connects cuts Skill 2 by another 3s. Musashi commits his ultimate and she simply blinks away again. The 50% slow for 1s from her mark detonation blunts the chase.

Liang's Skill 3 suppresses one enemy hero for 2.2s. Musashi's super armor covers only Illuminating Slash and the dash of his ultimate, so once the dash ends and he starts trading, the suppress goes through. Liang's Skill 2 circles also grant vision, which exposes flanking routes.

passive.description:
Musashi receives 1 Vigor upon using skills, for up to 2 stacks. While he has Vigor, he gains enhanced Basic Attacks that consume 1 Vigor, are not affected by Attack Speed, and reduce the cooldowns of Skills 1 and 2 by 1s upon hitting an enemy.
While he has 1 Vigor:
If the target's Health is above 50%, his next Basic Attack is enhanced to a dual-blade slash, dealing 120 (120 + 40% extra physical attack) extra physical damage.
If the target's Health is below 50%, his next Basic Attack is enhanced to a forward slash, dealing 45 (45 + 15% extra physical attack) (+ 6% of target's lost Health) extra physical damage.
While he has 2 Vigor:
His next Basic Attack lets him dash to the target, dealing 187 (20 + 100% physical attack) physical damage and slowing them by 25% for 1s.
passive.name: Passive Skill: Niten Ichiryuu

skill1.description:
Musashi unleashes a wave of sword energy forward that knocks down enemy projectiles, deals 390 (390 + 130% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies in its path, and slows the enemies by 25% for 1s.
He gains crowd control immunity when using this skill.
skill1.name: Skill 1: Illuminating Slash

skill2.description: Musashi dashes forward, dealing 210 (210 + 75% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies in his path. If he hits an enemy, he gains a shield that negates 330 (330 + 6% extra Health) damage and reduces this skill's Cooldown by 50%.
skill2.name: Skill 2: Extreme Speed

skill3.description:
Musashi locks onto an enemy hero and dashes toward them. Upon arrival, deals 400 (400 + 130% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies within range and launches them for 1s. The target is then marked by Musashi for a duel to the death for 5s. All of the target's recovery effects are delayed until after the duel.
Musashi has crowd control immunity and takes 50% less damage during the dash.
skill3.name: Skill 3: Duel to the Death

strategy.earlyGame: Jungle start is standard. Skill 2 refunds half its cooldown when it hits, so dashing through camps keeps you moving and puts your level 4 timing among the fastest in the jungle class. From your very first camp, drill the habit of weaving a basic attack after every skill: your Passive's empowered basics refund one second off Skill 1 and Skill 2 each, and that habit alone dictates both your clear speed and your gank quality. There's no need to force anything before level 4 — take river vision and scout your first duel target.
strategy.midGame: Once you have your Ultimate, hunt isolated enemies in the side lanes. The lock-on dash cannot miss, grants 50% damage reduction and super armor while traveling, and slaps a five-second healing delay on the target — the more a fighter relies on sustain, the harder you beat them. At Tyrant fights, Skill 1's hidden strength shows: it destroys enemy projectiles along its path, letting you shield your team in river skirmishes. This is the window to build an item lead through duels and take control of the game's second half.
strategy.lateGame: Past four items, the winning pattern is split-pushing a side lane and dueling whoever comes to answer. Against enemies below 50% HP, your empowered basic converts to a missing-HP execute strike, so your damage climbs as fights drag on. When you're needed in a teamfight, come in from a flank and point your Ultimate at the enemy carry — but a failed pick just hands them a reset once the healing delay expires. Before you commit, ask one question: can I kill this target within five seconds? If you hesitate, holding the dash wins more games than forcing it.
strategy.teamfight: Musashi is not a front-and-center teamfighter. Open by holding Skill 1 to swat down the enemy's key projectiles, then enter from a flank with Skill 2 once their crowd control is spent. Your ideal victims are overextended marksmen and mages. From the Ultimate's knock-up, alternate skills and empowered basics and the cooldown refunds keep your hands full the entire fight. Two rules: never linger where multiple enemies can hit you, and never waste a single empowered basic. Follow both and even a five-man brawl turns into the duel you wanted.

combos.title: The Five-Second Duel
combos.sequence: Skill 3 (1s launch, delayed healing) → enhanced Basic Attack → Skill 2 (shield, 50% cooldown refund) → enhanced Basic Attack → Skill 1 (slow) → enhanced Basic Attack
combos.description: The lock-on dash cannot miss, and Musashi takes 50% less damage with crowd control immunity while it travels. After landing, alternate skills and basics — each enhanced hit trims 1s off both Skill 1 and Skill 2. If the target lives through the five seconds of delayed healing, they simply recover and turn the duel around.

combos.title: Two-Vigor Flank
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (dash, shield, 50% cooldown refund) → Skill 1 (crowd control immunity, slow) → enhanced Basic Attack (at 2 Vigor: dashes to the target, 1s slow) → Skill 2
