combos.description: Casting Skill 2 into Skill 1 without a basic attack in between leaves Musashi holding 2 Vigor. That version of the enhanced basic dashes onto the target and adds a one-second slow. A Skill 2 that connected returns at half cooldown, so a target who survives can still be run down.

strengths: One-of-a-kind defense — Skill 1 shoots enemy projectiles out of the air
Top-tier dueling via an unmissable dash with a healing delay attached
Empowered-basic cooldown cycling keeps his output relentless
Missing-HP execute damage closes out targets below half HP
weaknesses: Breaking the skill-into-basic weaving rhythm craters his damage
Struggles in head-on brawls where multiple CC chains land on him
A failed Ultimate pick lets the target heal back up and turn on him

playstyle.style: A dual-wielder whose skills build hostility stacks that change his empowered attacks. Skill 1 cuts projectiles out of the air, and his ultimate forces a duel with the healing delayed.
playstyle.suited: Players who want to be the one issuing the duel — performing the complete swordsman, projectile-parries included.

synergy.reason: Absorbs enemy attention and skills with his heavy CC, allowing Li Bai to safely enter the fight.
Locks down enemies on the frontline, buying time for Li Bai to stack his passive and look for burst opportunities.

counters.reason: Heavily disrupts Li Bai's hit-and-run playstyle with long-range stuns and an ultimate that locks him down if he gets close.
Can guarantee a lockdown with his suppress the moment Li Bai gets close, preventing his i-frames or escape and securing the kill.

passive.skill_name: Passive Skill: Way of the Sword
passive.description: Whenever Li Bai hits a non-structure enemy unit with his Basic Attack, he gains 1 Sword Energy, for up to 4 stacks. Stacks last for 3s and their duration is reset for each enemy hit. At 4 stacks, he enters Way of the Sword, an enhanced state where he gains an extra 30 physical attack and unlocks his Ultimate.
passive.name: Passive Skill: Way of the Sword

skill1.description:
Li Bai can dash twice in the target direction with Drunken Sword Style, dealing 350 (350 + 110% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies in his path and stunning them for 0.5s while gaining 1 Sword Energy. He returns to his original location after using the skill a third time.
The interval between skill uses cannot exceed 5s.
skill1.name: Skill 1: Stupor Slash

skill2.description:
Li Bai conjures a Green Lotus Sword Formation around himself, dealing 200 (200 + 65% extra physical attack) physical damage to nearby enemies.
The sword formation deals 325 (325 + 115% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies touching its edge, while inflicting extreme slow for 1s and reducing their defense by 150 for 3s.
While creating the formation, Li Bai removes all debuffs from himself and becomes untargetable.
When he is inside the sword formation, he has a 10% chance to dodge Basic Attacks from enemies inside the formation (doubled for Basic Attacks dealt from outside the formation).
skill2.name: Skill 2: Stroke of Genius

skill3.description:
Li Bai transforms into sword energy and slashes 5 times at the target area, each slash dealing 240 (240 + 60% extra physical attack) physical damage. When hitting multiple enemy heroes, the damage is reduced by 15% for each subsequent hero hit, for a max reduction of 30%.
He removes all debuffs from himself and becomes untargetable for the duration of this skill.
skill3.name: Skill 3: Flickering Flurry

strategy.earlyGame: Jungle, no debate — and early Li Bai is genuinely weak. Your Ultimate stays locked until basic attacks build four Sword Qi stacks, and your clear speed is nothing special. Concede the opening buff scrap to your team and quietly farm safe routes until level 4. Weave basic attacks between skills even while clearing to keep Sword Qi topped up — it prevents the classic beginner disaster of reaching a kill window with your Ultimate still locked. If the enemy jungler invades, don't fight; use Skill 1's third cast to blink back to your origin point and leave. Surviving this phase is the whole assignment.
strategy.midGame: From level 4 on, there's one non-negotiable pre-gank ritual: hit a nearby minion or monster until Sword Qi is full, then go in. That's the Li Bai law. The sequence is Skill 1's double dash for the stun, Skill 2 to strip 150 physical defense, then the unlocked Ultimate for the five-slash flurry. Kill secured, take Skill 1's third cast back to your entry point and the counterattack never comes. Delete the enemy mid laner or marksman two or three times before the 10-minute mark and the item lead snowballs into full map control. Until Shadow Tyrant spawns, you should always be hunting your next mark.
strategy.lateGame: A five-item Li Bai is a nightmare for the enemy backline — but diving at a teamfight's opening bell is strictly forbidden. Both untargetability windows are strong, yet getting caught while enemy CC is still up means dying in one rotation. Wait in a flanking bush until two enemy lockdown skills are spent, then enter with Skill 1 and unload. Remember your Ultimate loses up to 30% damage per target when it strikes multiple heroes, so it's a scalpel for one isolated carry, not a bomb for their clumped frontline. Once the target drops, don't get greedy — take the exit.
strategy.teamfight: Li Bai's teamfight is 90% waiting. Fight the itch to enter on the engage; watch until enemy stuns and hooks are burned on your teammates, then move. Enter with Skill 1's dash, drop Skill 2's 150-defense shred under their feet, and carve the priority backliner with your Ultimate — two layers of untargetability mean almost nothing touches you in between. Kill confirmed, take Skill 1's third cast out of the fight. The moment right after, with Sword Qi empty, is your only true weakness, so hit a minion to rebuild stacks before you look for round two.

combos.title: Charged Assassination
combos.sequence: Basic Attack x4 (4 Sword Energy) → Skill 1 (two dashes, 0.5s stun) → Skill 2 (formation edge: defense reduction, 1s extreme slow) → Skill 3 (five slashes) → Skill 1, third cast (returns to the starting point)
combos.description: Skill 3 stays locked until Li Bai holds 4 Sword Energy, so top up on minions or monsters before committing. The defense shred and the extreme slow live on the formation's edge, not its center, so drag the target across it. Skill 3 loses up to 30% of its damage when it catches several heroes — pick someone isolated.

combos.title: Three-Dash In and Out
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (0.5s stun, 1 Sword Energy) → Basic Attack → Skill 1, second cast → Basic Attack → Skill 1, third cast (returns to the starting point)
combos.description: Each dash grants one Sword Energy and each basic attack grants another, so a single round trip reaches four stacks. That arms Skill 3 while leaving it unspent. The gap between casts cannot exceed 5s — hesitate and you lose the third cast, and the ride home with it.

strengths: Two layers of untargetability nullify enemy retaliation
Skill 1's return blink makes him nearly impossible to pin down
Massive single-target burst off a 150 defense shred into the flurry
weaknesses: The Ultimate stays locked without four Sword Qi stacks — setup is mandatory
Slow early clear; falling behind before coming online is hard to fix
Ultimate damage decays against multiple targets, so clumped fights hurt him
Demanding mechanics — mismanage the return blink and he kills himself

playstyle.style: A swordsman with a charge-and-release rhythm: basic attacks build sword energy that unlocks his ultimate. Dash in, phase through the counterattack with his untargetable sword formation, and exit on the return dash.
playstyle.suited: Players who decide their way out before they go in, and who enjoy polishing a routine until it becomes lethal.

synergy.reason: Provides shields and peel, greatly increasing survivability.

counters.reason: Has a skill that negates basic attacks for 2s, stalling sustained DPS for that window.
Can disrupt ultimates with his massive shield and heavy CC.

passive.description:
Every time Marco Polo deals damage with his Basic Attacks or skills, he places 1 stack of Destruction on his target (5 stacks on minions). At 10 stacks, they are converted into the Destroyed Defense effect for 5s, and he recovers 30 Energy.
His Basic Attacks and skills deal an extra 100 (100 + 35% extra physical attack) true damage to enemies with Destroyed Defense.
passive.name: Passive Skill: Chain Reaction

skill1.description:
Marco Polo fires 5 bullets in the target direction (firing speed scales with Attack Speed) and gains 10% Movement Speed while firing. Each bullet deals 151 (120 + 18% physical attack) physical damage to the first enemy hit and grants Marco Polo 10 Energy.
Every 3 bullets fired counts as 1 Basic Attack.
skill1.name: Skill 1: Resplendent Revolver

skill2.description:
Marco Polo blinks in the target direction.
Passive: When there are enemy heroes nearby, he gains 15% Movement Speed and deals 20% extra damage.
skill2.name: Skill 2: Roaming Gun

skill3.description:
Marco Polo blinks in the target direction, then moves slowly in the same direction while firing barrages of bullets at nearby enemies for 3s (Firing Speed is affected by Attack Speed). Every barrage deals 213 (170 + 25% physical attack) physical damage.
Every 3 barrages counts as 1 Basic Attack.
skill3.name: Skill 3: Fevered Barrage

strategy.earlyGame: Until your first attack speed item is finished, farming is the entire job. Skill 1 is your best CS tool — five bullets that clear minions and, when they carry through to your lane opponent, double as free harass. Every three bullets count as one basic attack, so your Passive's armor-break stacks build on their own while you farm. Even when the enemy engages, Skill 2's instant blink buys space immediately, letting you take CS a step further forward than most marksmen dare. Just keep one rule in the back of your mind: burn Skill 2 aggressively and you have no exit for the next several seconds.
strategy.midGame: Around 8 to 10 minutes, with your second attack speed item done, the Passive's armor break starts triggering in every single fight. Ten stacks shatter the target's defense, and every follow-up hit adds bonus true damage — the reason you can genuinely shoot it out with fighters and tanks who walk at you. Show up to Tyrant and mid-lane skirmishes, thread Skill 1 into the scrum to farm stacks, and keep an escape budgeted: Skill 2 first, the Ultimate's blink as the emergency reserve. Two dashes' worth of insurance converts directly into extra seconds of firing time — and firing time is Marco Polo's entire game.
strategy.lateGame: The closer you get to full build, the more the Ultimate's three-second barrage becomes a fight-deciding weapon. The spray hits every enemy around you, fires faster with attack speed, and late game it cycles armor-break stacks almost instantly. Catch the enemy team clumped on Overlord from a side angle and their frontline's defense simply peels away. The flip side: you crawl while channeling, and one hard stun cancels the whole thing. Who on their team has hard CC, and is it up? Counting that before you channel is the single habit that improves your Marco Polo the most.
strategy.teamfight: Your spot is the very back, at maximum Skill 1 range. Don't step up at the opening bell — pour bullets into the enemy frontline to build stacks while their crowd control gets spent. When an assassin dives, answer instantly with Skill 2 and keep shooting from the far side of your blink. Your window opens after their lockdown is committed: blink into a flank with the Ultimate and hose the whole fight down while drifting. Enemies with armor break active simply melt in order, so you don't need fancy target selection — just never stop moving, and never stop firing.

combos.title: Break Armor, Then Barrage
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (bullet spray, 10% Movement Speed) → Basic Attack → Skill 3 (blink, then 3s of barrages)
combos.description: Each bullet plants one stack of Destruction on whatever it hits. Skill 1 only fires 5 bullets at level 1, so weave in Basic Attacks to reach ten stacks. For the 5s of Destroyed Defense that follows, every Basic Attack and skill hit adds true damage on top. Barrage count is fixed by skill level — 12 at level 1 — and Attack Speed raises the firing speed, not the number of shots.

combos.title: Blink and Reset
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (blink in the target direction) → Skill 1 (bullets, 10% Movement Speed)
combos.description: Blink away from the engage with Skill 2, then fire bullets while backing off. The Skill 2 passive only runs while enemy heroes are near Marco Polo himself, and it adds 20% damage. Movement Speed goes up as well, though that amount scales with skill level. Skill 3's blink is a second exit, but committing to the barrage leaves him crawling.

strengths: Armor break plus true damage keeps his output relevant against tanky frontlines
Two blinks across Skill 2 and the Ultimate for total positional freedom
Bullets count as basic attacks, so Passive stacks build extremely fast
weaknesses: Crawls during the Ultimate's channel and loses it all to one hard CC
Underwhelming damage until his attack speed items come online
No burst — deny him sustained firing time and he goes quiet

playstyle.style: The definitive run-and-gun marksman — his revolver fires on the move, his stacks shred defenses into true damage, and two teleports serve both chase and escape.
playstyle.suited: Players who treat standing still as death, converting kiting technique directly into damage.

synergy.reason: Creates a safe environment for dealing damage with massive shields and CC.
Increases stability in the laning phase and teamfights with healing and CDR support.

counters.reason: High burst damage from stealth creates a huge threat of getting one-shot before being able to react.
Can rapidly close the gap with high mobility, making it extremely difficult to kite or peel.

passive.description:
Di Renjie gains 1 stack of Swift Justice for each Basic Attack used. Each stack increases his Attack Speed by 3.5%–7% and his Movement Speed by 5%, for up to 5 stacks.
On every third Basic Attack, Di Renjie attacks with a red or blue token at random.
passive.name: Passive Skill: Swift Justice

skill1.description:
Di Renjie tosses a random assortment of 6 red or blue tokens at the target area, dealing 150 (120 + 18% physical attack) physical damage.
Enemies hit by multiple tokens will only take 30% of the initial damage from subsequent tokens.
Red token: Explodes on hit and deals an extra 90 (90 + 18% extra physical attack) magical damage.
Blue token: Deals an extra 45 (45 + 9% extra physical attack) magical damage while slowing the enemy by 15% for 1s.
Six Tokens count as 1 Basic Attack. Damage dealt to the same target diminishes to 30%. Skill casting speed increases with Attack Speed.
skill1.name: Skill 1: Respect the Law

skill2.description:
Di Renjie tosses 8 tokens in a circle around him, gaining brief immunity to damage and crowd control, removing all debuffs from himself, and gaining 25% Movement Speed for 1s.
The damage and effects of these tokens are the same as those of Respect the Law.
skill2.name: Skill 2: Legal Immunity

skill3.description: Di Renjie tosses a secret golden token, dealing 300 (300 + 60% physical attack + 120% extra physical attack) physical damage and 300 (300 + 60% physical attack + 120% extra physical attack) magical damage to the first enemy hero hit and stunning them for 1s. This skill also reduces the target's physical defense and magical defense by 50%, while exposing their location for 5s. During this period, teammates moving toward the target enemy gain 10% Movement Speed.
skill3.name: Skill 3: Imperial Order

strategy.earlyGame: In the Farm Lane, simply never letting your basic attacks stop is a strength in itself. The Passive stacks attack speed and move speed with every swing, and holding it at five stacks is the ideal state. Just by taking CS, the token that fires on every third attack chips your lane opponent for free — the lead builds without any deliberate harass. Skill 1 pulls double duty on wave clear and poke, but your mana is finite, so don't spam it. Skill 2's invulnerability is your lifeline; never let a greedy early trade bait it out of you.
strategy.midGame: Level 4 hands Di Renjie a win-on-hit button. When the golden edict connects, it stuns for a second and cuts the target's physical and magic defense by 50% — with your jungler following up, even tanks don't survive it. When a gank arrives, the edict is the opening move, every time. Around 8 minutes, with two core items finished, you start beating your lane opponent in straight shootouts, so make every Tyrant fight. The no-mobility weakness never goes away, though: confirm where your teammates are before you ever step forward.
strategy.lateGame: Late-game Di Renjie lives and dies on one decision: when to press Skill 2. An invulnerability that also cleanses debuffs is about the best self-peel any marksman gets — but it's one charge. Let the assassin's lockdown actually land, then cast it, and their whole engage evaporates; panic-press it early and the follow-up kills you every time. On offense, put the Ultimate on the enemy carry and focus-fire through the five seconds of halved defenses. One more trick worth keeping: the edict grants vision of whoever it hits, which makes it a fine tool for flushing out ambushes in bushes.
strategy.teamfight: Your job is holding five Passive stacks and never stopping the shooting, all from the very back. The dream opener is landing the Ultimate on their engage hero — the stun blunts the dive, and the 50% defense cut invites your whole team to collapse. If you miss, no panic: steady basics and tokens over your frontline's shoulder are plenty of sustained damage. When someone finally jumps on you, that's the moment to stay calm — eat the CC first, then cleanse and go invulnerable with Skill 2. Land that reversal and the enemy has essentially nothing left that kills you. You can't cross walls, so never take a position where one blocks your exit.

combos.title: Halve Their Defense
combos.sequence: Skill 3 (1s stun, 50% physical and magical defense reduction for 5s) → Skill 1 (six tokens) → Basic Attack
combos.description: A landed golden token stuns for a second and cuts both defenses in half. Allies also move 10% faster toward the marked target, so a jungler arriving at the same time leaves no way out. Tokens after the first deal only 30% to the same target, which is why keeping basic attacks flowing beats spamming another volley.

combos.title: Absorb, Then Answer
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (immune to damage and crowd control, cleanses debuffs, 25% Movement Speed) → Basic Attack → Skill 3 (1s stun, 50% defense reduction)
combos.description: Press Skill 2 after the enemy's crowd control has already landed. Spend it early and the real lockdown arrives with nothing left to cleanse it. Once the immunity and the speed boost have reset the fight, send the golden token back at the diver for the stun and the defense shred.

strengths: Best-in-class self-peel: invulnerability plus a debuff cleanse on Skill 2
The Ultimate's 50% defense shred is a teamfight-opening button
Passive attack and move speed stacking for relentless sustained damage
Straightforward kit — an ideal first marksman
weaknesses: No mobility skill and no way to escape over walls
Missing the Ultimate loses both the stun and the shred, halving his impact
Random token colors make slow-based chase damage unreliable

playstyle.style: A marksman who scatters homing tokens, hiding a master-class defensive tool inside an easy kit: Skill 2's brief immunity plus cleanse works as both a beginner's insurance and an expert's outplay.
playstyle.suited: Players who want approachability and survivability in one — a first marksman that never stops being worth playing.

synergy.reason: Zilong's Skysplitter shocks enemies in range, and a skill landing on them within 5s launches those at the center for 1s. Dharma stocks 2 charges of Skill 1 every 9s, giving him the hits to set that launch off. A launched enemy is also easy to line up against a wall.

Daji's Strike a Pose stuns one target for 1.5s. That point-and-click stun is easy to land, so Dharma can pour Enlightenment Mantra into an enemy who cannot move, and each punch returns 85 Health to keep him in the brawl.

counters.reason: Zhuangzi enters a Dreamscape every 6s, cleansing crowd control from himself and blocking it for 2s, and Skill 3 cleanses nearby teammates as well. With no wall slam landing, Dharma loses the flying kick follow-up.

Di Renjie's Skill 2 grants brief immunity to damage and crowd control while removing every debuff on him, so even a wall stun will not hold him. Imperial Order then cuts defenses by 50% for 5s, stripping away the defense Dharma piles up with Mantra.

passive.description: Every time Dharma uses a skill, he receives a stack of Mantra which grants 32 physical defense and 32 magical defense for 5s, for up to 3 stacks. Using Skill 1 or his Ultimate grants 1 enhanced Basic Attack (and another 1 enhanced Basic Attack if he hits an enemy). Enhanced Basic Attacks deal an extra 28 (28 + 30% extra physical attack) physical damage and slow enemies by 15% for 2s.
passive.name: Passive Skill: Heart Meridian Mantra

skill1.description: Dharma dashes and punches, dealing 180 (180 + 100% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies in his path and launching them for 0.5s. He stocks 1 charge of this skill every 9s, for up to 2 charges. If he successfully knocks an enemy back into terrain with his Ultimate, the next use of this skill within 8s becomes a flying kick in the target direction. This kick deals extra physical damage equal to 15% of the target's lost Health.
skill1.name: Skill 1: Formlessness Mantra

skill2.description: Dharma unleashes a flurry of 5 punches every second for 4s for a total of 20 punches. Each punch deals 65 physical damage (50% extra damage to non-hero units), as well as physical damage equal to 0.35% of the target's max Health (increases by 0.25% for every extra 100 physical attack), and restores 85 (85 + 2.5% extra Health) Health. He can control the skill's direction while punching. While using the skill, he will automatically use enhanced Basic Attacks with the same effects as those of his Passive on nearby enemies. The recovery effect is halved for hits on non-hero units. Cancelling the skill will return 50% to 100% of its cooldown, depending on how long he used it for.
skill2.name: Skill 2: Enlightenment Mantra

skill3.description: Dharma throws a powerful punch forward, dealing 200 (200 + 100% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies within range and knocking them back. If enemies are knocked into a wall, they take an extra 200 (200 + 100% extra physical attack) physical damage and are stunned for 1s.
skill3.name: Skill 3: Truth Mantra

strategy.earlyGame: In the Clash Lane, your first teammate is the terrain — the walls — and the early game tests how well you use them. Level 1-3 trades lean on Skill 1's dash and the Passive's defense buff, and since Skill 1 holds two charges, the standing rule is one for offense, one banked for the exit. The only green light is the moment your opponent stands near a wall; otherwise, just soak the wave. Your empowered basic also slows on hit, so stack small hit-and-run chips to open an HP gap while you wait for level 4 to unlock the wall-slam game.
strategy.midGame: Once you have the Ultimate, every wall on the map becomes a Dharma kill zone. The recipe is simple: knock the target into a wall, the collision stuns for a second with bonus damage, and within eight seconds Skill 1 converts into a flying kick that adds 15% of their missing HP. Land the full string and most victims don't walk away. Riverbanks and jungle corridors are nothing but walls, so your presence at Tyrant fights is actually stronger than your laning. Skill 2's punch flurry doubles as healing and percent-HP damage, giving you surprising staying power in monster tug-of-wars.
strategy.lateGame: In late-game teamfights, Dharma's grade depends entirely on forcing fights into tight terrain. Start a fight in the corridor outside Overlord or around a jungle corner and you get the dream play — wall-stunning the enemy carry right in front of your team. In the wide-open river center, though, your knockback is just a shove and half your threat disappears. Claiming the strong bush early to control where the fight happens is your hidden late-game job. Keep three Passive stacks rolling and you hold your own in frontline slugfests too.
strategy.teamfight: You have exactly one objective: put an enemy backliner into a wall. Enter with Skill 1's dash, set your angle, then fire the Ultimate — and take the half-second before casting to confirm a wall actually sits behind them, because that pause is the difference between a kill and a whiff. Once the stun lands, finish with the flying kick and Skill 2's punch flurry. Skill 2 lets you steer mid-channel, but your movement is still restricted, so swinging it out in front of an enemy holding burst is asking to die. Canceling early is always on the table — take the kills that are actually there.

combos.title: Slam Them Into the Wall
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (dash, 0.5s launch) → Skill 3 (knockback; a wall impact adds damage and a 1s stun) → Skill 1 (flying kick, 15% of lost Health) → Skill 2 (punch flurry)
combos.description: Confirm there is terrain behind the target before the punch goes out. A wall impact adds a one-second stun, and any Skill 1 used within the next 8s becomes a flying kick worth 15% of the target's lost Health. Skill 1 stocks one charge every 9s up to two, so entering with both keeps the dash-to-kick chain unbroken.

combos.title: Stack Mantra and Stay In
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (0.5s launch) → enhanced Basic Attack (2s slow) → Skill 2 (20 punches over 4s, healing on every hit)
combos.description: Every skill cast adds a Mantra stack, layering physical and magical defense up to three times. Landing Skill 1 grants a second enhanced basic, so a connected dash means more swings and more slow. Skill 2 chips 0.35% of the target's max Health per punch while healing Dharma, and cancelling it early returns part of its cooldown.

strengths: Huge burst from the wall stun into the flying kick conversion
Strong brawling stats via the Passive's defense buff and Skill 2 healing
Percent-HP damage on Skill 2 chews through high-health targets
Two Skill 1 charges give him flexibility on offense and escape
weaknesses: Loses half his threat in open terrain with no walls
Restricted movement during Skill 2 makes him a target for big skills
A misjudged knockback angle shoves the enemy to safety instead

playstyle.style: A boxer whose knockback punches deal bonus damage when enemies hit walls. Terrain is half his weapon — the same skill is trivial in the open and lethal in a corridor.
playstyle.suited: Players who track wall positions instinctively, chasing the satisfaction of a perfectly placed slam.

synergy.reason: Luban No.7 has no escape skill and needs a frontline holding the ground. His passive scattershot hits three times for 4% of a hero's max Health each, so the longer Xiang Yu pins enemies down, the more of it lands, and Skill 1's 25% slow keeps them in the firing line.

Nakoruru's ultimate charge cuts the damage output of every enemy it hits by 30% for 3s, the same job Xiang Yu's No Retreat does, applied from the dive side as well as the front. Her Skill 1 mark tears off 6% of max Health, so it bites into tanky targets too.

counters.reason: Lam marks any enemy below 30% Health as Prey, adding 7.5-15% true damage to his Basic Attacks and skills. The low-Health window where Xiang Yu wants to fight back is exactly Lam's hunting ground, and Death From Below drags him out of any retreat.

Di Renjie gains 5% Movement Speed per Basic Attack, up to 5 stacks, and kites at range. When Xiang Yu closes the gap, Skill 2 hands him brief damage and crowd control immunity to slip away, while Imperial Order strips 50% of his defenses for 5s.

passive.description:
When Xiang Yu's Health drops below 30%, he gains 40% damage reduction for 6s. This effect can only be triggered once every 90s.
After using Righteous Fervor and No Retreat, Xiang Yu gains different enhanced Basic Attacks. Stocks up to 2 charges.
passive.name: Passive Skill: Resolute Will

skill1.description:
Xiang Yu charges in the target direction, knocking back enemies and launching them for 0.75s with a slash. The charge and slash each deal 225 (225 + 5% extra Health) physical damage.
His next Basic Attack is enhanced into a vertical chop that deals 445 (250 + 100% physical attack + 80% extra physical attack) physical damage and is guaranteed to be a critical hit with a base critical damage of 150%.
skill1.name: Skill 1: Righteous Fervor

skill2.description: Xiang Yu roars, slowing nearby enemies by 15% for 2s, dealing 275 (275 + 90% extra physical attack) magical damage, and reducing their damage output by 30% for 3.5s. He then gains an enhanced Basic Attack and a 25% Movement Speed boost that diminishes over 2s. The enhanced Basic Attack is a horizontal sweep that restores 350 (350 + 7% extra Health) Health (effect is reduced to 50% against non-hero units; the lower his Health, the higher the recovery, up to a maximum of 50%) and deals 235 (40 + 100% physical attack) physical damage.
skill2.name: Skill 2: No Retreat

skill3.description:
Xiang Yu charges up and unleashes an energy wave with his sword while gaining crowd control immunity and Undying, dealing 900 (900 + 260% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies along the path. Enemies in the inner zone take 50% extra damage and are stunned for 0.75s. The lower Xiang Yu's Health is, the more damage he deals, up to 50% extra damage. 20% of damage dealt is converted into Health.
Undying: Xiang Yu cannot be defeated and his Health will not drop below 1.
skill3.name: Skill 3: Hegemon's Slash

strategy.earlyGame: The lane badge at the top of this page reads Clash, following the official stats. The advice below assumes a roaming pick. On the global server, roam is his standard assignment. Attach to your marksman from level 1 and play the bodyguard: in skirmishes, Skill 1's knockback exists to bat divers away from your carry. In trades, Skill 2 is quietly vicious — it cuts the attack damage of every enemy in range by 30% for 3.5 seconds, so slapping it on top of the enemy's engage simply deletes their trade math. Maintain HP with the empowered basic's healing, rush tank items above all else, and be there when your jungler moves for the 4-minute Tyrant.
strategy.midGame: Through the mid game, with one or two defensive items done, Xiang Yu's value is measured in gank follow-ups. Skill 1's dash carries enemies with its knockback, so the trick is angling it to shove a fleeing target back toward your team — connect the knock-up and your side's full damage lands during it. In Tyrant and mid-lane collisions, stand at the very front and stop fearing a shrinking HP bar: drop below 30% and the Passive's 40% damage reduction triggers on its own, wrecking the enemy's damage math. Weaken overchasers with Skill 2 and swallow them whole — that's the mid-game pattern.
strategy.lateGame: The late game belongs to Xiang Yu. Right when enemy damage peaks, his kit peaks harder: 40% damage reduction below 30% HP, and an Ultimate that makes him unkillable — HP cannot drop below 1 — while it's active. The tank who was supposed to die first simply doesn't, and that stolen time becomes your team's counterattack window. The Ultimate also deals more and heals more the lower your HP sits, so a near-death swing hits harder than some fighters' full combos. At Overlord, soak every enemy cooldown at the front, then look for the answering blow.
strategy.teamfight: The job description is short: stand at the front, get hurt, then hit back. Your opening is a choice between shoving their frontline into your team with Skill 1 or batting an assassin off your carry. Fire Skill 2 the instant enemies clump — a 30% attack cut across their whole team visibly shrinks the damage your side takes. The Ultimate is for stepping into the enemy team on low HP: super armor and the unkillable effect mean you cannot die during the charge, and the slash stuns with 50% bonus damage on connect. The moment the Xiang Yu they thought was dead swings back is the moment fights flip.

combos.title: Shove and Launch
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (charge knocks back, then the closing slash launches for 0.75s) → enhanced Basic Attack (vertical chop, guaranteed critical hit) → Skill 2 (30% attack reduction for 3.5s, 2s slow) → enhanced Basic Attack (sweep, heals)
combos.description: The charge shoves enemies along its path, so angle it to push them toward your team. The slash at the end launches them for 0.75s. That window is for the vertical chop, which is always a critical hit. Enhanced Basic Attacks stock up to two charges, so casting Skill 2 first and swinging both afterward is equally fine.

combos.title: Swing From the Brink
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (cuts enemy attack by 30% for 3.5s) → Skill 3 (charge up with crowd control immunity and Undying) → enhanced Basic Attack (sweep, heals)
combos.description: Roar first — 30% less enemy attack damage for 3.5s makes the charge-up far cheaper. Skill 3 hits harder the lower Xiang Yu's Health falls, up to 50% extra, and 20% of the damage dealt returns as Health. His Health cannot drop below 1 during the charge, and enemies the blade catches are stunned for 0.75s and take that extra 50%. Falling under 30% Health adds 40% damage reduction, but only for 6s and only once every 90s.

strengths: Gets tougher as he gets lower via the unkillable Ultimate and 40% damage reduction
Skill 2's 30% attack cut suppresses an entire team's damage
Excellent peel with knockback and knock-up to protect his carries
The low-HP Ultimate hits far harder than a tank has any right to
weaknesses: Skill 1 is his only movement and can't cross walls — kiting ruins him
The Ultimate's charge-up is telegraphed and easy to sidestep
Missing the blade's edge means no stun and no bonus damage
Low damage and low pressure while his HP bar is still full

playstyle.style: A tank who becomes hardest to kill at the brink — 40% damage reduction kicks in below 30% Health. His knockbacks and attack-down debuff dull the enemy's edge exactly when late-game fights peak.
playstyle.suited: Players who want to be the wall that holds at the last moment, and who understand what an attack debuff is truly worth.

synergy.reason: Their combined high mobility allows them to easily follow up on chunked enemies and snowball with kills.
Groups enemies together, making it much easier to land the ultimate and AoE silence.

counters.reason: Possesses even higher mobility than Sima Yi, allowing him to easily escape or counter-engage.
Can completely peel and protect the target from burst damage with massive shields and CC.

passive.description:
Sima Yi gains vision of enemies casting skills within a range of 2,000 and gains 10 Shadow Force (up to 50).
After using the skill, Sima Yi condenses Shadow Force into a scythe, gaining an enhanced Basic Attack and 20 Movement Speed for 5s. Using the enhanced Basic Attack consumes all Shadow Force.
Each scythe strike deals 230 (230 + 46% magical attack) magical damage and true damage equal to Shadow Force. The first attack allows Sima Yi to dash behind the target and deals 300 (300 + 60% magical attack) magical damage (true damage is doubled).
For every 20 Shadow Force consumed, the enhanced Basic Attack's range increases by 3%.
passive.name: Passive Skill: Quiet Whispers

skill1.description:
Sima Yi gains crowd control immunity and begins controlling a spirit with high Movement Speed that lasts 2.5s.
The spirit deals 115 (115 + 23% magical attack) magical damage to enemies it passes through. When Sima Yi uses a Basic Attack or when the spirit's duration ends, Sima Yi moves to the spirit's location, dealing 115 (115 + 23% magical attack) magical damage to enemies in his path and slowing them by 25% for 1s.
skill1.name: Skill 1: Shadow Stings

skill2.description:
Sima Yi releases spiritual energy and suppresses enemies in the surrounding area, dealing 275 (275 + 55% magical attack) magical damage and silencing them for 0.75s. Inside the suppression zone, Sima Yi gains 10% increased recovery.
Passive: When Sima Yi takes magical damage, 25% is converted into Health recovery for 3s (halved for physical damage).
skill2.name: Skill 2: Barren Lands

skill3.description:
Sima Yi steps back and charges up briefly, then dashes to the target location, where he deals 530 (530 + 110% magical attack) magical damage (damage halved to enemies along his path).
If this skill is interrupted, 90% cooldown is returned.
skill3.name: Skill 3: Death Descends

strategy.earlyGame: Sima Yi lives in the mid lane. Before level 4, keep an eye on your Passive: every skill an enemy hero casts nearby feeds you 10 energy, up to 50. When you are near the cap, harass with the empowered basic attack — its first hit teleports you behind the target, so even enemies hugging their minion wave can't hide from it. Into a mage matchup, Skill 2's passive heals you for 25% of magic damage taken, which means you can accept extended trades. One hard rule: never step forward while both your mana and your energy are empty.
strategy.midGame: Once the 4-minute Tyrant contest starts, shove mid and rotate for ambushes on the side lanes and jungle. Skill 1 sends out a fast-moving spirit, but the crowd control immunity belongs to Sima Yi himself, not to the spirit. For the 2.5 seconds you probe ahead with it, nothing can lock your body down. Coming in sideways through brush is ideal. A basic attack — or the spirit expiring — pulls you to its position, so the long way around still closes fast. Chip with the behind-the-back empowered basic, then land Skill 2's 0.75-second silence to lock out their blink or CC before finishing the job. Your Passive also grants vision of enemy heroes who cast skills, so anyone charging a skill in brush gives away their position and hands you the ambush.
strategy.lateGame: Past 15 minutes, with Savant's Wrath and Void Staff complete, your one-shot threat is real — but you're as fragile as ever. Let teammates take the first hit in teamfights, and move only after the enemy has dumped skills, feeding you both energy and vision. Your Ultimate is a backstep into a long charged dash that works for offense or escape, and since an interrupted charge refunds 90% of the cooldown, deliberately showing the wind-up to bait enemy CC becomes more and more valuable as the game goes on.
strategy.teamfight: Your spot in a brawl is second wave. Because enemy skill casts charge your energy, entering from the flank right after their engage beats opening with a full combo — better damage, better safety. Hunt the isolated mage or marksman: the instant the empowered basic teleports you behind them, layer Skill 2's silence so they physically can't press their escape while you shred them. Skill 1 is effectively a blink since you can relocate to the spirit's position, so keep one charge in reserve as an exit — it changes your survival rate completely.

combos.title: Strike From Behind
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (steer the spirit; casting arms the scythe) → Basic Attack (move to the spirit, empowered hit) → Skill 2 (0.75s silence)
combos.description: Press Basic Attack and Sima Yi travels to wherever the spirit stands, with that first strike landing behind the target. True damage equals his Shadow Force, and only that opening hit doubles it. Shadow Force builds 10 at a time whenever an enemy casts a skill within 2,000 range, so he hits hardest right after they commit.

combos.title: Charge In and Silence
combos.sequence: Skill 3 (step back, charge up, then dash to the target location) → Skill 2 (0.75s silence) → Empowered Basic Attack
combos.description: Skill 3 halves its damage against enemies caught along the path, so angle it to land directly on the one target you want. Once you are on top of them, the silence shuts down their answer, and casting the skill has already re-armed the scythe. An interrupted charge returns 90% of the cooldown, which makes showing the wind-up a cheap way to bait out a dodge.

combos.title: Use the Spirit as Your Exit
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (crowd control immunity; send the spirit down your escape route) → Skill 2 (0.75s silence) → Basic Attack (move to the spirit's location)
combos.description: The spirit moves fast, and Sima Yi holds crowd control immunity the whole time he is steering it. Silence the chasers with Skill 2, then press Basic Attack to snap back to wherever the spirit ended up. The same trip fires when its 2.5s runs out, so a missed input still gets him out.

strengths: Energy charged by enemy skill casts plus a behind-the-target teleport gives elite ambush power
Skill 2's silence and 25% magic-damage healing make him a nightmare for mages
Skill 1 grants him crowd control immunity and relocates him to the spirit, working as both gap-closer and escape
An interrupted Skill 3 refunds 90% of its cooldown, so he can always re-engage
weaknesses: Healing is halved against physical damage, so marksmen grind him down
Damage depends on passive energy — enemies who hold their skills starve him
A clear damage trough opens right after his empowered basics are spent
Low base durability; a failed kill attempt invites an instant counter

playstyle.style: A mid-range assassin who sees enemies whenever they cast skills, then dives with a silence attached. Mechanically normal-difficulty, but his real power is converting vision into aggression.
playstyle.suited: Players who build their plays from information rather than reflexes — winning with judgement, not APM.

synergy.reason: Can constantly out-rotate and confuse the enemy using a combination of split-pushing and recalls.
Can lock down enemies for a long duration with his ultimate, creating a safe window to unleash maximum DPS.

counters.reason: Can easily win auto-attack trades thanks to superior mobility and damage reduction.
Constantly gets knocked back and kited, making it extremely difficult to close the gap and stack auto-attacks.

passive.description: Whenever Fuzi lands a Basic Attack, he gains 1 stack of Admonition for 5s, up to 5 stacks. At full stacks, he becomes enhanced for 5s. While enhanced, he gains 60 Movement Speed and 30% Attack Speed, while each Basic Attack deals an extra 80 (80 + 28% extra physical attack) true damage and reduces his Skill 1 and Skill 2's Cooldown by 1s.
passive.name: Passive Skill: Ancient Wisdom

skill1.description: Fuzi swings his ferule in the target direction, pulling enemies within range toward him and dealing 320 (320 + 100% extra physical attack) physical damage while slowing them by 25% for 1.5−2.5s (duration scales with skill level).
skill1.name: Skill 1: Corporal Punishment

skill2.description:
Fuzi enhances himself for 2s, during which he gains 25% Movement Speed and 45% damage reduction.
While enhanced, he reflects 50% of the damage taken after being hit by the first Basic Attack and slows his attackers by 15% for 2s. This reflected damage carries his Basic Attack's on-hit effects.
Passive: His Basic Attack has a 25% chance of being followed up with another Basic Attack that inflicts 50% damage and on-hit effects.
skill2.name: Skill 2: Intuition

skill3.description: Fuzi charges in the target direction, dealing 600 (600 + 200% extra physical attack) physical damage to the first enemy hero hit and binding them to his lamppost. While bound, the enemy hero will be confined for 5s within the area where his Ultimate hit, and deal 20% less damage.
skill3.name: Skill 3: Sage's Might

strategy.earlyGame: Take Skill 2 first in the clash lane — the damage reduction and bonus-attack procs let you clear the opening wave and trade at the same time. Fuzi's lifeline is his Passive: whether you have five stacks banked from hitting minions before you commit changes the fight entirely. The empowered state adds true damage and shaves the cooldowns of Skills 1 and 2, so at even HP you win most slugfests on math alone. Don't chase before level 4, and any time the enemy jungler disappears from the map, assume the river brush and back off.
strategy.midGame: At the 4-minute Tyrant fight, your job is to open by binding the enemy fighter or jungler with your Ultimate. Five seconds of restricted movement plus 20% reduced damage output means they fight the whole skirmish at a disadvantage. In lane, lean on your 1v1 strength to push the side, and drag anyone who collapses on you into melee with Skill 1. Skill 2 reflects 50% of the first basic attack you take while it's active — read the tell on an enemy's empowered attack and pop it in response, and you win the trade on that alone.
strategy.lateGame: True to his late-game label, Fuzi peaks once Doomsday and Blood Rage come online after 15 minutes. Five-stack true damage all but ignores armor, so almost nobody wins a straight brawl against you. But games are decided at Shadow Tyrant and Overlord, not in a side lane. Leave the 1v1 thirty seconds before the objective spawns, regroup with your team, and claim the position that lets you land your Ultimate as the fight's opening move.
strategy.teamfight: The dream scenario: bind the enemy carry right before the brawl starts and turn it into a 5v4. The dash latches onto the first hero it touches, so when their frontline is walling you out, look for a flank angle. Once the bind lands, activate Skill 2's 45% damage reduction and never stop swinging — as long as your basics connect, the stacks and cooldown refunds keep cycling, and Fuzi only gets stronger the longer the fight runs. Standing around without a target is the one thing that kills you.

combos.title: Opening Bind
combos.sequence: Skill 3 (dash, 5s movement confinement) → Skill 2 (damage reduction) → Basic Attacks → Skill 1 (pull back)
combos.description: The dash only catches the first enemy hero it touches, so find an angle past their frontline instead of driving through it. A bound target deals 20% less damage. Hold the 45% reduction (Lvl 1), keep swinging, and drag them back with Skill 1 when they drift to the edge of the zone.

combos.title: Stack Up Before You Commit
combos.sequence: Basic Attack ×5 (5 Admonition stacks → enhanced) → Skill 1 (pull + slow) → Basic Attacks
combos.description: Each landed Basic Attack adds a stack, and five of them open a 5-second enhanced window. While enhanced, every hit adds true damage and shaves 1s off Skill 1 and Skill 2. Five seconds is short, so stack on minions and close the distance immediately after.

combos.title: Reflect Counter
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (2s enhance, damage reduction) → Skill 1 (pull + slow) → Basic Attacks
combos.description: The enhanced state runs for only 2s, so press it just as the enemy winds up a Basic Attack. That first hit is reduced, 50% of it bounces back, and the attacker is slowed by 15% for 2s (Lvl 1). Pull them in with Skill 1 and take the trade.

strengths: Five-stack true damage makes him one of the game's best 1v1 brawlers
Skill 2's 45% damage reduction and reflect turn enemy aggression against them
The Ultimate's 5-second bind and 20% damage cut shuts down the enemy ace
A late-game power curve that keeps climbing as items complete
weaknesses: Needs uninterrupted basic attacks to function — kiting shuts him down hard
His only real gap-closer is the Ultimate; missing it leaves a long window
Skill 1's pull radius is small and whiffs against high-mobility targets
Without stacks, both his damage and durability are merely average

playstyle.style: A brawler who powers up through repeated basic attacks, pulls enemies in with his ruler, and reflects the first attack that hits his stance. He is built to win while being hit.
playstyle.suited: Players who like switching between offense and defense in a single beat — and savor the lesson taught when a reflect connects.

synergy.reason: The movement speed buff makes it easy to maintain his empowered charge state.
Provides shields and CC peel, allowing for safe dives into the enemy backline and clean disengages.

counters.reason: His ultimate restricts movement, completely shutting down the ability to maintain the charge state.
Her point-and-click stun easily stops the engage, leaving him vulnerable to heavy burst damage.

passive.description:
Normal Stance: Guan Yu gains 2% Movement Speed for every 200 units of distance he moves, entering Charge Stance upon moving 2,000 units. When Movement Speed drops below 375, exits Charge Stance, and the accumulated distance is reset after 0.7s.
When standing stationary near brush, recovers 30 Health and Energy every 0.5s.
Charge Stance: Enhances next Basic Attack, charging forward to deal an extra 500 (500 + 125% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies in his path and knocking them back. Gains 20% Movement Speed when moving toward enemy heroes.
When in Normal Stance, he can use Basic Attacks while moving.
passive.name: Passive Skill: Rider of Triumph

skill1.description:
Normal Stance: Guan Yu swings his blade, dealing 500 (500 + 140% extra physical attack) physical damage to nearby enemies.
Charge Stance: He charges forward, dealing 360 (360 + 120% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies in his path and knocking them back. He then attacks again, dealing 500 (500 + 160% extra physical attack) physical damage.
skill1.name: Skill 1: Heroic Charge

skill2.description:
Normal Stance: Guan Yu removes all crowd control effects from himself and gains 30% Movement Speed for 2s.
Charge Stance: He removes all crowd control effects from himself and leaps forward, dealing 650 (650 + 200% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies near his landing point and knocking them back. He also gains 30% Movement Speed for 2s.
skill2.name: Skill 2: Soaring Green Dragon

skill3.description:
Normal Stance: Guan Yu enhances himself for 10s. While enhanced, the distance required to enter Charge Stance is reduced by 75%.
Charge Stance: Guan Yu summons heavy cavalry on either side of himself that charge forward with him, dealing 620 (620 + 200% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies in their path and knocking them back. He then enhances himself for 10s. While enhanced, the distance required to enter Charge Stance is reduced by 75%.
skill3.name: Skill 3: Razor Cavalry

strategy.earlyGame: Guan Yu starts in the clash lane, but after the first two waves your top priority is simple: never stop moving. His Passive enters the charge state after 2000 units of travel, so every second spent standing in a lane staring at your opponent is a second spent being weak. Loop through the river and your own jungle to build a runway, then knock enemies flying with the charged basic attack, disengage, and repeat. Until level 4, resist every urge to chase — hit, knock them back, and leave. That alone wins you lane priority.
strategy.midGame: The game becomes Guan Yu's around the 4-minute Tyrant. Objective standoffs hand you runways for free, and a single blindside knockback into their backline can decide the fight before it starts. Cast Skill 3 in Normal Stance and you are enhanced for 10s, with the distance required to enter Charge Stance reduced by 75% — 2,000 units becomes 500, so re-engages come around far faster. When ganking, angle your approach so enemies get knocked toward your tower or your teammates — punting them to safety in their own territory is the classic first mistake every new Guan Yu makes.
strategy.lateGame: With two or three defense items like Overlord's Platemail and Blazing Cape done by 15 minutes, Charge Stance Skill 1 becomes your main tool. It charges forward, knocks enemies back for 10% of their max HP as physical damage, and adds the slash at the end of the charge on top. Being a percentage, it bites hardest on whoever stacked health. Your enhanced basic attack is flat, not percentage — an extra 500 (1,000 at level 15) plus 125% extra physical attack — so items are what scale it. At Shadow Tyrant and Overlord, your job is to crash sideways into the brush they're holding, wedge yourself between the boss pit and their team, and split their formation. You lack solo kill power, so leave knocked-back targets to your teammates and immediately start building the next runway. While an enemy with strong slows is alive, take the long way around and come from behind — never the front.
strategy.teamfight: Your teamfight prep starts 30 seconds early: run the perimeter and keep the charge state alive. The ideal entry clips their marksman and mage in a single line, and once you've run someone over, do not stop — Skill 2 cleanses crowd control and re-accelerates you for a second and third pass. Planting your feet in the middle of the scrum is the worst thing you can do. Keep making passes back and forth through their team, and the enemy never reforms their line while your own backline shoots for free.

combos.title: Ride Through With the Cavalry
combos.sequence: Build 2,000 distance (Charge Stance) → Skill 3 (charge alongside heavy cavalry, knockback) → run it back (required distance cut by 75%) → Empowered Basic Attack (charge + knockback)
combos.description: Only the Charge Stance version summons cavalry on either side and knocks back everything in the path. Press it in Normal Stance and no dash comes out — you just get the 10s buff. That buff cuts the distance needed to enter Charge Stance by 75%, so a short run-up is enough to set up another empowered Basic Attack.

combos.title: Cleanse and Rebuild the Run-Up
combos.sequence: Skill 2, Normal Stance (removes all crowd control, +30% Movement Speed for 2s) → run to rebuild distance → Empowered Basic Attack (charge + knockback)
combos.description: Charge Stance breaks the instant Movement Speed drops under 375, and the stored distance resets 0.7s later. When you get caught, leave instead of trading — Skill 2 strips every crowd control effect off him even in Normal Stance. At Lvl 1 it adds 2s of 30% Movement Speed, which doubles as the opening of your next run-up.

combos.title: Heal in the Brush, Then Charge
combos.sequence: Stand still near brush (30 Health and Energy every 0.5s) → run 2,000 distance → Empowered Basic Attack (charge + knockback)
combos.description: Even at Lvl 1 that regen returns 30 Health and Energy every half second, so top up at the edge of a brush instead of walking home. Standing still puts Movement Speed under 375, which clears Charge Stance and the stored distance alike. Heal first, then start the run and angle the charge so they land on your side of the lane.

strengths: Charge Stance Skill 1 knocks enemies back for 10% max HP physical damage — tanks included
Skill 2 self-cleanses CC, making him extremely hard to pin down
Elite formation-breaking; he creates teamfight openings single-handedly
Gets stronger just by running, so his farm dependency is low
weaknesses: Standing still drops the charge state, leaving him weak in tight scrums
Stacked slows or chained CC stop his feet and get him focused down
Demands runway knowledge and heavy mechanics — a genuinely hard hero
Lacks solo kill power; his knockbacks need teammates to convert

playstyle.style: A cavalry hero whose power is his run-up: 2,000 units of movement puts him in charge state, where his skills split formations with knockbacks. A stationary Guan Yu is barely a hero at all.
playstyle.suited: Players happy to never stop moving, who look at every teamfight and ask only: where do I split it open?

synergy.reason: The AoE CC cleanse allows her to continuously dance inside her ultimate without being locked down.
Can group enemies with his powerful AoE taunt, maximizing the AoE damage of her ultimate.

counters.reason: His suppress ultimate cannot be cleansed by Purify, completely shutting down her mobility.
High burst damage and silence create a huge risk of getting one-shot before being able to cycle skills.

passive.description: Every time one of Diaochan's skills deals damage, it places a floral mark on the target for 8s. At the maximum of 4 stacks, the marks will be activated, restoring 140 (140 + 1.5% extra Health) Health to her while dealing 140 (140 + 40% magical attack) true damage to nearby enemies and slowing them by 25%-50% for 1s.
passive.name: Passive Skill: Explosion of Fragrance

skill1.description: Diaochan sends out a lotus in the target direction, dealing 260 (260 + 55% magical attack) magical damage to enemies in its path and again on its way back.
skill1.name: Skill 1: Returning Lotus

skill2.description: Diaochan blinks to the target location and launches 3 lotus petals at nearby enemies. Each petal deals 140 (140 + 28% magical attack) magical damage and reduces Skill 2's Cooldown for up to 3s based on the locations of her and the target hit.
skill2.name: Skill 2: Petals in the Wind

skill3.description:
Diaochan conjures a lotus circle that deals 210 (210 + 50% magical attack) magical damage upon its appearance and disappearance. When she is in the circle, the cooldowns of her Skill 1 and 2 are further reduced.
Tapping the skill again will close the lotus circle.
skill3.name: Skill 3: Flowery Potential

strategy.earlyGame: Mid lane, and until level 4 it's a patience game. Skill 1's lotus travels out and back, so catching an enemy with both halves stacks two marks in one cast — that alone covers your waveclear and poke. Skill 2 is Diaochan's only escape, so don't throw it away on offense while gank threat exists. Since four marks detonate for damage and healing, you can actually take extended HP trades more confidently than your frame suggests. Your first item goal is an early Holy Grail to erase your mana problems.
strategy.midGame: From around 7-8 minutes, with Holy Grail and cooldown items online, Diaochan becomes a true close-range mage. On roams, close the gap instantly with Skill 2. Each petal that connects shaves up to 3s off Skill 2's cooldown, so landing all three point-blank strips nearly the whole 10-second timer and you can blink again right away. In skirmishes before Tyrant, lay down Skill 3's field first, then cycle Skills 1 and 2; the true damage and healing from mark detonations can push back even a numbers disadvantage. Diving while enemy stuns or silences are still up is suicide — count who has spent their CC before you go in.
strategy.lateGame: In the late game, Diaochan's detonation true damage hits tanks and squishies alike, no matter how much armor they've stacked, so her relative damage actually rises. After 15 minutes, never take a teamfight without Skill 3's field down — inside it, your Skill 1 and 2 rotation speeds up, and with the healing included you become a different hero entirely. The one matchup to respect is burst: if an enemy assassin has the damage to delete you before your healing catches up, hold Purify or Flash and let a teammate take the first engage.
strategy.teamfight: Teamfighting Diaochan comes down to one sentence: enter the middle the instant enemy CC is gone. With your field down, the enemy clump is your fuel — hitting multiple enemies chains mark detonations until your healing outpaces the damage coming in. The ideal is catching two or three enemies in the field and confusing their aim with Skill 2's teleports while you dance. The flip side: a single stun collapses everything, so before the fight starts, know exactly who on their team holds CC and what they haven't used yet.

combos.title: Dance Inside the Circle
combos.sequence: Skill 3 (open the circle; damage on appearance) → Skill 2 (blink + 3 petals) → Skill 1 (lotus out and back) → Skill 2
combos.description: Skill 1 and Skill 2 only cool down faster while Diaochan stands inside the circle, so place it where you can hold ground rather than on top of the enemy. Every petal that connects returns cooldown on Skill 2, up to 3s. Stay close enough for all three to reach.

combos.title: Four Marks, One Detonation
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (hits going out and coming back) → Skill 2 (3 petals) → marks detonate
combos.description: A mark goes on with every skill hit, and four of them detonate. The lotus damages enemies along its path both on the way out and on the way home, so a clean throw moves the count fast. The detonation is true damage and restores her Health at the same time.

combos.title: Blink Out
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (blink toward allies or a wall) → Skill 1 (lotus across the chase)
combos.description: Skill 2 is her only movement tool, and the window right after spending it on offense is when she gets hunted. Petals still fire at nearby enemies where she lands, so a chaser who eats one hands cooldown back. The lotus returns to her hand, which means a throw on the retreat can still catch them coming back.

strengths: The detonation loop of true damage and healing gives elite staying power in brawls
Skill 2's teleport refunds cooldown on every orb hit, so she never stops moving
Inside her Ultimate's field, faster skill cycling shreds multiple enemies at once
True damage core means her output never falls off against late-game tanks
weaknesses: A silence or stun that stops the combo gets her deleted instantly
Low base durability — burst damage before marks detonate is lethal
A melee-range mage at heart; long-range poke comps never let her touch them
Very Hard difficulty — below full mastery she's just a squishy melee

playstyle.style: A melee-range mage who dances through repeated blinks, her passive detonations healing her and dealing true damage. She fights from inside the enemy team — skill difference shows instantly.
playstyle.suited: Players who want to break the rule that mages stay back — dancing at the edge of every hitbox.

synergy.reason: Cleanses CC, allowing them to safely channel their vulnerable ultimate.
Acts as a durable frontline with shields, locking down enemies so skillshots can land easily.

counters.reason: Uses high mobility to quickly close the gap and easily kill her while she's rooted during her ultimate.
Can lock her down with point-and-click hard CC and instantly burst her squishy down.

passive.description:
Every time Angela deals damage with one of her active skills, she places 1 stack of Burning on the target while gaining 1 stack of increased Movement Speed herself. Both max out at 10 stacks and last for 3s.
Stacks on enemies cause the target to take an extra 10 (10 + 2% magical attack) magical damage from her active skills, while stacks on Angela increase her Movement Speed by 2%.
passive.name: Passive Skill: Flame Incantation

skill1.description:
Angela unleashes 5 fireballs in the target direction. When a fireball hits an enemy hero, it disappears and deals 280 (280 + 30% magical attack) magical damage. Fireballs deal an equal amount of damage to non-hero units in their path.
When multiple fireballs hit the same target, subsequent fireballs only deal 30% damage.
skill1.name: Skill 1: Scorching Barrage

skill2.description:
Angela unleashes a fireball in the target direction, which forms a flame vortex upon hitting an enemy or reaching its max range, stunning the first enemy hit for 1s.
The vortex deals 125 (125 + 20% magical attack) magical damage to nearby enemies every 0.5s and slows them by 30% for 1.5s.
skill2.name: Skill 2: Chaos Cinder

skill3.description:
Angela channels a blazing beam in the target direction, dealing up to 12 strikes of 150 (150 + 21% magical attack) magical damage to enemies in its way. Angela can adjust the direction of the beam while channeling.
While channeling the beam, Angela gains a shield that grants crowd control immunity and negates 850 (850 + 88% magical attack) damage.
Use the skill again after 0.5s to cancel the channeling.
skill3.name: Skill 3: Blazing Brilliance

strategy.earlyGame: Start Skill 1 in the mid lane. All five fireballs deal full damage to non-heroes, giving Angela some of the fastest waveclear in the game — prioritize the clear until level 4 and spend leftover fireballs poking your opponent. Skill 2's 1-second stun is your lifeline, but the projectile is straightforward and easy to read; throwing it early and missing turns you into a free target, so only aim it when the enemy stops to last-hit. Your Passive stacks burn and movement speed as skills land, so keep the output flowing.
strategy.midGame: From around 7 minutes with Savant's Wrath complete, almost anyone hit by Skill 2 is coming home with you. Shove mid, show yourself along the river, and time Skill 2 with your jungler's ganks. At Tyrant fights, the fire vortex's damage-over-time and slow let you seal off chokepoints, so you have a job even when you'd rather not take a straight shootout. Your Ultimate is your damage centerpiece, but you can only steer it while firing — while enemy blinks are unaccounted for, choose your starting position carefully.
strategy.lateGame: Once Void Staff joins the build after 15 minutes, a full combo off Skill 2 evaporates everything short of a tank. But enemy assassins are also complete, so stand diagonally behind your frontline at all times. Getting dove is actually your moment: the Ultimate grants an 850 shield with super armor, and dumping all twelve beam ticks point-blank means the assassin who came for a kill melts instead — the signature Angela experience. In the tight paths near Shadow Tyrant, pre-place Skill 2 to watch the entrance.
strategy.teamfight: The single biggest teamfight rule: don't spend Skill 2 at the start. Hitting a frontliner wastes the stun into shields and armor. Wait until the enemy divers jump onto your allies, then land it on their stalled backline or the assassin coming for you. From the stun, chain a burn-stacked Skill 1 and the Ultimate — nothing non-durable survives the sequence. The beam can be cancelled 0.5 seconds after it starts, so build the habit of cutting it the moment your target drops and saving the rest for the next exchange.

combos.title: Stun, Then Burn Through
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (1s stun + vortex) → Skill 3 (beam, up to 12 strikes) → Skill 1 (5 fireballs)
combos.description: The stun lasts one second, but the beam can be steered while it is firing. Track them as they start moving and stack the vortex's damage every 0.5s along with its 30% slow (Lvl 1). Fireballs after the first deal 30% damage to the same hero, so treat Skill 1 as the finisher rather than the payload.

combos.title: Answer the Dive
combos.sequence: Skill 3 (850 shield at Lvl 1 + crowd control immunity) → Skill 2 (1s stun) → Skill 1
combos.description: Start the beam the instant they land on you. While the shield holds, crowd control immunity keeps the channel from being broken. If the kill isn't there, use the skill again after 0.5s to cancel and walk away.

combos.title: Seal the Choke
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (placed into the path) → Skill 1 (follow-up)
combos.description: Skill 2 forms its vortex even when it reaches max range without touching anyone. Don't aim it at a target — put it where they have to walk. The vortex keeps dealing damage and slowing every 0.5s, so it costs them ground even on a miss.

strengths: One landed Skill 2 stun lets her solo-delete an enemy backliner
Ultimate's shield and super armor let her ignore CC and finish the beam
Passive burn stacks make consecutive skill hits snowball her damage
Five-projectile Skill 1 gives extremely fast waveclear
weaknesses: Every skill is a skillshot — strafing enemies are hard to hit
No blink, so self-defense is paper-thin right after Skill 2 misses
The Ultimate only steers while firing; a bad starting position is fatal
Skill 1 fireballs decay after the first hit on a hero, so single-target damage is inconsistent

playstyle.style: A turret mage whose burn stacks make every follow-up hit harder, finished by a steerable beam that chases runners down. Point her at the fight and she is the damage plan.
playstyle.suited: Players who want to be the main damage source without a complex kit — watching stacked numbers climb is the reward.

synergy.reason: Groups enemies together, making it easier for Luna to land skills on multiple targets and consistently reset her ultimate.
Provides CC cleanse and immunity, supporting the squishy Luna to safely dive into the enemy backline.

counters.reason: Can completely lock down Luna with strong targeted hard CC, neutralizing her ultimate's mobility.
Stacks marks by switching between ranged and melee, out-trading Luna before her combo lands.

passive.description:
Luna's Basic Attack has two forms. When the target is out of melee range, it automatically switches to the ranged form.
While in melee form, the 1st of every 3 of her Basic Attacks causes her to charge toward the enemy.
Every 3rd Basic Attack deals an extra 150 (150 + 35% magical attack) magical damage and marks the enemy for 5s. Structures cannot be marked.
For every 1 Magical Attack, she gains 0.03% Attack Speed.
passive.name: Passive Skill: Moonlight Dance

skill1.description: Luna unleashes a moon wave, dealing 400 (400 +65% magical attack) magical damage to enemies and marking them.
skill1.name: Skill 1: Crescent Slice

skill2.description:
Luna pulls in nearby enemies, dealing 160 (160 + 32% magical attack) magical damage. The attack stuns them for 0.5s and slows them by 25% for 2s. Luna also gains a shield that negates 450 (450 + 80% magical attack) damage for 2s.
Pulled enemies will also be marked.
skill2.name: Skill 2: Searing Stab

skill3.description:
Luna dashes to the target location, dealing 350 (350 + 60% magical attack) magical damage to enemies in her path.
If she hits a marked enemy, this skill's cooldown is reset and the mark is consumed.
skill3.name: Skill 3: New Moon

strategy.earlyGame: Luna is a jungler first. Open on both buffs and the camps between them and race to level 4, drilling the Skill 1 → Ultimate → third basic attack order into muscle memory as you clear. Everything Luna does rests on one rule: hitting a marked enemy with the Ultimate resets its cooldown. On your first ganks after level 4, resist the urge to show off a long chain — landing Skill 2's pull and stun to hold the target for your laner succeeds far more often than a greedy solo play.
strategy.midGame: From around 8 minutes, with one or two magic attack items done, Luna headlines every skirmish. The base pattern at Tyrant and mid: tag from range with Skill 1, enter with the Ultimate, refresh the mark with your third basic and Skill 2, and keep weaving in and out. Marks stick to minions too, so learn to chain Ultimates through waves and camps as transportation — it puts your chases and escapes in a different dimension. As long as you don't die, nobody out-farms you.
strategy.lateGame: Teamfights after 15 minutes are won before you enter. A Luna walking in the front door is just a squishy melee, so always start from a flank or the rear with a mark already on a perimeter enemy. Touch once and leave before their stuns and silences turn your way, then start the real dance once their CC is down. Skill 2's shield and 0.5-second stun erase hundreds of damage in a scrum — when you feel surrounded, restart from the pull rather than the attack and your survival rate climbs.
strategy.teamfight: A dropped chain is death, full stop. Throughout the fight, keep the next marked Ultimate target decided two steps ahead, and the instant one dies, switch to another enemy or a minion. While a mark lives, you enter and exit the fight at will — from the enemy's seat, an uncatchable nightmare. But one missed reset deletes your escape plan, so build the habit of confirming your exit mark one step before every overextension. Luna returns exactly what you put into her, and she demands commitment.

combos.title: Keep Skill 3 Rolling
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (apply the mark) → Skill 3 (dash; hitting a marked enemy resets its cooldown) → 3rd Basic Attack (re-apply the mark) → Skill 3
combos.description: Landing Skill 3 on a marked enemy resets its cooldown. Both Skill 1 and every 3rd Basic Attack apply that mark, so after each dash you bank three hits to set up the next reset. In melee form the 1st of every 3 attacks charges her at the enemy, which closes a small gap on its own.

combos.title: Pull First, Then Restart
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (pull + 0.5s stun + 450 shield + mark) → Skill 3 (hitting the mark resets the cooldown) → 3rd Basic Attack → Skill 3
combos.description: When they surround her, press Skill 2 before you press attack. Everything it pulls gets marked, and the 0.5s stun plus a 450 shield (Lvl 1) buys the beat she needs. They also lose 25% Movement Speed for 2s, which is enough to put Skill 3 back into that mark and restart the loop.

combos.title: Hop Through Minions
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (mark a minion) → Skill 3 (dash to it; the cooldown resets) → Skill 3 again to the next marked target
combos.description: Towers and crystals cannot be marked, but minions and jungle camps can. Use them as waypoints and Skill 3 chains far past its own range. Miss the marked target and no reset comes, which strands her exactly where she stopped.

strengths: Endless Ultimate resets grant mobility no one else in the game matches
Skill 2's pull, stun, and shield keep her alive in the center of brawls
Free entry and exit lets her bait enemy CC before the real engage
At full mastery, she can win a teamfight single-handedly
weaknesses: The instant the reset chain breaks, her escape disappears with it
A stun or silence mid-loop reduces her to a squishy melee
One of the hardest heroes in the game — low mastery means zero output
Tunnel vision mid-combo makes her slow to react to counter-ganks

playstyle.style: The moonlight duelist with a theoretically infinite combo: her ultimate resets whenever it hits a marked enemy. Maintain the mark-dash-mark loop and she never stops; drop it once and she's mortal again.
playstyle.suited: Players willing to drill one combo hundreds of times — few heroes reward mastery this steeply.

synergy.reason: Provides a solid frontline and CC, creating an environment where Ziya can safely focus on poking from the backline.
As a carry, she heavily benefits from Ziya's passive level cap increase, drastically boosting her late-game DPS.

counters.reason: Can instantly close the gap with high mobility and stealth, easily one-shotting the immobile Ziya.
Can safely deal poke and burst damage from an even further range than Ziya.

passive.description:
When Ziya deals damage to a target and they are defeated within 3s, he gains 1-3 EXP orbs.
When he reaches level 15, Sanctification Power is restored, granting the one-time skill Sanctify and increasing his level cap to level 25. Each level gained grants 20 Magical Attack.
Sanctify grants 1,200 EXP to a teammate, allowing them to break through their level cap, and potentially gain EXP orbs.
If Ziya acts as a support in the match, he grants additional Sanctification effects based on the teammate's class.
passive.name: Passive Skill: Sanctification

skill1.description: Ziya places a divine seal on enemies in the target area, dealing 70 (70 + 14% magical attack) magical damage, followed by 60 (60 + 12% magical attack) magical damage every 0.4s for a total of 7 hits. Sealed enemies will gradually lose up to 30% of their Movement Speed and 10% of their physical defense and 10% of their magical defense. If the skill hits any enemy, he gains a 30% Movement Speed boost that diminishes over 1s.
skill1.name: Skill 1: Divine Seal

skill2.description: Ziya unleashes divine retribution on wrongdoers, conjuring a magic circle that deals 3 strikes of damage to enemies in the target area. Each strike deals 60 (60 + 12% magical attack) magical damage. After a short delay, the magic circle explodes, dealing 300 (300 + 70% magical attack) magical damage to enemies and launching them for 0.75s.
skill2.name: Skill 2: Divine Punishment

skill3.description:
Ziya channels divine energy in the target direction, unleashing 3 shockwaves. The first 2 shockwaves each deal 120 (120 + 20% magical attack) magical damage, while the last deals 560 (560 + 80% magical attack) magical damage.
Upon reaching level 15, Ziya's Sanctification Power is restored, and there is a 20% chance of entering the Sanctifier state, allowing him to launch a shockwave while moving. Each subsequent level gained increases the chance of entering the Sanctifier state by 20%.
The charging lasts up to 2s, and moving or using the Ultimate again will immediately unleash the shockwaves. Charge time affects the attack range of the shockwaves, up to a distance of 1,800. Shockwaves deal 10% damage to structures in their path.
skill3.name: Skill 3: Universal Law

strategy.earlyGame: Ziya holds the mid lane, and until level 15 the job description reads: survive and soak experience. Place Skill 1 where the wave and the enemy overlap and it handles clearing, harass, and defense shred in one cast. Your Passive drops EXP balls from kills you've damaged, so pick them up religiously to build a level lead. With no blink, never leave tower range while the enemy jungler is dark. Skill 2's knock-up is your self-defense — waste it on offense and the bill arrives with the next gank.
strategy.midGame: Level 15 — roughly the 10-minute mark — is Ziya's turning point. Reaching it lifts your level cap to 25 on its own, and every level after that adds 20 magical attack. The same moment grants Sanctify, a one-time skill you aim at a teammate, never at yourself. Whoever you pick gains 1,200 EXP, breaks through their own level cap, and has a chance at EXP orbs; from the roam slot they also collect an extra Sanctification effect matched to their class. Hand it to the carry whose next level changes the most. Skill 3 shifts at level 15 as well, but only on a roll — 20% to enter the Sanctifier state, climbing 20% per level, which works out to every cast from level 19. Only in that state can you fire a shockwave while moving, charging up to 2s to stretch the range out to 1,800. Step up in Shadow Tyrant standoffs when the state procs, and settle for the standard three-shockwave cast when it doesn't. Shockwaves pass just 10% damage to towers and crystals, so leave the siege to your teammates.
strategy.lateGame: Late-game Ziya stands behind the backline — the deepest position on the map. Past level 20, your magic attack ranks among the game's highest, and two charged Ultimates connecting is enough to halve an enemy formation. Before Overlord, start seeding the chokepoints with Skill 1 thirty seconds ahead of the spawn to strip defense and speed until the fight favors you. Track the enemy assassin at all times, and when they're missing, hold the charge. If you get touched mid-channel, the lost fight is mostly on you.
strategy.teamfight: Seventy percent of Ziya's teamfight happens before the fight. Skill 1 walls off approach paths, and Skill 2 goes down early on the spot where their diver will land — press it before they jump, because pressing it after never connects. That's the field lesson worth remembering. Once the brawl starts, thread charged Ultimates in from maximum range and drive the lowest-HP enemies out of the fight one by one. While your blessed teammate rampages up front, you conduct the battle from beyond anyone's reach.

combos.title: Seal, Then Launch
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (strip Movement Speed and defense) → Skill 2 (delayed explosion, 0.75s launch) → Skill 3 (3 shockwaves)
