combos.description: A sealed enemy loses up to 30% Movement Speed and 10% of both physical and magical defense (Lvl 1). A slowed target makes the delayed magic circle far easier to place. Only the last of the three shockwaves hits hard, so use the 0.75s of hang time to get all the way to it.

combos.title: Charge to Full Range
combos.sequence: Skill 3 (charge up to 2s for 1,800 range) → Skill 1 (follow-up)
combos.description: Charge time scales the shockwave's range, and a full 2s reaches 1,800. Structures caught in the path take 10% damage. Any movement releases the wave early, so a full charge means standing still for the whole two seconds.

combos.title: Peel Off With the Speed Boost
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (on hit, +30% Movement Speed for 1s) → back off → Skill 2 (launch the pursuer)
combos.description: Ziya has no blink, so his getaway is the 30% Movement Speed that Skill 1 hands him whenever it connects. It diminishes across that 1s, which makes the first step after the cast the fastest one available. Drop the magic circle once the gap opens and the 0.75s launch ends the chase.

strengths: Sanctification is a one-of-a-kind buff that raises an ally's level cap
1800-range charged Ultimate enables safe poke and siege from another zip code
Skill 1's slow and defense shred dominates pre-objective standoffs
Passive EXP balls make building a level lead easy
weaknesses: No blink — self-defense rests entirely on predicting with Skill 2
Charging the Ultimate leaves him wide open, a gift for assassins
Power spikes at level 15, so falling behind early is hard to repair
Misusing the Sanctification target or timing halves his late game

playstyle.style: The mage whose level cap extends to 25 — growth itself is his identity. He fights with seals and shockwaves, and by the late game his raw stats leave other mages behind.
playstyle.suited: Players who love long-term investment: endure the early game, then collect with a hero who simply out-levels the lobby.

synergy.reason: Di Renjie's Imperial Order stuns the first hero hit for 1s and exposes their location for 5s, and teammates moving toward that target gain 10% Movement Speed. Liu Bang keeps Staggering Charge fully charged for 10s after teleporting, so he can cover the full 550 dash onto a target he can already see.

Butterfly's Death Dealer jumps onto a single enemy, and for 4s after the hit she takes 50% less damage from Basic Attacks. Skill damage still lands in full, and that is the gap Liu Bang's ultimate shield fills as he channels on her and arrives at her side. A kill resets her ultimate.

counters.reason: Marco Polo sprays 5 bullets with Skill 1 and keeps firing for 3s with Fevered Barrage, so stacks of Destruction pile up fast. Ten stacks break the target's defense, and every hit after that adds 100 true damage that Liu Bang cannot cut down by stacking defense.

Lu Bu is immune to crowd control while diving with Tremble, Mortals, and the landing launches everyone in range for 1s. Liu Bang's ultimate needs a 2.2s channel, so that launch cancels it outright. Inside the ring Lu Bu gains 150 physical and 150 magical defense on top.

passive.description: Liu Bang gains 1 mark every second, for up to 4 marks. Basic Attacks expend all marks, dealing an additional 80 (80 + 10% magical attack) magical damage per mark. At maximum marks, the next Basic Attack is enhanced into a ranged attack that deals 474 (294 + 100% physical attack + 42% magical attack) magical damage.
passive.name: Passive Skill: Royal Ambition

skill1.description:
Liu Bang gains a shield that negates 650 (650 + 20% extra Health) damage for 5s. Upon expiry, the shield detonates and deals 650 (650 + 90% magical attack) magical damage to nearby enemies.
After 1.5s, using the skill again will detonate the shield immediately. If the shield is broken, it will only deal 50% damage.
skill1.name: Skill 1: Dominator's Shield

skill2.description:
Liu Bang dashes a distance of 275−550 in the target direction, dealing 300 (300 + 40% magical attack)−600 (600 + 80% magical attack) magical damage to enemies in his path and stunning them for 0.75s.
This skill can be charged for up to 1s, and its effects depend on charging time. If the charge is interrupted or canceled, the cooldown will be reduced by 40%.
skill2.name: Skill 2: Staggering Charge

skill3.description:
Liu Bang selects a teammate and starts channeling in place, granting the teammate a shield that negates (480 + 12% target's extra Health)−(960 + 24% target's extra Health) damage. After 2.2s, he teleports to the teammate.
Upon arriving, Liu Bang gains 30% Movement Speed and restores 300 (300 + 8% extra Health) Health to himself and nearby teammates. He also fully charges Staggering Charge, keeping it charged for 10s.
After channeling for 0.4s, this skill can be used again to immediately teleport to the teammate, remove their shield, and deal 200 (200 + 40% magical attack)−400 (400 + 80% magical attack) magical damage to nearby enemies. However, he will not gain the recovery effect.
The longer he channels, the stronger the shield becomes and the more damage he deals upon ending the channeling early.
skill3.name: Skill 3: Battlefield Command

strategy.earlyGame: Liu Bang's default home is the clash lane. Until level 4, Skill 1's shield and delayed blast handle the waves, while the Passive's four-stack ranged empowered basic lets you chip melee opponents without ever being touched. Skill 2's charged dash is your only stun and it's precious — through the early game, hold it as the counter-punch for enemy jungler ganks. Liu Bang's real value unlocks with his Ultimate and its map-wide reach, so through this window, simply banking experience without dying earns a passing grade.
strategy.midGame: After the 4-minute Tyrant, your two-front war begins. Shove side waves, and the moment a teammate gets touched anywhere on the map, channel your Ultimate and warp to them. You arrive delivering shields, and for 10 seconds after warping, Skill 2 sits at max charge — meaning an immediate full-range stun dash the second you land. The 2.2-second channel is a complete opening, so always cast from brush or behind a tower. Your goal is planting one thought in every enemy's head: if Liu Bang is off the map, this could be a 5v6.
strategy.lateGame: With three or more defense items after 15 minutes, split push and make two defenders deal with you. A detail worth banking: your Ultimate's shield scales with the target's bonus HP, so it lands biggest on your beefiest tank or fighter. The gold-standard pattern is pushing a side lane until seconds before Overlord, then warping in as it spawns. And if five enemies start collapsing on you, the warp to a distant ally is itself your escape hatch.
strategy.teamfight: Fighting with your team from the start, the job is catching the enemy carry with Skill 2's stun and layering Skill 1's blast on top. The shield can be manually detonated 1.5 seconds after casting, so when enemies glue themselves to you, pop it yourself and waste nothing. Arriving from a side lane instead, drop onto their backline mid-fight and let the max-charge Skill 2 flip the board. Engage together or arrive late — read the enemy comp and pick your policy in the first half, and the hesitation disappears.

combos.title: Drop Into the Fight
combos.sequence: Skill 3 (2.2s channel → teleport to the ally) → Skill 2 (max-charge dash stun) → Skill 1 (shield) → Basic Attack
combos.description: The 2.2s channel leaves him wide open, so start it in brush or behind a tower. On arrival he heals himself and nearby allies, and Skill 2 stays fully charged for 10s. That means a 550-length dash and a 0.75s stun are ready the moment he lands.

combos.title: Pop Your Own Shield
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (shield) → Skill 2 (dash + 0.75s stun) → Basic Attack (spends marks) → Skill 1 re-tap (detonate)
combos.description: The shield damages nearby enemies when it expires, but a shield broken by the enemy first only deals half. From 1.5s after it goes up, you can detonate it yourself. Doing that point-blank while the stun holds is the reliable way to land it.

combos.title: Cut the Channel Short
combos.sequence: Skill 3 (channel) → re-tap after 0.4s (instant teleport + damage around the ally) → Skill 2 (dash stun)
combos.description: Cutting the channel at 0.4s gets you next to your ally without the wait. In exchange, the shield you handed them is removed and you get no healing. A longer channel means a stronger shield and more arrival damage, so wait it out whenever the fight allows.

strengths: The Ultimate projects pressure onto any fight from anywhere on the map
One warp delivers shields, healing, and his own escape in a single skill
A guaranteed max-charge Skill 2 stun for 10 seconds after every warp
Passive ranged empowered basics let him poke melee laners for free
weaknesses: The 2.2-second channel is a total opening and struggles when watched
Low personal burst — he rarely closes out a kill alone
Built around split play, so one bad Ultimate creates instant man-down fights
No CC beyond the single stun, so mobile enemies slip away repeatedly

playstyle.style: A tank whose shields explode and whose ultimate teleports him to any ally on the map. The mere fact that Liu Bang is missing from vision is pressure — the split-map specialist.
playstyle.suited: Players who love pressuring two places at once, flipping the board with a single warp.

synergy.reason: Provides reliable lockdown on enemies, creating openings for Han Xin to safely close the gap and unleash his burst damage.
Stops enemy movement with long-range stuns, heavily supporting Han Xin's engages and disengages.

counters.reason: If his escape routes are completely blocked by the ultimate, he cannot utilize his high mobility and will easily be killed.
Dodges Han Xin's attacks with high mobility and repeated blinks, wearing him down with her passive's sustain and true damage.

passive.description: Han Xin's every 4th Basic Attack launches the enemy for 0.5s and deals an extra 90 (90 + 35% extra physical attack) physical damage with 20% Physical Lifesteal. He gains 25-50% Attack Speed after landing a hit with a skill or an enhanced Basic Attack.
passive.name: Passive Skill: Killing Spear

skill1.description:
Han Xin leaps to the target location, dealing 250 (250 +85% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies within range and launching them for 0.5s.
He can leap again within 5s, dealing an equal amount of physical damage to enemies within range.
skill1.name: Skill 1: Ruthless Assault

skill2.description:
Han Xin dashes backward and enhances his next Basic Attack into a sweep for 3s, which deals 120 (120 + 50% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies within range.
If the Fight or Die! sweep is his 4th Basic Attack, it carries the 4th Basic Attack's extra effects.
skill2.name: Skill 2: Fight or Die!

skill3.description:
Han Xin executes a 4-strike flurry with his spear in a cone-shaped area in the target direction, each strike dealing 250 (250 + 65% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies within range, with the final strike launching enemies within range for 0.5s.
While using his Ultimate, he gains crowd control immunity and 30% damage reduction.
skill3.name: Skill 3: The Unrivaled Spear

strategy.earlyGame: Han Xin junglers almost always open from the blue buff side. The Passive's fourth-hit knock-up and 20% lifesteal mean that simply spacing out clean four-hit sequences keeps your HP topped while you clear at speed. Once your Ultimate unlocks at level 4, start ganking the lane being shoved in or any enemy slow to back off. Skill 1's double jump crosses walls, so appear from the wall behind your target rather than the river — suddenly there is no correct direction for them to run.
strategy.midGame: From around 7 minutes with your first core item done, Han Xin's hunting ground moves to the enemy jungle. Bounce through unwarded territory on double jumps, catch farmers alone, and vanish — that loop alone visibly stunts the whole enemy team's growth. Skip the opening exchanges at Tyrant and mid; your role is entering from the side once both teams are worn down and collecting what's left. And before every invade, decide your exit route first. Skip that step, and all the mobility in the game won't carry you home.
strategy.lateGame: After 15 minutes, Han Xin loses half his value the moment he stands in a front-on 5v5. Instead, push a side lane deep: two enemies come, hop a wall and vanish; one comes, kill him. That single repeated decision keeps the map in your team's hands. At Overlord, lurk in a flanking position and dive their backline after the fight starts. Your Ultimate carries super armor and 30% damage reduction while spinning, so committing under a tower or through a wall of enemy CC is a play you're allowed to make with confidence.
strategy.teamfight: Wait on the perimeter until the enemy's CC and attention are committed to your frontline, then take Skill 1 into their isolated backline. Land three basics, then time Skill 2's sweep as the fourth hit for a guaranteed knock-up, and spin your Ultimate through them to finish — that's the ideal script. When the target drops, don't chase; leave on Skill 1's remaining jump. A Han Xin who spent every movement skill on the way in is just a fragile spearman, so always keep one in the tank for the road home.

combos.title: Make the Sweep Your Fourth Hit
combos.sequence: Basic Attack ×3 → Skill 2 (dash opposite the aimed direction; next Basic Attack becomes a sweep) → Basic Attack (the sweep, landing as the 4th hit, 0.5s launch) → Skill 3 (4 strikes, final one launches)
combos.description: Skill 2 only arms the sweep — you still have to press Basic Attack to throw it. Bank three hits first and that sweep arrives as the 4th, carrying the 0.5s launch and 20% physical lifesteal. Run Skill 3's four strikes through the airborne target, and its final strike puts them back up.

combos.title: Leap In, Spin Out
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (leap + 0.5s launch) → Skill 3 (crowd control immunity + 30% damage reduction, 4 strikes) → Skill 1 (second leap to leave)
combos.description: The first leap launches everything in the landing area for 0.5s. Skill 3 runs with crowd control immunity and 30% damage reduction, so all four strikes finish even while their control is landing on him. The second leap expires 5s after the first — spend it on the way out, not the way in.

combos.title: Three Moves to Break Away
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (first leap) → Skill 1 (second leap, within 5s) → Skill 2 (dash opposite the aimed direction)
combos.description: Two leaps plus the reverse dash cover three moves' worth of ground in one motion. The awkward piece is Skill 2, which dashes opposite the direction you aim. While being chased, tap toward the enemy rather than toward where you want to end up.

strengths: Double jumps and the reverse dash give mobility few heroes can match
Passive knock-up and 20% lifesteal keep his HP healthy through repeated fights
Ultimate's super armor and 30% reduction let him finish combos through CC
Elite wall-hopping makes enemy jungle invades and escapes routine
weaknesses: Fragile base stats — one CC chain after his jumps are spent is lethal
Skill 2's reverse input is unique, and precision directly equals survival
Damage is built around reaching the fourth hit, so split-second trades underwhelm
Long stretches of solo play mean vision-starved games blunt his edge

playstyle.style: A spear fighter who lives in motion, chaining double-jump engages and knock-ups so the target never gets a turn. Kill, reposition, flow to the next target.
playstyle.suited: Players who believe standing still is losing — you enjoy movement itself and will drill positioning until it's muscle memory.

synergy.reason: Draws enemy attention and provides lockdown on the frontline, making it much easier for Wang Zhaojun to land her Skill 2 freeze.
Overlapping their massive AoE magic damage can absolutely decimate the enemy team in teamfights.

counters.reason: Her high mobility makes it easy to dodge the freeze skill, allowing her to quickly close the gap and burst Wang Zhaojun down.
His strong CC cleanse and immunity skills can completely neutralize Wang Zhaojun's biggest strength, her freeze, for the entire enemy team.

passive.description:
Upon leaving combat, Wang Zhaojun gains a shield that negates 450 (450 + 58% magical attack) damage. Enemies that deal physical damage to the shield will be chilled. When the shield disappears, it deals 400 (400 + 75% magical attack) magical damage to nearby enemies and chills them.
Her every third Basic Attack will be enhanced, firing 3 icicles that deal a total of 180 (180 + 36% magical attack) magical damage. Each icicle applies 100% of the Basic Attack's on-hit effects.
Hits from her active skills and enhanced Basic Attacks will chill enemies, reducing their Movement Speed by 25-50% and Attack Speed by 25-50% for 2s. These effects diminish over time.
passive.name: Passive Skill: Frozen Heart

skill1.description: Wang Zhaojun conjures a burst of exploding ice in the target location, dealing 350 (350 + 50% magical attack) magical damage and inflicting chill to enemies within range. She also gains vision of the area and any enemies hit for 2s.
skill1.name: Skill 1: Shattered Ice

skill2.description:
Wang Zhaojun summons a freezing circle in the target location. After a short delay, she deals 250 (250 +50% magical attack) magical damage to enemies within range and freezes them for 2.5s.
She deals an extra 150 (150 + 20% magical attack) magical damage to frozen enemies.
skill2.name: Skill 2: Frigid Prison

skill3.description:
Wang Zhaojun summons a snowstorm in the target location for 5s. The snowstorm deals 200 (200 + 35% magical attack) magical damage and inflicts chill to enemies within range every 0.5s.
Summoning a snowstorm grants her the shield from her passive.
skill3.name: Skill 3: Winter Is Here

strategy.earlyGame: In the mid lane, Skill 1 is your everything until level 4. It clears waves, and since it grants 2 seconds of vision at the impact point, firing scout shots into the river brush warns you of ganks before they happen. Your Passive shield regenerates out of combat and chills any physical attacker who breaks it, so trade confidently whenever the shield is up. Skill 2 has a long delay before it triggers, so at this stage only aim it at enemies rooted in place clearing the wave — anything else is a coin flip.
strategy.midGame: Wang Zhaojun's setup game begins with the 4-minute Tyrant. Drop your Ultimate's blizzard on the river entrance and that path is closed for 5 seconds — anyone forcing through eats chill that strips both movement and attack speed. When a gank arrives, pre-place Skill 2 on the enemy's escape route — more precisely, on the spot where they'll stand after using their blink. Land the 2.5-second freeze with your jungler present and the kill is all but booked. The Ultimate also refreshes your Passive shield, which is exactly the license you need to play forward.
strategy.lateGame: With Savant's Wrath and Void Staff done after 15 minutes, the blizzard's ticks turn genuinely heavy. Before Shadow Tyrant and Overlord fights, seed the chokepoint with your Ultimate early, warp their formation, and give your team the signal to commit. If the freeze → Skill 1 → empowered third basic sequence reaches their backline, the numbers advantage ends the game on the spot. You have zero mobility, so live in the deepest position — and when the enemy assassin vanishes from the map, your first thought should be about your own feet.
strategy.teamfight: Your contribution is decided by who you chill. Cooling down their frontline tank moves nothing. The target is their marksman: chill strips up to 50% of both movement and attack speed, which functionally disarms a carry — damage and kiting gone in one status effect. The ideal opening: blizzard on their backline's heads, Skill 2 on the retreat path, then Skill 1 and empowered basics to follow. Frozen enemies also take bonus damage, so tell your team before the fight to focus whoever's frozen first — it visibly changes the results.

combos.title: Slow Them, Then Freeze Them
combos.sequence: Skill 3 (5s snowstorm + regain the passive shield) → Skill 2 (delayed 2.5s freeze) → Skill 1 → 3rd Basic Attack (3 icicles)
combos.description: The snowstorm deals damage and applies chill every 0.5s. With up to 50% of their Movement Speed gone, they can't simply walk out of Skill 2's delayed circle. Frozen targets take extra damage, so pack Skill 1 and the empowered Basic Attack into those 2.5 seconds.

combos.title: Freeze the Retreat
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (placed where they'll fall back) → Skill 1 (chill + 2s vision) → 3rd Basic Attack (empowered)
combos.description: Skill 2 takes time to go off, so chasing with it never connects. Aim at where they're heading — a landed freeze holds them for 2.5s, long enough for your jungler to arrive. Skill 1 also reveals whoever it hits for 2s, so brush stops being cover.

combos.title: Scout Before You Commit
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (into brush or around a corner) → read the 2s of vision → Skill 2 (onto whoever shows up)
combos.description: Skill 1 grants vision of the target area and of any enemy it hits for 2s. On a 5s cooldown (Lvl 1), spending it on reconnaissance still gets it back quickly. If something shows, go place the freeze; if nothing does, return to the wave.

strengths: Skill 2's 2.5-second freeze converts into a near-guaranteed kill with follow-up
Chill strips movement and attack speed at once — brutal against marksmen
The Ultimate refreshes her Passive shield, making her tougher than she looks
Skill 1's vision grant makes her excellent at scouting and dodging ganks
weaknesses: Skill 2's trigger delay makes it nearly impossible to land unassisted
No movement skill — once an enemy reaches her, she rarely gets away
Damage lives in placed zones, so constantly moving enemies out-trade her
Enemies who step out of the blizzard halve her teamfight output

playstyle.style: A slow-acting lockdown mage who layers chill until enemies freeze solid. Her out-of-combat shield keeps her alive while her blizzard gradually strangles the enemy formation.
playstyle.suited: Players who prefer certainty over speed — tightening the net one degree of frost at a time.

synergy.reason: Can provide vision and armor shred, maximizing Prince of Lanling's burst damage potential.
Draws enemy attention during teamfights, making it much easier for a stealthed Prince of Lanling to flank and assassinate the enemy marksman.

counters.reason: Can secure vision with his skills, allowing his team to anticipate and counter Prince of Lanling's stealth engages.
Possesses extremely high durability and CC, able to tank Prince of Lanling's burst damage and counter-engage with lockdown.

passive.description: Gao Changgong's Movement Speed is increased by 15-30% when moving toward enemy heroes.
passive.name: Passive Skill: Secret Skill - Rush

skill1.description:
Gao Changgong slashes enemies within range, dealing 350 (350 +125% extra physical attack) physical damage. He also summons a shadow copy of himself to attack a random nearby enemy, which deals the same physical damage he does.
The shadow copy prioritizes attacking heroes with low Health.
skill1.name: Skill 1: Secret Skill - Split

skill2.description: Gao Changgong throws a shadow dagger in the target direction, dealing 200 (200 + 90% extra physical attack) physical damage to the first enemy it hits and slowing them immensely for 2s, which diminishes over time. Dagger hits place marks on enemies for 3s. His attacks on marked targets will stun them for 1s and restore 350 (350 + 10% extra Health) Health to him. When marks disappear, the enemy takes physical damage equal to 152 (140 + 12% lost Health) (plus an extra 1% for every 50 extra physical attack). The dagger is destroyed upon hitting an enemy hero.
skill2.name: Skill 2: Secret Skill - Sling

skill3.description: Gao Changgong immediately exits stealth, charging toward the target direction and dealing 700 (700 + 250% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies in his path.
skill3.name: Skill 3: Secret Skill - Strike

skill4.description: After a 1.5s delay, Gao Changgong enters stealth for 30s while gaining 15%-30% Movement Speed for 5s. Upon leaving stealth, he gains 30%-60% Attack Speed for 5s. Staying near an enemy while in stealth for over 3s will remove stealth automatically. Movement Speed and Attack Speed boosts scale with hero level.
skill4.name: Skill 4: Secret Skill - Shadow

strategy.earlyGame: Start on your own buffs and rush level 4. The reason is simple: Gao Changgong's assassination kit only comes online once the Ultimate's dash links into Skill 2's follow-up stun. His Passive grants 20% bonus move speed only while moving toward enemy heroes, so approach ganks through bushes rather than down the lane. Touch the bottom side of the map at least once before the Tyrant spawns at 4:00 — showing up with a numbers advantage decides that first objective more often than the smite does.
strategy.midGame: Your assassination power peaks around 8-10 minutes, when two core physical and penetration items are done. Skill 2's mark lasts 3 seconds, and the moment it disappears the target takes 152 (140 + 12% lost Health) physical damage. The scaling is on health already lost, not max health, so the mark pays out more the longer you chip at them first — and every 50 extra physical attack adds another 1% on top. Re-attacking a marked enemy stuns for 1 second and heals you, which makes even greedy dives surprisingly survivable. Before the Shadow Tyrant arrives at 10:00, walk the enemy jungle bushes once to map out your ambush routes.
strategy.lateGame: Past 15 minutes, tanks get too beefy and your value in front-to-front fights drops. Hunt the enemies who leave the group instead: the side laner pushing alone, the support walking out for vision. If Skill 2 connects, the stun plus percent damage almost always converts into a kill. Deleting one enemy right before the Overlord contest is your real win condition — treat full 5v5s as a last resort and only fight with a numbers edge.
strategy.teamfight: Never be the first one in. You are paper-thin, and a single crowd-control effect will end you, so wait until the enemy dumps their lockdown on your frontline before circling to the backline. Always open with Skill 2: a hit slows the target immensely for 2 seconds, and because that slow diminishes as it runs, the first second is when you close. Skill 3 covers the rest of the gap and sets up the 1-second stun from re-attacking the mark. Skill 1's clone automatically hunts the lowest-HP enemy hero, so in a scrum it cleans up chunked targets you can't physically reach.

combos.title: Stealth Entry Assassination
combos.sequence: Skill 4 (stealth after 1.5s + move speed) → Skill 3 (exit stealth, charge in) → Skill 2 (heavy slow + 3s mark) → Basic Attack (marked target: 1s stun + heal) → Skill 1 (AoE slash + shadow copy)
combos.description: Use stealth to get behind them, then close with Skill 3 before landing the dagger. Leaving stealth grants 30-60% Attack Speed for 5s, so the follow-up attack on the mark arrives without a gap. Miss the dagger and you lose both the stun and the heal, so only throw it from a range you can actually hit.

combos.title: Mark and Disengage
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (heavy slow + 3s mark) → Basic Attack (1s stun + heal) → Skill 1 (AoE slash + shadow copy) → Back off (the mark expires for bonus damage)
combos.description: The pattern for fights you cannot commit to. The mark expires after 3s and detonates for 12% of lost Health on top of its base value (140 at Lvl 1). The shadow copy prioritizes the lowest-Health hero, so it keeps chipping away once you have pulled out.

strengths: Single-target burst from Skill 2's 1s stun plus a mark that detonates for 12% of lost Health
Passive move speed makes chases and bush ganks reliably stick
Healing off marked targets lets him survive aggressive dives and chain fights
The clone auto-targets the lowest-HP enemy hero and cleans up scraps
weaknesses: Paper-thin defenses — a single CC chain usually kills him
Missing Skill 2 deletes the stun and percent damage, half his kit
No frontal fighting tools, so his impact fades in late 5v5s
The Ultimate is his only mobility, making exits after deep dives rough

playstyle.style: A classic stealth assassin: approach unseen, mark the target, and end it in one burst. The fight is mostly decided before he becomes visible.
playstyle.suited: Players who plan three different entrances before every fight, and who prefer one decisive judgement call over flashy mechanics.

synergy.reason: Provides damage reduction and CC immunity, increasing Mulan's safety when she dives deep into the enemy backline.

counters.reason: His powerful targeted hard CC can completely lock her down before she can dish out high damage in her Heavy Sword form.
Her high mobility and sustain allow her to dodge and absorb Mulan's combo, chunking her health in return.

passive.name: Passive Skill: Great Wall Guardian
passive.description:
While her dual swords are drawn, Mulan gains 40 Movement Speed, and her Basic Attacks and skills place 1 stack of Balance on enemy heroes every second for 5s. At 5 stacks, the marks detonate, dealing 225 (140% physical attack) physical damage to enemies while silencing them and slowing them immensely for 1s.
While her heavy sword is drawn, her Attack Speed is reduced, but Basic Attacks deal an extra (50% physical attack) damage. She also gains crowd control immunity and 45% damage reduction while using skills.

skill1.name: Skill 1: Snaking Strike / Sundering Slash

forms.description:
Mulan dashes in the target direction. During the dash, she can dash again by using the movement wheel. Each dash deals 134 (70 + 40% physical attack) physical damage to enemies in her path.
If she hits an enemy during the dash, she can use this skill again within 5s.

Mulan charges up and swings her sword in the target direction, dealing 216 (120 + 60% physical attack) −1,083 (600 + 300% physical attack) physical damage to enemies within range. Damage dealt depends on the duration of the charge.
If she charges up for 0.75s, hit enemies are slowed by 25% for 2s.
If she charges up for 1.5s or more, hit enemies are launched for 0.5s.
If she hits an enemy with this skill, she can use it again within 5s.

skill1.description:
Mulan dashes in the target direction. During the dash, she can dash again by using the movement wheel. Each dash deals 134 (70 + 40% physical attack) physical damage to enemies in her path.
If she hits an enemy during the dash, she can use this skill again within 5s.

skill2.name: Skill 2: Dagger Waltz / Blade Flurry

forms.description:
Mulan throws a sword in the target direction, dealing 400 (400 + 110% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies in its path. When the sword reaches its max range, it spins in place for 3s, dealing 160 (160 + 50% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies within range every 0.5s and reducing their Movement Speed by 25% for 1s.
She can retrieve the sword by walking next to it. Doing so reduces the skill's Cooldown by 5s.

Mulan advances in the target direction while slashing 4 times with her sword. Each slash deals 320 (320 + 85% extra physical attack) physical damage and knocks back enemies within range while reducing their Movement Speed by 25% for 2s.

skill2.description:
Mulan throws a sword in the target direction, dealing 400 (400 + 110% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies in its path. When the sword reaches its max range, it spins in place for 3s, dealing 160 (160 + 50% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies within range every 0.5s and reducing their Movement Speed by 25% for 1s.
She can retrieve the sword by walking next to it. Doing so reduces the skill's Cooldown by 5s.

skill3.name: Skill 3: Blooming Blade

forms.description:
Mulan draws her heavy sword, gaining 45% damage reduction while doing so and dealing 377 (200 + 110% physical attack) physical damage to nearby enemies. She also gains 60 physical attack for 5s.
She gains access to her heavy sword skills while her heavy sword is drawn.

Mulan draws her dual swords and makes a sweeping slash, dealing 377 (200 + 110% physical attack) physical damage to nearby enemies and gaining 60% Attack Speed for 5s.
She gains 40 Movement Speed and can use her dual sword skills while her dual swords are drawn.

skill3.description:
Mulan draws her heavy sword, gaining 45% damage reduction while doing so and dealing 377 (200 + 110% physical attack) physical damage to nearby enemies. She also gains 60 physical attack for 5s.
She gains access to her heavy sword skills while her heavy sword is drawn.

strategy.earlyGame: Mulan starts in the clash lane, and the early game belongs to her dual blades. That stance grants 40 Movement Speed and lets her basic attacks and skills place one stack of Balance per second, so build your laning around short trades that carry a target to the 5-stack detonation. The thrown sword is dual-blade Skill 2, and walking next to it to retrieve the sword cuts 5 seconds off that same skill's cooldown — which is exactly why you throw it toward your own escape route rather than behind the enemy. Until level 4 unlocks the greatsword, don't force kills; spend the time drilling mark management and sword pickups into muscle memory.
strategy.midGame: Level 4 is when Mulan actually starts playing. The core loop: stack five marks in dual-blade stance to detonate them, swap to the greatsword with Skill 3, and follow with a charged slash. The swap also raises her physical attack for 5 seconds, so land the swing inside that window. Mind the crowd control, though — the hit slows but does not root, and the silence itself only locks skills for 1 second. The target keeps walking. A full charge needs 1.5 seconds or more, which the silence cannot cover. The practical version is the 0.75-second charge: 25% slow for 2 seconds, pinning them down again. Greatsword skills grant unstoppable (CC immunity) and 45% damage reduction while they are active, so swing through the retaliation. Charge 1.5 seconds or more and the hit launches them for 0.5s — enough to finish any laner already below half HP.
strategy.lateGame: Late game, split your time between pushing side lanes and playing silence-bot in teamfights. The silence lasts 1 second. That sounds short, but dropped on a mage the instant they start a cast, it erases that spell outright — treat it as a tool for denying one action, not for muting someone through a fight. At Overlord contests, use dual-blade mobility to flank, then time the greatsword swap onto a marked target the moment fighting starts. Walk in through the front and you'll get surrounded and accomplish nothing; the entry angle is everything.
strategy.teamfight: Your job in a teamfight is to silence the one action the enemy most wants to take. Orbit the edge in dual-blade stance spreading marks, and save the fifth stack for the target you need muted. Watching an enemy mage start their cast animation and slamming the silence on top of it feels fantastic — their entire damage output just evaporates. Then swap to the greatsword and lean on the unstoppable frames to land a charged slash in the scrum. Even when you don't kill, the damage reduction gets you out alive more often than it should.

combos.title: Stacking Balance to Five
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (Light Sword Form: dash, recastable within 5s on hit) → Basic Attack → Skill 2 (Light Sword Form: sword throw, 25% slow at Lvl 1) → Basic Attack → Skill 1 (recast dash) → 5 Balance stacks detonate (1s silence + heavy slow)
combos.description: Balance goes on once per second at most, from Basic Attacks and skills alike, and each stack lasts 5s. Five separate touches are needed before it detonates, and a gap longer than a second starts dropping the earliest stack. Walking next to the thrown sword refunds 5s of Skill 2's cooldown, so throw it toward your own escape route.

combos.title: Heavy Charge After the Silence
combos.sequence: 5 Balance stacks detonate (1s silence + heavy slow) → Skill 3 (Light Sword Form: draw the heavy sword, 45% damage reduction, +60 physical attack at Lvl 1) → Skill 1 (Heavy Sword Form: charge 1.5s or more to launch for 0.5s) → Skill 2 (Heavy Sword Form: 4 slashes, knockback + 25% slow for 2s at Lvl 1)
combos.description: The silence runs out after one second. What holds the target through the charge is the heavy slow left behind it, plus the crowd control immunity on heavy sword skills. Charge 1.5s or longer for the launch; if they look like escaping, release at 0.75s and settle for the 25% slow.

strengths: The 5-stack silence plus slow creates windows where enemies simply can't answer
Unstoppable and damage reduction on greatsword skills shrug off CC-heavy comps
No mana — she trades on cooldowns alone, forever
Swaps between dual-blade mobility and greatsword burst to fit the moment
weaknesses: Charged greatsword swings whiff entirely if the enemy makes distance
Gap-closing leans on the dual-blade Skill 1 dash, so she gets kited hard
Picking the wrong stance leaves her with neither damage nor speed
No built-in sustain — holding lane after getting chunked is miserable

playstyle.style: A two-form fighter: agile dual blades that stack a silencing seal, and a heavy greatsword whose charged swings end the fight. Each form demands its own way of fighting.
playstyle.suited: Players who want to play two weapons in one match — and love the weight of a fully charged, fully landed heavy blow.

synergy.reason: Dun's Unruly Blade stuns the first enemy it hits for 1s and pulls him to the front, and the second cast of Wind Slash launches for another 1s. Against enemies pinned like that, Erin's enhanced Basic Attacks and laurel leaves land from the back line without her stepping up.

Xiang Yu's Righteous Fervor charges in, knocking enemies back and launching them for 0.75s, which peels divers off Erin. No Retreat then cuts enemy damage output by 30% for 3.5s, so the shots that do reach her hurt far less.

counters.reason: Lam's Death From Below slows everyone in the dagger's path, then dashes and drags them to where it landed. Erin's Skill 2 only makes her immune to slows, not to displacement, so she is hauled into his range before her speed boost can open the gap.

Mai Shiranui can throw KACHOUSEN every 3s, slowing hard on hit and cutting 50 magical defense for 3s. Skill 1's dash launches Erin for 0.75s, and her ultimate knocks her back while reducing physical attack by 20% for 2.5s, breaking Erin's rhythm before it builds.

passive.description:
Erin's Basic Attacks deal 166 (100% physical attack + 20% magical attack) physical damage and grant Energy. When Energy is at max, Erin speeds up, gains 1 stack of Laurel, and enhances her next Basic Attack.
Speed Up: Erin spends Energy to fly, increasing 30 Movement Speed per 100 magical attack, up to a maximum increase of 450 Movement Speed.
Enhanced Basic Attack: Erin's enhanced Basic Attack deals 269 (70 + 120% physical attack + 30% magical attack) physical damage to enemies in its path.
Her Pierce and Lifesteal stats are linked. Physical Pierce/Lifesteal and Magical Pierce/Lifesteal each use the higher of the two stats.
passive.name: Passive Skill: Elf Dance

skill1.description:
Erin shoots a laurel leaf, dealing 510 (510 + 115% extra physical attack + 100% magical attack) magical damage to enemies hit and gaining a stack of Laurel. Upon hitting an enemy hero or flying to its maximum range, the leaf starts flying in a circle, and enemies that come into contact with the circle take 170 (170 + 38% extra physical attack + 33% magical attack) magical damage and are slowed by 15% for 1s.
The skill's cooldown is reduced by 0.1s for every 100 Magical Attack, for a reduction of up to 1.5s.
skill1.name: Skill 1: Dance - Leaf Greeting

skill2.description:
Blessed by the Luminescent Forest, Erin immediately recovers full Energy, gains her Passive effect (including Speed Up, 1 Laurel stack, and an enhanced Basic Attack) and obtains another stack of Laurel.
Erin also becomes immune to slow and gains 20% Attack Speed for 3s.
skill2.name: Skill 2: Twirl - Forest Whisper

skill3.description:
At max Energy, Erin gains a stack of Laurel. When the skill is activated, she gains 10% Movement Speed and continuously consumes Laurel stacks to shoot leaves. Each leaf shot deals 130 (72 + 35% physical attack + 25% magical attack) magical damage to the enemy within range with the lowest Health. Each shot also reduces the cooldown of Twirl - Forest Whisper by 0.2s.
Waltz - Laurel Bloom is only unlocked at 6 Laurels. Laurel can be stacked up to 12 times.
Every 3 leaves counts as 1 Basic Attack.
skill3.name: Skill 3: Waltz - Laurel Bloom

strategy.earlyGame: Spend the first four minutes in the farm lane doing nothing but securing last hits. Erin is built around an unusual scaling scheme — magic attack raises both her move speed and her skill rotation — so finishing that first magic item is her real first power spike. Skill 1 is your harass tool: it stacks laurel marks on hit and deploys a slowing ring. Manage energy on a rhythm of one glide per three basic attacks and you'll stay half a step faster than the opposing marksman at all times.
strategy.midGame: Around the 10-minute mark, two completed magic items plus the Ultimate unlocking at 6 marks send her sustained damage through the roof. In Tyrant fights and skirmishes, gliding half a step off an enemy skill's flight path cuts your damage taken dramatically. When you get ganked, Skill 2 is the lifeline: it refills energy, grants slow immunity, and boosts attack speed all at once, which is enough to outrun one full rotation of chase. You're fragile while it's on cooldown, so pick the moment carefully.
strategy.lateGame: Erin approaching full build is the whole point of picking her. Her penetration and lifesteal apply whichever of physical or magic is higher, so her damage goes through any defensive itemization and she rarely loses an extended DPS race. Always fight from behind your frontline. Don't overthink targeting either — hit the nearest safe enemy, and the Ultimate's leaves will chase down the lowest-HP target on their own. Her win condition is uptime, not burst: staying alive and firing is the play.
strategy.teamfight: Hold the perimeter and settle into the rhythm of basic attack, glide, basic attack. When an assassin dives you, hit Skill 2 to speed up, ignore their slows, and slide behind your frontline. The Ultimate's leaves keep flying while you retreat, so your damage never actually stops. One habit worth building: don't glide just because you're pressured. Wait until you've seen one enemy dash skill before spending energy on movement, and you'll still have some banked when it really matters.

combos.title: Six Laurels to Open Skill 3
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (Laurel 1 on hit + 15% slow ring at Lvl 1) → Basic Attacks until Energy fills (Laurel 2 + next attack enhanced) → Enhanced Basic Attack → Energy fills again (Laurel 3) → Skill 2 (full Energy refill, Laurels 4 and 5) → Energy fills once more (Laurel 6) → Skill 3 (unlocked)
combos.description: Six Laurel stacks unlock the skill: one from Skill 1, one every time Energy reaches full, two from Skill 2. Flying spends Energy, so when the stacks matter more than position, stay on the ground and keep attacking. Each leaf chases the lowest-Health enemy in range and takes 0.2s off Skill 2's cooldown.

combos.title: Peeling Off a Diver
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (slow immunity for 3s + 20% Attack Speed at Lvl 1) → Flight (spend Energy to open the gap) → Skill 1 (15% slow ring at Lvl 1) → Enhanced Basic Attack
combos.description: Skill 2 refills Energy from empty and shuts out slows for 3s. Do not burn it just to rotate — hold it as the answer to a dive. Flight speed scales at 30 Movement Speed per 100 magical attack, capped at 450.

strengths: Magic attack raises her basic-attack damage and her glide speed at once
Glides plus slow immunity give her some of the best escapes of any marksman
Skill 3's leaves hunt the lowest-HP enemy and secure cleanup on their own
No mana - she camps lane indefinitely and out-farms her opposite number
weaknesses: Low burst, so out-damaging heals and shields takes real time
Loses all mobility the instant her energy runs dry
No answer to point-and-click CC — getting caught means dying
Heavily item-dependent, with little teamfight presence before 10 minutes

playstyle.style: An elven archer cycling energy and laurel marks to keep her empowered shots flowing. When the gears mesh her damage soars; when management slips, the whole engine audibly stalls.
playstyle.suited: Players who enjoy keeping resource gears meshed — where tidiness of play converts directly into consistent damage.

synergy.reason: Can provide follow-up damage on locked-down enemies and buff Zhang Liang's survivability.
Can attach to Zhang Liang to provide shields, allowing him to safely channel his CC skills.

counters.reason: Highly capable of peeling for allies by disrupting Zhang Liang's ultimate with massive shields and CC.
Can dodge Zhang Liang's skills with high mobility, instantly closing the gap to burst him down.

passive.description: After Liang's Basic Attacks or skills deal damage to a target twice within 1.5s, he enters a state of continuous attack, during which he deals 120 (120 +70% magical attack) true damage to the target every 1.2s.
passive.name: Passive Skill: Power Word - Trance

skill1.description:
Liang summons 4 magical barriers at the target location. When touched by an enemy, barriers disappear and deal 360 (360 +75% magical attack) magical damage while stunning the target for 0.75s. After the stun wears off, the enemy is slowed by 25% for 0.5s.
If the same enemy touches multiple barriers within a short period, subsequent barriers only deal half of the damage without the stun, and the enemy's is slowed by 25% for 1.25s.
skill1.name: Skill 1: Power Word - Barrier

skill2.description:
Liang conjures a circle of attrition at the target location for 5.5s. The circle deals 110 (110 + 24% magical attack) magical damage to 1 enemy within range every 0.5s and provides vision of the area. Non-hero enemy units take 50% more damage. He gains 60 Movement Speed while inside a circle of his.
He can have at most 2 circles up at the same time. He stocks 1 charge of the skill every 12s (affected by Cooldown Reduction), for up to 3 charges.
skill2.name: Skill 2: Power Word - Fate

skill3.description:
Liang uses a Power Word to suppress an enemy hero for 2.2s and deal 100 (100 +18% magical attack) magical damage to them every 0.5s.
If he finishes using this skill without being interrupted, a magic field is summoned at the target hero's location for 0.5s. Enemies that step into the field take 240 (240 +30% magical attack) magical damage and are stunned for 0.75s.
skill3.name: Skill 3: Power Word - Control

strategy.earlyGame: Skill 2 runs Liang's early mid lane. The circle deals 50% bonus damage to non-heroes for fast waveclear, and since two can be maintained at once, parking one in a river bush doubles as vision. Once the wave is shoved, use that vision to move with your jungler, and hit level 4 as fast as possible — the 2.2-second suppression is one of the longest lockdowns in the game, and from the moment it unlocks, your mid lane carries constant kill threat.
strategy.midGame: Mid game, your biggest job is picks with your jungler — catching an isolated enemy before objectives. Suppress whoever walks up for vision before the Tyrant or Shadow Tyrant and the objective is yours without a fight. One caution: Liang is rooted for the entire suppression. Only cast it within reach of your team's damage, or you'll land a perfect lockdown and then get left behind alone. Also, walk through your own Skill 2 circles when rotating — the move speed boost is a small habit with real mileage.
strategy.lateGame: Late game, who you suppress IS the match. The default target is the enemy's main carry, but the Ultimate is also a first-class counter to assassins diving your backline: read the landing spot of their dash, wait, and suppress on contact — they melt without taking a single action. Use Skill 1's four barriers to zone retreat paths and chokepoints, and let the Passive's true damage grind down even the frontline tanks.
strategy.teamfight: Stay behind your frontline at the very edge of Ultimate range. Open by dropping Skill 1 across the enemy's approach to stagger their entry with the multi-stuns, and lay Skill 2 at your feet to claim ground for your team. Don't rush the Ultimate — hold it for the most dangerous enemy, like the assassin the instant he commits. A stun zone lingers at the target's feet when suppression ends, so tell your team in advance to burst during that 0.75-second window; the kill rate difference is night and day.

combos.title: Suppression Pick
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (circle for vision, +60 Movement Speed while you stand in it) → Skill 3 (2.2s suppression on one enemy hero) → Skill 1 (4 barriers at the target's feet) → Basic Attack (chain within 1.5s to keep the Passive's true damage running)
combos.description: Those 2.2 seconds are exactly the window your team needs to arrive. Only a cast you finish leaves the magic field under the target for 0.5s, stunning anyone who steps in for 0.75s. Get interrupted and the field never appears, so cast from where nothing can reach you.

combos.title: Barrier Answer to a Dive
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (4 barriers across your escape route) → Skill 2 (circle at your own feet) → Basic Attack (retreat with +60 Movement Speed inside the circle)
combos.description: A barrier stuns for 0.75s on contact and leaves a 0.5s slow once the stun ends. While the chase stumbles, step onto your own circle and pull away with the 60 Movement Speed. The same enemy will not be stunned twice in a row, so treat the later barriers as slows.

strengths: The 2.2-second suppression reliably removes one enemy ace from any fight
Passive true damage keeps hurting even fully stacked tanks
Two circles deliver vision control and fast waveclear for mid priority
Barrier multi-stuns excel at zoning chokes and holding sieges
weaknesses: Rooted and defenseless during the Ultimate, which is hard to place in a scrum
No mobility skill, leaving him soft to ganks and assassin flanks
Barrier stuns don't re-apply to the same target, so lockdown can't be chained
Low burst — closing out kills alone is a struggle

playstyle.style: The definitive single-target suppressor: his ultimate holds one enemy helpless for over two seconds. Barriers and repeating true damage soften targets; the suppression converts them.
playstyle.suited: Players who answer the team's plea of 'someone stop that hero' — and understand how much one guaranteed shutdown is worth.

synergy.reason: Provides reliable lockdown, creating a situation where Mai can safely unleash her full combo.
Provides mobility and healing, making it much easier for Mai to execute her hit-and-run playstyle.

counters.reason: Can disrupt Mai's combos with unavoidable hard CC, completely neutralizing her high mobility.
Can prevent Mai's engage with long-range stuns and shields, tanking her burst damage.

passive.description:
Every 5s, Mai Shiranui enhances her next Basic Attack. The enhanced Basic Attack deals 100 (100 + 100% magical attack) magical damage to the target and knocks them back. Also restores 10 Energy to Mai Shiranui.
When Mai Shiranui is performing an enhanced Basic Attack or casting a skill, moving the movement wheel causes her to dash again and gain 50% Movement Speed that diminishes over 0.5s.
passive.name: Passive Skill: HISSATSU SHINOBI-BACHI

skill1.description:
Mai Shiranui dashes in the target direction. At the end of the dash, she launches a flying kick, dealing 600 (600 + 80% magical attack) magical damage to enemies within range and launching them for 0.75s.
She recovers 25 Energy if an enemy is hit.
skill1.name: Skill 1: HISHOU RYUUENJIN

skill2.description: Mai Shiranui throws her fan in the target direction, dealing 470 (470 + 90% magical attack) magical damage to the first enemy hit, slowing them immensely for 0.5s, and reducing their magical defense by 50 for 3s. She recovers 10 Energy if she hits an enemy. After landing a hit, the fan deals an equal amount of magical damage (halved against heroes) to the closest unit behind the target.
skill2.name: Skill 2: KACHOUSEN

skill3.description:
Mai Shiranui dashes in the target direction, dealing 800 (800 + 110% magical attack) magical damage to all enemies in her path and knocking them back while reducing their physical attack by 20% for 2.5s.
She recovers 25 Energy for each enemy hit.
skill3.name: Skill 3: CHOU HISSATSU SHINOBI-BACHI

strategy.earlyGame: Early mid lane is not the time to force anything. Mai's energy only refunds meaningfully on skill hits, so whiffing repeatedly leaves you unable to act at all. Clear waves with Skill 2's fan — it pierces to the unit behind the first target it hits, so lining it through a minion onto the enemy laner clears and harasses in one throw. Level 4 unlocks the Ultimate, and with rolls woven in, she finally becomes the ambush hero she's meant to be.
strategy.midGame: From level 4 on, shove mid quickly and roam the side lanes. Every engage starts with Skill 2 — the 50-point magic defense shred lasts 3 seconds, and the same combo does visibly different damage depending on whether it led. Sliding the stick during an empowered basic or skill triggers a roll, and the small habits pay huge dividends: roll to the wall side to cut off the escape, or roll out of the flight path of their answer skill. One extra input, dramatically better survival.
strategy.lateGame: Late game is entirely about timing your entry, not the size of the hit. One CC kills you, so hover the perimeter of frontal fights flashing roll threats, and commit Skill 2 into Skill 1 the instant the enemy's point-and-click CC or lockdown gets spent elsewhere. The Ultimate's knockback and 20% physical attack shred double as insurance — landing it on the enemy marksman buys defense and cuts their damage at once. Having the discipline to leave based on your energy bar is what actually decides your win rate.
strategy.teamfight: The ideal teamfight entry is three seconds late, after the scrum has started. Shred a target's magic defense with Skill 2, stack Skill 1's knock-up on top, push with the empowered basic, and finish with the Ultimate. When the full string lands, squishy targets simply disappear — but decide your roll-out path BEFORE you dive. The same input handles both aggressive and escaping rolls on this hero, so the escape route you hold in your head is your actual lifeline.

combos.title: Shred the Magical Defense First
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (magical defense −50 for 3s at Lvl 1 + 0.5s heavy slow) → Skill 1 (dash + 0.75s launch) → Enhanced Basic Attack (knockback) → Skill 3 (dash, knockback + physical attack −20% for 2.5s at Lvl 1)
combos.description: Whether the fan debuff lands first decides how much the same four inputs actually remove. The enhanced Basic Attack knocks the target back, so aim Skill 3 along the direction they were pushed. The three skills cost 205 Energy in total while hits refund only 70, so start the sequence on a full gauge.

combos.title: Fan Poke Through the Wave
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (thrown through a minion, same damage to the enemy behind) → Roll (slide the left stick during the cast, 50% Movement Speed for 0.5s) → Enhanced Basic Attack (knockback + 10 Energy)
combos.description: The fan carries the same magical damage to the closest unit standing behind whatever it hits first. Heroes take half of it, but this is one of the few ways to reach someone tucked behind the wave. Each throw costs 35 Energy and refunds 10 on a hit, so stop while 70 is still left for Skill 1.

strengths: Skill 2's 50-point magic defense shred multiplies her entire combo
Two dashes plus rolls deliver elite in-and-out mobility
Knock-up, knockback, and an attack shred give her real self-defense
Energy loops indefinitely as long as skills keep connecting
weaknesses: Whiffed skills drain energy and create dead time where she can't act
Zero defensive tools — a single CC ends her
Misrolled inputs send her the wrong way, straight into danger
High skill floor: her damage tracks directly with practice

playstyle.style: A close-range burst mage who weaves empowered attacks and dashes while managing an energy bar. The hands are busy, but a clean sequence simply deletes the target.
playstyle.suited: Players who want their combos to flow like choreography, and enjoy optimizing inside the constraint of an energy resource.

synergy.reason: Dolia can reset his powerful AoE ultimate, allowing them to completely dominate teamfights.
Resetting her ultimate allows for extremely powerful chain-kill potential.

counters.reason: His strong lockdown abilities can disrupt her positioning, bursting her down before she has a chance to reset an ally's ultimate.
Can disrupt Dolia's supportive actions with continuous CC, severely reducing her impact in teamfights.

passive.description:
Dolia takes the form of a mermaid while in water, reducing slow effects by 50% and recovering 60 (60 + 1% extra Health) Health and 5 Mana every second. Her Basic Attacks become splashes of water that deal area damage.
Her Recovery skill becomes Mermaid's Gift, which can be used to form a covenant with a selected teammate. This teammate becomes the priority target for Celestial Melody.
passive.name: Passive Skill: Mermaid's Gift

skill1.description:
Dolia sings, unleashing 4 soundwaves that spread out around her. The first 3 deal 135 (135 + 20% magical attack) magical damage and inflict a 7.5% slow.
The 4th soundwave deals 270 (270 + 40% magical attack) magical damage and inflicts a 30% slow for 1s. This soundwave triggers echoes when hitting enemies, dealing 150 (150 + 24% magical attack) magical damage. While in water, it stirs up a wave that knocks back nearby enemies and stuns enemies next to her.
Echoes triggered by non-hero units have a shorter range and only deal 50% damage.
skill1.name: Skill 1: Ode

skill2.description:
Dolia leaps forward and transforms into a mermaid. If she lands on solid ground, she creates a pool of water and restores 320 (320 + 40% magical attack) Health to her and her nearby teammates. While in the pool, teammates recover Health and Mana at the same rate as Dolia's.
Cooldown is reduced by 25% if used while in water.
The pool disappears if she leaves it for 4s.
skill2.name: Skill 2: Wavemaker

skill3.description:
Dolia channels for a short time, resetting the cooldown of a skill for a teammate within range. The skill that gets reset is the one with the longest remaining cooldown. In return, Dolia takes on a Cooldown of 10 (+120% of the current skill Cooldown) seconds herself.
If the teammate does not use the reset skill, the cooldown of Celestial Melody is reduced by 20%. If the teammate uses the reset skill within 5s, it does not consume Energy, and any earnings from defeating enemies with that skill are shared evenly with Dolia.
This skill prioritizes the teammate with whom she has formed a covenant. If no teammates are nearby, she resets one of her own skills. If the reset fails, the cooldown of Celestial Melody is significantly reduced.
skill3.name: Skill 3: Celestial Melody

strategy.earlyGame: Pick your contract partner at spawn — usually the marksman or jungler who'll be your late-game gun. Shadow that partner early and actively force skirmishes around the river, because Dolia in water is a different hero: Mermaid mode passively regenerates her HP and MP, and Skill 1 upgrades into an AoE knockback plus stun. The 4-minute Tyrant fight happens in the river, and it's her first showcase — simply standing in the water before the enemy arrives is already an advantage.
strategy.midGame: Mid game is for drilling the Ultimate's timing into muscle memory. It resets the skill with the longest remaining cooldown in range, so casting it right after an ally fires their ultimate returns that ultimate almost every time. Shadow Tyrant and Overlord contests are her home turf — river terrain stacked with Skill 2's water field generation. Even on dry land, Skill 2's landing zone hands sustained healing to every ally standing in it.
strategy.lateGame: Her late-game value collapses into one sentence: your ace's ultimate fires twice. Partner's ultimate lands, Ultimate immediately after — whether that single input happens determines the entire teamfight's math. From the enemy's perspective, the big skill they just played around is coming again, and there's essentially no answer. If you die, the reset supply stops, so position behind even your contract partner. Not dying is itself your biggest contribution — accept that fully.
strategy.teamfight: Step one of fight prep: lay a water field at your feet with Skill 2 before it starts. On the water, you sustain while fighting, and diving assassins get bounced by Skill 1's knockback and stun. From there, just sync the Ultimate with your team's big cooldowns. It isn't flashy, but when your allies out-sustain everything on the field and every enemy engage gets bounced back, the fight turns more one-sided than any scoreboard suggests. Even retreats favor you — moving through water halves slows on her.

combos.title: Bring Your Own Water
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (leap forward, create a pool on landing + heal allies) → Skill 1 (cast inside the water for knockback + stun) → Basic Attack (mermaid splash, area damage)
combos.description: Away from the river, Skill 2 carries the water with you and turns Skill 1 into hard crowd control. Prying a diver off your carry is the most reliable thing Dolia does. Standing in the pool restores Health and Mana every second, but it vanishes 4s after she leaves it, so place it where you intend to stay.

combos.title: A Second Cast for Your Ally
combos.sequence: Ally lands a major skill → Skill 3 (reset the skill with the longest remaining cooldown) → Skill 2 (lay a pool for sustain)
combos.description: The reset always takes the longest remaining cooldown on one ally in range. Time it right after the big cast and it cannot pick the wrong skill. Covenant partners get priority, so the ally you choose at spawn is the one this play serves.

strengths: The Ultimate's instant reset of allied ultimates is unique support power
In water she gains healing, hard CC, and AoE attacks all at once
Skill 2 carries a water field anywhere, so she works far beyond the river
The contract system stacks resources on your ace and sharpens the win condition
weaknesses: The Ultimate's cooldown depends on ally skills, so it rotates poorly alone
Out of water, Skill 1 loses its CC and her self-defense collapses
Almost no personal damage — she creates nothing by herself
Her value craters when teammates don't understand the reset mechanic

playstyle.style: A mermaid support who lays down pools of water where allies standing in them recover Health and Mana. Skill 3 is unique in the game: it instantly refreshes one ally's skill — she hands out time itself.
playstyle.suited: Players who want to produce someone else's highlight play, making the split-second call of whose cooldown matters most.

synergy.reason: Provides massive AoE CC, creating a safe environment for Nakoruru to unleash her burst damage.
Can group enemies while providing stealth and armor shred, perfectly setting up Nakoruru's engages.

counters.reason: Can neutralize Nakoruru's dive and burst damage with massive shields and knockbacks.
Can easily burst Nakoruru down in close quarters using his i-frames and overwhelming damage.

passive.description: When Nakoruru hits an enemy with a skill, her next Basic Attack is enhanced, for up to 3 stacks. Her next Basic Attack summons Mamahaha, who deals damage to nearby enemies based on the number of stacks, with each stack dealing 120 (120 + 37% extra physical attack) physical damage.
passive.name: Passive Skill: DANCING SWORD ARTS

skill1.description:
Nakoruru summons Mamahaha to attack the enemy, dealing 380 (380 + 120% extra physical attack) physical damage and marking them with an Eagle Eye Mark.
Further damage dealt by her will activate the marks, dealing physical damage equal to 6% of the target's Health (max damage to monsters from the mark capped at 300).
Every 40 additional Physical Attack increases max Health by 1%. Activating the mark will reduce the cooldown of AMUBE YATORO by 2.5s and recover 35 Mana.
skill1.name: Skill 1: AMUBE YATORO

skill2.description:
Nakoruru dashes forward, dealing 400 (400 + 130% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies in her path. For every enemy hero hit, she recovers 400 (400 + 5% extra Health) Health.
When this skill hits a monster, it deals 50% more damage. Hitting non-hero units restores 50% of the Health restored when hitting heroes.
skill2.name: Skill 2: RERA MUTSUBE

skill3.description:
Nakoruru summons Mamahaha, gaining 50% Movement Speed for 6s which diminishes over time. She can ignore terrain once while flying.
Using this skill again causes her to charge toward the target area, dealing 600 (600 + 190% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies within range. Enemies hit by her are slowed by 25% and deal 30% less damage for 3s.
Passive: Nakoruru summons Mamahaha to fly with her after staying out of combat for 4s, increasing her Movement Speed by 10%. She loses the Movement Speed increase upon re-entering combat.
skill3.name: Skill 3: KAMUI MUTSUBE

strategy.earlyGame: Nakoruru lives in the jungle. Skill 2 deals 50% bonus damage to monsters and heals on hit, giving her both clear speed and sustain through camps. Take both buffs and head straight to level 4 — the moment the Ultimate's 50% speed boost and terrain hop unlock, the quality of her ganks changes completely. The early trap is mana: detonating Skill 1's mark with any other damage refunds 35 MP, so build the habit of always following up a mark instead of leaving it to expire.
strategy.midGame: Mid game, wall-hop ganks from outside vision are your main weapon. Fly in through an unwarded route, mark with Skill 1, and detonate with the charge — with the max HP percent damage included, that string takes most targets to half or lower. At Tyrant and Shadow Tyrant contests, the standard play is landing the Ultimate's charge on the enemy jungler: their damage output drops 30% for 3 seconds, which tilts the entire objective burn in your favor on paper.
strategy.lateGame: The mark's max HP percent damage keeps her honest against tanks even late. But she has no exit tool after committing, so opening a fight from the front is off the table. Wait in side bushes and hunt chunked or isolated enemies instead. Her Ultimate's flight passive — activating after 4 seconds out of combat — quietly wins the late game's map movement: reset in a bush after each fight and you'll reach the next one before anybody else.
strategy.teamfight: Enter from the flank or the back. Your first job isn't damage — it's landing the Ultimate's charge on the enemy's main damage dealer to shred their output by 30%. Put that debuff on their marksman and your frontline's lifespan visibly stretches. From there, loop Skill 1 marks into detonations while weaving empowered basics onto chunked targets. Each detonation refunds 2.5 seconds of Skill 1's cooldown, so as long as you keep connecting, the pressure never stops.

combos.title: Wall Hop into a Detonation
combos.sequence: Skill 3 (summon Mamahaha: +50% Movement Speed, cross terrain once) → Skill 1 (Eagle Eye Mark) → Skill 3 recast (charge in and detonate the mark) → Skill 2 (dash + heal per enemy hero hit) → Enhanced Basic Attack
combos.description: The mark only fires when other damage reaches the target, taking 6% of their max Health. Detonating refunds 2.5s of Skill 1's cooldown and 35 Mana, so the pressure never stops. Anyone caught by the charge deals 30% less damage for 3s.

combos.title: Jungle Route Without Mana Trouble
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (+50% damage to monsters, heals on hit) → Skill 1 (mark) → Enhanced Basic Attack (detonate)
combos.description: Skill 2 hits monsters for 50% more and still heals, at half the amount heroes give you. Mark damage on monsters caps at 300, but the 2.5s cooldown refund and 35 Mana come back all the same. Hold this order and you move camp to camp without running dry.

strengths: Out-of-vision ganks powered by the 50% speed boost and terrain hopping
The mark's max HP percent damage stays relevant against tanks
The charge debuff cuts an enemy ace's damage output by 30%
Skill 2's healing and monster bonus keep clears fast and healthy
weaknesses: An all-in kit with no escape when the dive goes wrong
MP-hungry — missing mark detonations leads to fast burnout
No answer to hard CC; getting caught means dying on the spot
The speed boost decays over time, so prepared enemies blunt the ambush

playstyle.style: A straightforward, hard-hitting assassin who fights alongside her hawk. Land a skill, follow with an empowered attack, repeat — and her dash heals, giving her more staying power than she looks.
playstyle.suited: Players who want to learn the assassin role without a very-hard kit. Simple sequence, satisfying damage.

synergy.reason: Absorbs enemy CC on the frontline, creating a safe environment for Ukyo to channel his ultimate.
Can peel for Ukyo with shields and heavy CC, creating openings for him to secure kills.

counters.reason: His high durability and CC like silences can completely shut down Ukyo's skill combos.
Can dodge Ukyo's attacks with overwhelming mobility while consistently dealing damage.

passive.skill_name: Passive Skill: CONCEALED SABRE HAZY BLADE
passive.description:
Ukyo Tachibana's next Basic Attack is enhanced to a quick-draw slash that has longer range, dealing 40 (40 + 35% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies and slowing them by 15−30% (scales with hero level) for 2s. Enemies on the edge of the attack take 80 (80 + 70% extra physical attack) extra physical damage. Damage is halved against non-hero units. He recovers 125 (125 + 2% extra Health) Health.
The quick-draw slash has a cooldown of 4−5s (scales with hero level). Cooldown is shortened by 0.5s upon dealing skill damage.
passive.name: Passive Skill: CONCEALED SABRE HAZY BLADE

skill1.description:
Ukyo Tachibana leaps backward and slashes enemies in his path, dealing 330 (330 + 150% extra physical attack) physical damage and activating the skill's second phase. If no enemy units are hit, the second phase will be activated after 2s.
If he returns near the start point of phase 1 after using phase 2, he enhances the second phase to slash enemies in a larger range, and his Ultimate's Cooldown is reduced by 1s for every enemy hero hit (halved for non-hero units). For every 2% Health lost by the target, this skill's damage is increased by 1%.
skill1.name: Skill 1: CONCEALED SABRE SWALLOW SWIPE

skill2.description:
Ukyo Tachibana slashes in the target direction, dealing 580 (580 + 190% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies within range.
Enemies at the far end of the area are stunned for 0.75s.
skill2.name: Skill 2: CONCEALED SABRE HEAVENLY HACK

skill3.description:
Ukyo Tachibana quickly slashes 4 times in the target direction, with each slash dealing 210 (210 + 65% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies within range. If an enemy hero is hit, each slash restores 300 (300 + 4.5% extra Health) Health to him.
The healing is halved if only non-hero units are hit.
skill3.name: Skill 3: CONCEALED SABRE SNOWFALL SLASH

strategy.earlyGame: Ukyo is primarily a jungler, though his dueling power makes clash lane workable. Clear camps around the Ultimate's four slashes and Skill 1, weaving the Passive's iai slash into every camp — skill damage refunds 0.5 seconds of its cooldown per hit, so clean rotations alone speed up your route. What matters before level 4 is internalizing tip range: both the iai slash and Skill 2 only pay their bonuses when they land at the very edge of their reach.
strategy.midGame: Around 10 minutes, with two physical items done, Ukyo wins almost any small-scale fight he takes. The ideal engage starts with Skill 2's tip stun — pour the Ultimate's four slashes into the 0.75-second lock, and the healing per enemy hero hit lets you out-sustain the brawl. He has genuine 1v2 potential, but he also folds instantly to CC, so while enemy lockdown is still up, measure the fight from one step back.
strategy.lateGame: Late game, his bait game on side lanes shines. Shove the wave; if one enemy comes, cook them at tip range — if two come, double-jump out with Skill 1. Repeat, and you're feeding your team a permanent numbers advantage. Never enter teamfights through the front: the CC-saturated middle is a death zone for Ukyo. Flank, wait for the formation to crack, and enter on a chunked target with the tip stun.
strategy.teamfight: Ukyo's teamfight is a continuous act of measuring tip distance inside the chaos. Too close and the bonus vanishes; too far and nothing lands. Watch for the enemy's dash, jump backward with Skill 1, and land the iai slash at the tip as they arrive — when that counter connects, the aggressor is the one who gets shredded. Angle the Ultimate through as many enemy heroes as possible: the healing stacks per hit, so slashing through two or three from the side actually keeps you healthier than dueling one target point-blank.

combos.title: Far-Edge Stun into Four Slashes
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (hit at the far end of the area for a 0.75s stun) → Skill 3 (4 slashes, healing for each enemy hero hit) → Basic Attack (quick-draw slash, bonus damage at the tip)
combos.description: Where Skill 2 connects changes what it is. Only a hit at the far edge stuns for 0.75s, and that is the window all four slashes fit into. Every point of skill damage trims 0.5s off the quick-draw slash's cooldown, so the closing hit arrives in time.

combos.title: Swallow Swipe Round Trip
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (leap backward and slash) → Basic Attack (quick-draw slash at tip range) → Skill 1 phase 2 (land near the phase 1 cast point for the enhanced slash)
combos.description: Hit even one enemy unit and phase 2 is available immediately. Whiff and you wait 2s, which makes this a trade you open only when you are confident. Returning near the original cast point widens the slash and refunds 1s of Skill 3's cooldown for each enemy hero hit.

strengths: Tip hits pay out damage, healing, and a stun all at once
The Ultimate's multi-hit healing wins extended small-scale brawls
Skill 1's double jump covers both aggression and clean exits
Skill hits refund the Passive's cooldown, keeping his output constant
weaknesses: Everything depends on spacing — wrong range means no damage and no healing
Fragile at baseline; getting CC'd is his number one cause of death
Skill 1's unusual movement takes real practice to stop misplaying
Struggles to show his strengths in CC-heavy frontal teamfights

playstyle.style: A swordsman defined by spacing: his draw-cut rewards hitting at the very tip of its range, so every fight is measured in single steps. His backward leap makes enemies whiff at the moment they commit.
playstyle.suited: Players who love fighting-game footsies — turning a one-step difference in distance into a weapon.

synergy.reason: Can safely unleash high DPS from a distance by following up on Arthur's silences and knock-ups.
Can easily secure assassinations from behind while Arthur keeps the enemies silenced.

counters.reason: His true damage ignores Arthur's armor, so stacking defence does not stop him shredding through.
Her high self-sustain and mobility completely neutralize Arthur's close-quarters brawling, allowing her to easily win trades.

passive.description: Arthur invokes the Holy Vanguard to recover 100 (100 + 2.5% extra Health) Health every 2s. If his Movement Speed is impaired, he recovers an extra 100 (100 + 2.5% extra Health) Health every 2s.
passive.name: Passive Skill: Holy Vanguard

skill1.description:
Arthur gains 30% Movement Speed for 3s and enhances his next Basic Attack, where he dashes forward to deal 325 (325 + 100% extra physical attack) physical damage and silence the target for 1.25s.
The enhanced Basic Attack also marks the target enemy hero for 5s. His Basic Attacks and skills deal extra magical damage to marked enemies equal to 1% of their Health.
Allies near marked enemies gain 10% Movement Speed.
skill1.name: Skill 1: Valiant Charge

skill2.description: Arthur summons holy shields that orbit him for 5s, dealing 285 (145 +80% physical attack) physical damage every second to nearby enemies.
skill2.name: Skill 2: Whirling Strike

skill3.description:
Arthur raises Excalibur and leaps at the target enemy hero, dealing magical damage equal to 16% of their Health and leaving behind a holy seal. Enemies within range of the seal are launched for 0.5s.
The seal lasts 5s and deals 85 magical damage to enemies within range every second.
skill3.name: Skill 3: Might of Excalibur

strategy.earlyGame: Arthur takes any clash lane matchup. He has no mana, and his Passive restores 100 Health every 2 seconds. While his Movement Speed is impaired, that same amount is restored a second time every 2 seconds, so getting chunked never forces him out. The regen also carries 2.5% of his extra Health, which turns every HP item straight into staying power. From level 1, trade with Skill 1's dash plus its 1.25-second silence and follow up with the Skill 2 spin. Against melee fighters, let Skill 2 handle the wave and hit level 4 first. At the 4-minute Tyrant, rotate to the river as the designated silence-bot for enemy interrupt skills.
strategy.midGame: Once the Ultimate unlocks, his gank follow-up becomes elite. It's a point-and-click leap with a knock-up that cannot miss — when your jungler shows up, stacking Ultimate into Skill 1 chains nearly 2 seconds of lockdown, and kills usually just happen. Make roaming mid a habit after every shove. A failed Arthur roam costs almost nothing thanks to the Passive's regen and move speed, and a successful one hands you mid priority outright. It's simply good investment.
strategy.lateGame: Late game, you're the frontline trigger for engages. The Ultimate deals 16% of the target's HP as magic damage, so HP-stacked enemies actually take more — the jump works whether you point it at a carry or a frontliner. The prime target is the enemy mage: slam Skill 1's silence onto their cast animation and their big spell fizzles entirely, which is miserable to play against. Just confirm your team is actually following before you go in, or you're volunteering as the death vanguard.
strategy.teamfight: The teamfight plan is refreshingly simple: Ultimate the priority target, Skill 1 to silence the retaliation, keep Skill 2 spinning, keep swinging. Because the mechanics are easy, target selection is your entire contribution — default to the enemy backline, but if your side is collapsing, switch to bouncing the assassin who dove your own carries. Skill 2 keeps dealing damage while you move, so spin it on the chase and the retreat alike; it's never wasted.

combos.title: An Engage That Cannot Whiff
combos.sequence: Skill 3 (leap to the target, 16% of Health at Lvl 1, 0.5s launch inside the seal) → Skill 1 (+30% Movement Speed, next attack enhanced) → Enhanced Basic Attack (dash + 1.25s silence + 5s mark) → Skill 2 (spin) → Basic Attack
