combos.description: Skill 3 picks an enemy hero directly, so it never misses. Chain the 0.5s launch into the 1.25s silence and the target is locked out of their kit for almost the whole stretch. While the mark holds, every attack and skill adds magical damage worth 1% of their Health, which bites hardest on high-Health targets.

combos.title: Spin Before You Commit
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (start the spin first) → Skill 1 (+30% Movement Speed) → Enhanced Basic Attack (dash + 1.25s silence) → Basic Attack (the mark adds 1% of the target's Health)
combos.description: Starting the spin before the dash turns every second you stay attached into damage. Nothing comes back at you during the silence, so finish your window and step out. Afterwards the Passive returns Health every 2s, and it returns more while your Movement Speed is impaired.

strengths: No mana plus constant regen makes him impossible to shove out of lane
The point-and-click Ultimate and silence make every catch stick
16% HP damage on the Ultimate hurts even stacked frontliners
A simple kit that doubles as the best classroom for fighter macro
weaknesses: Ranged kiting can whittle him down before he ever closes the gap
No shields or immunity — his only answer to focus fire is regen
Flat damage scaling; he can't become the late-game carry
Spending Skill 1 to engage leaves him no tool to disengage

playstyle.style: The textbook fighter: passive regeneration, a silencing charge, and a percent-Health ultimate. Nothing complicated, and he does an above-average job in every phase of the game.
playstyle.suited: Players looking for their first hero — learning fundamentals while still winning, sword-and-shield classic.

synergy.reason: Can quickly follow up on Wukong's burst damage to secure the kill.
Can draw aggro and chunk enemies, making it much easier for Wukong to safely dive in and clean up.

counters.reason: Has high armor and CC, allowing him to tank Wukong's burst damage and counter-engage.
Can counter Wukong's engage with AoE damage and damage reduction, easily bursting him down in return.

passive.description:
After using a skill, Wukong enhances his next Basic Attack, where he charges at the target to deal 648 (475 + 100% physical attack) physical damage. This damage is always a critical hit.
He has a base Critical Rate of 20%, but his base Critical Damage is only 150%.
passive.name: Passive Skill: The Great Sage

skill1.description:
Wukong chants a protective spell that lets him resist the next enemy skill used on him. The spell lasts up to 1.5s. If a skill is successfully resisted, he becomes invincible for 0.2s and gains a shield that negates 859 (600 + 150% physical attack + 15% extra Health) damage for 4s.
He gains 40% Movement Speed for 1s when using this skill.
skill1.name: Skill 1: Protective Shroud

skill2.description:
Wukong dashes in the target direction. If he dashes into an enemy, he leaps into the air and gains 90% Movement Speed that diminishes over 1s. Using a Basic Attack or skill will interrupt this leap.
Monster Slayer: Dashing into monsters will deal 274 (240 + 20% physical attack) true damage to them. If the monster has less than 15% Health, it will take grievous damage. This does not affect Overlords or Tyrants.
skill2.name: Skill 2: Furious Advance

skill3.description:
Wukong rams his staff into the earth, dealing 250 (250 + 80% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies within range and launching them for 1s.
He also places 3 marks on enemies within range. When his Basic Attacks hit a marked enemy, the target loses a mark and takes an extra 270 physical damage.
skill3.name: Skill 3: Golden Cudgel

strategy.earlyGame: Wukong owns one of the fastest jungle clears in the game. Skill 2 deals true damage to monsters and outright executes any monster below 15% HP (Tyrant and Overlord excluded), so his full clear beats most junglers by a camp. The catch: his crit damage starts capped at 150%, so his early dueling is weaker than the highlight reels suggest. Farm to level 4 without greed, and keep one eye out for the enemy jungler's invade — that's the only real threat.
strategy.midGame: Everything changes around 8-10 minutes with one or two attack speed and crit items done. His post-skill empowered basics always crit, which means every point of crit damage on your items is pure scaling. Gank by entering with Skill 2's dash, then empowered basic into the Ultimate's knock-up into detonating brands with basics. Hold Skill 1 in reserve as insurance against their answer skill instead of burning it for movement — your success rate climbs immediately.
strategy.lateGame: At full build, a single empowered basic deletes backliners. His body stays soft, though, so never walk in through the front. Wait in side bushes or behind walls and strike from behind the moment enemy eyes face forward. One trick: pre-channel Skill 1 right before you dive. Catching their reaction skill is far easier that way than pressing it reactively, and a successful block's shield plus 0.2 seconds of immunity transforms your odds of walking out alive.
strategy.teamfight: Opening the teamfight is a mistake. Wukong's job is spotting the handful of seconds when the enemy backline's peel thins out. Enter with Skill 2's speed, empowered basic, Ultimate knock-up, then detonate the brands with basics while another guaranteed crit lands. Everything crits, so squishy targets die before the knock-up ends. Finish, then take Skill 2's second dash to complete the exit. Whether you chase a second kill comes down to one question: is Skill 1 still up?

combos.title: Stacking Guaranteed Crits from Behind
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (dash + 90% Movement Speed) → Enhanced Basic Attack (always crits) → Skill 3 (1s launch + 3 marks) → Enhanced Basic Attack (spends a mark for 270 extra) → Skill 1 → Enhanced Basic Attack
combos.description: Every skill cast enhances the next Basic Attack, and that hit always crits. Slotting Skill 1 in purely as filler buys one more enhanced attack. Whether two of them land inside the 1s launch is what decides if a squishy target drops.

combos.title: Block First, Then Answer
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (up to 1.5s, absorbs one enemy skill) → Block succeeds (0.2s invincibility + an 859 shield for 4s) → Skill 2 (dash) → Enhanced Basic Attack (always crits) → Skill 3 (1s launch + marks)
combos.description: The block window is 1.5s at most. Reacting to their counter-skill is usually too slow, so raise it just before you commit. A successful block hands you 0.2s of invincibility and a shield to fight through, while a whiff burns the full 12s cooldown at Lvl 1.

strengths: Post-skill empowered basics always crit, giving elite late-game burst
Skill 1 can nullify one key enemy skill and flip entire duels
The monster execute makes his jungle clear among the fastest anywhere
40% speed from Skill 1 and 90% from Skill 2 start both his engages and his exits fast
weaknesses: His damage stays modest until crit items actually come online
Whiffing the Skill 1 block exposes just how soft his defenses are
Reliant on empowered basics — attack-dodging enemies blank him
The knock-up is his only CC, so fleeing targets are hard to pin

playstyle.style: A crit assassin built around parrying: Skill 1 blocks an enemy skill, and a successful block grants invincibility and a shield that flows into his knock-up combo. The whole kit is a mind game.
playstyle.suited: Players who love reading the opponent one step ahead — and accept the risk of guessing wrong for the thrill of a perfect parry.

synergy.reason: Huang Zhong trades mobility for 200 physical and magical defense during his 15s Turret Mode, so he needs someone holding the ground in front of him. Lapulapu's Raging Sea leaves fissures for 5s that chip and slow by 30% anyone walking in on the turret.

Diaochan camps inside her lotus circle to cycle Skills 1 and 2 until the fourth floral mark detonates for true damage, which needs enemies to stay in range. Lapulapu's Skill 2 launches them for 0.75s, and his ultimate's fissures hold them there.

counters.reason: Marco Polo can blink with Roaming Gun every 5s. Lapulapu's Raging Sea has a wind-up before it lands, which is all the time Marco needs to leave the area, and his own ultimate opens with a blink so he keeps firing from outside the fissures.

Lu Bu's Basic Attacks and skills gain 35% Physical Pierce while his halberd is not enchanted, cutting straight through the 100 Physical Defense Lapulapu gets from his passive. Inside his ring of slaughter Lu Bu gains 150 of each defense, so standing and trading there favors him.

passive.description: Lapulapu gains 100 Physical and Magical Defense. When there are teammates within a range of 800, the teammate with the lowest Health also gains this bonus. When there are no teammates within range, Lapulapu gains an extra 50% Physical and Magical Defense.
passive.name: Passive Skill: Sea Beast's Favor

skill1.description:
Tap: Lapulapu slashes with his blade, dealing 498 (320 + 110% physical attack) physical damage to enemies and slowing them by 30% for 1s. This skill's cooldown is then reduced by 50%. He recovers 100 (100 + 2% extra Health) Health for each enemy hit by the slash. Effect is halved against non-hero units.
Tap and hold: Lapulapu throws his weapon in the target direction, dealing 498 (320 + 110% physical attack) physical damage to enemies hit and slowing them by 15% for 1s. After his weapon drops to the ground, it continuously deals 99 (75 + 15% physical attack) physical damage. When Lapulapu retrieves his weapon, he slashes nearby enemies and knocks them back.
When this skill hits an enemy, it reduces their physical defense by 50 for 2s.
skill1.name: Skill 1: Torrential Blade

skill2.description: Lapulapu charges in the target direction, dealing 529 (400 + 80% physical attack) physical damage to enemies along the path and launching them for 0.75s. After they land, enemies are slowed immensely for 1s.
skill2.name: Skill 2: Island's Blessing

skill3.description:
Lapulapu briefly charges up, then cleaves the ground, dealing 650 (650 + 180% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies within range, launching them for 1s, and interrupting their skill use.
The ground remains fractured for 5s, and enemies caught in the fissures take 80 (80 + 25% extra physical attack) physical damage per 0.5s, and are slowed by 30%.
skill3.name: Skill 3: Raging Sea

strategy.earlyGame: Start the game glued to your marksman in the farm lane. Lapulapu's Passive, Sea Beast's Favor, raises defenses for both himself and the lowest-HP ally nearby, so simply standing next to your carry does work — camping a bush alone wastes the buff. Once you have Skill 2, punish any enemy who steps up by dashing in for a short trade with the knock-up. Skill 1's tap slash comes back fast and heals you on every hit, so spam it freely whenever a brawl breaks out. And don't forget to rotate toward mid before the Tyrant spawns at four minutes.
strategy.midGame: From level 4 onward, Lapulapu's hidden strength is that his Ultimate interrupts enemy skill casts. One charged strike can cancel a channeled ultimate or a Recall mid-cast, so at Tyrant fights, time it on top of the enemy jungler's Punish attempt. Between roams, you can also pre-throw your weapon with Skill 1 (hold) to tag enemies with the 50 physical defense shred before your team commits. You're the one eating hits at the front of every fight, so start playing forward in earnest around the six-minute mark, once your first core defensive item is finished.
strategy.lateGame: The Shadow Tyrant fights after ten minutes are where you earn your keep. Skill 2 into Ultimate chains two knock-ups for roughly 1.75 seconds of total airtime — whether your team's damage lands inside that window decides the fight, so only engage within range of your allies. The rift lingers for five seconds, and dropping it across a narrow chokepoint in front of the Overlord pit dramatically slows any enemy approach. The Passive does boost your defenses by another 50% when you're alone, but you have no kill threat, so never chase deep. In retreats, cover the back line with the weapon throw's slow.
strategy.teamfight: Skill 2 is your signal to start the fight. Drag the knocked-up target into your Ultimate's charge and force the brawl on top of the rift — that's the ideal shape. Once the scrap starts, keep landing Skill 1's tap slash; the healing and cooldown refunds make you far harder to kill than you look. Be picky about who you launch: aim for an overextended mage or marksman, never the enemy tank. And the instant you see a healing or recall channel start, cancel it with your Ultimate's interrupt. It's unglamorous work, but it wins games.

combos.title: Double Knock-Up Lockdown
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (0.75s knock-up) → Skill 3 (1s knock-up + fissures) → Skill 1 tap (self-heal)
combos.description: Spend the 0.75 seconds they are airborne finishing the Skill 3 charge. They land, get launched again for a full second, and the fissures stay on the ground for 5s. The closing tap slash returns 100 Health per enemy hit, so you can hold the spot instead of backing out.

combos.title: Weapon Throw Shred
combos.sequence: Skill 1 hold (throw, -50 physical defense) → Retrieve the weapon (knocks nearby enemies back) → Skill 2 (dash + knock-up)
combos.description: The thrown weapon keeps dealing damage where it drops, and anyone in its path is slowed by 15% for 1s. Retrieving it slashes and knocks back everyone nearby, so picking it up doubles as a shove. The defense shred only runs 2s — time the dash to land inside that window.

strengths: Passive raises defenses for himself and the lowest-HP nearby ally at once
Ultimate interrupts enemy skill casts, shutting down channeled abilities
Skill 1's healing and cooldown refunds make him excel in extended brawls
Skill 2 into Ultimate chains a punishing double knock-up
weaknesses: Low personal damage — his lockdown is wasted without allied follow-up
Ultimate needs a charge-up and often misses high-mobility targets
Skill 2 is his only dash, leaving no escape after he commits
No answer to long-range poke and gets chipped down for free

playstyle.style: A walking aura: he armors himself and whichever ally is lowest, automatically. His sweeping ultimate interrupts channels — a breakwater built to crush the enemy's biggest cast.
playstyle.suited: Players drawn to making teammates tougher just by existing, saving games with one perfectly timed interrupt.

synergy.reason: Provides sustained healing, allowing them to survive longer in teamfights and dish out continuous auto-attack damage.
Provides massive shields and excellent peel to protect the low-mobility Hou Yi from diving assassins.

counters.reason: Ignores terrain to directly dive the backline and easily burst down the defenseless Hou Yi.
Uses high mobility to close the gap, chaining attacks and silences to burst them down before they can react.

passive.description:
Hou Yi gains 1 stack of Chastising Shot every time he hits an enemy with his Basic Attack, for up to 3 stacks. Each stack increases his Attack Speed by 2–4% for 3s.
At max stacks, he becomes enhanced for 3s. While enhanced, his Basic Attacks shoot 3 arrows (counts as 1 Basic Attack), dealing a total of 120% of a normal Basic Attack's physical damage.
passive.name: Passive Skill: Chastising Shot

skill1.description: Hou Yi enhances his Basic Attacks to deal 224 (100 + 75% physical attack) physical damage. While the Passive's enhancement is in effect, using Skill 1 will cause the 3 arrows to deal a total of 120% of a normal Basic Attack's physical damage plus 50% damage to 2 more enemies or structures in front of him within range (without on-hit effects). This effect lasts 4s.
skill1.name: Skill 1: Arrow Volley

skill2.description:
Hou Yi orders the Sun Tower to attack the target area, gaining vision of the area.
After a short delay, he deals 480 (480 + 110% extra physical attack) magical damage to enemies within range and reduces their Movement Speed by 25–50% for 2s. Damage and slow effects are halved against enemies on the edge of the skill's range.
skill2.name: Skill 2: Afterglow

skill3.description:
Hou Yi shoots a flaming arrow in the target direction, which explodes upon hitting an enemy hero. The explosion deals 800 (800 + 120% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies within range.
The arrow stuns the first enemy hero hit for 0.75–3.5s (depending on how far it has flown), while slowing enemies in the explosion's range by 30% for 1s.
skill3.name: Skill 3: Burning Sun Arrow

strategy.earlyGame: Your first job in the farm lane is building those three Passive stacks cleanly. Chastising Shot empowers Hou Yi after three basic attacks, turning each shot into a spread of three arrows, so the laning rhythm is simple: step up and trade only while empowered, back off when it drops. With zero mobility skills, stay away from the river bushes around the four-minute Tyrant whenever you've lost track of the enemy jungler. Skill 2 grants vision at range, so fire it into bushes ahead of time — it's your cheapest insurance against ganks while you farm.
strategy.midGame: Once you hit level 4, Hou Yi joins fights he isn't even standing in. The Ultimate's stun scales up to 3.5 seconds with flight distance, and a cross-map arrow flipping a skirmish is a regular occurrence — when your teammates start posturing at mid, line one up from an off-angle. From around seven minutes, with one or two attack speed items finished, you become the primary teamfight damage source: lay Skill 2 across the enemy's escape path for the slow, and learn to hold ground behind your front line pumping triple arrows.
strategy.lateGame: At Shadow Tyrant and Overlord standoffs, the single most important question is whether your Ultimate is still in your pocket. Land it on the enemy carry from long range and the extended stun hands you a free numbers advantage; miss it, and Skill 2's slow is your only anti-dive tool left. So the iron rule: only fire once the enemy formation has settled. Empowered Skill 1 also sends 50% damage into two enemies in front of you and towers, so keep three stacks rolling and melt turrets with it during sieges. Hold your position one step behind the front line, no exceptions.
strategy.teamfight: Hou Yi's spot is the very back row, yet his damage reaches the whole battlefield. Opening the fight with your own Ultimate is perfectly fine — if it tags the mage lurking behind the enemy tank, your win condition is all but locked in. Once the brawl starts, lean on the triple arrows' natural spread and shred the front line together with everyone stacked behind it. When an assassin dives you, drop Skill 2 at your own feet, let them walk into the slow, then re-space. Save Flash as your final trump card instead of burning it at the first sign of danger.

combos.title: Long-Range Stun Follow-Up
combos.sequence: Skill 3 (up to 3.5s stun by flight distance) → Skill 2 (2s slow) → Basic Attack ×3 (into the enhanced state)
combos.description: The flaming arrow's stun scales with how far it has flown, from 0.75s up to 3.5s, so distance is what you are buying. While the target is frozen, drop Skill 2 on them — its delayed impact is otherwise easy to walk out of. Three basic attacks max the Passive, and for the next 3s each attack becomes a three-arrow volley.

combos.title: Triple Volley Siege
combos.sequence: Basic Attack ×3 (3 Passive stacks) → Skill 1 (3 arrows + 50% to 2 enemies in front) → Basic Attack (4s)
combos.description: Three stacks put Hou Yi in a 3s enhanced state, and casting Skill 1 during it fires the three arrows on activation as well. 50% of that damage also reaches two enemies in front of him or a structure, which is why the pattern serves sieges and brawls alike. Skill 1's own buff runs 4s, adding 224 (base 100 at Lvl 1) to every basic attack.

strengths: Empowered triple arrows shred multiple enemies and towers at once
Ultimate's cross-map stun picks off targets from outside the screen
Skill 2 scouts bushes safely with long-range vision
Simple mechanics make him an ideal first rapid-fire marksman
weaknesses: No mobility skills whatsoever — once caught, he can't escape alone
Damage lives in basic attacks, so attack speed debuffs cripple him
Skill 2's delayed impact makes it hard to land on its own
Missing the Ultimate leaves almost nothing to stop divers

playstyle.style: The embodiment of sustained fire: at full stacks every attack looses three arrows. If your position is right the piloting is simple — DPS as a raw, physical experience.
playstyle.suited: Players who want the power of shooting without complication — an entry point to marksmen that never stops scaling.

synergy.reason: Pulls enemies in, making it easier for Liu Bei to land his close-range shotgun burst.
Can lock enemies down with strong CC, creating openings for Liu Bei to unleash his burst damage.

counters.reason: Can completely shut down Liu Bei's engage with her heavy arsenal of CC.
Can easily dodge Liu Bei's attacks while consistently poking him down with her high mobility and range.

passive.description:
Liu Bei's shotgun holds 4 shells. The two middle shells deal 87 (50% physical attack) physical damage to the enemy, while the other two shells on either side deal 52 (30% physical attack) physical damage. Every hit on an enemy hero grants him 1 stack of Combat Instinct, giving 5–10 Physical Pierce for 6s. Combat Instinct stacks up to 12 times.
Only the 2 middle shells from each shot can crit and trigger equipment effects. Structures are not affected by extra shells.
passive.name: Passive Skill: Reinforced Shells

skill1.description: Liu Bei increases his Movement Speed by 40% for 1.5s. The next Basic Attack is a double shot, with each shell dealing 148 (110 + 22% physical attack) physical damage.
skill1.name: Skill 1: Dual Shot

skill2.description:
Liu Bei smashes into the enemy, knocking them back and dealing 300 (300 + 100% extra physical attack) physical damage before stopping.
Hitting an enemy hero reduces this skill's cooldown by 2s.
skill2.name: Skill 2: Leading the Charge

skill3.description:
Liu Bei cleanses himself of all crowd control effects and gains crowd control immunity for 3s.
He also gains 100 physical attack and a shield that negates 1,000 (1,000 + 15% extra Health) damage for 6s.
While the shield is active, 60% of the damage he deals to enemy heroes and 20% of the damage he deals to minions and monsters is added to the shield.
Shield points are capped at 150% of the initial value.
skill3.name: Skill 3: Hearts and Minds

strategy.earlyGame: Liu Bei is played jungle first. His Passive shotgun fires four pellets and all four only connect at point-blank range, so hug every buff monster while you clear — your camp speed improves visibly. Level 4 and the Ultimate unlock is your first real decision point; until then, don't force anything and just bank your second buff rotation. When you do gank, enter with Skill 2 from the enemy's escape side so the knockback shoves them toward your teammates. Every pellet that lands stacks physical defense shred, so make it a rule: fight inside their face and empty everything.
strategy.midGame: Six to eight minutes, when your core damage item finishes, is when Liu Bei runs wild. Skill 3 cleanses CC, grants three seconds of CC immunity, and converts 60% of the damage you deal to enemy heroes into shield. Press it the moment enemy CC turns toward you and the brawl becomes one-sided. At Tyrant and Overlord, keep the stack condition straight: Combat Instinct only builds when a pellet hits an enemy hero, so hammering the boss adds nothing. What the boss does feed is the shield — 20% of the damage dealt to minions and monsters comes back as shield points. Open Skill 3 to thicken the shield while you burn the objective, then turn the pellets onto whoever contests. Sequenced that way, the shred is stacked in time for the Smite duel. When you spot an isolated target, walk them down while saving Skill 2 for the chase — holding the dash in reserve is what separates good Liu Bei players from impatient ones.
strategy.lateGame: Past ten minutes, switch to entering fights second. The moment enemy CC and attention lock onto your front line, flank with Skill 2 onto their back line and delete a squishy with point-blank pellets — that's Liu Bei's signature win condition. The Ultimate's shield rebuilds as long as you keep shooting, so answer panicked CC chains with your immunity window and simply out-damage them. Once it expires, though, you're just a melee hero; don't get greedy after a kill. Secure the Shadow Tyrant buff, then close out with the numbers advantage.
strategy.teamfight: In teamfights, Liu Bei becomes the star a few seconds after the opening, not at it. Wait until the enemy dumps skills and CC on your front line, then Skill 2 onto something soft and unload — pellets, Skill 1's double shot, more pellets. If they try to stop you, cleanse instantly with your Ultimate and keep firing. The outer two pellets whiff at range, so your teamfight position is permanently inside the enemy's pocket. From their perspective, the fight is basically lost the moment lockdown stops working on you. Cycling shields in the middle of the scrum, he plays like a fighter wearing a marksman's tag.

combos.title: Shove, Then Unload
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (dash + knockback / -2s cooldown on hitting a hero) → Basic Attack (4 shells) → Skill 1 (+40% Movement Speed for 1.5s, double shot) → Basic Attack
combos.description: The dash knocks the target back and leaves Liu Bei standing where it ended. Walk back into range and keep firing — that re-approach is part of the combo, not a mistake. Every shell that hits an enemy hero adds a stack of Combat Instinct, up to 12, and his Physical Pierce climbs with it.

combos.title: Walking Through the CC
combos.sequence: (The moment enemy CC lands) Skill 3 (cleanse + 3s CC immunity) → Skill 2 → Basic Attack → Skill 1
combos.description: Skill 3 strips the crowd control already on him and blocks anything new for 3s. It also grants 100 physical attack and a 1,000 shield (both Lvl 1), so treat those three seconds as pure damage time. 60% of the damage he deals to enemy heroes flows back into the shield, which rebuilds up to 150% of its initial value.

strengths: Devastating point-blank burst when all four pellets connect
Ultimate's cleanse and 3-second immunity walk through enemy CC
Damage dealt converts into shield, so he gets tankier as he swings
Pellet hits stack armor shred, keeping damage high even into tanks
weaknesses: Damage falls off sharply at range as the outer pellets stop connecting
Skill 2 is his only dash; miss it and he can neither chase nor leave
Extremely vulnerable to CC the moment his Ultimate wears off
Only the two center pellets crit, making item efficiency awkward

playstyle.style: A shotgun brawler who walks his damage forward. His ultimate cleanses CC and grants a huge shield, letting him force the range where every pellet connects.
playstyle.suited: Players who want to dictate the range of every exchange, and commit fully to the simple rule: closer is stronger.

synergy.reason: Garo has no movement skill, and drawing her longbow costs her 20% Attack Speed, so she cannot escape on her own once someone closes in. Zhang Fei knocks the diver back with Skill 1, and the 1.25s roar of his ultimate lets him stand in front of her while invincible.

Lady Sun gains 80% Movement Speed when she rolls next to an enemy hero, so her game is about stepping forward. Zhang Fei can leap to that same spot with Skill 2 and hand her a 650 shield, and the 10% physical defense cut from Frag Grenade also carries his own physical damage.

counters.reason: Diaochan blinks with Petals in the Wind, and every petal that connects shaves 3s off its cooldown, so she slips out of Zhang Fei's knockback and gust and repositions at once. Her floral marks detonate at 4 stacks, spraying true damage while restoring 140 Health to her.

Lu Bu is crowd control immune while diving with his ultimate, so Zhang Fei's knockback cannot stop the engage, and the 1s launch on landing catches the ally he is covering. Souleater stacks 350 shield per soul, and 25% of the remaining shield converts to Health each second at 2 shield per 1 Health.

passive.name: Passive Skill: Dark Potential
passive.description: Before transforming, Zhang Fei's Basic Attacks increase Madness by 3. After transforming, using skills will shake the ground and slow nearby enemies by 25% for 2s.

skill1.name: Skill 1: Forbidden Domain / Mad Slaughter

forms.description:
Zhang Fei swings his snake spear, dealing 600 (600 + 150% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies within range and knocking back enemy heroes.
Hitting an enemy unit increases Madness by 3.
Zhang Fei smashes the ground, dealing 741 (600 + 150% extra physical attack + 4% Health) physical damage to enemies within range. Enemies in the center are launched for 0.5s.

skill1.description:
Zhang Fei swings his snake spear, dealing 600 (600 + 150% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies within range and knocking back enemy heroes.
Hitting an enemy unit increases Madness by 3.

skill2.name: Skill 2: Leaping Savior / Stampede

forms.description:

skill3.name: Skill 3: Unbridled Outburst
skill3.description:
Zhang Fei roars in the target direction for 1.25s, generating a powerful gust of wind and gaining a shield that negates damage equal to 40% of his Health for 15s. While roaring, he gains crowd control immunity and invincibility. The wind knocks enemies back and deals 600 (600 + 150% extra physical attack) physical damage, and enemies at the end of its path are stunned for 1.5s. His Movement Speed increases by 50% while he is in the wind.
Ferali Form: While he is in Ferali Form, his Basic Attacks deal an extra 220 (220 + 100% extra physical attack) damage. When Ferali Form ends, Forbidden Domain is automatically triggered.

strategy.earlyGame: The lane opens with you swinging basic attacks next to your marksman. It looks menial, but every pre-transformation swing adds 3 Madness, and how fast you fill that bar is quite literally how strong you are. Skill 2's landing shield covers multiple allies at once, and it pays 3 Madness for the cast plus 1 more for every ally it shields — so time it for the instant a teammate is about to eat damage. In trades, cut off enemy chases with Skill 1's knockback; landing it on an enemy unit is another 3 Madness. Bank a full Madness bar before the Tyrant spawns at four minutes and the transformation is ready for the first skirmish.
strategy.midGame: Whether your Ultimate is available defines mid game Zhang Fei — with it up, he's a different hero. The roar carries 1.25 seconds of invincibility and CC immunity, so its strongest use is a head-on counter to enemy engages. Enemies caught at the far edge of the storm are stunned for 1.5 seconds, which means the clean blast comes from half a step back rather than point-blank. Around Tyrant and Overlord, sit on the transformation and answer whoever moves first. While transformed, your basic attacks carry bonus damage, so you can moonlight as a damage threat too.
strategy.lateGame: In teamfights after ten minutes, Zhang Fei's reason to exist is entering the fight holding a shield worth 40% of his max HP. During Shadow Tyrant standoffs, stand one step forward so the enemy initiation lands on you, absorb it, then answer with the roar. Just manage the knock-away direction carefully — launching the enemy carry toward your team is game-winning, while launching them to safety makes you the villain instantly. Remember that Skill 1 auto-casts when the transformation ends, so you can factor that final knockback into your closing sequence.
strategy.teamfight: Zhang Fei's teamfight is a checklist. Pre-shield your team with Skill 2, answer the enemy's dive with the roar, split their formation with the storm — and only then start swinging. The 1.25 seconds of invincibility exists to make enemy ultimates whiff, so firing it early with nothing to counter is a waste. Watch for the enemy ult animation, then blow them away, and the battlefield goes quiet in an instant. While transformed, every skill you cast also slows nearby enemies, so you can even run down the stragglers yourself.

skill3.name: Skill 3: Return of the Armsmaster
skill3.description:
Chicha unleashes all five weapons, gaining a Movement Speed boost for 2s and 35% Attack Speed, and breaking the Fighting Spirit stack limit for 6s.
During this time, she commands all five weapons to attack, with each Basic Attack dealing an extra 40 (40 + 13% extra physical attack) physical damage.
While using this skill, she can use her Basic Attack while moving. Overkill Form will remain active once entered.

strategy.earlyGame: Chicha is a fighter whose brawling literally heals her. Every basic attack restores Health and cycles her to the next, longer-ranged weapon, so in the farm lane the first rule is simple: never stop swinging. Fighting Spirit stacks expire after four seconds, so keep the gaps between attacks short. The polearm and spear of Defense Form are her shortest reach, and overextending there is how you die. Step to an enemy hero only when the bow's Overkill Form comes around. Learning that rhythm is your lifeline until level 4.
strategy.midGame: From level 4, one question drives everything: can you cast Skill 3 while in Overkill Form? Cast it with the bow in hand and the form stays locked in, and she can attack while moving. Entering Overkill Form also cuts the cooldowns of Skill 1 and Skill 2 by half the instant it triggers. Once your first attack speed item finishes around six minutes, start showing up to Tyrant fights. Health comes back on every basic attack, so extended damage races rarely go against you. One quiet trick that wins real games: pre-cycle your weapon on minions until you are two or three swings from the bow before the fight starts.
strategy.lateGame: With three or four items done past the ten-minute mark, Fighting Spirit pushes her attack speed past the normal cap and her sustained trading gets hard to beat. She is also the first target in any teamfight, so open behind your front line and use Skill 3 as the counterpunch once the divers commit. At Shadow Tyrant standoffs, prioritize a position where you can keep swinging over hiding and waiting. The moment your attacks stop, Fighting Spirit drops and the healing stops with it. Never stopping is the best defense she has.
strategy.teamfight: Half of Chicha's teamfight is decided by which weapon she is holding when it starts. The ideal is the bow's Overkill Form: entering it halves the cooldowns of Skill 1 and Skill 2, and layering Skill 3's move-and-shoot on top lets her kite backward while grinding the enemy line down. Every basic attack heals her mid-brawl, so a chunk of the damage she takes can simply be punched back. When an assassin jumps her, fighting back and cycling the weapon forward often keeps her alive longer than running would. The six seconds where Fighting Spirit has no stack limit hold her entire teamfight in miniature.

It is only worth aiming at enemies with a wall behind them. The follow-up arrows add true damage equal to 10% of the Health the target has lost, and she keeps crowd control immunity and 15% damage reduction while firing.

playstyle.suited: Drill until you can name the next weapon without looking. If you can already call it out mid-fight, she pays the practice back — three heroes' worth of tools in one body.

strategy.earlyGame: Fang works in the farm lane or the jungle, and either way the game plan is the same: four mark stacks, instant detonation. In lane, hit Skill 1 for the attack speed and range boost, land four basic attacks on your opponent, and watch the trade swing hard your way. His Passive adds bonus damage against monsters, so as a jungler he burns down the four-minute Tyrant about as fast as anyone in the game. That same Passive reveals enemy heroes lurking nearby, which makes bush ambushes far easier to smell out. Whatever you do, keep Skill 2 in reserve as your escape.
strategy.midGame: From around seven minutes, with one or two damage items finished, you become an objective monster — the monster bonus and mark detonations stack up, and Tyrant and Overlord visibly melt a size faster under your shots. When a teammate catches someone, the standard play is dropping your Ultimate's tornado on their escape route to box them in. Damage inside the tornado is doubled and tornado ticks also stack marks, so layered with Skill 1, squishy targets rarely make it out. Just remember Skill 2 is your only self-defense tool; spend it with care.
strategy.lateGame: Late game Fang designs teamfights around tornado placement. Pre-place it on the tight terrain in front of Shadow Tyrant and the enemy must either eat the doubled-damage core or break formation walking around it. Past ten minutes, cut back on solo play: Skill 2's untargetable dash is excellent, but the seconds after it's spent leave you genuinely defenseless, and getting caught there kills you through any item lead. In sieges, mark detonations splash onto enemies packed under the tower, so lean on your front line and grind forward together.
strategy.teamfight: Open every teamfight with the tornado. Place it where the enemy back line will retreat — or where your front line will shove them — and let the five-plus seconds of doubled damage shrink the battlefield. From there, boost your attack speed with Skill 1 and stack marks off everything the tornado touches; a brawl with chained four-stack detonations is Fang's private playground. When assassins dive, slip through them with Skill 2, leave the burning trail's slow behind, and re-position behind your front line. The detonations are area damage — the tighter the enemy clumps, the harder you hit.

playstyle.suited: Players who shoot in four-counts — efficiency-minded types who fold their dodge into their offense.

Diaochan deals only magical and true damage, so the immunity to physical attacks Consort Yu gains from Skill 2 does nothing. Her floral marks detonate at 4 stacks for true damage and a 1s slow. Petal hits refund up to 3s of Petals in the Wind's cooldown, letting her blink back into range again and again.

strategy.earlyGame: Treat Consort Yu's early game as a waiting room until attack speed items come online. Her charged shots fire faster the more attack speed she has, so with a bare inventory the wind-up is clumsy and forced poke just bleeds HP and mana. Focus on clean last-hits, and only fight back with Skill 2 when the enemy physical marksman starts a trade — for a short window she takes no physical damage at all, turning their confident all-in into a total whiff. At the four-minute Tyrant, simply follow your team's call; you have nothing to force there yet.
strategy.midGame: From six or seven minutes, one finished attack speed item turns her into a different hero. The charge visibly speeds up, and the Ultimate's volley count grows with attack speed too, so every item purchase translates directly into damage you can feel. Against a physical lane opponent, fight face-to-face around Skill 2 and shove them off the tower. When the enemy mage shows up instead, the immunity means nothing — take your positioning a full step deeper. At objective fights, the iron rule is to hold Skill 2 until the actual engage.
strategy.lateGame: After ten minutes, decide in advance whose skill your Skill 2 is answering — plan it before the fight, not during. If the enemy carry is physical, canceling their main burst with one well-timed immunity breaks the entire teamfight math. During Shadow Tyrant standoffs, charge your shot from the very back row and commit to punishing anyone who backs off too slowly. The Ultimate returns you to your starting position after the pounce, so even a deep catch has a guaranteed ride home. Magic burst is the one thing you can't answer, though — never give the enemy mage a clean angle on you.
strategy.teamfight: Consort Yu stands in teamfights holding a few seconds that erase physical damage entirely. The highlight play is timing Skill 2 the instant the enemy's physical assassin or marksman commits, then beating them down with the empowered basic attack while their damage does nothing. With the Passive's follow-up shots and slow layered on, you can kite them to death from there. Hold the Ultimate until the enemy's plan shows itself, then use the stun to set up your team's focus fire. Charged shots root you briefly, so pick windows when enemy CC is pointed somewhere else.

Landing grants 20% Attack Speed for 4s, so the charged shot that follows arrives inside the 2s slow rather than chasing the short stun.

playstyle.suited: Players who want to win the carry-versus-carry duel, timing the immunity against the enemy's biggest swing.
