skill3.name: Skill 3: Into the Void

strategy.earlyGame: Kui roams as an aggressive support, but the early job isn't landing hooks — it's standing where a hook is possible. Fade into the mid bushes or along the river, and the moment an enemy steps forward, drag them in with Skill 2. One connected hook becomes a first-blood setup for your team, and every kill or assist permanently grows Kui's HP. The punishment for whiffing is severe, so until level 4, only pull targets who aren't hiding behind their minion wave. The four-minute Tyrant spawn is also prime time for an ambush hook on anyone rotating in.
strategy.midGame: Level 4 completes the lockdown script. Skill 2's hook marks the first enemy it hits with Into the Void, and Skill 3 stuns marked targets continuously — up to 16 devours land on someone who cannot move. Before Tyrant or Overlord, a single hook from outside vision forces the enemy to start the fight a player down. Choose the target well: the enemy marksman or mid laner. Nobody on your team celebrates a hooked tank. Keep stacking kill participation and Void Devour climbs with it; 20 stacks is 3,600 extra Health, and Kui quietly ends up as durable as a front-liner.
strategy.lateGame: Late game Kui bets entire matches on one hook. During Shadow Tyrant standoffs, lurk in a bush half a step behind your front line and wait for the enemy carry's positioning mistake — patiently, for as long as it takes. When the pull lands, chain your Ultimate and Skill 1 for lockdown and damage while your team collapses on the target. The reverse is just as true: with no mobility skill, getting caught means dying on the spot. The Passive does splash damage around you when you take a massive hit or die, so even your worst moments carry a threat — but play careful, and make the one hook count.
strategy.teamfight: The ideal teamfight starts before the teamfight: one clean pull. Yank a back-liner out of formation with Skill 2 and you open five against four. Once the brawl is live, land Skill 1 at point-blank range to spread the mark — enemies right next to Kui take 250% magical damage and are marked with Into the Void. Stack Skill 3 onto them and the mark holds them in a continuous stun through all 16 devours. Because his effects cluster around his own body, you will wade into the enemy's half of the fight, and whether you survive it depends on the Health you banked earlier. When the hook whiffs, don't linger trying to salvage it; fall back into your lines immediately.

combos.title: Hook Into Lockdown
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (Into the Void mark + pull) → Skill 3 (continuous stun on marked targets) → Skill 1 (area damage + slow)
combos.description: The chain hook marks the first enemy it hits with Into the Void and pulls them to Kui. Skill 3 only stuns targets carrying that mark, and Skill 2 is his one way to place it from range. Each devour grants a 46 (Lvl 1) shield, so being surrounded does not drop him right away.

combos.title: Marking at Point Blank
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (250% damage + Into the Void on adjacent enemies) → Skill 3 (continuous stun on marked targets)
combos.description: The Into the Void mark is not hook-exclusive: Skill 1 deals 250% magical damage to enemies standing right next to Kui and marks them there too. Skill 2 sits on a 13s cooldown at Lvl 1 against Skill 1's 5s. Right after a missed hook, this is what he falls back on.

strengths: One hook creates a numbers advantage before the fight even starts
Skill 3 keeps anyone marked with Into the Void in a continuous stun
Kills and assists permanently stack HP toward front-liner bulk
Deals damage around him even in death, so he's never a free kill
weaknesses: No mobility skill — once caught, he usually just dies
Whiffing the hook leaves him nearly useless for several seconds
His effects center on his own body, forcing risky positioning
A pull without allied follow-up is just a one-way ticket

playstyle.style: A fisherman support who hooks one enemy and serves them to his team. Every landed hook is the starting gun of a fight, and his void-gate ultimate swallows entire groups.
playstyle.suited: Players who want the crowd's roar when the hook lands — and accept the responsibility when it doesn't.

synergy.reason: A frontline tank with great sustain, maximizing the value of Yuhuan's continuous healing and damage support.
Mutual heals and movement speed buffs boost the team's overall sustain and mobility, making them highly resilient in extended fights.

counters.reason: Overwhelming mobility allows him to close the gap instantly, bursting Yuhuan down before she can heal her team.
Safely pokes with ultra-long-range snipes from well outside Yuhuan's damage and healing radius.

passive.description:
Yuhuan changes the melody to produce different skill effects.
War: Skills deal 90 (90 + 15% magical attack) extra magical damage to enemy units within a range of 800.
Peace: Skills restore 35 (35 + 6% magical attack) Health to allies, while also restoring (+ 6% extra Health) Health to herself.
passive.name: Passive Skill: Poignant Melodies

skill1.description:
Yuhuan releases up to 4 sound waves, dealing 250 (250 + 42% magical attack) magical damage to enemies and slowing them by 25% for 1s. Sound waves deal 300 (300 + 30% magical attack) extra magical damage to minions and 100% of this amount to monsters.
After using the skill, the next Basic Attack will deal 150 (150 + 20% magical attack) extra magical damage.
skill1.name: Skill 1: Tragic Beauty

skill2.description: Yuhuan plucks the strings, gaining 50% Movement Speed that diminishes over time. After 1.5s, she deals 275 (275 + 55% magical attack) magical damage to all enemies within a range of 600−800 and stuns them for 0.75s.
skill2.name: Skill 2: Mournful Tempo

skill3.description: Yuhuan rises into the air and plays a melody, becoming untargetable while airborne and removing all crowd control effects. When finished playing, she recovers 960 (800 + 120% magical attack + 5% extra Health) Health, restores 50% of this amount to allies within a range of 500, and deals 500 (500 + 75% magical attack) magical damage to enemies within range.
skill3.name: Skill 3: Unending Sorrow

skill4.description:
Yuhuan changes the melody to Melody of Peace, in which skills provide area healing.
War: Skills deal 90 (90 + 15% magical attack) extra magical damage to enemy units within a range of 800.
Peace: Skills restore 35 (35 + 6% magical attack) Health to allies, while also restoring (+ 6% extra Health) Health to herself.
skill4.name: Skill 4: Melody of Peace

strategy.earlyGame: Mid lane Yuhuan starts with learning the Passive toggle. Clear waves in the damage stance for the bonus minion damage, and flip to the healing stance the moment you take poke — that one habit alone transforms her lane sustain. Skill 1's notes home in on enemies, and deal bonus damage to minions, so the pre-level-4 gameplan is simply notes, empowered hit, repeat. Even when the enemy jungler collapses on you, Skill 2's speed boost and delayed stun turn the gank around — she can push the lane far more confidently than she looks.
strategy.midGame: From level 4, everything hinges on one decision: is the Ultimate for healing, or for dodging? While performing, Yuhuan is untargetable and cleansed of CC, so timing it against enemy burst makes their biggest cooldowns hit air. Wait until you see the enemy assassin's ult animation before you rise — wasting their entire combo never stops feeling great. At Tyrant and Overlord fights, your job is holding the line: patch up chipped teammates with the healing stance and the post-performance area heal. From around eight minutes, your second magic item brings real poke damage online too.
strategy.lateGame: After ten minutes, Yuhuan plays the unkillable back-liner. You don't have the burst to delete anyone, so during Shadow Tyrant standoffs, chip away with the homing notes and answer dives with Skill 2 first, Ultimate second. Simply having the Ultimate available is deterrence — enemy assassins hesitate to jump a target who can vanish mid-combo. When your front line runs low, stabilize them with the healing stance and the area heal, and drag the fight into the long, grinding version that favors you. The only way Yuhuan loses is panicking and stepping forward at the wrong moment.
strategy.teamfight: Your teamfight spot is half a step behind the front line. Once it starts, flip to the damage stance for the bonus area damage and keep cycling Skill 1's notes into empowered basic attacks. When a diver turns onto you, drop Skill 2's soundwave, speed away, and let the stun land 1.5 seconds later as they chase — lockdown over your shoulder. If burst stacks onto you, rise with the Ultimate: the enemy wastes their damage, then eats your area heal on the way down. Leave the kills to your teammates; your job is making the enemy's math stop working, over and over.

combos.title: Finish the Empowered Hit
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (up to 4 sound waves, 25% slow for 1s) → Empowered Basic Attack (bonus magical damage) → Skill 1
combos.description: Casting Skill 1 empowers her next Basic Attack with bonus magical damage. The slow lasts 25% for only 1s, so that hit has to land immediately rather than after a pause. Keep the War melody on and every skill cast also chips enemies within 800 range.

combos.title: Switching to Peace
combos.sequence: Skill 4 (switch to the Peace melody) → Skill 1 → Skill 2 (0.75s stun after 1.5s)
combos.description: Under the Peace melody, every skill cast restores 35 (Lvl 1) Health to allies in range, and Yuhuan is healed on top of that. The damage rotation never stops for it, so cycling skills behind a chipped frontline is the whole job. Once the team pushes back, change the melody to War and the same casts become extra damage.

combos.title: Playing Through the Burst
combos.sequence: (Timed to enemy burst) Skill 3 (untargetable + cleanses her own CC) → Skill 2 → Skill 1
combos.description: While airborne she cannot be targeted, and the crowd control already on her is removed. Used early it absorbs nothing, so the trigger is the animation of their big skill. When the performance ends she heals herself and allies in range, and enemies in range take damage.

strengths: Passive toggle covers damage and healing in a single kit
Ultimate's untargetability and cleanse make enemy burst whiff
Empowered basic attacks refund cooldowns for relentless uptime
Area healing sustains her team through long teamfights
weaknesses: Low burst damage — she rarely finishes kills alone
Skill 2's stun lags 1.5 seconds behind and isn't guaranteed
Thin self-defense against dives while the Ultimate is down
Can't carry alone; her impact depends on allied damage

playstyle.style: A musician mage who switches between an offensive and a healing stance, capped by an untargetable ultimate that both dodges the enemy's aim and restores her team.
playstyle.suited: Players who want to conduct the balance between damage and healing themselves — every stance call visible in the result.

synergy.reason: Zhang Fei's Skill 3 gust blows enemies back and stuns the ones that reach its far end for 1.5s. Chano can pre-place up to 4 traps, so the spot enemies get shoved into is often already trapped. After Zhang Fei transforms, using skills slows everything nearby by 25% for 2s.

Lapulapu's Skill 2 charges through, launching enemies for 0.75s and then slowing them immensely for 1s. An enemy stuck in place is easy for Chano to catch with his traps and wolf spirits. His passive also hands 100 Physical and Magical Defense to the lowest-Health ally within 800 range.

counters.reason: Skill 4 puts Gao Changgong into stealth 1.5s after casting and keeps him hidden for 30s, while his passive adds 15-30% Movement Speed whenever he moves toward an enemy hero. The spacing Chano takes from the brush does not stop that approach, and once Skill 2's dagger marks him, every follow-up attack stuns for 1s.

Musashi's Skill 1 knocks enemy projectiles out of the air, and Chano fights with arrows, so even the powerful shot he fires while airborne is erased mid-flight. Skill 3 locks onto a hero, dashes in and launches for 1s, and he takes 50% less damage throughout that dash.

passive.description:
While in the brush, Chano gains 10-20% increased Movement Speed and accumulates Concealment, which reaches its maximum after 1s. When leaving the brush, he consumes Concealment to perform a leap, with the distance increasing based on the amount accumulated.
Entering the brush also enhances his next Basic Attack into a double shot (counts as 1 Basic Attack), with each arrow dealing 175 (70 + 60% physical attack) physical damage. The double shot has a 4s cooldown.
He deals 25% more damage to monsters while in the brush.
passive.name: Passive Skill: Hunting

skill1.description:
Chano leaps into the air, gaining a Movement Speed boost and the ability to traverse terrain. While airborne, his Basic Attack becomes a powerful long-range arrow, dealing 475 (230 + 140% physical attack) physical damage and knocking back enemies (without applying crowd control), while also extending his air time.
Each 1% Attack Speed increases the arrow's damage by 2.
If he doesn't use the enhanced Basic Attack while airborne, he stores one with normal Attack Range for 3s upon landing.
If he uses the enhanced Basic Attack while moving the movement wheel away from the target, he dashes for a short distance in that direction.
skill1.name: Skill 1: Soaring Signal

skill2.description:
Chano throws a wolf spirit trap at the target location, exposing the enemy that triggers it and dealing 380 (380 + 90% extra physical attack) physical damage. A wolf spirit is also summoned at the trap's location to attack the enemy that triggered it.
Traps become invisible 2s after deploying. Up to 4 traps can be deployed simultaneously.
The wolf spirits inherit 25% of Chano's base stats and half of his Critical Damage, and each attack slows the target by 5-10% for 1s, for up to 5 stacks.
skill2.name: Skill 2: Lupine Trap

skill3.description:
Chano activates his Leader Stance, summoning (2 + Skill 2 charges) wolf spirits to charge in a designated direction, consuming stored charges of Skill 2 and activating all nearby traps.
He gains the Mounted Archery ability, allowing him to move while attacking and increasing his Movement Speed by 10%, Physical Attack by 50, and Attack Speed by 20% for 8s.
Each Basic Attack activates nearby targetless wolf spirits to join the attack.
skill3.name: Skill 3: Leader Stance

strategy.earlyGame: Chano defaults to the farm lane, but his Passive's 25% bonus monster damage inside bushes makes jungle a well-established alternative. Either way, one rule governs everything: touch a bush before you swing. Entering one empowers your next basic attack into a double shot, and leaving one converts stored stealth value into a jump whose distance scales with how long you lurked. In lane, weave between the river and your own bushes — land the double shot, jump away, repeat — and you'll hold an HP lead through nothing but hit-and-run. Also get in the habit of placing Skill 2 traps at the river entrances before level 4.
strategy.midGame: From six or seven minutes, with your first attack speed item done, trap management becomes the center of your job. Skill 2 holds up to four charges, and each trap is vision, damage, and a wolf-spirit attacker in one package. Seed them around Tyrant, Overlord, and the enemy jungle entrances, and gank detection and gank punishment become the same action. When someone closes in, escape skyward with Skill 1 and shove pursuers back with the powerful arrow's knockback. The recoil trick — inputting away from your target as the arrow fires to slide backward — is worth drilling in the practice room until it's muscle memory.
strategy.lateGame: Late teamfights are decided by the setup, not the fight. Lay two to four traps around the Shadow Tyrant pit, then wait in a bush with full stealth value — that's the ideal opening stance. On engage, detonate everything at once with your Ultimate, send the wolf-spirit pack charging in, and kite backward through the eight seconds of mounted archery. That rolling barrage while sliding away from their front line is Chano's whole kit in one motion. Whatever you do, avoid flat open ground: without bushes, he loses most of his mobility and turns into an ordinary marksman.
strategy.teamfight: Chano's teamfight starts from the side bushes, not the front line. Chip from the outside with stealth jumps and double shots, and when heads turn toward you, take to the air with Skill 1. Slide your landing spot with the recoil movement so nobody can pre-aim your touchdown. Save the Ultimate as a counter to the enemy's dive — the wolf pack plus its stacking slows flips the momentum in one cast. Keep steering enemies toward wherever your traps still sit. Chano's teamfight is half over the moment the battlefield has become his backyard.

combos.title: Brush In, Brush Out
combos.sequence: Enter the brush (next Basic Attack becomes a double shot) → Basic Attack → Leave the brush (leap scaled to Concealment)
combos.description: Stepping into a brush turns the next basic attack into a double shot worth 175 per arrow (base 70 at Lvl 1). The double shot runs on a 4s cooldown, and Concealment fills in 1s. If you want the longer leap, wait that one second before stepping out.

combos.title: Trap Field Detonation
combos.sequence: Skill 2 ×4 (placed early, invisible after 2s) → Skill 3 (fires every nearby trap + wolf charge) → Basic Attack (mounted archery)
combos.description: Up to four traps can sit on the map at once, and each turns invisible 2s after it lands. Skill 3 spends the stored charges to set off every nearby trap and sends (2 + charges) wolf spirits charging in. During the 8s of mounted archery, each basic attack pulls an idle wolf spirit into the fight.

combos.title: Aerial Shot and Slide
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (leap, crosses terrain) → Basic Attack in the air (475 damage + knockback) → Input away to slide
combos.description: The airborne arrow knocks enemies back, but it applies no crowd control. Push the movement wheel away from the target as you fire and Chano slides a set distance in that direction afterward. Land without firing and one empowered basic attack at normal range is stored for 3s.

strengths: Ultimate's mounted archery keeps damage flowing on the move
Bush stealth jumps and double shots enable pure hit-and-run
Four traps handle vision, zoning, and ambush punishment at once
Bonus monster damage in bushes makes jungle a genuine option
weaknesses: Lacks burst, so low targets often escape before they die
Loses most of his mobility on open ground without bushes
Damage leans on basic attacks and wolves, weak to attack speed debuffs
High mechanical demands — stealth and recoil tricks take practice

playstyle.style: A hunter who charges empowered leaps by lurking in brush, ringing the battlefield with wolf-spirit traps. His ambush angles decide who fires first — and firing first is most of the fight.
playstyle.suited: Players who treat bushes and vision as weapon components — building the game from the ambush outward.

synergy.reason: Easy to follow up on burst damage, ensuring targets are pushed past the kill threshold.
Pokes and wears down enemies in teamfights, setting up perfect kill opportunities for dives.

counters.reason: High mobility and CC allow her to kite effectively, making it extremely difficult to land skills on her.
Overwhelming mobility allows her to dominate close-quarters combat and completely outplay you.

passive.description:
Heaven-Earth Form: Yang Jian gains Resistance (up to 60-90%, scaling with Ultimate level) when his Basic Attacks and skills deal damage. Upon reaching max Resistance, he enters Heaven-Earth Form, gaining crowd control immunity. Attacking a hero in this state knocks back nearby enemies, enhances his skills and Attack Range, and grants 600 Max Health.
Heavenly Eye: Hits with his skills grant 1 stack of Energy (up to 3 stacks). When enemies move away from Yang Jian, the Heavenly Eye fires light beams, dealing 80 (+25% extra physical attack) physical damage and recovering 60 (+1% extra Health) (halved against non-hero units).
Outside Heaven-Earth Form, Yang Jian's Resistance is capped at 25%.
passive.name: Passive Skill: Mind Games

skill1.description:
Yang Jian summons the Heaven Hound to charge forward, dealing 200 (200 + 60% extra physical attack) physical damage, marking the hit enemy, and granting vision of them (lasts 5s). While the mark is active, he can use the skill again to dash to the enemy, dealing 300 (300 + 90% extra physical attack) physical damage, as well as additional physical damage equal to 15% of the target's lost Health.
If the skill misses, Heaven Hound will remain at the endpoint, searching for targets. When Yang Jian approaches, Heaven Hound returns to its master, reducing this skill's remaining cooldown by 25%-50%.
If an enemy dies while marked, this skill's cooldown is reset.
skill1.name: Skill 1: Unleash the Hound

skill2.description:
Yang Jian sweeps with his spear, dealing 350 (350 + 100% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies in range, slowing them by 15% for (2s) and stunning them for (1/2s, doubled if the target's remaining Health percentage is higher than Yang Jian's).
After hitting an enemy with this skill, Yang Jian's Basic Attacks deal an additional 125 (125 + 36% extra physical attack) true damage (lasts 5s).
skill2.name: Skill 2: Vain Disillusionment

skill3.description:
Yang Jian uses Heavenly Eye to fire 3 light beams, dealing 340 (340 + 110% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies in their path, while recovering 300 (300 + 4.5% extra Health) Health (halved for non-hero units).
If multiple light beams hit the same target, subsequent light beams deal only 30% damage and recover 50% Health.
skill3.name: Skill 3: Sight of Origin

strategy.earlyGame: Yang Jian wants to fight in the Clash Lane before level 4, not after. Skill 2's stun doubles in length when the target's HP percentage is higher than yours, so trading back after eating some damage is where he shines — never fear an even exchange. If a bush looks suspicious, send in Skill 1's War Hound first; five seconds of vision on whatever it touches exposes any ambush before it springs. Once the Ultimate arrives at level 4, its built-in healing transforms your staying power, so start forcing 1v1s and take the lane by the throat.
strategy.midGame: When the Tyrant spawns at 4:00, shove your wave before rotating. Landing Skill 1 pre-fight applies the mark and vision, and the recast dash adds missing-HP damage that finishes chases. Against enemy heroes, the Passive shifts into its empowered mode with bonus HP and resistances, which makes small skirmishes Yang Jian's home turf. Around 7-8 minutes, with one core item done, run a loop: pick a 1v1 on the side, and when two enemies collapse, use the hound's vision to back off clean. That XP gap compounds fast.
strategy.lateGame: Past 15 minutes, baiting enemies out in a side lane beats standing in the middle of every 5v5. Your 1v1 stays strong even at even items, and when you cannot secure the kill, the Ultimate's healing still lets you hold ground. Always shove a wave before Shadow Tyrant or Overlord starts — every defender the enemy sends is a body missing from the objective fight. Since your resistances stack into super armor, entering brawls two or three seconds late means less CC (stuns and other lockdown) aimed your way and a much longer rampage.
strategy.teamfight: Yang Jian's teamfight is a flank job: circle the edge and delete enemies who are already chipped. The five-second true-damage window after Skill 2 connects is the core of your output, so squeeze in every basic attack you can while the stun holds. The Ultimate's lasers heal more when they strike multiple enemies — the moment you get surrounded is exactly when to fire. One habit worth stealing: hold the Skill 1 recast until the enemy burns their blink, and the dash almost never whiffs. As long as the mark is up, you can always re-chase.

combos.title: Hound-Led Entry
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (mark + 5s vision) → Skill 1 recast (charge, +15% of the target's lost Health) → Skill 2 (0.5s stun) → Basic Attacks (+125 true damage)
combos.description: Land the hound to place the mark, then recast to close the gap. Once Skill 2 connects, basic attacks carry 125 true damage for 5s, so the damage comes down to how many swings fit inside the stun. That stun doubles whenever the target's Health percentage sits above Yang Jian's.

combos.title: Punishing From Behind
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (stun doubles against targets healthier than you) → Basic Attacks (+125 true damage) → Skill 3 (3 beams, 300 Health recovered)
combos.description: The further your Health percentage sits below theirs, the longer Skill 2 holds them. Trade back and Skill 3 returns 300 (+4.5% extra Health). Beams stacked onto one target only recover 50% from the second beam onward, so angle them across several enemies instead.

combos.title: Retrieving a Missed Hound
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (stays at the endpoint on a miss) → Walk up to recall it (25%-50% of the remaining cooldown refunded) → Skill 1 (mark) → Skill 1 recast (charge)
combos.description: A hound that misses stays at its endpoint and keeps searching for targets. Approach it and it returns to Yang Jian, cutting 25%-50% off the remaining cooldown. That makes throwing it into a bush a check you rarely pay for.

strengths: Skill 2's stun doubles when he is lower on HP, making counter-trades brutal
Passive resistances stack into super armor, winning long brawls
Ultimate and Passive healing let him hold ground through item deficits
War Hound's vision exposes bush ambushes while he engages
weaknesses: Missing Skill 1 removes his only gap closer until the cooldown returns
Anti-heal items gut the sustain his whole game plan leans on
Fishing for the doubled stun by staying low on HP is a risky gamble
Long-range poke that never lets him close distance leaves him without a play

playstyle.style: A fighter who grows more resistant the longer he brawls, transforming into a towering form that sweeps the frontline. Missing-Health damage plus true damage lets him melt tanks head-on.
playstyle.suited: Players who want to win extended slugfests — the answer to every unkillable frontline you've ever fought.

synergy.reason: After transforming, each of Zhang Fei's skills shakes the ground and slows nearby enemies by 25% for 2s. Nuwa lays her cross and matrix explosions on the ground, so enemies that lose their footing are far easier to catch in them. His Skill 3 roar makes him invincible for 1.25s, letting him hold the front.

Mozi's Skill 3 raises an energy barrier for up to 3.3s that stuns any enemy touching it every 0.5s. Pinned enemies are easy for Nuwa to box in with matrices, and her Skill 4 line cannot miss them. His Skill 2 shell adds a 1s stun where it explodes.

counters.reason: Han Xin's Skill 1 leaps to a target location and can be used a second time within 5s. Nuwa's matrices block the path of enemy heroes, but they buy no distance against someone who jumps rather than walks. His Skill 3 adds crowd control immunity and 30% damage reduction.

Gao Changgong's Skill 2 dagger slows immensely for 2s and leaves a mark; his attacks on a marked target stun for 1s while restoring 350 Health to him. Nuwa's only escape is her 30s Skill 3 teleport, and she cannot lay out matrices while locked down.

passive.description: Nuwa gains 10-20% vision, Basic Attack range, and skill range (increases with hero level).
passive.name: Passive Skill: Divine Consciousness

skill1.description:
Nuwa unleashes energy in the target direction, dealing 225 (225 + 42% magical attack) magical damage to enemies in its path and knocking them back. After hitting an enemy, the energy gradually stops and expands in a cross shape, forming a matrix. This deals 225 (225 + 42% magical attack) magical damage to enemies hit.
The cross deals an extra 50% damage to enemies at its center, and sets off explosions if it touches matrices.
skill1.name: Skill 1: Divine Glow - Creation

skill2.description:
Nuwa creates a matrix that only she can traverse and enemy heroes cannot pass through. Each matrix lasts 3.5s.
Whenever a matrix is hit by one of Nuwa's other skills, it sets off an explosion that deals 210 (210 + 40% magical attack) magical damage to nearby enemies.
When matrices fuse, they deal 180 (180 + 35% magical attack) magical damage (+50% extra damage in the center) on collision and knock back enemies for 0.5s. Collisions gain up to 30% extra range based on the initial distance between matrices. Up to 3 matrices can be stocked. When multiple matrices explode simultaneously, they only deal damage to the same target once.
skill2.name: Skill 2: Divine Glow - Coalescence

skill3.description: Nuwa teleports to the target location while gaining 30% Movement Speed and a shield that negates 600 (600 + 9% extra Health) damage for 2s. She also deals 300 (300 + 57% magical attack) magical damage to enemies within the target area and slows them by 25-50% for 0.5s. Enemies take less damage the farther away they are from her, down to 50% of the initial damage.
skill3.name: Skill 3: Divine Glow - Emergence

skill4.description: Nuwa releases pure energy, dealing 600 (600 + 115% magical attack) magical damage to enemies in its path. The pure energy will set off an explosion if it touches a matrix.
skill4.name: Skill 4: Divine Glow - Annihilation

strategy.earlyGame: Nuwa's Passive extends her basic attack and skill cast range, so from level 1 she farms mid from a step farther out than her opponent can reach. There is no reason to push up — thread Skill 1 through the spot where the enemy overlaps their minions and let the chip damage add up. Skill 2's walls are insurance before they are offense: block the gank path your jungler is not watching and any dive loses a full beat. Sit on Skill 3. Its warp and shield are the only reason she survives a collapse, so keep it pocketed until the gank threat is genuinely gone.
strategy.midGame: The Tyrant spawn at 4:00 begins Nuwa's setup game. Lay two Skill 2 walls in the narrow paths leading to the pit, then thread Skill 1 into anyone touching them — the chain explosions plus the cross's bonus damage carve chunks out of enemies before the fight even starts. Since the matrix blocks only enemy heroes, smart placement seals both their retreat and their reinforcement route. After your first core item, her damage takes a real jump, so cycle between shoving mid and spending time on wall placement until the objective area belongs to you.
strategy.lateGame: Once Shadow Tyrant and Overlord are on the line after 10 minutes, a single wall rewrites the geometry of a fight. Seal the pit entrance and the enemy eats a detour while your team pokes them apart. Ideally you bank all three Skill 2 charges before anything starts. Stay at the absolute back, and treat Skill 3's warp and shield as an anti-assassin escape button, never an engage tool. Warp out, drop one more wall behind you, and the chase simply dies. A prepared Nuwa is oppressive; an unprepared one is a minion with a health bar.
strategy.teamfight: Nuwa's job starts ten seconds before the fight does. Read the enemy's approach path, pre-lay walls, and thread Skill 1 into the densest clump for chain explosions. Once the brawl is live, wall placement is the judgment call that defines her: cut off a fleeing enemy at the nose, or drop one between their assassin and your carry as a screen. The most painful mistake in practice is walling off your own team's retreat — when in doubt, bias the placement toward the enemy side. Keep Skill 3's warp and shield in reserve as your final card.

combos.title: Chained Cross Detonation
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (place a matrix, lasts 3.5s) → Skill 1 (knocks back, then expands into a cross that touches the matrix and sets it off) → Skill 4 (pure energy touches a matrix and explodes)
combos.description: Place one matrix, then send Skill 1's energy into it. The energy halts where it connects, expands into a cross, and the matrix it touches goes off for 210. Center the cross on the target for the extra 50%, and land Skill 4 before the 3.5s runs out.

combos.title: Sealing The Chase Lane
combos.sequence: Skill 3 (teleport to the target location, 600 shield, 300 damage and a 0.5s slow) → Skill 2 → Skill 2 (fusion collision knocks back for 0.5s) → Skill 1 (knock back)
combos.description: Enemy heroes cannot pass through a matrix, which turns the lane behind a Skill 3 teleport into a sealed corridor. Fusing two of them knocks enemies back for 0.5s, and a wider initial gap grows that collision by up to 30%. A stalled chaser then eats another knockback from Skill 1.

strengths: Passive range lets her poke from outside any retaliation distance
Walls become hero-only terrain that dominates every chokepoint
Wall-triggered chain explosions give a setup mage real burst damage
Skill 3's warp and shield answer one dive attempt for free
weaknesses: Needs setup time, so sudden brawls and mobile skirmishes blunt her
Skill 3 is her only escape; she is helpless right after using it
A misplaced wall can seal her own team's retreat
Open ground with no chokepoints devalues her walls sharply

playstyle.style: A mage with some of the longest range in the game, dropping judgement from off-screen. Her matrix corridors are paths only she can walk, letting her chip enemies who can never reach her.
playstyle.suited: Players fully committed to winning from safety — custodians of the one advantage that never gets traded: distance.

synergy.reason: Movement Speed buffs and heals strongly support deep dives onto the enemy backline.
Provides strong shields and CC to hold the frontline during messy post-dive teamfights.

counters.reason: Hard suppression ultimate guarantees he can stop your dive and turn the fight around.
Continuous damage and sustain allow her to completely neutralize close-range dive attempts.

passive.description:
Nezha receives a shield that negates 75 (75 + 1.5% extra Health) true damage for every enemy hero he damages with a skill, for up to 800 (800 + 20% extra Health) true damage in total. This also triggers Wind-Fire Wheels 1 time, increasing Movement Speed by 5% for 3s, for up to 5 stacks.
The true damage shield can be recovered at the spawn point.
When he deals damage using Basic Attacks or Scorching Ember, or deals damage to a non-hero unit, he only gets a shield negating 20 (20 + 0.5% extra Health) true damage.
Each target can trigger Wind-Fire Wheels up to 1 time.
passive.name: Passive Skill: Scorching Ember

skill1.description:
Nezha deals 345 (345 + 105% extra physical attack) physical damage to nearby enemies and places Scorching Ember on them, dealing 45 (45 + 20% extra physical attack) true damage to the enemy every second for 5s, for up to 3 stacks. Damage increases by 50% with each stack. Scorching Ember also reduces the target's Health recovery by 15%.
The duration of Scorching Ember is refreshed when Nezha deals damage to the target.
skill1.name: Skill 1: Fire-tipped Spear - Sweep

skill2.description:
Flips behind the target to deal 150 (150 + 65% extra physical attack) physical damage. He also gains a shield that negates 24 (24 + 0.5% extra Health) true damage, halved for non-hero units.
This skill cannot be used on the same target again for 3s.
skill2.name: Skill 2: Red Armillary Sash - Bind

skill3.description:
Nezha selects an enemy hero and flies to their location, dealing 450 (450 + 170% extra physical attack) physical damage and knocking them back.
After landing, Nezha gains 10% damage reduction and 20% Resistance for 4s.
This skill enters a 50%-100% Cooldown based on flight distance. If the target is untargetable upon arrival, Nezha waits until the untargetable state ends and then immediately knocks the target back (can wait up to 0.5s).
skill3.name: Skill 3: Universe Ring - Skyfall

skill4.description:
Nezha unleashes the universe ring, dealing 140 (140 + 45% extra physical attack) physical damage to all enemy heroes across the entire map and gaining vision. Enhances the range of Universe Ring - Skyfall to cover the entire map for 5s.
Heroes revealed by this effect cannot use recall.
skill4.name: Skill 4: Universe Ring

strategy.earlyGame: Nezha's first four levels are about patience. Do not force wins in the Clash Lane — tag enemies with Skill 1, let the five-second true-damage burn and its healing reduction do the grinding, and settle for short trades. Every skill hit on an enemy hero banks a true-damage shield, so lots of brief touches beat one long slugfest. Skill 2 rolls you behind a target for free hits, but remember it locks out on that same target for three seconds and burns your escape route. Priority number one is simple: reach level 4 without dying.
strategy.midGame: Nezha's game starts moving the moment you learn Skill 3, Universe Ring - Skyfall. Spot a low-HP or isolated backliner on the minimap and fly straight to them. The landing knockback breaks their position while an ally collapses from the other side. For four seconds after landing you take 10% less damage at level 1 and gain 20% Resistance, so you can commit harder than it looks. The skill enters only 50%-100% of its cooldown depending on flight distance, so short hops come back fast. Range grows from 2,400 at level 1 to 3,600 at level 4. In a Tyrant standoff, pressuring the opposite side of the map without showing yourself forces the enemy to split bodies. Check the minimap for follow-up before every flight — that one habit erases most of this hero's deaths.
strategy.lateGame: After 15 minutes Nezha is the teamfight start button. Skill 3, Universe Ring - Skyfall, is a one-way ticket, so only fly onto targets your team can reach within five seconds. The dream window is the enemy marksman stepping forward. Dive, knock them back out of the formation, then stack Skill 1's Scorching Ember; its 15% healing reduction slows every patch-up the support attempts. Skill 4, Universe Ring, moves nobody. It damages and reveals every enemy hero on the map, and for the next five seconds Skyfall reaches all of them. Revealed heroes cannot recall, so backing off to reset stops being an option. During Shadow Tyrant or Overlord standoffs, simply holding the dive warps the enemy backline's positioning. Great Nezhas save it for the two or three moments per game that actually decide something.
strategy.teamfight: Nezha flies first or flies last — nothing in between. If your team has another initiator, the late dive is safer: wait for the enemy CC (stuns and other lockdown) to be spent, then drop on whoever is left carrying. After landing, stack Skill 1's burn to three, keep rolling behind fleeing targets with Skill 2, and let the true damage cook. Your shield rebuilds as long as skills keep connecting, which makes the center of the brawl the safest place you can stand. What you cannot beat is a spread formation kiting you in the open, so push for fights in tight terrain.

combos.title: Map-Wide Ambush
combos.sequence: Skill 4 (140 damage and vision on every enemy hero; Skill 3 reaches the whole map for 5s) → Skill 3 (fly in, knock back) → Skill 1 (Scorching Ember) → Skill 2 (flip behind)
combos.description: For those 5 seconds Skill 3 can reach any enemy hero on the map. Revealed heroes also lose access to recall, so anyone trying to go home is fair game. Landing grants 10% damage reduction and 20% Resistance for 4s, which buys the time your team needs to arrive.

combos.title: Keeping the Burn Alive
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (ignite Scorching Ember) → Skill 2 (flip behind for 150 damage and a shield) → Skill 1 (re-ignite to stack the burn)
combos.description: Scorching Ember ticks 45 true damage per second for 5s and grows 50% stronger with each of its 3 stacks. It also cuts the target's healing by 15%, which matters against sustain picks. Skill 2 cannot repeat on the same target for 3s, and that wait lines up closely with Skill 1's 5s cooldown.

strengths: Skill 3 dives straight onto a distant backliner, and Skill 4 stretches its range across the whole map for 5s
True-damage burn plus healing reduction breaks sustain-heavy heroes
Shield stacks off every skill hit, keeping him alive in the scrum
Post-landing damage reduction and resistances make dives stick
weaknesses: Skill 3 has no return trip; without follow-up he dies alone
Lacks burst, so targets can slip away before the burn finishes them
Shield depends on landing skills; whiff and he is suddenly fragile
Minimal self-defense before level 4 and easily bullied in lane

playstyle.style: A fighter who stacks true-damage shields and drops from the sky onto one chosen enemy with Skill 3. Skill 4 stretches that dive across the whole map for five seconds, and the enemies it reveals cannot recall. He is a marksman-catching device — his whole kit erases one target's escape options.
playstyle.suited: Built for players who want guaranteed delivery on 'kill that one hero and we win'. If you can spend one second on the minimap before committing and judge whether your team can follow, you have the aptitude. Restraint counts as much as nerve — two or three flights a game, saved for the moments that decide something.

synergy.reason: Groups enemies together, making it easy to hit multiple targets with your skill combo.
Provides cooldown reduction and sustain, enabling relentless poke.

counters.reason: High mobility and burst damage allow her to instantly close the gap and one-shot you.
Forces engages from long range with his ultimate, catching you before you can escape.

passive.description:
Whenever Gan uses a flying sword skill at a target location, Mo unleashes an equal number of swords to the same location at the same time to deal equal damage. Flying sword skills share usage caps.
Flying swords place 1 stack of Sword Energy on enemies hit. If a flying sword hits a marked target, each stack deals 75 (75 + 12% magical attack) magical damage.
If multiple flying swords hit a marked target at the same time, subsequent hits only deal 50% of this damage.
Gan & Mo's Basic Attacks deal 300 (300 + 25% magical attack) magical damage.
passive.name: Passive Skill: Forever Entwined

skill1.description:
Gan unleashes Splitting Swords in the target direction, dealing 300 (300 + 50% magical attack) magical damage twice to enemies within range and knocking them back, while also retreating in the opposite direction. Reduces hit enemies' Magical Defense by 150 for 3s.
Passive: Each defeat or assist grants Gan & Mo 1 Splitting Sword, increasing their magical attack by 15, for up to 20 stacks.
skill1.name: Skill 1: Guard Her Grave

skill2.description:
Unleash flying swords in the target direction, dealing 325 (325 + 45% magical attack) magical damage to enemies in their path, and an extra 75 (75 + 12% magical attack) magical damage to enemies with Sword Energy.
Flying sword skills share a usage cap, with one charge restored every 5-6s (cooldown reduces with skill level). When the same Sword Energy is triggered multiple times, the second time onwards only deals 50% damage.
skill2.name: Skill 2: Coupled Blades - Short

skill3.description:
Unleash flying swords in the target direction, dealing 325 (325 + 45% magical attack) magical damage to enemies in their path, and an extra 75 (75 + 12% magical attack) magical damage to enemies with Sword Energy.
Flying sword skills share a usage cap, with one charge restored every 5-6s (cooldown reduces with skill level). When the same Sword Energy is triggered multiple times, the second time onwards only deals 50% damage.
skill3.name: Skill 3: Coupled Blades - Long

skill4.description:
Immediately gains 2 uses of flying sword skills and enhances the next flying sword skill to unleash more swords.
Passive: Increases field of vision by 15% and increases the usage cap of flying sword skills by 1. Each time a flying sword hits an enemy, this skill's cooldown is reduced by 1s.
skill4.name: Skill 4: Freshly Forged

strategy.earlyGame: Gan & Mo outrange the entire mid lane from level 1. Everything about the duo's damage flows from crossing Skill 2's short-range blades with Skill 3's long-range blades at a single point, so the second volley detonates the Sword Energy the first one left behind — spend the opening waves calibrating that intersection distance on stationary minions. Blade skills draw from a shared usage cap that only restores one charge every five to six seconds, which means never stepping forward right after emptying it. If someone jumps you, Skill 1's knockback-and-hop-back buys exactly one reset. That is the only insurance policy you own; price it accordingly.
strategy.midGame: From about 7-8 minutes, with your first core item finished, one clean intersection removes close to half of an enemy mage's HP. Before the 4:00 Tyrant or the 10:00 Shadow Tyrant, simply raining blades from maximum range onto anyone entering the pit forces the enemy to open the fight pre-chipped — that is Gan & Mo's brand of pressure. Skill 1 banks bonus magic attack on every kill and assist, so involvement snowballs the damage curve on its own. Skip the roams. Push mid, step back, carve sword qi into whoever contests, repeat.
strategy.lateGame: With Skill 1 grown to 15-20 stacks, a single intersection deletes a marksman outright — which is precisely why the enemy will spend everything to reach you. Two non-negotiables: stand behind every teammate, and never fight with a wall at your back. Do not hunt with Skill 1 either; hold it as the reaction card you play the instant someone commits to the jump. During Overlord fights, dropping blades from outside the pit's perimeter slowly bends the enemy formation out of shape until someone makes the mistake you have been waiting for.
strategy.teamfight: Gan & Mo never need to walk forward in a teamfight. From the deepest backline, punish any enemy frontliner who stops moving by crossing the short and long blades on their feet — that alone is a full shift's work. Priority targets: pre-fight clumps and anyone locked down by your team's CC. Chasing sprinting targets with blades is wasted ammunition. Skill 1's 150 magic defense shred also boosts your allied mage, so land it on the focus target first. Empty the charges, take one step back, wait for the refill. Guard that rhythm and you survive.

combos.title: Crossing the Blades
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (short-range flying swords, applies Sword Energy) → Skill 3 (long-range flying swords into the same spot, +75 per Sword Energy stack) → Basic Attack (300 magical damage)
combos.description: When Gan sends flying swords, Mo mirrors the same number into the same spot, so every cast lands doubled. Get Sword Energy on the target first and the follow-up volley adds 75 magical damage per stack. Charges only refill one every 5-6s, so pick your retreat before you empty them.

combos.title: Reloading With Skill 4
combos.sequence: Skill 4 (instantly stock 2 flying sword uses, enhance the next one) → Skill 3 → Skill 2
combos.description: Skill 4 is ammunition, not damage. It hands back two charges at once and makes the next flying sword summon more blades. Every flying sword that connects shaves 1s off Skill 4's cooldown, so accuracy shortens the wait for the next reload.

combos.title: Answer to a Dive
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (knock back while retreating in the opposite direction, -150 Magical Defense) → Skill 3 → Skill 2
combos.description: Skill 1 is the only way Gan & Mo create space on their own. Bounce the diver, back off, and pour both blade skills into the 3s window where their Magical Defense sits 150 lower. Spend it on offense and there is nothing left the next time someone jumps you.

strengths: Crossed blade intersections burst enemies from beyond retaliation range
Skill 1 banks up to 20 stacks of magic attack off kills and assists
Knockback plus hop-back on Skill 1 is genuine anti-assassin insurance
The 150 magic defense shred amplifies every magic dealer on the team
weaknesses: Damage tracks intersection accuracy one-to-one; the skill floor is steep
No mobility skill, so a closed gap almost always means death
Blade charges are finite and the pressure vanishes once they are spent
No hard CC of their own, so they cannot lock anyone down solo

playstyle.style: An extreme-range artillery mage whose paired blades both strike wherever he aims — one act of aim, double the payload. Accuracy converts directly into multiplied damage.
playstyle.suited: Players who want their aim rewarded at the highest multiplier in the game — snipers at heart.

synergy.reason: Provides follow-up CC and peel on engages, creating guaranteed kill opportunities.
Capitalizes on Athena's engages to follow up with massive burst damage.

counters.reason: Mobility buffs and silence skills can easily disrupt your engage attempts.
High mobility and displacement skills completely throw off your skill combos.

passive.description:
Able to move freely in her Divine form after dying, gaining 30 Movement Speed and a new Divine skill to aid teammates.
When resurrected, flies toward the nearest allied tower, dealing 600 (600 + 180% extra physical attack) physical damage and launching enemies within takeoff range for 0.75s.
passive.name: Passive Skill: Divine Awakening

skill2.name: Skill 2: Unstoppable Spear / Victory Call

Hitting enemies with Holy Advance and Immovable Aegis resets Unstoppable Spear's cooldown.
Enhanced Basic Attacks deal an extra 40% damage to non-hero units.

Enhanced Basic Attacks deal an extra 40% damage to non-hero units.
Athena spreads her wings, granting a nearby teammate a shield that negates 250 (250 + 80% physical attack + 5% extra Health) damage for 2s.

Each time she is attacked by an enemy hero while her Aegis is raised, her counterattack damage increases by 10% and her Aegis's casting time is reduced by 10%, for up to 5 stacks.

After 1.5s, she uses her Aegis to perform a counterattack, dealing 450 (450 + 150% extra physical attack) magical damage to enemies in range. Each time she is attacked by an enemy hero while her Aegis is raised, her counterattack damage increases by 10% and her Aegis's casting time is reduced by 10%, for up to 5 stacks.

Athena flies toward the nearest allied tower. During takeoff, she deals 600 (600 + 180% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies in range (scales with hero level) and launches them for 0.75s. She also protects nearby teammates and causes them to retreat with her.
This active skill cannot be used when the respawn timer is below 10s.
If Athena uses her Ultimate while dead, she cannot grant protection or follow-up effects to teammates after resurrecting.

strategy.earlyGame: Athena's laning is a level-2 trade loop: jump in with Skill 2, land the empowered basic attack, dash out with Skill 1 — and because a connected Skill 1 refunds Skill 2's cooldown, you immediately get another round trip. Run that cycle and only your opponent's health bar moves. The empowered hit adds 6% of the target's missing HP, so the more chipped they are, the harder it lands. Level 4 unlocks the full all-in: two shields with CC immunity layered on top. The only real way to throw it is whiffing, so pick your jump target with care.
strategy.midGame: Around 7-8 minutes, one core item in, Athena's mobility starts cashing checks. Shove your side wave, then use Skill 2's leap to cut through the river and hit the 4:00 Tyrant or any skirmish from the flank. Before diving, count the enemy's key lockdown skills — if one is still up, time Skill 1's one second of CC immunity to slide through it and reach the backline safely. Do not rush the Ultimate out either. Its retaliation grows every time enemies strike the braced shield, so the moment they focus you is the moment it starts printing damage.
strategy.lateGame: Late-game Athena is a time bomb strapped to the enemy backline. As long as Skill 1 and the Ultimate keep connecting, Skill 2 keeps refreshing, and no amount of running rescues a marksman you have decided to keep. Do not overlook the Passive: on death she respawns at the nearest allied tower with a knock-up burst, so in defensive scenarios even a death converts into a play. That insurance barely functions when you are the one diving deep, so measure your entry. At Shadow Tyrant, slide in from behind after both sides have traded skills — that is where she cuts deepest.
strategy.teamfight: Decide one thing before every teamfight: whose face are you living in. Athena's damage is stacked empowered basics, so swapping targets mid-fight means killing no one. The ideal is single-minded pursuit of the enemy marksman. Slip the first lockdown with Skill 1's CC immunity, raise the Ultimate against their counterattack so every hit feeds the retaliation, then dump it back on them. One detail everyone forgets in practice: you can walk while the shield is braced. Drifting toward your escape route during those seconds is often the difference between a reset and a respawn.

combos.title: Riding the Resets
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (leap) → Empowered Basic Attack (+180, plus 6% of the target's lost Health) → Skill 1 (dash, knock back; a hit resets Skill 2) → Skill 2 → Empowered Basic Attack
combos.description: A Skill 1 that connects refunds Skill 2's cooldown on the spot. The empowered attack adds 6% of the target's lost Health, so it bites harder the longer the fight runs. Miss Skill 1 and the loop stops dead, leaving you parked in their team with nothing.

combos.title: Brace, Then Answer
combos.sequence: Skill 3 (1,200 shield, crowd control immunity) → Absorb their attacks to grow the counter → Counterattack after 1.5s (450 magical damage; a hit resets Skill 2) → Skill 2 → Empowered Basic Attack
combos.description: Every hit an enemy hero lands on the raised Aegis adds 10% counterattack damage and cuts 10% off its casting time, up to 5 stacks. Raising it after they commit is what makes the answer heavy. The counterattack also refunds Skill 2, so the follow-up leap is waiting the moment it lands.

strengths: Skill 1 and Ultimate hits refund Skill 2, so her mobility never runs dry
Shields with CC immunity slip enemy lockdown on demand
Missing-HP empowered basics give her a real answer to tanks
Tower respawn passive turns defensive deaths into tempo, not losses
weaknesses: A whiffed Skill 1 or Ultimate stalls the reset engine mid-combo
No burst, so disciplined enemies can recover before she finishes them
Respawn is fixed to the nearest allied tower — weak while sieging
Reset bookkeeping is expert-level; sloppy play accomplishes nothing

playstyle.style: A shield-and-dash fighter who doesn't stop at death — she remains on the field as a divine spirit, supporting her team, and her respawn descent hits like a skill. Dying is part of her kit.
playstyle.suited: Players who like aggressive, deep engages — with the unique insurance that even death leaves work done.

synergy.reason: Heavy healing and peel create an ideal environment for him to stand his ground and output massive DPS.
Significantly boosts his survivability when diving the enemy team, maximizing his ultimate's potential.

counters.reason: Anti-heal from his ultimate completely nullifies your main strength: sustain.
Applies freezes and slows to grouped allies, severely limiting your team's positioning.

passive.description:
When taking damage, Cai Yan gains 35% Movement Speed that diminishes over 2s. She also recovers 250 (250 +50% magical attack) Health per second for 2s.
The passive can only be triggered once every 10s.
passive.name: Passive Skill: Can't Touch This

skill1.description: Cai Yan plays a tune, increasing her Movement Speed by 40% and restoring 60 (60 + 20% magical attack) Health to teammates every 0.5s for 3s. Restores 50% less Health to non-hero units.
skill1.name: Skill 1: Healing Hymn

skill2.description:
Cai Yan launches a sound wave that bounces between enemies. Each hit deals 270 (270 + 48% magical attack) magical damage and stuns the enemy for 0.75s.
Each sound wave bounces up to 6 times, and the same target can only be hit by 2 bounces. The second bounce inflicts only 25% of the initial damage and stun duration.
skill2.name: Skill 2: Earworm

skill3.description: Cai Yan plays her harp, restoring 90 (90 + 45% magical attack) Health to the teammate with the lowest Health within range every 0.5s for 5s while increasing their physical defense and magical defense by 200 (200 + 30% magical attack).
skill3.name: Skill 3: Tune of Tranquility

strategy.earlyGame: Cai Yan's assigned seat is directly beside her marksman from minute zero. The early job is not damage — it is making sure your partner cannot die. When the enemy commits, answer with Skill 2's ricochet stun; if they are tangled up with their minion wave, the bounces chain-stun and the trade collapses in your favor. After every exchange, walk alongside with Skill 1 running and the chip damage simply refunds itself, letting your partner keep farming instead of recalling. Until the Ultimate arrives at level 4, check bushes, hold position, and refuse to be the one caught forward.
strategy.midGame: Cai Yan's presence grows from the 4:00 Tyrant onward. While your team burns the boss, the flank is the most dangerous moment on the map — meet whoever walks in with Skill 2, and the ricochet stuns stall the contest cold. Her Ultimate spends five seconds auto-targeting the lowest-HP ally in range with healing and a defense buff, so rather than panic-casting mid-brawl, open it just before the enemy's burst lands. Between the Passive's speed surge on taking damage and her self-heal, she is far harder to catch than the health bar suggests.
strategy.lateGame: Late fights become a staring contest over Cai Yan's Ultimate — the enemy wants it forced early, you want it perfectly timed. Absent anti-heal, its five seconds of rolling heals and defense buffs absorb an entire round of enemy focus. Stand diagonally behind your carry, and cast it where only the ally you intend to save sits inside the ring; that placement is the entire skill expression of this hero, because a frontliner soaking the heal is a wasted Ultimate. Fill your slots with team utility items and forget your own scoreline entirely.
strategy.teamfight: Cai Yan's teamfight reduces to two real decisions: spend Skill 2 on the enemy's entrance or on their retreat, and choose whose feet the Ultimate covers. The ricochet multiplies against clustered enemies, so its highest value is meeting the opening dive; if it misses, drop back and wait out the cooldown. A teamfight where the healer dies first is close to an automatic loss — never surrender the backmost position, no matter how won the fight looks. And triage coldly: the ally who can still fight outranks the ally who is already doomed.

combos.title: Stunning the Dive
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (0.75s stun per bounce) → Skill 3 (5s of healing and +200 to both defenses on the lowest-Health ally) → Skill 1 (40% Movement Speed, 3s of rolling heals)
combos.description: The sound wave bounces up to 6 times, and the same target can be caught by 2 of them. The tighter the enemies stand with the minions, the more bounces connect. Skill 3 picks the lowest-Health ally in range on its own, so open it where only the ally you mean to cover is inside.

combos.title: Escorting the Retreat
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (40% Movement Speed, 60 Health every 0.5s) → Skill 2 (stun the chasers)
combos.description: Start Skill 1 the moment the call to fall back goes out. You move 40% faster and hand out 3s of healing while catching up to the team. Once the chasers bunch together, send the wave through — the bounces spread across several of them and the pursuit ends there.

strengths: Ultimate auto-locks the lowest-HP ally with heavy healing and defenses
Ricochet stuns multiply against clumped divers
Passive speed burst and self-heal make her deceptively hard to catch
A simple kit that delivers steady value in every single game
weaknesses: Near-zero damage of her own; she cannot create a win condition alone
Anti-heal items cut her entire reason for existing in half
Ricochet targets are uncontrollable; pinning one specific enemy is hard
Caught by CC first, she dies before a single heal goes out

playstyle.style: The fundamental healer: she walks and heals simultaneously, defends herself with a bouncing stun, and tilts every extended fight through sheer sustained restoration.
playstyle.suited: Players who read their team's health bars as their own report card — taking pride in victories built from quiet work.

synergy.reason: Can perfectly chain massive burst damage while enemies are locked down by your ultimate.
Creates engage opportunities for your ultimate by grouping enemies and providing movement speed.

counters.reason: Pokes safely from outside your ultimate's range, whittling down your health before you can close the gap.
High-damage artillery skills from long range will completely prevent you from engaging.

When this skill hits an enemy, its Cooldown and Mana cost are reduced by 50%. If there are already 3 dark orbs present, restores 150 (150 + 60% magical attack) Health instead.

skill3.name: Skill 3: Forsaken Contract

strategy.earlyGame: Play Donghuang's roam aggressively from the opening seconds. Spin up three dark orbs with Skill 1 and walk into the enemy jungle alongside your own jungler — every orb touch deals percent max-HP magic damage and heals you, so even-numbers shoving matches in tight bushes are fights you simply do not lose. Contest every River Sprite to stunt the enemy jungler's curve. Your first real kill window opens the moment the Ultimate arrives at level 4, and here is the quiet truth: enemies still holding Flash are usually the careless ones.
strategy.midGame: The midgame runs through the 4:00 Tyrant and Overlord control afterward. Camp the bushes around the pit early, flush corridors with Skill 2 for damage and slows, and fish for the third orb's stun. The headline play is Flash into the Ultimate: two seconds of suppression that nothing interrupts, with the damage share letting your team pour burst into their star while they carry part of the bill. Track your own Flash cooldown obsessively — whether that card exists changes how far the enemy backline dares to walk.
strategy.lateGame: Late-game Donghuang is a walking arrest warrant with the enemy carry's name on it. Just pacing the frontline with the Ultimate available forces their marksman to hang at maximum range, halving their output before anything happens. Spend the suppression exclusively on marksmen and assassins — never tanks, because the damage-share math simply does not produce a trade against beefy targets. The counter-suppress is just as strong: when an assassin lands on your backline, clamp them, press your orbs into their face, and grind them down.
strategy.teamfight: In teamfights Donghuang either authors the opening or erases the enemy's. Attacking, Flash plus the Ultimate binds their centerpiece for two seconds while your team's burst flows in. Defending, catch divers with orbs and Skill 2's stun. The critical caveat: you are rooted during your own suppression, so casting it in the middle of their team is a signed confession — the beating starts the instant the lock ends. Suppress inside your team's range, no exceptions. And since activating the Ultimate instantly refunds three orbs, your grind damage never stops ticking while you hold them.

combos.title: Flash Into Suppression
combos.sequence: Flash → Skill 3 (2s suppression, both share all damage taken, 3 dark orbs granted instantly) → Dark orb contact (3% of the target's Health, 162 Health back) → Skill 1 (300 damage; with 3 orbs out, restores 150 Health)
combos.description: Donghuang has no mobility skill of his own; Flash is what closes the gap. Those 2 seconds share all damage taken between both heroes, and the trade only pays inside your team's range. The three orbs granted on cast spin 25% faster during the hold, stripping 3% of the target's Health on every contact.

combos.title: Winning The Orb Grind
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (creates one orb; a hit cuts its Cooldown and Mana cost by 50%) → Skill 1 → Skill 1 (three orbs out; a hit now restores 150 Health) → Keep the orbs in contact (3% of the target's Health, 162 Health back) → Skill 2 (first orb slows, second slows immensely, third stuns for 1s)
combos.description: A Skill 1 that connects halves its own Cooldown and Mana cost, which is how three orbs go up in seconds. Every orb contact takes 3% of the target's Health and returns 162 Health to Donghuang. Skill 2 drops each orb further out than the last, and the stun rides on the third — keep distance before firing.

strengths: Suppression shares damage, trading his life for their fed carry
Orb percent damage and self-healing dominate close-range brawls
Flash plus the Ultimate is a simple, nearly unmissable pick tool
A tank who moonlights as an early-game invade threat
weaknesses: Long-range poke comps never let his orbs touch anyone
He is rooted during suppression; casting beyond ally range is fatal
Skill 2's trajectory is honest and demands predictive casting
No mobility skill, so his Flash timer quietly decides fights

playstyle.style: A suppression tank who seizes one enemy for two full seconds — sharing the damage he takes with his captive. His orbs sustain him on the frontline; the plan is simply: I hold, you hit.
playstyle.suited: Players who move games through guaranteed lockdown, wagering their own body as the stake.

synergy.reason: Perfectly follows up your group pull with devastating AoE burst damage.
Massive AoE burst damage perfectly synergizes with your pull and lockdown combo.

counters.reason: Uses untargetable skills to dodge your pull and counters with heavy burst damage.
Strong long-range CC stops your engage attempts dead in their tracks before you can get close.

passive.skill_name: Passive Skill: The Laws of Nature
passive.description:
After Guiguzi leaves the enemy's field of vision for 3s, his next Basic Attack will be enhanced, dealing 300 (300 + 55% magical attack) magical damage to enemies within range and slowing them by 25%−50% (increases with level) for 1.5s.
If he is not in the enemy's field of vision when using the enhanced Basic Attack, this skill's cooldown will be increased to 10s.
passive.name: Passive Skill: The Laws of Nature

skill1.description:
Guiguzi covers himself in spriteflies that camouflage him from enemy sight for 4s. While camouflaged, he gains 40% Movement Speed and deals 450 (450 + 60% magical attack) magical damage to each enemy he touches, while reducing their physical defense and magical defense by 25% for 4s. This effect can only be triggered once on each enemy.
The camouflage disappears when he deals damage to enemies in any other way.
skill1.name: Skill 1: Prophecy - Hidden Hand

skill2.description: Guiguzi summons a large number of spriteflies that surround him, dealing 100 (100 + 15% magical attack) magical damage every 0.5s for 2s to enemies within range, after which he pulls them in and stuns them for 1s, dealing 400 (400 + 60% magical attack) magical damage. If an enemy hero is hit, Guiguzi and teammates within range gain a shield that negates 600 (600 + 120% magical attack) damage.
skill2.name: Skill 2: The Animist

skill3.description:
Guiguzi orders spriteflies to cover himself and teammates within a range of 1,500, camouflaging everyone after 1s. The camouflage lasts for 4s, during which he and his teammates gain 30% Movement Speed and vision of the nearest enemy hero.
While camouflaged, using Basic Attacks, skills, or inflicting debuffs on enemies will immediately remove it.
skill3.name: Skill 3: Prophecy - Out of Sight

strategy.earlyGame: Guiguzi should have walked half the map before his first recall — that is the correct pace. Touch the mid wave for a moment, then slide toward a side lane under Skill 1's camouflage and 40% movement speed. Ghost through the enemy laner's back, and merely brushing them carves 25% off both defenses; your laner collapsing onto that debuff turns into a kill from thin air. One rule above all: attacking anything breaks the camouflage. The touch already did the work, so keep your hands to yourself.
strategy.midGame: Guiguzi's busiest window is the thirty seconds before each Tyrant spawn. Tuck into the pit-side bush with your jungler, and anyone who wanders up eats Skill 2's pull-and-stun — objective and numbers advantage in one motion. The Ultimate's team-wide camouflage can hand your side the opening of an entire teamfight, but spending it casually on travel leaves nothing for the moment that matters; commit it to engages, full stop. The free vision of the nearest enemy hero it grants sharpens every ambush you set.
strategy.lateGame: In the late game a single engage decides everything, which makes Guiguzi's stealth the trump card of trump cards. The script: cloak all five with the Ultimate, spread across the objective approach, and land Skill 2's pull on the enemy's structural piece — usually the carry. But understand that your durability is paper against late-game damage, and the two-second channel can be burned through, shield and all. Always start the play from inside your team's effective range. Solo hero-ball adventures are this hero's number one loss condition.
strategy.teamfight: The ideal sequence never changes: vanish the team with the Ultimate, thread Skill 1 through the enemy line to stamp the 25% defense shred on priority targets, then channel Skill 2 in the thick of their formation. Two seconds later the pull and stun compress them into one tidy package for your team's AoE. The shield on hero contact absorbs some of the opening fire, but the channel is your single point of failure — start it while their attention is fixed on your frontline, in that stolen instant when nobody is looking at you.

combos.title: Cloaked Team Approach
combos.sequence: Skill 3 (camouflages the team after 1s, 30% Movement Speed for 4s) → Skill 1 (contact cuts both defenses by 25%) → Skill 2 (pull and 1s stun after 2s)
combos.description: The camouflage drops the instant he uses a basic attack, a skill, or applies a debuff to an enemy. Touch nothing until the team is in position. Shred both defenses by 25% with Skill 1, then channel Skill 2 in the clump so the pull-stun arrives together with your team's damage.

combos.title: Bush Capture
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (camouflage, 40% Movement Speed, 25% off both defenses on contact) → Skill 2 (pull and 1s stun after 2s, 600 shield to allies on a hero hit) → Empowered Basic Attack (300 damage, 1.5s slow)
combos.description: Skill 2 needs a 2s channel, so starting it at a range they can simply walk out of wastes the cast. Close with Skill 1 first and the pull lands. The empowered attack requires 3s outside enemy vision, which the wait in the bush has already paid for.

strengths: Team-wide camouflage lets him dictate exactly when fights begin
Pull-stun engage plus ally shields makes his openings devastating
Skill 1's 25% dual-defense shred raises the whole team's damage
Stealth and speed give him unmatched roaming range for ambushes
weaknesses: Paper durability — a failed engage usually costs him his life
Skill 2's two-second channel whiffs badly against anyone who reads it
His openings evaporate if teammates do not follow up instantly
Close to zero solo damage or kill threat

playstyle.style: The architect of ambushes: he cloaks his entire team and delivers an invisible squad to the enemy's doorstep, with a mass pull and shields to finish the design.
playstyle.suited: Players who want to direct the whole team's opening act — enjoying the uncredited glory of an ambush that worked.

synergy.reason: Hard CC guarantees lockdown on enemies, allowing Kongming to safely land his combo and ultimate.

counters.reason: Can invade early when mobility is low to apply pressure and disrupt Kongming's farm.
Can survive the burst damage and stick tightly to shut down Kongming's mobility.

passive.description:
Kongming gains 1 mark for 10s every time his active skills hit an enemy, for up to 5 stacks. Upon reaching max stacks, he summons 5 prisms, which circle around him for 10s and attack the nearest enemy unit, dealing 135 (135 +25% magical attack) magical damage.
Prisms prioritize enemy heroes. They deal 40% less damage to monsters and 40% extra damage to minions.
passive.name: Passive Skill: Time for Tactics

skill1.description:
Kongming fires 3 prisms in the target direction, each dealing 460 (460 + 80% magical attack) magical damage to enemies in its path. When multiple prisms hit the same enemy, subsequent hits only deal 20% damage.
Each prism triggers 1 Strategic Mark. He stocks Arcane Assault every 7.5s, for up to 2 charges.
skill1.name: Skill 1: Arcane Assault

skill2.description:
Kongming blinks in the target direction, creating magic fields at the start and the end of the dash that each deal 350 (350 + 52% magical attack) magical damage to nearby enemies. When an enemy takes damage twice from this skill within 5s, they are inflicted with extreme slow. This effect diminishes over 3s.
When an enemy takes damage from multiple fields at the same time, the second magic field only deals 50% damage.
He stocks 1 charge of this skill every 7.5s (affected by Cooldown Reduction), for up to 2 charges.
skill2.name: Skill 2: Time Shift

skill3.description:
Kongming targets an enemy and starts channeling a Spirit Bomb, which deals 450 (450 + 55% magical attack) magical damage. Non-hero enemy units that are targeted or in the Spirit Bomb's path will take extra damage and be launched for 0.5s. Enemies take 2% extra damage from Spirit Bombs for every 1% Health lost.
When a Spirit Bomb hits and defeats an enemy hero, Kongming gains a full stack of marks, and this skill's Cooldown is reduced by 80%.
If the targeted enemy hero is defeated while the Spirit Bomb is being channeled, the Cooldown of this skill will still be reduced by 80%.
skill3.name: Skill 3: Winning Strategy

strategy.earlyGame: How the midgame treats Kongming is decided by how cleanly he plays before level 4. Fan Skill 1 through waves to farm seal stacks, keep the five-stack orbs orbiting, and take short trades while they hover — the orbs fly at the nearest enemy automatically, so your opponent stepping up for a last hit is your cue to chip them. Skill 2 carries two charges, but the arithmetic is fixed: spend one aggressively, and the other is your ticket home, always. Finish this phase without dying once and you have already passed.
strategy.midGame: Kongming's show starts when the Ultimate comes online. Hunt anything below half HP — the missile scales with missing health, so a chipped target eats far more than the tooltip suggests. Land the kill and 80% of the cooldown refunds with seals instantly maxed, and the hunt loops straight into the next victim. Shove mid, show up to the 4:00 Tyrant, and fan Skill 1 from the perimeter to pre-chip the fight. One discipline: while the enemy still holds two or more lockdown skills, forcing entries with Skill 2 stays in the pocket.
strategy.lateGame: Late-game Kongming demands almost unreasonable patience. Enemies walk in tight packs with magic defense stacked, and a casual entry is nothing but food for their lockdown. So orbit the fight, cycle Skill 1 to keep the seals alive, and watch the blinks and CC leave their hands. The instant someone's HP crosses the execute line, cut an angle with Skill 2 and let the Ultimate fly. After the first kill, resets start flowing with a full orbit of orbs — flip from statue to storm and keep pressing. That toggle between stillness and violence is the entire hero.
strategy.teamfight: Kongming starts every teamfight outside its walls. Sprinkle Skill 1 to hold the seals, let the orbs freelance in the frontline scrum, and study which target is bleeding. The Ultimate gets blocked by whoever stands in between, so create diagonal firing lines with Skill 2 or Flash before releasing. A detail most players miss: even if an ally finishes the target during your charge-up, the 80% refund still triggers — never hesitate over kill-secure anxiety. The moment after firing is your most defenseless; confirm the exit before you ever commit.

combos.title: Executing the Chipped Target
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (3 prisms build marks) → Skill 2 (blink to open the line) → Skill 3 (Spirit Bomb, +2% damage per 1% Health the target has lost)
combos.description: The bomb gains 2% damage for every 1% of Health the target has already lost, so the pick is someone under half. Skill 2 leaves a magic field at both ends of the blink, meaning the approach itself keeps feeding marks. Land the kill and Skill 3's cooldown drops by 80% while the marks refill to max at once.

combos.title: Blink-and-Poke
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (3 prisms, 1 mark per hit) → Skill 2 (blink back, magic fields at both ends) → Passive prisms follow up
combos.description: Because Skill 2 drops a field where you leave and where you land, retreating still deals damage. An enemy caught by it twice within 5s is hit with an extreme slow. Reach 5 marks and the 5 prisms attack the nearest enemy on their own for 10s, which punishes anyone who keeps chasing.

strengths: Kills refund 80% of the Ultimate's cooldown and instantly max his seals
Two blink charges create angles and escapes on demand
Auto-attacking orbs apply constant pressure while he stays out of reach
Missing-HP scaling on the Ultimate erases anything left low
weaknesses: The Ultimate is body-blocked by enemies standing in the way
Paper-thin the moment both blink charges are spent
Ordinary damage whenever his seal stacks lapse
Misjudge the execute line and he becomes a decoration

playstyle.style: A tactician mage who orbits auto-attacking orbs at five marks and blinks in and out of range. His lock-on ultimate needs its channel protected — choosing when and where to cast is the skill.
playstyle.suited: Players who plan like it's a chess puzzle — meticulous preparation behind the fireworks.

synergy.reason: Combines strong basic attacks and CC to fully capitalize on Da Qiao's rapid engages and disengages.
Teleporting allies in to follow up on Mulan's ambushes gives a huge advantage in teamfights.

counters.reason: Exceptional mobility allows him to dive the backline and burst Da Qiao down before she can support her team.
High disengage capabilities make it easy to negate Da Qiao's ultimate summons.

passive.description:
Da Qiao boosts her own Movement Speed by 30.
When the koi in Leaping Koi Tide and Severing Surge leaps past another skill's tide, it triggers a tide explosion, dealing 140 (140 + 25% magical attack) magical damage and slowing enemies by 30% for 1s.
For every 250 Magical Attack, the skill range of Leaping Koi Tide and Severing Surge increases by 50, with a maximum increase of 200.
passive.name: Passive Skill: Law of Infinity

skill1.description: Da Qiao summons a koi that leaps in the target direction, dealing 300 (300 + 55% magical attack) magical damage to enemies in its path and launching them for 0.5s. The koi creates a tide that deals 75 (75 + 12% magical attack) magical damage to enemies every 0.5s for 2.5s. Using skills increases Da Qiao's Movement Speed by 30% for 2.5s.
skill1.name: Skill 1: Leaping Koi Tide

skill2.description:
Da Qiao conjures a magic circle for 4s that grants vision. When it closes, she teleports a teammate to the spawn point, removing all debuffs. They can return via the portal at the Crystal.
If no hero teleports, the magic circle leaves behind a mark a teammate can touch to recall.
