Pei switches to tiger form, gaining 15% Movement Speed for 1s and enhancing his next 2 Basic Attacks for 5s.
First Enhanced Basic Attack: He dashes at the target, dealing 185 (20 + 100% physical attack) physical damage and inflicting them with extreme slow. After using the first enhanced Basic Attack, the duration of the second will change to 5s.
Second Enhanced Basic Attack: He deals 185 (20 + 100% physical attack) magical damage to enemies within range in front of him.

forms.description:
Pei switches to tiger form, gaining 15% Movement Speed for 1s and enhancing his next 2 Basic Attacks for 5s.
First Enhanced Basic Attack: He dashes at the target, dealing 185 (20 + 100% physical attack) physical damage and inflicting them with extreme slow. After using the first enhanced Basic Attack, the duration of the second will change to 5s.
Second Enhanced Basic Attack: He deals 185 (20 + 100% physical attack) magical damage to enemies within range in front of him.

Pei switches to Human Form, gaining 15% Movement Speed for 1s and enhancing his next Basic Attack for 5s.
The enhanced Basic Attack allows him to fire a stronger Inner Energy at the target, dealing 265 (100 + 100% physical attack) magical damage to the target and enemies in a cone-shaped area behind them.

strategy.earlyGame: Pei toggles between human and tiger with an Ultimate available from level 1, giving him one of the fastest jungle starts in the game. Shred your first buff with tiger-form empowered basics, and once the second buff is down, start eyeing an invade — almost no jungler beats Pei in a straight early-game scrap. Human form has longer basic attack range, and hitting the same target within 3 seconds scales the damage up to triple the base, so finish camps in human form: the kill is faster and the energy refunds come quicker.
strategy.midGame: The gank template is a two-act play: chip in human, execute in tiger. Human form's Skill 1 deals 8% of current HP plus a slow, so even tanks feel the poke, and adding Skill 2's shield plus 30% attack speed makes you genuinely scary at range. Once the target drops below half HP, swap to tiger and pounce with the wall-crossing double dash into empowered basics. Constantly weigh the 4-minute Tyrant against the enemy's buffs — the instant you spot their jungler, steal the resources on the opposite side. Half-map control is the mid-game ideal.
strategy.lateGame: Late teamfights are an exercise in patience. Both forms stay fragile, so open every fight in human form from the very back: throw Skill 1, maintain Skill 2's shield, and kite. The only time you swap to tiger is when the enemy's CC is spent and a target below 40% HP is clearly in view. Dive, finish them with empowered basics, and even after the kill, immediately return to human form and re-establish distance. Repeating 'tiger is for executions only' like a mantra puts you at exactly the right level of caution.
strategy.teamfight: Your default is playing human form like a marksman: chip the frontline with Skill 1's percent damage, cycle your shield, and kite backward. The reason you never tiger-dive the clump is simple — the instant you transform, multiple CCs come flying. Your go signals are the enemy's stuns being spent and the backline's HP bars. When both line up, swap to Tiger Form, use a side wall for the double dash to erase their reaction time, and get into their carry's face. Secure the kill, skip the chase, and return to human-form range to rejoin the line. That whole loop is one set.

combos.title: Soften in Human, Finish as Tiger
combos.sequence: Human Form Skill 1 (8% of current Health + 1.5s slow) → Skill 3 (switch to tiger form, next 2 Basic Attacks enhanced) → Tiger Form Skill 2 (pounce; latch onto terrain for 1s and pounce again) → First Enhanced Basic Attack (dash in with an extreme slow) → Tiger Form Skill 1 (bite)
combos.description: Human form Skill 1 adds 8% of the target's current Health, so the chip damage starts there. After the swap, pounce into terrain and use the 1s latch to change your angle before pouncing again. The enhanced Basic Attacks only last 5s, so dawdling on the wall lets them expire. The closing bite gains 1% damage for every 1% of Health the target has lost, which is what fixes the order.

combos.title: Swap Back and Kite
combos.sequence: Skill 3 (return to human form, next Basic Attack enhanced) → Enhanced Basic Attack (energy blast covering the cone behind the target) → Human Form Skill 2 (shield + Attack Speed boost) → Basic Attacks while backing off → Human Form Skill 1 (slow)
combos.description: Coming out of tiger form turns your next Basic Attack into a blast. It also covers the cone behind the target, so it still catches several enemies while you give ground. Human form has the longer Basic Attack range and returns 5 Energy per hit. Stay on one target within 3s and the bonus damage builds up to triple its base.

strengths: Form swapping covers both ranged poke and melee burst in one kit
The Ultimate is available from level 1, giving elite early fighting power
Human Form Skill 1's percent damage cuts through even tanks
Tiger Form's wall dashes open up a rich menu of ambush angles
weaknesses: Both forms are fragile; teamfight focus fire melts him quickly
No hard CC of his own, so picks depend on allied lockdown
Fighting at the wrong range for his current form halves his damage
Without an early snowball, his late-game presence thins out fast

playstyle.style: An assassin who shifts between human and tiger stances — poke at range as a human, execute up close as a tiger. You are effectively piloting two kits plus an energy bar.
playstyle.suited: Players drawn to stance-dance heroes who want to train fast, situational decisions about which form is right now.

synergy.reason: The Animist pulls enemies in and stuns them for 1s, so Force Field Suppression lands on the whole pile; while electrified, its electric wave steals 25 Movement Speed for every hero it hits. Enemies Guiguzi brushes past under Prophecy - Hidden Hand also lose 25% of both defenses for 4s.

Battlefield Command restores 300 Health to Liu Bang and nearby teammates the moment the warp completes. Force Field Suppression already gives Biron a shield that negates 900, and the heal plus Liu Bang's own shield stack on top, letting Biron hold the ground he pushed into.

counters.reason: Menki banks Mass every time he casts, and every 10 Mass gives him 8 Physical Defense and 8 Magical Defense, blunting the hits Biron uses to build charge. Dream Bubble flies out and back, piling up to 4 stacks of slow on him, so the follow-up after his dash never lands.

Landing a halberd skill on an enemy hero enchants Lu Bu for 8s, adding true damage to his Basic Attacks and skills that Biron's defenses cannot reduce. Inside the ring from Tremble, Mortals, Lu Bu also gains 150 physical and 150 magical defense, so the longer the brawl runs the worse it gets.

passive.description:
Biron's mace accumulates charge when he lands hits with Basic Attacks or unenhanced skills.
At 30 charge or more, his mace becomes Electrified. Basic Attacks deal 40 (40 + 14% extra physical attack) physical damage and restore 70 (70 + 1.5% extra Health) Health to him. Skills also receive different enhancement effects, but hits from enhanced skills do not build up charge.
Basic Attack hits accumulate 5−10 charge, and skill hits accumulate 8−16 charge. He can stock up to 90 charge.
passive.name: Passive Skill: Fearless Chariot

skill1.description:
Swings his weapon twice, dealing 265 (265 + 100% extra physical attack) physical damage each time and restoring 100 (100 + 1.5% extra Health) Health, plus an extra 2% of lost Health.
Electrified Enhancement: Damage is increased to 400 (400 + 150% extra physical attack) physical damage, and restoration is increased to 200 (200 + 2.3% extra Health) Health, plus 4% of lost Health.
skill1.name: Skill 1: Electrifying Charge

skill2.description:
Dashes forward, dealing 281 (150 + 75% physical attack) physical damage to enemies in his path. The next Basic Attack after the dash is enhanced, dealing 375 (200 + 100% physical attack) physical damage and slowing enemies by 25% for 2s.
Electrified Enhancement: If he has accumulated 30 charge or more, the enhanced Basic Attack deals 562 (300 + 150% physical attack) physical damage. It also launches and stuns targets for 1s, then slows them by 25% for 1s.
The first enhanced Basic Attack costs 30 Energy.
skill2.name: Skill 2: Storm Strike

skill3.description:
Biron slams his mace into the ground, dealing 450 (450 + 120% extra physical attack) physical damage and slowing enemies by 30% for 1.5s. He also generates a shield that negates 900 (900 + 18% extra Health) damage for 6s.
Electrified Enhancement: Increases damage to 580 (580 + 195% extra physical attack) physical damage and boosts the shield to negate 1,450 (1,450 + 21% extra Health). Also generates an electric wave that deals 200 (200 + 75% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies and steals 25 Movement Speed from each hero, granting it to Biron.
The range of the electric wave increases with the Ultimate's level.
skill3.name: Skill 3: Force Field Suppression

strategy.earlyGame: Biron pushes hard in the clash lane early — as long as his gauge is up. Basic Attack hits accumulate 5−10 charge and skill hits accumulate 8−16. At 30 or more the mace goes Electrified and every skill gains an enhancement. Punch a few minions to clear 30 before you start anything with your opponent. Charge stocks up to 90, so loading extra before you commit is never wasted. Enhanced Skill 1 heals 1% more for every 1% of HP you are missing. That is what makes low-HP slugfests survivable, and the moment your opponent thinks they have chunked you down and steps in is usually where you win.
strategy.midGame: From level 4, once empowered Skill 2's knockup and stun come online, Biron transforms into a premier gank-followup hero. Clear waves while banking Energy, and the second your jungler arrives, dash in with Skill 2 and lock the target down for a full second with the empowered basic attack — that's essentially a guaranteed kill. The iron rule before the 4-minute Tyrant: fill your gauge before walking down to the river, because empty-gauge Biron is just a target. After shoving your lane, hit the enemy's jungle camps to keep the gauge topped up while you raid.
strategy.lateGame: Late game you are the frontline diver and disruptor. Enhanced Skill 3 raises its area damage from 450 to 580 and its shield from 900 to 1,450 absorbed (level 1 values). Soak the enemy's opening burst with that 6-second shield and buy your team the window to counterattack. The enhanced version also sends out an electric wave that steals 25 Movement Speed from every hero it hits and grants it to Biron, so the more enemies surround you, the faster you move — good for the dive and good for the exit. Healing comes from enhanced Skill 1 and Electrified basic attacks, not from Skill 3. The shield buys the time; the swings bring the HP back. The only thing to fear is being kept at range. Against comps that stack slows from distance, save Flash as your instant gap-closer until the very end. Charge and Flash: managing those two is the whole late game.
strategy.teamfight: The fight starts 30 seconds before the fight. Hit nearby minions or jungle camps to bank Energy, then walk in loaded. Engage with Skill 2's dash, stop their momentum with the empowered basic attack's knockup, and immediately follow with the Ultimate's shield and AoE slow. Close with empowered Skill 1 in the middle of their clump — the more enemies it hits, the more you heal. And once you're below half HP, empowered Skill 1's healing spikes hard, so the longer you persist in the scrum, the harder you become to kill.

combos.title: Charge to 30, Then Open
combos.sequence: Basic Attacks until charge reaches 30+ → Skill 2 (dash) → Enhanced Basic Attack (1s launch and stun) → Skill 3 (Electrified shield + electric wave) → Skill 1 (two swings, healing on each hit)
combos.description: Basic Attack hits build 5-10 charge and skill hits build 8-16; at 30 the mace turns Electrified. The engage hinges on Skill 2 — while Electrified, the Basic Attack after the dash lands a 1s launch and a stun at the same time. Hits from enhanced skills build no charge at all, so once the shield and the heal are spent, go back to Basic Attacks and rebuild.

combos.title: Comeback at Low Health
combos.sequence: Confirm 30+ charge → Enhanced Skill 1 (two swings, healing that scales with the Health you've lost) → Skill 2 (dash out)
combos.description: Skill 1 swings twice and heals on each hit, and while Electrified that healing grows with the Health you're missing. Swing it in your chaser's face, then change your angle with Skill 2's dash. Below 30 charge the healing stays at its base value — check the gauge before you commit to the swing.

strengths: With all three empowered skills up, few clash laners match his overall kit
Empowered Skill 1's healing scales with missing HP for dramatic comebacks
Empowered Skill 2 chains a dash into a reliable stun to start plays
Empowered Ultimate's 1500 shield lets him live in the middle of the brawl
weaknesses: At zero Energy his damage, healing, and CC all turn mediocre at once
Short skill range leaves him helpless against long-range kiting
Needs pre-fight gauge charging, so he reacts poorly on short notice
Skill 2's dash is his only mobility, leaving few retreat options

playstyle.style: An armored bruiser who charges his mace and discharges it in electrified slams. Shields and area slows hold the frontline while his charge cycle creates waves of burst.
playstyle.suited: Players who romanticize the heavyweight blow — fighting to the rhythm of charge and release.

synergy.reason: Compensates for the lack of mobility with speed buffs, facilitating smooth tower sieges with summoned bots.
Peels enemies away, creating a safe environment for Milady to summon bots and land her ultimate.

counters.reason: Ignores the bots and uses high mobility to quickly close the gap and instantly burst them down.
Can easily wipe out entire armies of painstakingly summoned bots with wide AoE skills.

passive.description:
When Milady defeats an enemy, a mechanical minion is summoned to automatically attack other enemies for 6s. At the end of their duration, minions merge with another nearby minion of the same level and upgrade themselves (up to a max of Lvl 3). If there are no suitable minions to merge with, they self-destruct, dealing 200 (200 + 30% magical attack) magical damage (explosion radius increases with minion level).
Minion Basic Attack: 120 (120 + 25% magical attack) magical damage. Health: 500 (500 + 110% magical attack).
Movement Speed: 450 (450 + 10% magical attack).
Minions deal 75% damage to structures. Merging increases Basic Attack and self-destruction damage by 30%, and max Health by 20%.
Up to 4/2/1 minion(s) can exist at the same time. Once exceeding the limit, older minions will attempt to merge or self-destruct.
passive.name: Passive Skill: Mechanical Minions

skill1.description:
Milady commands an aircraft to fly in the target direction, attacking the enemy nearest to it multiple times along its path. Each attack deals 65 (65 + 10% magical attack) magical damage. After every two attacks, the aircraft attacks the nearest target an extra time, dealing 140 (140 + 20% magical attack) magical damage.
Using this skill again during flight splits the aircraft into two smaller aircraft. Each attacks the enemy nearest to it multiple times, dealing 65 (65 + 10% magical attack) magical damage. Enemies attacked by both aircraft have their Movement Speed reduced by 25% for 1.5s.
skill1.name: Skill 1: Air Superiority

skill2.description:
Milady airdrops 2 mechanical minions in the target location, dealing 100 (100 + 20% magical attack) magical damage to nearby enemies upon landing. The mechanical minions activate after a 1s delay to search for the nearest enemy to attack.
She stocks 1 charge of this skill every 12−15s (affected by Cooldown Reduction), up to 3 charges.
skill2.name: Skill 2: Forced Invasion

skill3.description:
Milady fires a signal device at a target enemy or structure, marking it for 3s. Non-structure units are stunned for 0.75s. While marked, the target takes 80 (80 + 4% magical attack) magical damage every 0.5s and is slowed by 15%. When the mark expires, it explodes, dealing magical damage to the target and nearby enemies, equal to 25% of the total damage taken during the mark's duration.
If the target dies while marked, immediately summons 3 mechanical minions. While the Ultimate is active, allied mechanical minions in range gain 100% Attack Speed and Movement Speed, and will rush to attack the marked target.
Can be used on structures, but does not stun them.
skill3.name: Skill 3: Chaos Field

strategy.earlyGame: Milady's job from the first wave is simple: drop robots with Skill 2 and shove everything into the enemy tower. Skill 2 banks a charge roughly every 15 seconds up to three stocks, so resist the urge to dump all of them — with no mobility skill in her kit, a robot dropped at your own feet is the only gank insurance you have. When the enemy jungler vanishes from the minimap, hug your tower. Skip the 4-minute Tyrant fight entirely and keep shoving mid instead; the pressure you generate is what lets your teammates rotate freely.
strategy.midGame: Around the 10-minute mark, the moment the enemy mid laner drifts to a side lane is your cue to take the tower. Your Ultimate fires directly at towers and crystals, ticking damage while the mark lasts and detonating for an extra 25% of the damage dealt when it expires — stack that with your robots and towers evaporate. Never cross an unwarded river alone; a caught Milady is a dead Milady. After the tower falls, don't chase. Wait for the next wave and your Skill 2 stocks to recover before stepping up again, and the throws stop happening.
strategy.lateGame: You lose the burst race against traditional mages late, so win with siege instead. Nobody else can chip high-ground towers while robots soak the tower shots — you don't even need a minion wave to start the job. If the enemy turtles, don't force a dive; grind them down with Skill 1 fighter jets and endless robot waves and win the patience war. Before Overlord or Shadow Tyrant spawns, bank all three Skill 2 stocks about 30 seconds early and the standoff practically plays itself.
strategy.teamfight: Your spot in teamfights is the very back. Keep Skill 2 rolling to feed robots forward, and recast Skill 1 to split the fighter jet in two — enemies clipped by both take a 25% slow that lets your team close the gap. When an assassin jumps you, land your Ultimate on them for the 0.75-second stun, sic your frenzied robots on the target, and walk away. Milady doesn't win face-to-face damage races, so hold your position until you've seen at least one enemy dash hit the ground.

combos.title: Mark-and-Siege
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (drop 2 minions) → Skill 3 (mark the tower) → Skill 1
combos.description: The minions soak the tower's shots while the mark ticks every 0.5s. With Skill 3 running, allied minions in range gain 100% Attack Speed and Movement Speed and rush the marked target. When the mark expires it explodes for 25% of the damage dealt to that target during it (Lvl 1). Structures cannot be stunned, so this is damage only.

combos.title: Anti-Dive Mark
combos.sequence: Skill 3 (0.75s stun) → Skill 2 (drop 2 minions at your feet) → Skill 1 (recast to split)
combos.description: Fired straight at the diver, the signal device stuns for 0.75s and slows by 15%. While the sped-up minions swarm that target, a fresh pair at your feet walls off the approach. Enemies attacked by both split aircraft are slowed 25% for 1.5s (Lvl 1). Kill the target before the mark expires and 3 more minions spawn on the spot.

strengths: Robots soak tower shots, letting her break towers without minions
Ultimate fires directly at towers for the fastest siege of any mage
Every kill spawns another robot, so long brawls tilt numbers her way
Skill 2 stocks keep the shove pressure running nonstop
weaknesses: No mobility skill; once gap-closed she cannot shake pursuers alone
AoE mages that clear her robots in one cast gut her damage
Enemies who kite outside robot range blunt her kill threat
Weak personal burst; loses head-to-head damage races

playstyle.style: A commander mage who spawns robots on takedowns and merges them into stronger units. Her own damage is modest — the army's upkeep and placement is the real weapon.
playstyle.suited: Players who enjoy leading units rather than piloting a carry — winning through the swarm, not the self.

synergy.reason: Fevered Barrage blinks Marco Polo into the enemy team, then walks him through it for 3s. An attached Yaria rides along, and her Skill 2 — range widened 20% while attached — works up to three enemies at once. Attaching also cuts her active skill cooldowns by 30% on the spot.

Cirrus takes flight at level 4 and ignores terrain from then on, carrying an attached Yaria over walls into a gank. His Cloud Descending dash stuns for 0.5s, and Yaria's own Skill 1 — tracking 20% further while attached — reaches the same target. Detaching by hand refunds 50% of her Ultimate's cooldown.

counters.reason: Garo's passive makes her Basic Attacks and skills bite extra hard into shields, so the shield Yaria attaches drains faster than usual. Once it runs out the attachment ends and Yaria is exposed again. Silent Arrow's 0.5s silence lands on her as well.

Gan drops flying swords on a chosen spot and Mo mirrors the same number onto it, doubling every volley. Freshly Forged banks two more uses to fire at once, and the teammate Yaria is attached to eats that whole salvo. Guard Her Grave knocks back while cutting 150 Magical Defense for 3s.

passive.description: When affected by hard crowd control effects (excluding suppression effects), Yaria instantly removes all crowd control effects from herself and turns into a deer spirit for 4s. While in deer spirit form, she gains new skills, and all of her skills' cooldowns are refreshed. During this period, she cannot use Basic Attacks or be targeted, and nearby enemies are slowed by 15%. This effect has a 60−48s cooldown (depending on skill level).
passive.name: Passive Skill: Deer Spirit

skill1.description:
Yaria directs a soul with her staff, dealing 250 (250 + 30% magical attack) magical damage to enemies in its path and knocking them back. The soul will track the nearest enemy hero after reaching its max range, dealing 250 (250 + 30% magical attack) magical damage to them, launching them for 0.5s, and exposing them for 5s.
Deer Spirit Form: Deer spirit form ends instantly.
skill1.name: Skill 1: Wandering Beam

skill2.description:
Yaria deals 200 (200 + 30% magical attack) magical damage to the 3 closest random enemies within 5s, prioritizing heroes. She cannot use Basic Attacks for the duration of the skill.
Deer Spirit Form: Leaps forward.
skill2.name: Skill 2: Accelerating Blitz

skill3.description:
Attaches to a teammate, granting them a shield that negates 1,000 (1,000 + 60% magical attack + 8% of target's extra Health) true damage. Attachment ends when the shield is exhausted or when leaping in the target direction to detach. She becomes untargetable and unable to use Basic Attacks while attached.
Attaching to a hero immediately reduces her active skills' cooldown by 30% and grants them these extra effects:
Skill 1: Soul tracking range increased by 20%.
Skill 2: Attack range increased by 20%.
Ultimate: Manually detaching reduces Ultimate's cooldown by 50%.
Deer Spirit Form: Slow aura's area of effect widened.
skill3.name: Skill 3: Verdant Protector

strategy.earlyGame: Start the game standing behind your mid laner or marksman, letting Skill 2's auto-targeting bolts help with the chip damage while you fire Skill 1 into bushes for safety checks. The energy orb homes in and knocks up any hero it detects, so one cast tells you whether an ambush is waiting. Until Yaria learns her Ultimate attach at level 4, she is honestly just a soft target — take river vision only inside your allies' range, because nothing in her kit justifies walking ahead alone.
strategy.midGame: From level 4 on, the default play is attaching to your best-fed carry — usually the jungler or the marksman. What you hand them is a shield that negates 1,000 true damage, rising to 1,500 and 2,000 as Skill 3 levels up. Attaching immediately cuts your active skills' cooldowns by 30%. That is a one-time reduction at the moment you attach, not a discount that lasts while you ride. What does last for the whole attachment is 20% more tracking range on Skill 1 and 20% more attack range on Skill 2. The key habit: detach yourself before the shield breaks. A manual detach cuts 50% off Skill 3's cooldown, which beats eating the full downtime every time. Hold the attach in reserve right before the 4-minute Tyrant or any Shadow Tyrant fight after 10 minutes.
strategy.lateGame: In late-game teamfights, your one shield decides whether the carry lives. Assassin burst is instant — reacting after the dive starts is usually too late, so climb on as soon as a fight looks likely. Watch the shield's remaining health, hop off just before it shatters to collect the cooldown refund, then climb right back on. The window immediately after you detach is your most dangerous moment; hard CC triggers your Deer form (once per 60 seconds), but it will not save you from the second stun.
strategy.teamfight: Stay mounted on your carry, spread Skill 2's sustained damage, and knock up divers with Skill 1 to blunt their momentum. Your Passive Deer form only triggers on hard CC like knock-ups and knock-backs, making you untargetable while slowing everyone nearby — trading it for one wasted enemy engage tool is a clean win. Picking the right host is part of the job, too. Sitting on an ally nobody is attacking wastes the shield, so identify the one player actually being focused and move.

combos.title: Re-Attach Cycle
combos.sequence: Skill 3 (attach to an ally) → Skill 1 (+20% tracking range) → Skill 2 (+20% attack range) → Skill 3 (leap off to detach)
combos.description: Attaching cuts her active skill cooldowns by 30% at once and widens Skill 1's tracking and Skill 2's attack range by 20% each. The shield she hands over negates true damage, and the attachment ends the moment it is exhausted. Detaching by leaping in a target direction cuts Skill 3's cooldown by 50%, so step off early rather than waiting for the break.

combos.title: Deer-Form Reset
combos.sequence: (Take hard crowd control → deer spirit form) → Skill 2 (deer form: leaps forward) → Skill 1 (deer form: ends the form early) → Skill 3 (re-attach)
combos.description: Hard crowd control other than suppression strips every effect off her and turns her into a deer for 4s. She cannot be targeted in that window, and nearby enemies are slowed by 15% (30% at Lvl 15). All of her cooldowns refresh, so leap clear with Skill 2, drop the form with Skill 1, and put the shield straight back on a carry. The passive runs on a 60−48s cooldown, so a second chain of crowd control has no answer.

strengths: Her all-damage shield cancels one lethal burst on a carry
Manual detach refunds half the cooldown for high shield uptime
Deer form absorbs hard CC and wastes enemy engage tools
Skill 1 scouts bushes and knocks up in a single cast
weaknesses: Zero solo damage or durability; helpless once her team collapses
Deer form runs once per 60 seconds and loses to chained CC
No healing in her kit; drawn-out poke wars wear her down
Attaching to the wrong host throws the entire shield away

playstyle.style: A guardian who possesses an ally and becomes their shield — protection in its final form. Her deer transformation cleanses CC on reflex, and her chosen hero simply does not die alone.
playstyle.suited: Players who never hesitate to be someone's shield, reading the fight through their partner's eyes.

synergy.reason: Guiguzi's Skill 3 camouflages teammates within 1,500 range as well, so Cirrus can reach the back line unseen. Anyone his Skill 1 brushes past loses 25% physical defense for 4s, which raises the landing damage of Soaring Whirlwind.

Yaria's Skill 3 attaches to a teammate and hands over a shield that absorbs 1,000 true damage. Taking it right before the dive lets Cirrus absorb the first shot of the focus fire. Her Skill 1 tracks an enemy hero, launching them for 0.5s and exposing them for 5s.

counters.reason: Liang's Skill 3 suppresses one enemy hero for 2.2s. Suppression blocks skill casts, so Cirrus cannot use Soaring Whirlwind to shed crowd control and slip out. Skill 1 also lines up 4 barriers on his approach, each stunning for 0.75s on contact.

Donghuang's Skill 3 suppresses for 2s, and both sides share all damage taken during it. Cirrus is pinned in place and eats whatever Donghuang eats. Using the skill also spawns 3 dark orbs at once, and each orb that touches him deals magical damage equal to 3% of his Health.

passive.description:
Once Cirrus reaches level 4, he takes flight and can permanently ignore terrain. Using Basic Attacks grants Breath, which increases Movement Speed by 0-60 but drains quickly. When hitting enemies with Basic Attacks or skills, he places stacks of Lacerate on them for 2s, for up to 5 stacks. Lacerated enemies take physical damage equal to 0.24% Health when they move (increases by 0.02% for every 50 extra Physical Attack). Damage increases with stack count, for up to 10 times the initial value.
Lacerated enemies take 4.6 (2.7% physical attack) physical damage every 0.2s. Lacerated heroes only take 50% of this damage when not moving, while minions and monsters take full damage regardless of whether they are moving.
passive.name: Passive Skill: Through the Clouds

skill1.description:
Cirrus charges up, gaining 60% Movement Speed, then dashes forward, gaining a shield that negates 300 (300 + 100% extra physical attack) damage. He deals 200 (200 + 80% extra physical attack) physical damage and stuns enemies hit for 0.5s. If he hits a hero, he can also jump back a certain distance in any direction.
Dashing will knock back non-hero units. Canceling the charge-up will return 20% of the Cooldown.
skill1.name: Skill 1: Cloud Descending

skill2.description: Cirrus throws wind blades, dealing 150 (150 + 50% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies twice and slowing them by 12.5% for 1s. For the next 4s, he gains 20% Attack Speed, and his Basic Attack gains increased range and unleashes 3 razor-sharp feathers. The feathers deal 34 (20% physical attack), 51 (30% physical attack), and 85 (50% physical attack) physical damage respectively, each one traveling farther than the last.
skill2.name: Skill 2: Razor Wind

skill3.description:
Cirrus gains 30% damage reduction for a short time and sweeps the target hero into the air, removing any crowd control effects he is under. During this time, he is untargetable and can move. Upon landing, he deals 360 (360 + 120% extra physical attack) physical damage, and launches the target for 0.5s.
He deals 10% more damage on landing for every stack of lacerate. The target sent flying will only take damage from Cirrus while in the air. Cirrus's Movement Speed in the air scales with his level. If there's no enemy within range as he takes flight, he'll still deal the same amount of damage upon landing.
skill3.name: Skill 3: Soaring Whirlwind

strategy.earlyGame: Level 4 is the first real checkpoint. That is when Cirrus takes flight, and from then on he permanently ignores terrain — there is no upkeep, so once you get there it never drops. The flip side: through level 3 he is a grounded assassin who cannot cross walls, and that stretch is his weakest. Camp clearing runs on Lacerate, the 2-second debuff (up to 5 stacks) his basic attacks and skills apply. Lacerated targets take damage every 0.2s, and minions and monsters take the full amount whether or not they are moving. Camps melt, and level 4 arrives early. Until then keep deep invades rare, since an ambush leaves you no escape route. Only touch the 4-minute Tyrant when your team can collapse on it from both sides.
strategy.midGame: Level 4 is where Cirrus comes online. Approach from over-the-wall angles that wards rarely cover. Skill 1 builds 60% Movement Speed while you hold it (level 1) and dashes forward when you release, stunning whatever it hits for 0.5s. The dash travels straight ahead — it does not swing you around behind the target, so set up the angle yourself before you commit. Only after hitting a hero can you jump a set distance in any direction. Use it to disengage, or to land on the side they are running toward. Canceling the charge-up refunds 20% of the cooldown, so pull out instead of forcing a read that has gone wrong. Basic attacks grant Breath, worth up to 60 Movement Speed, but it drains quickly. You are fast for a few seconds after swinging rather than stacking speed the longer you fight. Finish a core item by 10 minutes and farm isolated side laners to widen the lead.
strategy.lateGame: A frontal late-game collision is a death sentence for Cirrus. Wait at a flank or behind a wall, and commit to the back line only after one or two enemy CC skills have been burned. The order is Skill 1's stun into basic attacks, then Skill 2. Once the wind blades land their slow, you get 4 seconds of 20% Attack Speed with extended basic attack range and three feathers per swing. When everyone turns on you, that is Skill 3. It cuts incoming damage by 30% (level 1; 60% at level 3), clears the crowd control on you, and sweeps the target into the air. While airborne you cannot be targeted and can still move — that is the window that makes their return fire whiff, and it ends in your landing hit. Landing damage rises 10% per stack of Lacerate on the target, so how much you carved before the lift is how hard it lands. Lacerate deals percent-HP damage to enemies while they move, which means a tank trying to run bleeds the most.
strategy.teamfight: Never call the engage yourself. After your tank absorbs the opening, come in from fog straight onto the enemy marksman or mage. Stun with Skill 1 and stack Lacerate with basic attacks. If you get chased, cut their speed with Skill 2's slow and leave straight over a wall — terrain does not apply to you. Skill 3 works as a finisher or as an escape hatch. Landing damage grows 10% per stack of Lacerate, so swinging first and lifting second makes the hit land far heavier. Used defensively, the value is simply the airborne window where nothing can target you. One target at a time. Greeding for a second kill is how you never make it home.

combos.title: Lacerate-Loaded Abduction
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (12.5% slow, Lacerate) → Skill 1 (dash, 0.5s stun) → Basic Attack → Skill 3 (sweep the target into the air)
combos.description: Landing damage rises 10% per stack of Lacerate, so stack first and carry second. Skill 1 grants 60% Movement Speed while charging (Lvl 1), and hitting a hero also lets him jump back in any direction. A target held in the air only takes damage from Cirrus, so your team's follow-up counts for nothing here. The 0.5s launch on landing closes it out.

combos.title: Cleanse and Exit
combos.sequence: Skill 3 (removes crowd control, take flight) → Reposition in the air → Landing (0.5s launch) → Skill 1 (charge speed to disengage)
combos.description: Casting Skill 3 removes every crowd control effect on Cirrus and keeps him untargetable while airborne. Damage taken also drops 30% for a short time (Lvl 1), which is what turns focus fire aside. Even with no enemy in range as he lifts off, the landing still deals its full damage. From there, charge Skill 1 for 60% Movement Speed (Lvl 1) and leave across the terrain his level-4 flight ignores.

strengths: Terrain-ignoring flight opens gank angles wards cannot cover
Lacerate's percent-HP damage bleeds moving targets, tanks included
Skill 3's untargetable window makes enemy burst whiff
Every basic attack grants Breath for a short burst of chase speed
weaknesses: Paper-thin defenses; eating CC first usually means dying first
Skill 1 only dashes straight forward; over-committing leaves no way back
Cannot join teamfights head-on; entry timing is unforgiving
Open ground with no walls strips away his mobility edge

playstyle.style: An assassin who gains permanent flight at level 4 and crosses terrain as if it weren't there. His power is the angle of attack — appearing from over a wall no one was watching.
playstyle.suited: Players who have ever looked at a wall and wished they could cross it. You see terrain as material, not rules.

synergy.reason: Guiguzi's Skill 2 pulls enemies in after 2s and stuns them for 1s. With the group packed together, Li Xin's Skill 2 sweeps its whole path through several of them at once. Landing that pull also shields nearby teammates for 600, covering his way in and out.

Cai Yan's Skill 3 heals the lowest-Health ally in range every 0.5s and adds 200 physical and magical defense, which fits how far forward Li Xin stands. Her Skill 2 stuns for 0.75s on every bounce, opening the gap he has no hard crowd control to make himself.

counters.reason: Zhang Fei's Skill 1 knocks back every enemy hero it hits, shoving Li Xin straight back out after he closes. Skill 3 layers on 1.25s of crowd control immunity and invincibility plus a shield worth 40% of his Health for 15s, so the window Li Xin needs closes.

Allain's Skill 1 launches whoever stands in front of him for 0.75s, and at 3 marks it also grants crowd control immunity, so Li Xin's dash cannot break the sequence. His passive Fury stacks 20% damage reduction and a heal, so the longer the duel runs the wider the gap.

passive.name: Passive Skill: Ashen Razor / Scorched Strikes / Void Slice
passive.description:
Standard Form: Li Xin's Basic Attacks and Chaos Waves grant 10 EXP upon hitting a hero.
Domination Form: Every 1% extra Attack Speed grants 0.15% physical damage reduction. Domination Energy boosts this effect by 50%-100% (scales with Domination Energy).
Revenge Form: Every 1.5 extra physical attack grants 0.1% Attack Speed. Revenge Energy boosts this effect by 50%-100% (scales with Revenge Energy).
Upon transforming from Standard Form to Domination or Revenge Form, Li Xin gains maximum Domination or Revenge Energy (up to the limit of 100). Maintaining the transformation consumes 10 of the respective Energy per second. When transforming between Forms, Li Xin loses all Energy from the current Form and gains (100 - current Energy) Energy for the new Form.

Domination Form: Every 1% extra Attack Speed grants 0.15% physical damage reduction. Domination Energy boosts this effect by 50%-100% (scales with Domination Energy).

skill1.name: Skill 1: Lightning Dash / Righteous Charge / Righteous Fervor
skill1.description: Li Xin dashes in the target direction.

forms.description: Li Xin dashes in the target direction.

Li Xin charges up, then dashes in the target direction, dealing 150 (150 + 50% extra physical attack)-450 (450 + 150% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies in his path, in addition to extra physical damage equal to 12% of the targets' lost Health. The damage maxes out after charging for 1s. While charging, he gains 25% damage reduction and crowd control immunity, and retains crowd control immunity until the dash ends. If charging is interrupted, 40% Cooldown is refunded.

Li Xin purifies slow effects and charges up for up to 3s, gaining crowd control immunity, 80 Movement Speed (diminishes over 2s after charging ends), and recovering 65 (65 + 1% extra Health) Health every 0.5s. While charging, Li Xin automatically uses Basic Attacks, each of which deals 50% of their usual damage. 2 automatic Basic Attacks count as 1 standard Basic Attack.
Charging for 1s grants 45% Attack Speed, diminishing over 2s after charging ends.
Each of Li Xin's Basic Attack hits reduce Righteous Fervor's Cooldown by 1s.
