skill4.skill_name: Skill 4: Dark Awakening / Force Mastery / Force Break

strategy.earlyGame: Until level 4, Li Xin is one of the last heroes in the clash lane you want brawling with. His base mode hits soft, so stick to flicking Skill 2's sword qi from range for last hits and harass, and dash out with Skill 1 the moment someone commits onto you. The Passive's base mode grants bonus EXP whenever a basic attack or Skill 2 tags a hero, so even safe poke pays out experience. Against a lane bully, conceding waves under tower is exactly the right amount of cowardice.
strategy.midGame: At level 4 you leave base mode behind: Skill 3 awakens Light (Dominance), Skill 4 awakens Dark (Berserk). Dominance turns bonus attack speed into physical damage reduction and holds up in a straight brawl. Berserk turns bonus physical attack into attack speed and drowns people in swings. Neither choice is locked for the match. Once awakened, Skill 4 becomes the mode swap — no cooldown, uninterruptible by crowd control, and it deals 200 damage (level 1) to nearby enemies on the switch. What carries over, though, is only (100 − your current energy), so swapping on a full gauge wastes the transfer; spend the mode you are in first. Energy drains 10 per second, so awaken right before contact instead of burning the gauge on the walk over.
strategy.lateGame: Late game, Dominance Li Xin holds the front during tower defenses and Overlord standoffs, using the damage reduction to eat the enemy's opening swing. Berserk Li Xin skips the main fight entirely, split pushing and deleting whoever peels off to stop him in a 1v1. Energy only fills to the cap of 100 when he awakens out of base mode with Skill 3 or Skill 4 — swapping between the two forms hands him just (100 − his current energy). Time the awakening to the engage call and save the swap for when the gauge is already low. Get that order wrong and you run dry mid-fight, back to something close to base-mode Li Xin.
strategy.teamfight: In Dominance, fight half a step behind your tank, sliding Skill 2's sword qi into the crowd and deciding on every cooldown whether to chase with Skill 1 or hold it. The damage reduction is real, but you are not an actual tank — stay out of stacked CC zones. In Berserk, enter from the fight's outer edge and use your attack speed to delete an isolated backliner first. Your best window is the first fight, before the enemy has read your mode — show them steel or show them speed, and warp how they play the rest of the game.

combos.title: Light Awakening Loop
combos.sequence: Skill 3 (Light Awakening: switch modes, energy to 100) → Skill 1 (Righteous Charge: 25% damage reduction while charging, plus damage equal to 12% of the target's lost Health) → enhanced Basic Attack (longer range, piercing, +50% damage) → Skill 2 (Blade Flurry: 4 sword bursts, each restoring Health) → enhanced Basic Attack
combos.description: After Light Awakening, every skill cast upgrades his next Basic Attack into a longer-range piercing hit. Enhanced Basic Attacks and skill hits each cut 1s from every cooldown, which is why a swing belongs between the skills. Blade Flurry heals on each of its four bursts, so it pays off more the longer the trade runs.

combos.title: Seal First, Then Gouge
combos.sequence: Skill 4 (Dark Awakening: switch modes, energy to 100) → Skill 3 (Shadow Seal: a circle that explodes after a delay and launches enemies for 0.75s) → Skill 2 (Brutal Gouge: 25% slow for 2s at Lvl 1, and a gouge) → Basic Attack (his shadow swings as well)
combos.description: Dark Awakening fills Revenge Energy to 100, and it drains 10 per second from there. Shadow Seal detonates on a delay, so plant it first and let the gouge's slow hold them inside the ring. Basic Attacks on a gouged target add damage, and against heroes they return Health too.

strengths: Picks Dominance or Berserk to fit whatever the draft needs
Dominance converts attack speed into damage reduction for brawls
Berserk converts attack into attack speed and drowns 1v1s in swings
Skill 2 sword qi clears waves from a safe distance
weaknesses: Feeble before level 4; a lost lane is slow to repair
Each mode burns 10 energy per second and gases out in long fights
A form swap only grants (100 - current energy), so swapping on a full gauge wastes it
Skill 1 is his only mobility, so layered CC leaves no exit

playstyle.style: A fighter who alternates between the Dominance (light) and Berserk (dark) modes. Light converts attack speed into damage reduction and shortens his cooldowns for a durable, grinding style; dark converts physical attack into attack speed and opens with a knock-up field. Switching transfers energy between the two, so you are always choosing which side to lean on.
playstyle.suited: Players who want to swap between offence and defence as the fight demands, and who treat learning two full skill sets as extra options rather than extra work.

synergy.reason: Ming's Skill 1 links to a teammate, handing over main attack stat and 10% Attack Speed, which offsets the slower attack interval Garo accepts in longbow stance. A direct Skill 2 hit strips an extra 25% magical defense, so the delayed blast from Silent Arrow lands harder.

Zhang Fei's Skill 2 leaps to his teammates and shields everyone in range for 650 plus 13% of his extra Health, standing in for the escape Garo does not have. Skill 1 knocks back any enemy hero it hits, prying assassins off her before they finish the kill.

counters.reason: Marco Polo blinks with Skill 2 on a 5s cooldown, erasing the 125 extra range Garo buys with her longbow. With an enemy hero nearby he deals 20% more damage and gains 15% Movement Speed, and Garo has no movement skill to rebuild the distance.

Gao Changgong holds 30s of stealth from Skill 4 and gains 15-30% Movement Speed while moving toward enemy heroes. Once he arrives, Skill 2 marks Garo and his next attack on that mark stuns her for 1s, leaving no time to reset her longbow.

passive.description: Garo's Basic Attacks and skills deal 50% extra damage against shields.
passive.name: Passive Skill: Piercing Arrow

skill1.description:
Garo enchants her longbow, extending her attack interval by 25% but also increasing her attack range by 125. Every Basic Attack costs 50 Mana and deals an extra 32 (32 + 7% extra physical attack) magical damage every 0.5s for 2s.
This skill can be used again to cancel the enchantment, increasing her Movement Speed by 20 and restoring her attack interval and range. Every Basic Attack restores 6 (5 + 1% physical attack) Mana on hit and an extra 200% Mana when the target is an enemy hero.
skill1.name: Skill 1: Enchanted Arrows

skill2.description:
Garo shoots a piercing arrow in the target direction, dealing 300 (300 + 60% extra physical attack) magical damage to enemies in its path while silencing them for 0.5s and reducing their Movement Speed by 25% for 1s.
After a delay of 1s, the area the arrow passed through explodes, dealing 600 (600 + 120% extra physical attack) magical damage to enemies within range.
She casts the skill faster as she gains Attack Speed. Casting speed increases by 1% for every 1.5% Attack Speed, for a maximum increase of 100%.
skill2.name: Skill 2: Silent Arrow

skill3.description:
Garo creates a magic circle in her current location for 8s. Using this skill again will destroy the magic circle.
When she is in the circle, she gains 20% Movement Speed and 20% Critical Rate. Upon destroying the magic circle, she gains 20% Movement Speed and 20% Critical Rate if she is inside it, or half of these bonuses if she is outside it. Creating or destroying the magic circle will deal 380 (380 + 85% extra physical attack) magical damage to enemies within range.
Passive: Critical hits from her Basic Attacks reduce the target's Movement Speed by 30% for 0.5s. If her Basic Attack lands a critical hit on the same target again within 1s, the Movement Speed reduction is increased to 50%.
skill3.name: Skill 3: Sphere of Purity

strategy.earlyGame: Garo's early game in the farm lane is an exercise in restraint. Skill 1's longbow adds 125 attack range, but every arrow that lands costs 50 Mana and her attack interval stretches by 25%, so leaving it on permanently runs you dry. Use the longbow for wave clear and a few pokes, then stow it — attacks with the bow stowed restore Mana, at triple value against heroes. The faster that toggle becomes a habit, the faster she improves. She has no mobility skill, so stay off the river bushes whenever the enemy jungler is unaccounted for. Until your first crit item finishes, farm beats fighting every time.
strategy.midGame: Garo's game starts around 10 minutes, once one or two crit items are done. The Ultimate's passive slows targets on every critical hit, so as long as you keep landing arrows, nobody closes the distance. When sieging, abuse the longbow's range to chip towers from beyond any retaliation. The moment an enemy initiator shows their face, stop them cold with Skill 2's 0.5-second silence. Walking anywhere alone, however fed you are, remains a death sentence.
strategy.lateGame: A full-build Garo is a stationary artillery platform that deletes everything in reach. Drop Skill 3 underfoot and, while she stands inside the circle, she gains 20% Movement Speed and 20% Critical Rate — the bonus is hers, not the team's. From maximum longbow range the chained crit slows alone keep enemies from ever walking to you. If someone does close in, recast Skill 3 while you are still inside it: destroying the circle grants the same 20% Movement Speed and 20% Critical Rate and deals area damage on the way out. Collapse it from outside and you only get half. Before Overlord fights, glance at your Mana bar first. A Garo who can't afford her longbow is just a slow marksman.
strategy.teamfight: Open teamfights by dropping your Ultimate underfoot and shooting the nearest frontliner from inside the circle. Don't force shots at their backline; hitting whatever is in range is how the crit slows stay unbroken. When an assassin dives, answer with Skill 2's silence and 50% slow, collapse the circle for the speed burst, and kite behind your tank. Her Passive deals 50% bonus damage to shields, so shielded carries — normally the hardest targets on the map — melt fastest of all against Garo.

combos.title: Artillery Emplacement
combos.sequence: Skill 3 (deploy the circle) → Skill 1 (enchant the longbow, +125 range) → Basic Attack (keep firing)
combos.description: Inside the circle she holds 20% Movement Speed and 20% Critical Rate. A critical hit slows the target 30% for 0.5s, and a second crit on the same target within 1s deepens that to 50%. Creating the circle deals damage in range on its own. Every longbow hit costs 50 Mana and her attack interval is longer while it is out, so her uptime is decided by her Mana bar.

combos.title: Silence into Kite
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (0.5s silence, 25% slow) → Skill 3 (recast to collapse the circle) → Skill 1 (stow the longbow, +20 Movement Speed) → Basic Attack (kite)
combos.description: Half a second of silence will not stop a diver; it costs them their opening move. The strip the arrow passed through explodes 1s later for a second, larger hit. Collapsing the circle gives her 20% Movement Speed and 20% Critical Rate if she is still inside it, half that if she has stepped out. Stowing the longbow adds another 20 Movement Speed and restores her attack interval, which is when kiting starts.

strengths: Longbow range is among the longest of any marksman for one-sided poke
Critical hits apply slows that stall anyone walking toward her
Passive deals 50% bonus damage to shields, shredding shield-heavy comps
Standing inside Skill 3's circle gives her 20% Movement Speed and 20% Critical Rate
weaknesses: No mobility skill whatsoever; once touched, her team is the plan
The longbow devours MP, and sloppy management switches her damage off
Longbow mode stretches her attack interval by 25%, losing close-range duels
Little presence before crit items; the early game is pure survival

playstyle.style: The anti-shield specialist: her attacks deal 50% bonus damage to shields. Longbow stance extends her reach while silencing arrows enforce her terms from afar.
playstyle.suited: Players who draft against the enemy composition — the counter-pick mind that answers shield-stacking teams with one clean answer.

synergy.reason: By clumping enemies up, he can maximize Sun Ce's strong AoE damage.
By refreshing his cooldowns, she allows him to unleash his powerful CC combo a second time.

counters.reason: His cleanse ability can completely negate Sun Ce's strong CC combos.
His high sustain and CC resistance allow him to simply face-tank the engage.

passive.description:
Every 6s, Sun Ce's next Basic Attack is enhanced, dealing an extra 209 (110 + 60% physical attack) physical damage and restoring 104 (55 + 30% physical attack + 3% lost Health) Health to him.
Whenever he receives physical damage or true damage or hits a target with a skill, he gains 1 stack of Undaunted, for up to 10 stacks. Each stack increases his Physical Defense by 16-32 for 6s.
passive.name: Passive Skill: Raging Tide

skill1.description:
Sun Ce dashes in the target direction, dealing 199 (125 + 45% physical attack) physical damage to enemies in his path. At the end of the dash, he deals 399 (250 + 90% physical attack) physical damage to enemies within range.
After a short delay, he deals another strike of equal physical damage to enemies within range and launches them for 1s.
skill1.name: Skill 1: Wave Render

skill2.description:
Sun Ce strides forward and hacks at enemies within the target area, dealing 296 (180 + 70% physical attack) physical damage and placing 1 stack of slow on them. Each stack reduces the target's Movement Speed by 15% for 2s, for up to 3 stacks. He can use this skill 3 times before it enters cooldown, with each hack dealing 25% more physical damage than the previous one.
The Cooldown of the Basic Attack is refreshed every time he uses this skill.
skill2.name: Skill 2: Typhoon

skill3.description:
Sun Ce gains crowd control immunity and pilots his ship forward for 12s. While moving, the ship accelerates continuously and knocks back enemy minions and non-ancient monsters in its path, dealing 549 (350 + 120% physical attack) physical damage to them.
He can disembark while moving by using the skill again. When the ship collides with a wall, structure, ancient monster, or enemy hero, or when the time is up, it will explode. The explosion deals 549 (350 + 120% physical attack) physical damage to enemies within range and launches them for 1-1.5s (duration increases with time traveled).
He gains 5 stacks of Undaunted if the ship's explosion hits an enemy.
While he is piloting the ship, a nearby teammate can tap a button to embark. The teammate will disembark when they are hit by hard crowd control, when they use a movement skill, or when Sun Ce disembarks.
skill3.name: Skill 3: Set Sail!

strategy.earlyGame: Sun Ce hunts for lane control with level 2 trades in the clash lane. The core pattern is Skill 1 in, Skill 2, weave a basic attack, then Skill 2 again — each Skill 2 cast hits 25% harder and resets your basic attack cooldown, so punctuating casts with swings hurts far more than mashing. His Passive stacks physical defense every time he takes physical damage, so against AD matchups, brawl freely; the empowered basic attack every 6 seconds heals enough to win the war of attrition.
strategy.midGame: From level 4, the boat is Sun Ce's calling card. While sailing you have super armor — immune to knock-ups and the like — and can carry one teammate, so scooping up your mid laner for a gank is a devastating play. The ideal rhythm: sail to a side lane before the 4-minute Tyrant, create a numbers advantage, then arrive at the pit on spawn. The boat detonates on contact with walls and enemies, knocking targets up, so watch your spacing against terrain, not just your target. Winding routes are where boats go to die.
strategy.lateGame: Late game, Sun Ce is the team's designated engage. The longer the boat sails, the longer the knock-up — up to 1.5 seconds — but steering gets harder too, so pre-plan the shortest hidden approach before you commit. Aim for their backline. If the hit misses, swallow your pride, hop off mid-route, and join the frontline fight with Skill 1 and Skill 2. A boat that connects cleanly on the right target ends the teamfight before it begins; a solo boat launched beyond your team's reach is Sun Ce's single most common way to lose.
strategy.teamfight: Launch from bushes or from behind walls. Hop off just before impact so only the boat connects — you stay free to act during the knock-up, letting you layer a max-range Skill 1 for the second knock-up in the chain. With the target locked down, unload all three Skill 2 casts with basic attacks in between. While enemy Flashes are still up, holding the boat and firing it as the follow-up to an ally's CC is the disciplined play. With his defense stacks rolling, Sun Ce is far harder to kill than he looks.

combos.title: Ram and Double Launch
combos.sequence: Skill 3 (set sail, crowd control immunity) → Collide with a hero or wall (explosion launches for 1-1.5s) → Skill 1 (dash its full distance) → Skill 2 ×3
combos.description: The explosion's launch scales with how long the ship travelled, so a longer approach buys a longer hold. A connecting explosion also returns 5 stacks of Undaunted, which is what keeps him standing in the brawl. Dashing Skill 1 its full distance adds an area hit, and a second strike lands shortly after to launch again for 1s. Walls and structures set the ship off too, so scout the route before you commit.

combos.title: Lane Trade Cadence
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (dash) → Skill 2 → Basic Attack → Skill 2 → Basic Attack → Skill 2
combos.description: Each Skill 2 cast refreshes his Basic Attack cooldown. Weaving a swing between hacks beats spamming them, and every hack deals 25% more than the one before it. The slow stacks up to three times, 15% each for 2s (Lvl 1). His enhanced Basic Attack comes back every 6s with healing attached, and every skill hit adds an Undaunted stack for more Physical Defense.

strengths: The boat crosses the map and ferries an ally straight into ganks
Boat explosion plus Skill 1 chains two knock-ups back to back
Stacks physical defense when hit, winning drawn-out AD brawls
Empowered-attack healing outlasts lane wars of attrition
weaknesses: The boat detonates on walls, so one steering error wastes the engage
Missing both the boat and Skill 1 leaves no CC and easy kiting
Solo engages without follow-up lock enemies down but kill nothing
Noticeably soft at fight start before his defense stacks build

playstyle.style: A fighter who sails a ship into the enemy team. The boat opens the fight, then he disembarks and brawls, sustained by empowered-attack healing. Ninety percent of playing him is the entrance.
playstyle.suited: Players who want to personally start every teamfight — and dream of engages that carry the whole enemy team with them.

synergy.reason: Pulling enemies together makes it much easier for Wan'er to land the AoE burst from her intersecting brush strokes.

counters.reason: His point-and-click suppression CC interrupts her dash, stopping her from taking flight.

passive.description:
Enhances every 3rd Basic Attack, dealing an extra 255 (255 + 50% magical attack) magical damage to enemies in a line. When brush strokes intersect, nearby enemies take 255 (255 + 50% magical attack) magical damage (damage is reduced by 50% for successive hits within 1s).
Recovers 100 (100 + 22% magical attack) Health and gains an enhanced Basic Attack when near intersecting brush strokes.
passive.name: Passive Skill: Piercing Brush

skill1.description: Flings a powerful drop of ink in the target direction, dealing 200 (200 + 40% magical attack) magical damage to enemies hit. Upon reaching the end of its range, the ink explodes, dealing 200 (200 + 40% magical attack) magical damage to nearby enemies.
skill1.name: Skill 1: Ink Burst

skill2.description:
With her current location as the finishing point, Shangguan starts writing from a target location, dealing 150 (150 + 20% magical attack) magical damage where her brush lands. Enemies touched by her brush strokes take 300 (300 + 40% magical attack) magical damage and are slowed by 25% for 2s.
This skill can be stocked every 10s (affected by Cooldown Reduction), for up to 2 uses.
skill2.name: Skill 2: Seething Script

skill3.description:
Dashes wildly with her brush, dealing 250 (250 + 32% magical attack) magical damage to enemies in her path. If she hits an enemy or ink left behind by another active skill, she can dash again in the target direction within 3s. If she dashes 3-5 times, she will jump into the air, becoming untargetable and cleansed of all crowd control effects, and perform continuous attacks on nearby enemies, dealing 460 (460 + 70% magical attack) magical damage. The number of attacks is decided by the number of dashes, with 3/4/5 dashes yielding 4/7/10 attacks. When hitting the same unit multiple times, subsequent hits deal only 25% damage.
She can dash up to 5 times, and she can attack and use skills between dashes. If interrupted, the skill's Cooldown is reduced by 20%-80%, depending on the number of dashes performed.
skill3.name: Skill 3: Finishing Stroke

strategy.earlyGame: Before level 4, Shangguan is a paper mage who can't take off yet. Use Skill 2's brush and Skill 1's ink for wave clear, and fish for the Passive detonation that triggers where the two trails cross — it chips enemies and heals you at the same time. Simply playing around that intersection roughly doubles your harass output on the exact same casts. Her gank resistance is poor, so sit toward your tower whenever river vision is down, and don't bother showing up for the 4-minute Tyrant before level 4.
strategy.midGame: The moment you learn your Ultimate, Shangguan becomes an assassin. Dash three to five times through ink or enemies and you ascend — untargetable, cleansed of all CC, raining ink on everything below, with five dashes granting the maximum number of strikes. You can do this under an enemy tower with total impunity, so the mid-game job is roaming to the farm lane and solo-diving the enemy marksman. With a core item done by around 10 minutes, anyone caught under a clean take-off simply melts.
strategy.lateGame: Late game, one failed take-off can be the losing moment of the match. If your dashes get interrupted you are stranded in the middle of five enemies, so before committing, confirm the enemy's lethal lockdown — any suppression-style ultimate — has already been spent. Always enter from a flank. Poke with the Skill 2 into Skill 1 crossing detonation until your target drops below roughly 70% HP and their escape is burned, and your take-off success rate climbs dramatically. The landing recovery is long, so have the discipline to skip take-offs you can't confirm.
strategy.teamfight: Spend the fight's opening at the back, scattering crossing detonations and collecting the heals while you read the fight. Two or more enemy CCs down is the take-off signal. You can dash along your own ink trails without touching a single enemy, so pre-draw your approach route in ink. Once airborne, the strikes fire automatically at whatever stands nearby, which makes the launch point everything — land your final dash right beside their carry. Repeat hits on the same unit deal only 25% damage, so a position that catches two or three bodies adds up to more total damage. Land toward your own team, always. Taking off through the enemy frontline is a mistake everyone in the lobby can identify.

combos.title: Ink First, Then Take Off
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (brush stroke, 2s slow) → Skill 1 (lay ink across it) → Skill 3 (5 dashes along the trails)
combos.description: Where ink from two different skills meets, nearby enemies take extra damage. Touching her own strokes restores Health and readies an enhanced Basic Attack. Every dash that clips an enemy or another skill's ink buys another dash within 3s, so the route you draw first decides how far the chain runs. Five dashes turn into 10 strikes from the air, and she is untargetable and cleansed of all crowd control throughout.

combos.title: Bent-Route Take Off
combos.sequence: Skill 2 → Skill 3 (2 dashes) → Skill 1 (fresh ink on the route) → Skill 3 (last 3 dashes)
combos.description: She can cast between dashes, so a new ink line mid-chain bends the approach angle. Run out of things to touch and the chain simply stops; breaking it there refunds 20-80% of the cooldown depending on how many dashes went out. Three dashes yield only 4 strikes from the air. Decide before the first dash whether five are actually reachable.

strengths: Untargetable and CC-immune while airborne, dealing unanswerable damage
Crossing brush and ink detonations poke and heal simultaneously
Solo tower dives delete enemy backliners from level 4 onward
Flexible dash routes make her entry angle nearly unreadable
weaknesses: Among the hardest heroes in the game; one missed dash means death
Hard CC before take-off shuts down her entire game plan
Long landing recovery invites the counter-kill if the target survives
Minimal self-defense before level 4 and extremely gankable

playstyle.style: An ambush mage who detonates intersecting ink strokes. Skill 3 chains a fresh dash every time she clips an enemy or a stroke, up to five; three or more launches her skyward, untargetable while the strikes rain down.
playstyle.suited: Players who love puzzle-combos with linking conditions — and the omnipotence of a fully-routed flight.

synergy.reason: Lam's Skill 3 drags enemies to where his dagger landed. Allain's Death at Sunset rewards exactly that clustering, dealing up to 100% more damage the closer the targets are. Lam's passive adds true damage to anyone under 30% Health, so fewer escape the follow-up.

Yaria's Skill 3 attaches to Allain with a shield scaled by 8% of his extra Health, which suits a bruiser build. She cannot be targeted while attached, so she rides through his Moonlight Flash dashes. Her Skill 2 auto-fires at the 3 closest enemies during the brawl.

counters.reason: Donghuang's Skill 3 suppresses for 2s, cutting off Allain's attack chain and the Fury he builds from it. Both sides share damage taken during the suppression, so Allain bleeds while his own team focuses Donghuang. Dark Impact's third orb adds a 1s stun.

passive.description:
Allain's Basic Attack speed is very high. For each attack, he strikes once with each of his dual swords Crimson Shadow and Spirit Guardian, dealing 75 (22 + 30% physical attack) magical damage and 75 (22 + 30% physical attack) physical damage. Every first Basic Attack lets him dash to the target. Every third Basic Attack, he swings both swords at the same time, dealing 115 (36 + 45% physical attack) true damage and then entering a longer Basic Attack cooldown. When his Basic Attacks and skills hit enemy heroes, he gains Fury, increasing his Physical and Magical Pierce by up to 40% and damage reduction by up to 20%. Upon reaching max Fury, he recovers 168 (80 + 50% physical attack) Health, with a cooldown of 8s.
The lower his current Health, the more Health he recovers, for up to 3 times the base recovery.
His Physical Lifesteal takes 75% effect and applies to magical and true damage. His Basic Attacks only carry 60% of on-hit effects.
passive.name: Passive Skill: Howling Blade

skill1.description:
Allain swipes upward, dealing 177 (110 + 38% physical attack) magical damage, 177 (110 + 38% physical attack) physical damage twice, and launching targets directly in front of him for 0.75s. After the initial strikes of this skill, he performs different follow-up strikes depending on how many marks he has stacked.
1 Mark: Strikes twice more, the first strike dealing 177 (110 + 38% physical attack) magical damage and the second strike dealing 177 (110 + 38% physical attack) physical damage.
2 Marks: Increases the launch range and strikes another 2 times, the first strike dealing 177 (110 + 38% physical attack) magical damage and the second strike dealing 177 (110 + 38% physical attack) physical damage. He can move slowly while performing the strikes.
3 Marks: Increases the launch range and strikes another 2 times, the first strike dealing 177 (110 + 38% physical attack) true damage and the second strike dealing 312 (180 + 75% physical attack) true damage. He can move slowly and gains crowd control immunity while performing the strikes.
He gains stacks when his Ultimate and Basic Attacks hit enemies. Skill 1 can trigger 50% of the Basic Attack's on-hit effects, and can grant lifesteal and deal critical damage.
skill1.name: Skill 1: Meteor Kill

skill2.description:
Allain dashes in the target direction, dealing 144 (100 + 25% physical attack) physical damage and 144 (100 + 25% physical attack) magical damage to enemies in his path and reducing their Movement Speed by 15% for 1.5s. He also gains 10% Movement Speed for 3s, and his next 3 Basic Attacks gain 40% extra Attack Speed.
He stocks 1 charge of this skill every 10s (affected by Cooldown Reduction), for up to 2 charges.
skill2.name: Skill 2: Moonlight Flash

skill3.description:
Allain selects a target hero and leaps into the air for 1.5s, during which he can move and is untargetable. He then smashes into the ground, dealing 254 (175 + 45% physical attack) physical damage and 254 (175 + 45% physical attack) magical damage to enemy heroes. The closer the heroes are to him, the more damage they take, for up to 100% extra damage. He gains marks and Fury for every enemy hero hit.
This skill produces different effects depending on whether the targeted hero is an enemy or a teammate. When he lands, he grants himself or the targeted teammate a shield that negates 627 (450 + 100% physical attack) damage. For every extra enemy hero hit, the shield's strength is increased by 1/3.
skill3.name: Skill 3: Death at Sunset

strategy.earlyGame: Allain's first rule in the clash lane: never commit before your marks are stacked. Marks build from basic attacks and Ultimate hits, and at three stacks Skill 1 becomes a different move entirely — true damage, super armor, and a wide knock-up. Until level 4, build marks through short basic-attack exchanges, fire Skill 1, and step back without chasing. His Passive heal at full rage scales with missing HP — up to triple — so a slightly bruised Allain wins brawls that look even on paper.
strategy.midGame: From about 10 minutes, once a lifesteal item finishes, Allain stops losing side-lane 1v1s. His Passive cuts item lifesteal to 75% of its effect, but in exchange it drains from his magical and true damage as well. Each basic attack lands one magical and one physical hit, with true damage added on every third — damage that would normally heal him for nothing now feeds the drain. The base pattern is split pushing to bait defenders, then running them down with Skill 2 dashes. Join teamfights late from a flank bush, and time Skill 3's 1.5-second untargetable window against the enemy's biggest skill to make it hit nothing but air.
strategy.lateGame: Your late-game job is diving the enemy carry — but always on the counterpunch. Wait for enemy CC to land on your teammates, then close with Skill 2 and deliver basic attacks into a three-stack Skill 1. The Ultimate can finish a chase, but the play that wins late games is casting it on an ally the instant you're focused: you vanish for 1.5 seconds, share the landing shield, and reset the exchange. The one thing to never forget — the moment marks and rage lapse, Allain turns abruptly soft.
strategy.teamfight: Pick the single most dangerous enemy and refuse to leave them alone. Skill 2 holds two charges, so spend the first to close and the second to cut off the escape route. Three basic attacks into Skill 1 pushes through most interrupts thanks to super armor, lifting everyone around the target. Because rage grants penetration and damage reduction as it builds, Allain is at his strongest in a fight's second half — surviving the opening volley is the entire job description.

combos.title: Three-Mark Skill 1
combos.sequence: Basic Attack ×3 (build marks) → Skill 1 (fire it at 3 marks)
combos.description: Marks come from his Basic Attacks and from Skill 3 hits. One mark already adds follow-up strikes, but three widens the launch range, adds two true-damage strikes, and grants crowd control immunity on top. He can even walk slowly through those strikes, so small interrupts do not break them. Fired bare, Skill 1 is a 0.75s launch and nothing more.

combos.title: Dash-Fed All-In
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (dash, next 3 Basic Attacks speed up) → Basic Attack ×3 (marks) → Skill 1 (3 marks) → Skill 3 (dive on a target hero)
combos.description: Skill 2 stocks a charge every 10s and holds two of them. The three sped-up swings after the dash are exactly the three marks Skill 1 wants. Skill 3 hits harder the closer the heroes are, up to double damage, and every hero caught by the landing returns marks and Fury for the next rotation.

combos.title: Ally-Targeted Escape
combos.sequence: Skill 3 (target an ally, 1.5s airborne) → Landing (shield for him and the ally) → Skill 2 (leave)
combos.description: Leaping the instant focus fire arrives buys 1.5s of being untargetable, with free movement on top. The shield grows by a third for every enemy hero the landing damages, so the middle of the fight is the thicker place to come down. The smash still deals its damage even when the pick was a teammate. Treat it as a way back into the fight, not only as an exit.

strengths: Physical, magic, and true damage; no defensive build blanks him
Lifesteal runs at 75% effect but drains from his magical and true damage too
Three-stack Skill 1 is a super-armored, wide-area knock-up
One Skill 3 covers chasing, dodging, and shielding an ally
weaknesses: His real damage only arrives once marks and rage are stacked
Chained slows and kiting starve his stacks and his healing
Basic attacks apply item effects at only 60%, demanding build knowledge
Mobility lives on Skill 2; with charges spent he can't chase or run

playstyle.style: A swordsman who deals physical, magical, and true damage all at once — there is no right defense against him. Knock-up chains flow into an untargetable ultimate that resets the exchange.
playstyle.suited: Players who like an all-rounder that resists counter-building, with a vanishing act to punctuate every combo.

synergy.reason: His movement speed boost and healing heavily support the kiting needed to maintain the soul chain.

counters.reason: Her excessive mobility makes it easy to break the soul chain and kite away.

passive.description:
Augran's Basic Attacks vibrate his dagger-axe to resonate with an enemy's soul for 3s. The soul resonance deals 88 (50% physical attack) physical damage upon connection and will continue to deal damage with increasing frequency unless it is broken. When it ends, it deals a further 211 (70 + 80% physical attack) magical damage.
The soul resonance's initial and final damage carry 100% of the on-hit effect, while the rest carries 50%.
passive.name: Passive Skill: Soul Resonance

skill1.description:
Augran carves a path to the afterlife, dealing 280 (280 + 95% extra physical attack) magical damage to targets it hits.
The path accelerates after hitting walls or the Life-Death Border, then deals an additional 150 (150 + 60% extra physical attack) magical damage to enemies hit. While on the path, Augran ignores terrain and gains 50% Movement Speed. The first time the path hits a wall, it creates an afterlife bridge. When Augran traverses the bridge, he gains a burst of Movement Speed, while nearby enemies are slowed by 15%.
Augran can use this skill again to recall his dagger-axe, entering the Seer State for 4s. If his Basic Attacks target an enemy with less than 10% Health (750-1,500 for monsters depending on hero level), Augran will instantly execute them.
This skill deals full contact damage to non-hero units. The dagger-axe will automatically be summoned back when the skill's cooldown ends.
skill1.name: Skill 1: Path of Passing

skill2.description:
Augran swings his dagger-axe, dealing 200 (200 + 60% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies in front and slowing them by 25% for 1s. He then leaves behind a Life-Death Border, marking enemies who touch it. Enemies who touch the dead branches on the border also take 140 (140 + 45% extra physical attack) magical damage and are slowed by 25% for 1s.
Augran enhances his next Basic Attack, dealing 50% extra damage to the target and recovering 80 (80 + 1.5% extra Health) Health for himself. If there are marked enemies within range, the resonance applies the same extra damage and recovery effect for each marked target.
This skill also knocks back non-hero units. The resonance can link to up to 3 targets. When resonating with non-hero units, the recovery effect is only 50% effective.
skill2.name: Skill 2: Death's Precipice

skill3.description:
Augran channels his divine power and descends from the sky, dealing 380 (380 + 150% extra physical attack) physical damage to nearby enemies and knocking them back for 0.5s. If he hits an enemy hero, he recovers 750 (750 + 12% extra Health) Health and conjures their spirit counterparts to assist him for 8s.
After descending, he enters the Seer State for 8s. If his Basic Attacks hit a target with less than 10% Health (750-1,500 for monsters depending on hero level), they will deal a fatal blow instantly.
Every enemy hero hit increases recovery by 50%, up to a max increase of 100%. The conjured spirits inherit 30% of Augran's physical attack. They can only use Basic Attacks, but have higher Movement Speed and Attack Speed.
skill3.name: Skill 3: Conductor of Souls

strategy.earlyGame: Augran's jungle clear runs on never letting the Passive's soul link drop. Basic attacks tether souls, and weaving in Skill 2's empowered attack pushes damage and healing into several targets at once — double camps barely scratch your HP bar. Full clear to a fast level 4, then lay down Skill 1's path and gank from an angle the terrain was supposed to forbid. Pick the lane where the enemy is overextended rather than the one being shoved in; the success rates aren't close. Take the 4-minute Tyrant off the momentum of a converted gank.
strategy.midGame: From level 4, Skill 1's path becomes the axis of your game. On the path you ignore terrain and move 50% faster, and touching a wall builds a bridge that accelerates you further — arriving behind someone from a route that never appears on their screen is a feeling no other jungler offers. In fights, Skill 2's wall marks multiple enemies so your empowered attacks drain all of them at once; that healing is your lifeline. When a target runs low, recast Skill 1 for the execute stance and finish anyone under 10% HP with a basic attack. Learn to harvest that final sliver and your kill count doubles.
strategy.lateGame: In late teamfights, the correct Augran timing is right after the opening burst exchange ends. Your burst is modest, but as long as links and walls keep touching multiple enemies, the healing never stops — the longer the brawl runs, the harder you are to remove. Once low-HP enemies start piling up, drop the Ultimate into their midst. Its healing scales with every enemy hero struck, up to double, and the landing grants 8 seconds of execute stance to cull dying targets in sequence. The phantom that mirrors an enemy even papers over a numbers disadvantage now and then.
strategy.teamfight: Position where the soul link can reach at least two enemies at all times. Place Skill 2's wall across predicted paths so every marked enemy eats the empowered attack's echo and feeds you healing. The Ultimate also doubles as an emergency heal button — cast even after the focus fire lands, it often stands you back up. The only real fear is chained CC. Both the links and the executes require standing next to enemies, so against multiple stunners, wait until your teammates have baited the CC out before stepping forward.

combos.title: Path Through the Border
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (Death's Precipice: leaves a Life-Death Border, 25% slow for 1s at Lvl 1) → Skill 1 (Path of Passing: drive it into that border for bonus damage; on the path he ignores terrain and gains 50% Movement Speed at Lvl 1) → enhanced Basic Attack (+50% damage and Health back) → Skill 1 recast (Seer State for 4s: executes targets under 10% Health)
combos.description: The path accelerates the moment it meets a wall or the Life-Death Border, and every hit after that carries bonus magical damage. Drop the border first and run the path through it, and the upgrade no longer depends on where the walls happen to be. Enemies who touch the border are marked, and the resonance copies the enhanced Basic Attack's extra damage and healing onto every marked target.

combos.title: Descend and Spread the Marks
combos.sequence: Skill 3 (Conductor of Souls: descend, 0.5s knockback; hitting an enemy hero restores Health and conjures spirits for 8s) → Skill 2 (Death's Precipice: the border marks several at once) → enhanced Basic Attack (extra damage and healing on every marked target) → Basic Attack (Seer State for 8s: executes targets under 10% Health)
combos.description: Recovery on the descent grows 50% per enemy hero hit, capped at double. Its crowd control is a knockback that shoves enemies away instead of pinning them, so do not plan a lockdown around it. The more targets the border marks, the more the healing stacks — the resonance links 3 at most.

strengths: Soul links and empowered attacks heal off several enemies at once
Execute stance culls anyone who drops below 10% HP
The terrain-ignoring path hides his gank angles completely
Ultimate's huge heal and phantom flip losing brawls
weaknesses: Low burst; enemies who disengage early escape his damage
Healing and executes demand melee range, so chained CC ruins him
Link damage needs time to ramp and loses short exchanges
Managing the path and recasts is busy work that takes practice

playstyle.style: A fighter who links souls with his halberd and partitions the battlefield with walls of life and death. Enemies caught in his territory take escalating damage — he doesn't chase, he encloses.
playstyle.suited: Players who like building their own terrain — architects who think in setup first, execution second.

synergy.reason: Zhang Fei's Skill 2 leaps in and grants teammates in range a shield that negates 650 damage, so Ao'yin can spend the 10s of True Dragon Sword while holding a forward position. His Skill 3 blows enemies back and stuns those caught at the end of the gust for 1.5s.

counters.reason: Arli blinks with Skill 1, and while her parasol is left behind she gains 30-60 Movement Speed. Ao'yin's sword energy covers an area but cannot keep pace with that footwork. Skill 2 knocks down nearby projectiles, and Skill 3 pushes him back out of range.

Consort Yu's Skill 2 makes her immune to physical attacks for 2s. Almost all of Ao'yin's output is physical, so only the true damage portion of Flaming Palm still lands. The same skill clears every slow on her, undoing the 15% slow from Infinite Vastness.

passive.description:
The elemental Dragon Souls from Ao'yin's last 2 skill attacks will be attached to his primary and secondary swords. He deals 165 (100% physical attack) physical damage with his primary sword, and if there are other enemies nearby he will also attack them with his secondary sword to deal 57 (35% physical attack -70% physical attack) physical damage.
When using skills, he gains 1 Dragon Soul mark (up to 3 marks) and 1 enhanced Basic Attack. Using the enhanced Basic Attack expends all marks, unleashing Dragon Souls that attack the target (Each mark grants 1 extra attack, with subsequent hits dealing half damage). Effects vary depending on the type of Dragon Soul attached to his primary sword.
When switching between elements, Dragon Souls of the same element is prioritized.
passive.name: Passive Skill: Hidden Dragon

skill1.description:
Ao'yin unleashes a wave of sword energy, gaining 1 extra Dragon Soul mark and dealing 270 (270 + 70% extra physical attack) physical damage and 70 (70 + 16% extra physical attack) true damage (and 50% splash damage behind the target) to up to 3 targets within range.
Use of Flaming Palm attaches 1 Fire Dragon Soul to his sword, allowing him to deal an extra 15 physical damage during Basic Attacks. If a Fire Dragon Soul is attached to both swords, he deals 50% more damage. If a Fire Dragon Soul is attached to his primary sword, the first strike of his enhanced Basic Attack will deal 97 (48 + 30% physical attack) true damage while the subsequent two strikes will deal an equal amount of physical damage.
Skill use speed scales with Attack Speed.
skill1.name: Skill 1: Flaming Palm

skill2.description:
Ao'yin unleashes sword energy, dealing 180 (180 + 45% extra physical attack) physical damage to up to 3 targets within range (dealing 50% splash damage behind the targets), and recovering 150 (150 + 2.5% extra Health) Health upon hit.
Use of Downpour attaches 1 Water Dragon Soul to his sword, allowing him to recover 18 Health and 0.5% Mana from Basic Attacks. If a Water Dragon Soul is attached to both swords, he recovers 50% more. If a Water Dragon Soul is attached to his primary sword, his enhanced Basic Attacks will deal 97 (48 + 30% physical attack) physical damage each strike, for a total of 3 strikes. Landing a hit on the enemy recovers 150 (150 + 2.5% extra Health) Health.
Recovery effects are halved against non-hero units. Skill use speed scales with Attack Speed.
skill2.name: Skill 2: Downpour

skill3.description:
Ao'yin unleashes a wave of sword energy, gaining 30% Movement Speed (diminishes over time). He also deals 180 (180 + 45% extra physical attack) physical damage (with 50% splash damage) to up to 3 targets within range and knocks them back.
Use of Riding the Wind attaches 1 Wind Dragon Soul to his sword, granting him 16 Movement Speed. If a Wind Dragon Soul is attached to both swords, he gains an extra 50% Movement Speed. If a Wind Dragon Soul is attached to his primary sword, he will deal 97 (48 + 30% physical attack) physical damage and knock back the enemy with every strike of his enhanced Basic Attack, for a total of 3 strikes.
Skill use speed scales with Attack Speed.
skill3.name: Skill 3: Riding the Wind

skill4.description:
Ao'yin reveals his true white dragon form and soars into the sky for up to 4.5s, then dives forward. During this time, he is untargetable and ignores terrain, but cannot attack. He deals 400 (400 + 80% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies in his path and slows them by 15%.
Upon landing, he deals the same amount of physical damage and applies Dread to nearby enemies for 1s. Targets afflicted with Dread will involuntarily move away from Ao'yin.
Ao'yin then unsheathes his True Dragon Sword, gaining 20% Attack Speed and 25 Attack Range, and the ability to attack up to two additional targets for 10s.
Ao'yin can switch his swords' elemental Dragon Souls while in flight.
Flight speed increases with his Ultimate's level.
skill4.name: Skill 4: Infinite Vastness

strategy.earlyGame: Ao'yin spends the early farm lane playing around Skill 2. It sweeps up to three targets with sword energy and restores Health on hit, and with a Water Dragon Soul on his primary sword every strike of the enhanced Basic Attack heals him again. Recovery is halved against non-hero units, so the real refund comes from landing it on the enemy laner. Refunding poke on his own is what separates him from most marksmen. Every skill cast banks a Dragon Soul mark (up to three), and the enhanced Basic Attack spends them all in one flurry, so waves die faster if you stack marks before swinging. Until your first attack-speed core item is done, your job is collecting CS from behind your support's shoulder, nothing more.
strategy.midGame: Around 10 minutes with two core items, Ao'yin's engine revs up. Skills 1 through 3 all cast faster as his Attack Speed rises, so the more speed you build, the tighter the loop between casts and enhanced Basic Attacks. Open trades with Skill 1 — the true damage folded into it goes through armor — then cash in an enhanced Basic Attack while holding three marks. If someone sticks to you, Skill 3's sword energy knocks them back and buys the space. Skill 4's flight and dive is the control window: the landing Dread drives enemies away from him, and for the next 10 seconds he gains 25 Attack Range and bonus Attack Speed. Hold it as the trump card for taking or defending towers.
strategy.lateGame: Late-game Ao'yin wins through flexibility: heal with Skill 2 when you get chipped, take Skill 3's speed boost when you need to disengage, lead with Skill 1 when you want damage through. His last two casts decide which Dragon Souls sit on his primary and secondary swords, and those decide what the next enhanced Basic Attack does. Taking one beat to ask which element you actually want is what separates good Ao'yin players from great ones. Matching the same soul on both swords amplifies its effect by half, so repeating a skill is a legitimate choice. At Overlord standoffs, hold a spacing where enemy CC can't reach you and shove diving frontliners off with Skill 3's knockback.
strategy.teamfight: In teamfights, Ao'yin sits behind the frontline and keeps the damage flowing. Never start the fight yourself — wait out one or two enemy dash skills first. If someone sticks to you, answer with Skill 3: the sword energy knocks them back, and with a Wind Dragon Soul on his primary sword all three strikes of the enhanced Basic Attack knock back as well. Heal the chip damage off with Skill 2. The moment the enemy's momentum fully dies is the cue for Skill 4 — the dive and the landing Dread scatter them, and the True Dragon Sword gives you 10 seconds of extra range, Attack Speed, and up to two additional targets per swing. His secondary sword strikes a second nearby enemy on its own, so the messier the brawl, the higher his real output. Simply walking around holding two or three marks changes your burst when a pick appears.

combos.title: Three-Mark Flurry
combos.sequence: Skill 3 (Movement Speed and knockback) → Skill 1 (grants an extra mark) → Enhanced Basic Attack (spend every mark)
combos.description: Each skill cast banks 1 Dragon Soul mark and 1 enhanced Basic Attack, and Skill 1 adds a second mark by itself. Marks cap at 3. The enhanced Basic Attack spends all of them, each mark adding one more strike, with everything after the first at half damage. His swords carry the souls of his last 2 skill attacks, so with a Fire Dragon Soul on the primary sword the flurry opens with true damage.

combos.title: Dive and Take Over
combos.sequence: Skill 4 (soar up to 4.5s, then dive forward) → Landing (1s Dread) → Basic Attack (True Dragon Sword, up to 2 extra targets) → Skill 1 (rebuild marks)
combos.description: In the air he is untargetable and ignores terrain, but he cannot attack at all. Dread forces enemies to move away from him, so it scatters a group rather than pinning it. The real payoff is the 10s after landing: 20% Attack Speed (Lvl 1), 25 extra Attack Range, and hits on up to two additional targets. Souls can be swapped mid-flight, so choose the element you want before you touch down.

combos.title: Reset When Stuck To
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (heals on hit) → Enhanced Basic Attack (Water Dragon Soul on the primary sword: heals per strike) → Skill 3 (knock them back)
combos.description: Skill 2 hits up to 3 targets and returns Health on every hit. With a Water Dragon Soul on his primary sword, the enhanced Basic Attack lands 3 strikes and each one that connects heals him again. If they are still on him, Skill 3 knocks them back and adds 30% Movement Speed (Lvl 1) to re-space. None of these three moves relocate him — this is healing and a shove, not a dodge.

strengths: His skills cast faster as Attack Speed rises, so speed items buy raw volume
Skill 2's healing lets him refund poke himself, rare for a marksman
Skill 3's knockback shoves off anyone who sticks to him
Banked marks and Skill 4's dive cover both burst and area control
weaknesses: Skill order changes his buffs, and a misplay directly cuts his damage
The loop is slow before attack-speed items, muting his early pressure
Disengage means Skill 3's speed boost or a long-cooldown Skill 4; layered CC runs him down
Busy piloting; sloppy mark management leaves him a jack of no trades

playstyle.style: A twin-blade marksman whose Dragon Souls change with his recent casts, his main and off-blade striking separate targets at once. His real output in brawls exceeds what the numbers suggest.
playstyle.suited: Players who study how damage is actually delivered — theorists who pick soul combinations to match the situation.

synergy.reason: Guiguzi's Skill 2 pulls enemies in and stuns them for 1s. Against a target held in place, Haya lands Crescent Wave and Wayward Rays back to back and triggers the mark for a 0.5s stun. Guiguzi's own passive enhanced Basic Attack slows for 1.5s, which helps her link hold.

Nakoruru's Skill 3 charges into an area, slowing the enemies it hits by 25% for 3s. The same charge cuts the damage they deal by 30%. A hero Haya links to struggles to walk out of range and hits back softer, so Moonscape Mirage runs its full 1.5s.

counters.reason: Arli blinks with Skill 1, then teleports back to her parasol if she uses the skill again within 4s. Two displacements are enough to break the Moonscape Mirage link. Skill 3's knockback pushes Haya away as well, and Crescent Wave whiffs against the blink.

Donghuang's Skill 3 suppresses for 2s, leaving Haya no window for Moonscape Mirage or the shield on Wayward Rays. The third orb of Dark Impact stuns for 1s, and every orb that touches her restores 162 Health to Donghuang, giving back the damage she chipped in.

passive.description: Haya carries up to 3 moon crystals. Using Crescent Wave or Wayward Rays consumes 1 moon crystal. Once all are used, the skills enter full cooldown, and she gains an enhanced Basic Attack that fires 3 extra orbs, each dealing 50 (50 + 10% magical attack) magical damage. Targets hit by Crescent Wave or Wayward Rays will be marked, and hitting them again will trigger different effects.
passive.name: Passive Skill: Moon's Farewell

skill1.description:
Haya unleashes a beam of moonlight forward, dealing 350 (350 + 75% magical attack) magical damage.
If the beam triggers a mark, the target also takes 100 (100 + 22% magical attack) true damage.
skill1.name: Skill 1: Crescent Wave

skill2.description: Haya unleashes 3 glazed orbs, the first dealing 120 (120 + 22% magical attack) magical damage, and the next 2 dealing 60 (60 + 11% magical attack) magical damage. She also gains a shield that negates 250 (250 + 40% magical attack) damage for 3s and gradually gains Movement Speed over the next 2s, maxing out at a 30% increase. If she hits marked enemies, they will be stunned for 0.5s. Subsequent hits will only inflict 50% of the stun effect.
skill2.name: Skill 2: Wayward Rays

skill3.description:
Haya links to a hero for 1.5s, gaining 50% damage reduction. The link breaks if they move too far apart, refunding 75% of Moonscape Mirage's cooldown. If the link remains unbroken after 1.5s, both enter the mirage, granting her a shield that negates 300 (300 + 70% magical attack) damage.
While inside the mirage, her skill cooldowns are reduced by 50%. If she uses Moonscape Mirage again while inside the mirage, she moves 700 units away from the target.
skill3.name: Skill 3: Moonscape Mirage

strategy.earlyGame: In the mid lane, Haya's bread and butter is landing Skill 1 at max range, then hitting the imprinted target again to stack true damage on top. While you still hold moon rings, Skill 1 and Skill 2 cycle on very short cooldowns, but spending all three drops you onto normal cooldowns—so keep one cast of Skill 2 in your pocket for escapes whenever the enemy jungler's shadow appears. Skill 2 also grants a shield and a speed boost, so until you unlock the Ultimate at level 4, avoid overextending and fight around the imprint stun as a counter tool.
strategy.midGame: Around the 4-minute Tyrant spawn, the Ultimate starts paying off. Group with your jungler and link onto an enemy support warding the river or an isolated mid laner. Hold the link for 1.5 seconds and you drag them into the mirage, where the 50% cooldown reduction lets you dump Skill 2's stun and Skill 1's true damage on them one-sidedly. A practical tip worth remembering: cast the link right after the enemy burns their blink, and it's far harder to break. Once your first magic core item is done, the imprint combo alone puts enemy mages at death's door.
strategy.lateGame: Late-game Haya is all about choosing who disappears into the mirage. Isolate the enemy marksman or mage with the Ultimate before a teamfight starts and you've effectively created a 4v5. Link a tank by mistake, though, and you can lose the brawl inside the mirage—pick your target carefully. After spending all three moon rings, your empowered basic attack fires three orbs' worth of damage, so always tack it onto the end of a combo. The vision fights before Shadow Tyrant after 10 minutes are exactly where a single-target catch hits hardest.
strategy.teamfight: Don't join the opening scrum head-on. Sit behind your frontline, spread imprints, and keep Skill 2's shield in reserve. If an enemy assassin dives your backline, link Skill 3 onto that assassin — hold it for 1.5 seconds and the two of you drop into the mirage together, which is what pulls them off your carries. Recast Skill 3 inside the mirage and Haya herself moves 700 units away from the target, resetting the spacing. When attacking, punish whoever steps up out of position with the Skill 1 into Skill 2 imprint stun and focus them down with your team. You have no area damage, so committing everything to deleting one target beats spraying into a clumped enemy team.

combos.title: Mark, Stun, Empowered Hit
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (applies the mark) → Skill 2 (0.5s stun on a marked target, plus a shield and a speed boost) → Skill 1 (true damage) → Empowered Basic Attack (3 orbs)
combos.description: A mark exists only after Skill 1 or Skill 2 connects. On a marked target, Skill 2 turns into a 0.5s stun and Skill 1 adds true damage. Those three casts empty all three moon crystals, so the Basic Attack that follows fires three orbs.

combos.title: Mirage Isolation
combos.sequence: Skill 3 (1.5s link, 50% damage reduction at Level 1) → both enter the mirage (skill cooldowns cut 50%, plus a shield) → Skill 2 (applies the mark) → Skill 1 (true damage) → Skill 2 (0.5s stun)
combos.description: Even if the target walks out of range and the link snaps, 75% of Moonscape Mirage's cooldown is refunded. Hold it for the full 1.5s and the two of you drop into the mirage alone. Cooldowns are halved in there, so the 7-second wait after spending the moon crystals lasts only 3.5 seconds.

combos.title: Peel the Diver
combos.sequence: Skill 3 (link the enemy stuck on your teammate; 50% damage reduction at Level 1) → the enemy is pulled into the mirage after 1.5s → recast Skill 3 (700 units of separation)
combos.description: This is the defensive line: link whoever jumped your backline. Damage taken drops by 50% at Level 1, so Haya can be the one soaking the hits instead. After 1.5s the diver goes into the mirage with her, and a recast opens 700 units, clearing that enemy away from your carry.

strengths: Repeated single-target burst through imprint true damage and stuns
The Ultimate isolates one enemy in the mirage, forcing a pseudo-1v1
Moon rings enable low-cooldown spam plus a shield and speed for self-defense
The link's displacement doubles as peel to protect your carries
weaknesses: Everything flows through imprints, so whiffing the first hit stalls the kit
The link breaks at range, making high-mobility heroes miserable matchups
Thin area damage means weak waveclear and zone control
Juggling rings, imprints, and links earns the Very Hard difficulty tag

playstyle.style: A lunar mage who spends three moon rings on her casts and halves incoming damage through her linking ultimate. The skill ceiling lives in hiding the vulnerable moment when the rings run dry.
playstyle.suited: Players who enjoy covering resource gaps with positioning craft — and will practice through the very-hard label.

synergy.reason: Guiguzi's Skill 2 pulls enemies in and stuns them for 1s. Yao can land Starlight Slice on the clumped group, picking up passive healing and Star Power at the same time. Skill 1 also strips 25% of their physical and magical defense.

Skill 2 gives Sun Bin and nearby teammates 130 Movement Speed for 2s, so Yao can close the gap without spending Star Rush and keep Return to Dust as an escape. Skill 3's energy field slows enemies immensely for 1s.

counters.reason: Liang's Skill 3 suppresses one enemy hero for 2.2s. Yao cannot cast Return to Dust while suppressed, so the Star Reduction he has banked keeps draining his Health. Skill 1 also drops 4 barriers across the lanes he wants to dash through.

Donghuang's Skill 3 suppresses a hero for 2s, and both of them share all damage taken during it. Yao can neither rewind with Return to Dust nor trigger his passive healing, since no skill goes off. Skill 2's third dark orb adds a 1s stun on top.

passive.name: Passive Skill: Gift of the Stars
passive.description: Yao recovers 70 (70 + 2% extra Health) Health when his skills hit an enemy unit, or half if they miss. Skill uses grant stacks of Star Power. At max stacks, enhances his next skill for 3s. Using the enhanced skill then enhances his next Basic Attack, letting him dash at the target and deal 100 (100 + 30% extra physical attack) physical damage.

Star Power mimics this skill, slowing units hit by both him and the stars by 25% for 2s.
