strategy.earlyGame: Ying lives in the jungle, though she can hold the clash lane in a pinch. Every skill cast banks one Resonance stack and your next basic attack spends them all, so drill the skill-into-basic-attack rhythm on camps from your very first clear — the one-stack sweep is what keeps your clear speed honest. Once you hit level 4 and unlock your Ultimate, start showing up to river 2v2s: layering its knock-up with Skill 1 lets you flip counter-ganks even at a numbers disadvantage. Just keep deep invades to a minimum before your stacks are flowing, because she is easy to shut down early.
strategy.midGame: Skirmishes around the Tyrant (the buffed boss that spawns at 4:00) are where Ying spikes. Finish one attack speed item and her resonance skills come out noticeably faster — attack speed feeds their animation at a 50% ratio — so your hit count climbs in a hurry. Approach from a side bush with Skill 2's charged dash, pop enemies up with Skill 1, then weave in a basic attack: the two-stack rapid thrusts chunk hard. Every resonance proc also refunds 1.5 seconds on Skill 1 and Skill 2, which is exactly why the longer a fight drags on, the faster she spins.
strategy.lateGame: Past the 10-minute mark, fights hinge on when you commit Skill 3. Super armor runs for the whole cast and damage taken drops by 30% at rank 1, so the ideal pattern is to watch one key piece of enemy CC (crowd control) get spent, then dive in with the back-and-forth knock-ups. Cycling all three skills builds three stacks, and your next basic attack becomes Zenith - Wildfire: she leaps into the air, ignores terrain, and unleashes a sweeping strike across a wide area — exactly what you want against enemies who back off. Her actual durability is only fighter-average; do not chase deep while Skill 3 is down.
strategy.teamfight: Resist the urge to lead the charge — stacking Skill 3 on top of an ally's engage is far more reliable. Knock the clump around with the back-and-forth passes, fire the second phase, Roaring Sun, and fight on top of the burn zone it leaves behind. From there, keep the loop simple: one skill, one basic attack, over and over, so the resonance sweeps and cooldown refunds never stop. Against runners, build three stacks first and release Zenith - Wildfire — she ignores terrain on the approach and unleashes a wide sweeping strike. One habit that pays off: aim the second-phase sweep at the spot where knocked-up enemies will land — it almost never misses.

combos.title: Three-Stack Wildfire
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (charged dash) → Skill 1 (0.5s launch) → Skill 3 (repeated launches) → Basic Attack (3 Spear Will stacks)
combos.description: Each skill cast banks 1 Spear Will stack. Fire all three, then a Basic Attack spends them on the airborne charged strike, which ignores terrain while she is in the air. Spear Will skills can crit, so this also serves as the chase tool on a retreating target.

combos.title: One-Stack Grind
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (0.5s launch) → Basic Attack (1 Spear Will stack) → Skill 2 (15% slow) → Basic Attack (1 Spear Will stack)
combos.description: Slot exactly one Basic Attack after each skill. The one-stack Spear Will skill flurries with a Movement Speed boost and a shield, and every trigger shaves 1.5s off Moonslash and Cloudchaser. Attack Speed items speed up the Spear Will cast itself at 50% efficiency.

combos.title: Starburn Counter-Engage
combos.sequence: Skill 3 (repeated launches + crowd control immunity) → Second phase, Roaring Sun (sweep + 3s trail of fire) → Skill 1 (0.5s launch)
combos.description: Skill 3 grants crowd control immunity and 30% damage reduction at Lvl 1. Meet the enemy engage with the back-and-forth launches, then use the second phase to interrupt the remaining dashes and lay the fire trail. Time the sweep to where the launched enemies will land.

strengths: Resonance cooldown refunds make her output snowball the longer a fight runs
Multiple knock-ups from Skill 1 and the Ultimate dominate skirmishes and brawls
Super armor plus 30% damage reduction on the Ultimate makes her hard to stop
Attack speed also accelerates resonance skills, so her items never go to waste
weaknesses: Demands constant skill-and-basic-attack weaving; the execution bar is high
Burst lags behind true assassins, letting targets slip away half-dead
Her teamfight presence drops sharply while the Ultimate is on cooldown
Only average durability — getting chain-CC'd before stacking up is lethal

playstyle.style: A spear fighter who banks resonance through skills and spends it on basic attacks, triggering one of three arts depending on the count. Stack management is combo selection.
playstyle.suited: Players who want stack-counting to become second nature — the rhythm of loading and releasing.

synergy.reason: She absorbs enemy aggro and CC in teamfights, creating an opening to safely join the fight.
By disrupting the frontline, she makes it easy to pick off isolated enemies or squishy backline targets.

counters.reason: His point-and-click hard CC guarantees lockdown, completely shutting down high mobility like wall-hopping.
His strong suppression stops any flank attempts in their tracks, leaving them vulnerable to get focused down by the enemy.

passive.skill_name: Passive Skill: Jade Carriage - View from Above
passive.description:
Feyd can move freely on walls, where his Basic Attacks become ranged (and can be used while jumping).
He gains the following while on top of a wall:
Jade Carriage: Stocks Stepping on Jade uses 10% faster.
View from Above: Gains 15% increased field of vision.
Crowd Control Penalty: Crowd controls last 25% longer.
passive.name: Passive Skill: Jade Carriage - View from Above

skill1.description:
Feyd moves swiftly forward, dealing 360 (360 + 110% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies in his path and launching them for 3/4s. At the same time, he gains 50% Attack Speed and enhances his next 3 Basic Attacks.
Melee: Each attack deals 75 (75 + 20% extra physical attack) physical damage and restores 155 (155 + 1.5% extra Health) Health.
Ranged: Each attack deals 50 (50 + 13% extra physical attack) physical damage and bounces to the nearest unit within range on hit.
skill1.name: Skill 1: Jade Chase - Returning Strike

skill2.description:
When on the ground: Feyd leaps onto the target wall. The leap's range increases by 4% for each skill level.
When on a wall: Feyd steps on jade, jumping to the target wall.
Stocks 1 use of this skill every 10s, for up to 4 uses.
skill2.name: Skill 2: Stepping on Jade

skill3.description:
Feyd swings his jade blade in a horizontal sweep around him, dealing 240 (240 + 70% extra physical attack) physical damage. (If he's on a wall, he will dash to the target area, then slash.) He marks all hit enemies and activates the skill's second phase, Hardened Jade Strike.
Hardened Jade Strike: Feyd slashes each marked target 4 times, causing the marks to shatter, dealing 140 (140 + 45% extra physical attack) physical damage that ignores untargetable states.
If a target's Health falls below 1/8, they will be Jadeified and shatter, being defeated.
skill3.name: Skill 3: Hardened Jade Seal

strategy.earlyGame: Feyd's wall-walking Passive is one of a kind, and you should lean on it from minute one. Clear your jungle, then scout the enemy's farm state from the walls before level 4 — you get 15% wider vision up there and your basic attacks become ranged, so you're poking and gathering information at zero risk. The standard gank is Skill 2 onto a wall, then Skill 1 to drop down and land the 0.75-second knock-up. One caveat to burn into memory: slows and CC applied to you last 25% longer while you're standing on a wall.
strategy.midGame: Around 8 minutes, once your first physical damage item is finished, the side-lane walls become your hunting grounds. Roam wall to wall with at least two Skill 2 stacks in reserve (you bank one every 10 seconds, up to four), and when you spot a low-HP target, unload the full kit: Skill 1, three empowered basic attacks, the Ultimate's mark, then its follow-up strike. Any enemy below 1/8 HP dies to that strike guaranteed — Feyd never knows the pain of a kill escaping on a sliver. Front-on brawls are not his game, so kill and leave, every time.
strategy.lateGame: From 15 minutes on, commit to entering fights late. Dive in at the start and his lack of bulk gets exposed, so perch on a wall, wait for a few enemy CC abilities to be spent, then drop. Your target list is short: the isolated marksman or mage, nobody else. Skill 1's drop knock-up leads into empowered basics (which heal you at melee range), and the Ultimate's mark plus follow-up strike closes the deal. When you're down to your last Skill 2 stack, stop chasing and save it for the trip back to a wall — that discipline is what keeps you alive.
strategy.teamfight: Skip the head-on collision entirely and time your entrance from the outer walls. The moment enemy eyes lock onto your frontline, drop in from the side and put Skill 1 into a backliner. Skill 3's sweep marks everything it touches, and the follow-up, Hardened Jade Strike, ignores untargetable states as it shatters those marks. An enemy who goes untargetable to slip away still takes it, so long as the mark is on them. Take the kill, Skill 2 back to a wall, and reset for the next pick. A trick that pays real dividends: choose a wall along the enemy's escape route before the fight starts — the kills you collect go up noticeably.

combos.title: Wall Entry Ambush
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (leap from the ground onto a wall) → Basic Attack from the wall (ranged) → Skill 1 (move + 0.75s launch, +50% Attack Speed) → 3 melee enhanced Basic Attacks → Skill 3 (sweep applies marks) → Hardened Jade Strike
combos.description: On a wall his Basic Attacks turn ranged, so he chips away from a spot they cannot reach. Skill 1 moves him forward as it damages the path, which carries him off the wall and into the launch. Land the three enhanced Basic Attacks in melee range: each one restores 155 Health at Lvl 1, while the ranged version carries no healing at all.

combos.title: The 1/8 Execute
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (0.75s launch) → Skill 3 (sweep applies marks) → Hardened Jade Strike (shatters the marks)
combos.description: The shortest path onto a fleeing low-Health target. Once a target sits below 1/8 Health, the Hardened Jade Strike jadeifies them and the kill is guaranteed. It also ignores untargetable states, so going untargetable buys them nothing. Whether you reach them at all comes down to the Skill 1 launch stopping their feet.

combos.title: Wall Swap Reset
combos.sequence: Hardened Jade Strike → Skill 2 (jump to a different wall) → Basic Attack from the wall (ranged)
combos.description: Skill 2 stocks one use every 10s and holds up to 4. Spend one the moment the kill lands and the ranged chip damage starts again from safety. Crowd control lasts 25% longer while he stands on a wall, so a wall inside enemy range turns the reset into a death sentence.

strengths: Wall movement plus ranged basics enable zero-risk scouting and poke
Skill 3's execute guarantees kills below 1/8 HP — nothing slips away
The follow-up strike shatters marks even through untargetable states
Skill 1's knock-up and 50% attack speed give brutal short-window stickiness
weaknesses: Slows and CC on him last 25% longer while he is standing on a wall
Mobility falls off a cliff once his Skill 2 stacks run dry
No stats for front-on brawling — late fight entries are mandatory
Struggles to show his identity in open areas with few walls

playstyle.style: An assassin who walks on walls, claiming a vertical dimension no one else can use. Ranged attacks from above and sudden drops give him attack lines that simply don't exist for grounded heroes.
playstyle.suited: Players who find value in spaces nobody else is using — and enjoy being the only one fighting in three dimensions.

synergy.reason: Providing shields, she extends the time Alessio can deal damage while airborne.
Clumping enemies up allows Alessio to maximize the AoE damage of his basic attacks.

counters.reason: With high mobility and burst damage, he can quickly delete targets before they have a chance to escape.
Her insane instantaneous burst damage can easily punish and disrupt Alessio's positioning.

passive.description:
Alessio's Basic Attack fires a shell that deals area damage, plus extra physical damage equal to 0.5% of the target's Health. While he is grounded, the shell can be blocked by enemy heroes.
—The new Captain Red Hawk's ability to improvise is his greatest virtue, according to him.
passive.name: Passive Skill: Rebellious Little Hawk

—Biron chipped in to help fund Alessio's upgraded shells, but even then, Alessio can only use them sparingly.
skill1.name: Skill 1: Upgraded Shell

skill2.description:
Alessio throws a smoke bomb, creating a smoke cloud that grants stealth to himself and his teammates for 3.5s. The bomb's explosion sends him into the air, granting him Movement Speed for 0.8s. While airborne, he can move and use Basic Attacks and skills while ignoring terrain. Using Basic Attacks or the Ultimate while airborne causes him to stay airborne longer.
While airborne, Skill 2 will not throw smoke bombs, and Basic Attacks cannot be blocked by enemies.
—"Give 'em a good scare!" Alessio is a master when it comes to making an entrance.
skill2.name: Skill 2: Legendary Hero Debut

skill3.description:
Alessio leaps into the air, gaining brief crowd control immunity, then locks onto an enemy hero and fires 5 shells at them, with each shell dealing 350 (350 + 80% extra physical attack) (+ 6% of target's lost Health) physical damage to enemies within the explosion's range. If the same target is hit by multiple shells, subsequent shells only deal 25% damage. Only 1 shell can be diverted to another enemy hero other than the locked-on target.
"You here for the fireworks?"
skill3.name: Skill 3: Sunset Fireworks Show

strategy.earlyGame: Head to the farm lane and aim to have level 4 plus your first attack item before the Tyrant fight at 4:00. Your Passive shells deal splash damage plus bonus damage equal to 0.5% of the target's max Health at level 1, so simply angling shots to clip the enemy marksman through the minion wave wins you trades. The catch: grounded basic attacks can be blocked by enemy heroes, so when their frontline wedges itself in between, take the farm instead. When things get dicey, reach for Skill 2. The smoke cloud stealths you and nearby allies for 3.5 seconds, and the blast carries you airborne — a burst of Movement Speed for 0.8s plus free passage over terrain is enough to break away.
strategy.midGame: Between 8 and 10 minutes, with your crit core online, you become the centerpiece of every fight. When rotating to objectives, drop Skill 2's smoke (3.5 seconds of stealth) over your team and the whole rotation vanishes off the enemy's screen — ambushes practically set themselves up. In fights, save Skill 1's three enhanced shells for the moment enemies clump: the bigger splash plus 1% max HP bonus shreds groups. That smoke is your lifeline for both attack and escape, so never burn it just to walk somewhere faster.
strategy.lateGame: By the late game you are the fire source the enemy most wants gone, which is exactly why you stand one step behind your frontline at all times. When someone dives you, Skill 2 into the air and cast your Ultimate while airborne: five missiles rain down under super armor, each adding 6% of the target's missing HP as bonus damage — as a finisher on softened targets, it's as reliable as they come. Another enemy hero can soak exactly one missile for the target, so the moment your mark stands alone is the moment you fire.
strategy.teamfight: Open from behind your frontline, farming splash damage onto the clump with enhanced shells, and only step up once the enemy's engage tools are spent. If you're already airborne from the Ultimate, recasting Skill 2 in the air trades the smoke for unblockable basic attacks — you shoot straight past the frontline into their carries. Stack missiles onto anything escaping low. Here's a positioning habit worth stealing: place the smoke half a step behind you rather than at your feet, so you vanish right in front of the assassin who just jumped in — the survival difference is night and day.

combos.title: Airborne Full Burst
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (load upgraded shells) → Skill 2 (smoke + airborne) → air Basic Attacks → Skill 3 (5 shells)
combos.description: While airborne he ignores terrain and can still move, attack, and cast. Basic Attacks and Skill 3 used in the air extend his airtime, so shooting keeps him off the ground. Each missile adds 6% of the target's lost Health at Lvl 1, which is why softened targets fall fastest.

combos.title: Unblockable Air Mode
combos.sequence: Skill 3 (leap + missiles) → Skill 2 while airborne → air Basic Attacks
combos.description: On the ground his shells can be blocked by enemy heroes. Cast in the air, Skill 2 skips the smoke bomb and instead makes Basic Attacks unblockable, so you shoot past the frontline straight into the backline. That is the answer to a tank-stacked comp.

combos.title: Smokescreen Ambush
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (smoke, 3.5s stealth) → Basic Attack from stealth → Skill 1 → 3 enhanced Basic Attacks
combos.description: The smoke hides teammates as well as Alessio. Drop it ahead of an objective and dump the upgraded shells onto whoever walks in. Enhanced Basic Attacks have a larger area and add physical damage equal to 1% of the target's Health.

strengths: Splash basic attacks with max-HP scaling put real damage into tanks
Smoke stealth and airborne movement cover both self-peel and ambushes
Airborne shots ignore body-blocking and reach the enemy backline directly
Missing-HP scaling on the Ultimate reliably finishes softened targets
weaknesses: With Skill 2 and the Ultimate down he has no escape and melts on the ground
Grounded basic attacks get body-blocked by the enemy frontline
Another enemy can soak one Ultimate missile, blunting it in brawls
The airborne game plan is punished hard by lock-on skills and anti-air CC

playstyle.style: A sky-pirate marksman with splash cannonballs and a smoke screen that cloaks his whole team. His aerial missile ultimate executes one named target — carry, trickster, and support in one hat.
playstyle.suited: Players bored of orthodox shootouts, weaving tricks and team utility to stay forever off-script.

synergy.reason: By engaging the teamfight and disrupting enemies, he creates a safe environment for Luara to output damage.
He acts as a durable frontline tank, peeling enemy assassins away from Luara.

counters.reason: Her high mobility allows her to bypass Luara's kiting and consistently deal damage.
His high burst damage can instantly delete Luara before she has a chance to scale.

passive.description:
When using Skill 1 and her Ultimate, Luara gains up to 2 serpent blades that attack enemies during her Basic Attacks.
She gains a 5% Attack Speed boost for 3s when using skills, for up to 3 stacks.
passive.name: Passive Skill: Serpent's Envoy

skill1.description:
Luara gains 60 Movement Speed that diminishes over 2s and a serpent blade. While the serpent blade is active, she gains a brief Movement Speed burst and can leap over a wall once.
The serpent blade attacks targets continuously, dealing 50 (30 + 12% physical attack) physical damage (attack speed scales with her Attack Speed).
Every 3 serpent blade attacks count as 1 Basic Attack. Attacks grant vision of the attacked target, and deal 50% damage to secondary targets.
skill1.name: Skill 1: Deadly Fang

skill2.description:
Luara summons the Fire Serpent at the target location. After a short delay, the Fire Serpent charges at her, dealing 350 (350 + 100% extra physical attack) magical damage to enemies in its path, slowing them by 25% for 2s, and pulling them back slightly (not considered a crowd control effect).
If Luara has active serpent blades, the serpent blades immediately attack enemies hit by the Fire Serpent. If she does not have active serpent blades, 25% of Skill 2's Cooldown is returned.
skill2.name: Skill 2: Furtive Attack

skill3.description:
Luara summons the Fire Serpent in the target direction, dealing 450 (450 + 140% extra physical attack) magical damage to enemies in its path and blinding them for 1.5s. This skill can be used while moving.
Luara enhances herself and gains a serpent blade. While enhanced, she gains Energy every time she deals damage with Basic Attacks and skills. Each time she reaches max Energy, she rains fire on nearby enemies, dealing 150 (150 + 45% extra physical attack) magical damage and launching enemies within range for 1/3s.
Blinded enemies cannot deal damage with Basic Attacks, and their skill projectiles will deviate from their normal trajectories by a random offset and hit enemies along the way.
skill3.name: Skill 3: Blazing Glare

strategy.earlyGame: Take the farm lane and let the serpent blades do the early work until your first attack speed item is finished. Pick up a blade with Skill 1, land a basic attack, and the blade cuts the target continuously while granting vision of it — an enemy who ducks into a bush stays visible and keeps bleeding. Feel a gank coming? Skill 1 again: 60 bonus Movement Speed (up to 120 at max rank) and one free wall vault while it lasts, which most junglers cannot answer. The boost diminishes over 2 seconds, so pick your exit before you press it. She has no burst this early, so prioritize last-hitting over hero kills.
strategy.midGame: Around 10 minutes, with two attack speed core items online, her sustained damage starts to bite. Every skill cast raises her Attack Speed for 3 seconds, stacking up to three times, so keep Skill 1 and Skill 2 rolling instead of hoarding them. Three serpent blade hits count as one basic attack, which means your attack speed directly sets how fast the blades cut. In skirmishes, drop Skill 2's fire serpent behind the enemy: it charges back toward you, carving through everyone in its path, slowing them by 25% at rank 1 (up to 50%) and pulling them back slightly — that pull is not a crowd control effect. Hold a blade when it lands and the blade immediately attacks every enemy the serpent hit. Jumped by a basic-attack jungler? Skill 3. Their attacks deal nothing for 1.5 seconds, and that window is enough to turn the fight around.
strategy.lateGame: With full build in sight, build your marksman duels around Skill 3. A blinded enemy cannot deal damage with basic attacks, and their skill projectiles deviate from their path at random, so for those 1.5 seconds you are effectively fighting a player up. The same cast hands her a serpent blade and enhances her. While enhanced, every point of damage she deals with basic attacks and skills charges Energy — damage dealt, not damage taken — and each time the bar fills, fire rains down and launches nearby enemies for 1/3s. That is genuine self-peel against an assassin glued to your back. The catch: Energy only builds while you are attacking, so backing out of range turns the buff into a dead card. Knowing exactly when to step out is where Luara players separate.
strategy.teamfight: Your job is steady area damage: keep two serpent blades cycling from behind your frontline. Land Skill 3 on the enemy marksman as the fight opens and their basic attacks deal nothing for 1.5 seconds while you push in with the buff running. If someone dives you, do not just retreat — keep attacking, fill the Energy bar, and the fire rain's 1/3s launch pries them off. Once there is space, take Skill 1's speed and wall vault to reset. One escape trick: when running, drop the fire serpent behind your pursuer. It charges back to you straight through them, leaving a slow behind as it goes.

combos.title: Serpent Blade Kiting
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (+60 Movement Speed, 1 serpent blade) → Basic Attacks to keep the blade cutting → vault a wall to reset spacing
combos.description: Every 3 serpent blade strikes count as 1 Basic Attack, and the blade grants vision of whatever it hits. That keeps a target lit up even after they duck into a bush. While Skill 1 is active she can also leap over one wall, which doubles as the escape route.

combos.title: Blind Counterplay
combos.sequence: Skill 3 (1.5s blind + 1 serpent blade) → sustained Basic Attacks → fire rain at max Energy (1/3s launch) → Skill 2 (25% slow)
combos.description: Blinded enemies cannot deal damage with Basic Attacks, so landing this on an attack-reliant hero buys 1.5s of free trading. While enhanced, every point of damage builds Energy, and each time it caps she rains fire that launches nearby enemies. That also answers an assassin who sticks to her.

combos.title: Fire Serpent Pull-Through
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (1 serpent blade) → Skill 2 (summon behind the enemy) → the serpent's charge (slow + slight pull)
combos.description: The Fire Serpent always charges back toward Luara, so summoning it behind a target guarantees the path runs through them. With a serpent blade active it immediately carves everyone the serpent clips; without one, 25% of Skill 2's cooldown is returned instead.

strengths: Blades that keep cutting the target and grant vision of it, beating bushes and escape attempts
The 1.5s blind shuts off the damage of any basic-attack hero
Skill 1's 10s cooldown keeps the speed boost and wall vault coming, making her hard to catch
The 1/3s knock-up from the fire rain during her enhanced state doubles as anti-assassin self-peel
weaknesses: Zero burst; targets often walk away before she can finish the job
Cashing in the self-buff means staying forward and eating damage
Skill-heavy comps blank the blind and cut deep into her identity
Heavily attack-speed dependent — underwhelming until the core is built

playstyle.style: A marksman who carries up to two serpent blades: every basic attack sends them slicing at the target, and three blade hits count as one basic attack. The blades also grant vision of whatever they cut, so her damage and her scouting run on the same track.
playstyle.suited: Players who enjoy running two damage sources at once — her own attacks and the blades already in the air. The fire serpent asks you to read placement and timing yourself, and she is rated Hard. If you would rather win on positioning than on raw reaction speed, she fits.

synergy.reason: She can chain her powerful AoE burst with the terrain and CC created by Ata.
It's easy for her to land skills and secure kills when Ata isolates and locks down enemies.

counters.reason: He can deal one-sided damage from long range, completely denying Ata's engage.
Her high mobility dodges Ata's skills, while her high armor penetration bursts down tanks instantly.

passive.skill_name: Passive Skill: Child of the Sea
passive.description: Ata's lost Health is stored in a buffer for 7s, and he recovers Health from the buffer equal to 40%/20% of the damage he deals to enemy heroes / non-hero units respectively (recovery is increased by 1%/0.5% for every 1,000 extra Health). After 7s, Ata's buffered Health will diminish by 3% Health per second. Basic Attacks deal 70 (70 + 35% extra physical attack) extra physical damage.
passive.name: Passive Skill: Child of the Sea

skill1.description:
Ata leaps and slams his anchor into the ground, dealing 460 (460 + 13% extra Health) physical damage. He then bounces forward, dealing the same amount of physical damage and launching enemies within range for 0.5s.
If he hits multiple enemies, the damage is reduced by 20% for each additional enemy, down to 60% of the initial damage. Deals 30% extra damage to minions.
After the bounce, he rolls in the target direction. He gains crowd control immunity while using this skill.
skill1.name: Skill 1: Wavewalking

skill2.description:
Ata hurls his anchor in the target direction, dealing 225 (225 + 70% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies in its path and reducing their Movement Speed by 30% for 1.5s. If the anchor hits a wall, Ata will pull himself and any enemies in his path to the wall and smash into it, dealing 250 (250 + 10% extra Health) physical damage and stunning any enemies smashed for 0.5s.
Passive: Using Skill 2 enhances the next Basic Attack, pulling the target enemy to Ata.
skill2.name: Skill 2: Sea Anchor

skill3.description:
Ata erects a high wall in a cone-shaped target area that blocks heroes and lasts for 4s. When erected, the wall deals 350 (350 + 120% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies in front of him.
While using the Ultimate, he gains crowd control immunity.
skill3.name: Skill 3: Ghost Ship

strategy.earlyGame: The lane badge at the top of this page reads Clash, following the official stats. The advice below assumes a roaming pick. Roam from the opening minutes — Ata can meaningfully gank as early as level 2. When Skill 2's anchor clips a wall, it charges in and slams enemies into the terrain for a 0.5-second stun (the classic wall-slam), so simply herding someone toward lane-side walls manufactures kills. And thanks to his Passive, every hit on an enemy hero claws back 40% of your stored lost HP, which means slightly reckless trades actually work in your favor. Manufacture even one kill before the 4:00 Tyrant and your jungler takes off running.
strategy.midGame: In skirmishes, you dive first — no exceptions. Skill 1's double jump deals damage on both hops, knocks up on the second landing, and grants super armor throughout, so you can shrug off enemy CC and press their backline. After casting Skill 2, your next empowered basic attack drags its target right in front of you: wall-slam, drag, team focus fire — that chain is the standard play. As anti-heal items start showing up in enemy builds, your Passive sustain thins out, so slot an early defensive item to compensate.
strategy.lateGame: When the Shadow Tyrant and the Overlord become the stakes, everything starts with Skill 3's barrier. It raises a cone-shaped wall that heroes cannot pass for 4 seconds — lay it between the enemy frontline and backline and you get to hit one half with all five. Around boss pits, the tight corridors make the detour it forces that much longer. Dive the carry you cut off with Skill 1: both landings deal damage, but only the second one launches enemies for 0.5s. Line your team's damage up with that launch and the target does not walk away. The barrier's angle has to be decided in a split second, so rehearse the placement in your head before the fight breaks out.
strategy.teamfight: Lead the charge alongside your team's engage and treat getting hit as part of the job description: lost HP banks into your Passive, and every strike on an enemy hero recovers 40% of it, which makes the center of the brawl Ata's healing zone. Alternate the super armor windows on Skill 1 and the Ultimate and CC barely touches you, while the barrier severs escapes and reinforcements at once. From experience: angling the barrier to shut reinforcements out beats trying to cage enemies in — your team moves more freely and you avoid the classic own-goal.

combos.title: Wall Slam Relay
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (anchor into terrain → charge, 0.5s stun) → enhanced Basic Attack (pull to Ata) → Skill 1 (second landing, 0.5s launch)
combos.description: An anchor that catches terrain pulls Ata along and smashes everyone in his path into the wall for a 0.5s stun. The enhanced Basic Attack then drags the target right in front of him, and the second landing of the double jump launches them again. Herd them along a wall before you throw, or the charge never happens.

combos.title: Ghost Ship Split
combos.sequence: Skill 3 (4s barrier + 350 frontal damage) → Skill 1 (crowd control immunity, 0.5s launch) → Basic Attacks
combos.description: The barrier blocks heroes, so laying it between their frontline and backline lets your whole team focus one half. Skill 1 carries crowd control immunity as well, so their answer does not stop him stepping in. Buffered Health comes back at 40% of the damage he deals to enemy heroes, which is why the middle of the brawl is where he lasts longest.

strengths: Passive converts lost HP back through attacks — brawling makes him tankier
Deep CC kit: a wall-slam stun, an empowered-attack drag, and a 0.5s launch
Super armor on Skill 1 and Skill 3 lets him work straight through CC
Skill 3's barrier reshapes terrain for splits and cutoffs on demand
weaknesses: Anti-heal purchases gut the Passive's sustain
Short reach with little answer to long-range kiting
No solo burst — kills depend on allied damage arriving
A misangled barrier can lock your own team out of the fight

playstyle.style: A tank who reclaims lost Health by hitting people — offense as defense. His ghost-ship wall partitions fights, and his low-Health recovery punishes anyone who leaves the job half done.
playstyle.suited: Players who find passive tanking dull, balancing the books through counterattack.

synergy.reason: Yaria attaches to a teammate and grants a shield that absorbs 1,000 true damage. Taking it before Feathered Tempest gives Umbrosa the room to finish all 8 strikes inside the enemy line. Skill 1 tracks an enemy hero and launches them for 0.5s.

Zhuangzi's Skill 3 cleanses teammates and hands out a 600 shield with 1.5s of crowd control immunity, so Umbrosa keeps dancing instead of getting locked down. Skill 1's butterflies slow enemies by 30% for 2s, which makes the chase easier.

counters.reason: Skill 2 makes Di Renjie briefly immune to damage and crowd control while removing all of his debuffs. Umbrosa's Feathered Tempest dive lands on nothing during that window. Skill 3 then stuns for 1s and halves both of her defenses.

Daji's Skill 2 is a targeted stun that locks a hero down for 1.5s. Catching Umbrosa right after her Feathered Tempest dash cuts the 8-hit dance short. Her passive strips up to 3 stacks of magical defense, so the follow-up Soul Impact hits hard.

passive.description:
When attacking distant targets, Umbrosa's Basic Attack throws out a rebounding blade. She can only attack again once the blade returns. However, if she uses her Basic Attack just before the blade returns, it will instantly rebound forward for another strike.
While in ranged mode, every 1% Attack Speed increases her damage by 1.5. Each consecutive rebound of the blade further increases its damage and flight speed by 5%, stacking up to 3 times.
When attacking nearby targets, Umbrosa switches to melee mode. Her Basic Attack becomes a flurry of 3 rapid strikes, dealing a total of 110% physical attack physical damage.
Each Basic Attack applies a Mark to the enemy. Marked enemies take extra damage when hit by Feathered Tempest.
passive.name: Passive Skill: Whirling Featherblades

skill1.description:
Umbrosa sweeps the surrounding area, dealing 250 (250 + 80% extra physical attack) physical damage and slowing enemies by 15% for 2s.
She then enters the Frenzied state for 3s, during which she gains 25% Movement Speed that diminishes over time and 60% Attack Speed.
skill1.name: Skill 1: Feverish Dance

skill2.description:
Umbrosa dashes forward, knocking back enemies in her path (not considered a crowd control effect) and dealing 150 (150 + 50% extra physical attack) physical damage. At the same time, she triggers the Featherblade marks of all hit targets and spreads them to nearby enemies.
If there are enemies ahead, Umbrosa performs a graceful dance, throwing flying blades that strike 8 times, each dealing 110 (110 + 38% extra physical attack) physical damage and recovering 45 (45 + 0.8% extra Health) Health (healing is halved when hitting non-hero units). If Umbrosa is in the Indomitable state, the final strike deals an extra 100% damage. Each hit consumes 1 stack of the target's marks, dealing an extra 40 (40 + 15% extra physical attack) physical damage.
She can move freely while dancing, and using the skill again will cancel its effects. If the dance is not triggered, the skill's cooldown will be reduced to 60% of the original.
skill2.name: Skill 2: Feathered Tempest

skill3.description:
Umbrosa reignites her former glory as an Austren, dealing 400 (400 + 140% extra physical attack) physical damage to nearby enemies while gaining 50% temporary Health and 50% Movement Speed that diminishes over time. She also enters the Indomitable state for 4s. Any recovery effects will be tallied only after the state ends.
If Umbrosa is defeated while this skill is not on cooldown, she will resurrect after a short delay. Upon resurrecting, she will deal 400 (400 + 140% extra physical attack) physical damage to nearby enemies, and this skill will enter cooldown.
Passive: When leveling up this skill, Feathered Tempest gains an additional 2 strikes of damage, while her melee Basic Attack gains an additional 1 strike of damage. Additional strikes deal 50 physical damage each.
If her temporary Health is expended, she will immediately exit the Indomitable state. When she resurrects, she only gains 50% of the Health she would have gained if the skill were actively used.
skill3.name: Skill 3: Final Frenzy

strategy.earlyGame: Clear speed is the calling card. Umbrosa's Passive changes shape with range — a spinning featherblade at distance, a fast three-hit string up close — and tapping basic attack just as the blade returns bounces it back out with 5% more damage and projectile speed per bounce (up to three). Drill that timing on jungle camps until it's muscle memory. Everything changes at level 4: the Ultimate's temporary HP equal to 50% of your health turns invades and slightly greedy ganks into genuine options.
strategy.midGame: This is a snowball hero, so from 8 to 12 minutes you're prowling the map for anyone farming alone. Open with Skill 1's 60% attack speed steroid, stack marks with the close-range strings, then Skill 2's dash into the multi-hit dance to spend them — healing on every hit while the damage pours in. You can move during the dance, so literally sidestep enemy skills mid-combo while you keep carving. If the fight turns, recast Skill 2 to cancel the dance and leave. There is always another target.
strategy.lateGame: Five-on-five head-on collisions are not her format, so play the late game as a pure flanker. A few seconds into the fight, when every enemy eye is fixed forward — that's your cue. Cast the Ultimate for the 50% temporary HP and its AoE damage, dive the backline, and one squishy dies before the buffer runs out. Even if you fall, dying while the Ultimate is off cooldown triggers a revival with another AoE burst, so you force the enemy to pay one-and-a-half deaths' worth of resources for one of yours. That math is the whole terror of this hero.
strategy.teamfight: Never take the opening engage. Sit on the perimeter, flick featherblades in to pre-stack marks, and watch for the enemy's key CC to be spent. Then commit: Skill 1 into Skill 2's dance to detonate the marks, healing through the chaos at the center of the fight. During the Ultimate's buffed state, the dance's final hit gains 100% bonus damage, so simply sequencing Ultimate before Skill 2 buys you a whole damage tier. And from live play: revive right when the enemy has forgotten the mechanic exists, drop the AoE on their heads, and watch entire fights flip.

combos.title: Stack the Marks, Then Dance
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (sweep, 15% slow + 60% Attack Speed) → melee Basic Attacks to stack Featherblade marks → Skill 2 (dash + 8-hit dance)
combos.description: Skill 1 sweeps the area for a 2s 15% slow, then hands her 60% Attack Speed at Lvl 1 through the 3s Frenzied state. Use that window to pile marks on with the melee flurry while they cannot walk away. Each dance hit consumes one mark for extra damage, so the number you banked decides how hard the dance lands.

combos.title: Indomitable All-In
combos.sequence: Skill 3 (50% temporary Health + 4s Indomitable) → Skill 2 (dance finale deals 100% extra) → Skill 1 → Basic Attacks
combos.description: Dancing while Indomitable adds 100% damage to the final strike. Reverse the order and that bonus is simply gone. Spending the temporary Health ends Indomitable on the spot, which makes this an entry with no exit planned. If Skill 3 is off cooldown when she dies, she resurrects and hits everyone nearby for 400 at Lvl 1.

combos.title: Featherblade Rebound Poke
combos.sequence: Ranged Basic Attack (throw the blade) → Basic Attack just before it returns (the blade rebounds forward) → keep rebounding to build the 5% bonus up to 3 stacks
combos.description: She cannot attack again until the blade comes home. Input the next Basic Attack just before it arrives and the blade rebounds forward for another strike. Each consecutive rebound raises that blade's damage and flight speed by 5%, stacking up to 3 times. It spends no skill and still applies marks, which makes it the prep work before an engage.

strengths: Range-shifting basics let her fight at whatever distance the enemy picks
Skill 2's dance moves and heals, so she out-sustains extended exchanges
50% temp HP plus a death revival forces better-than-even trades
Skill 2's cooldown drops to 60% when the dance whiffs, keeping the kit fast
weaknesses: The blade-bounce timing takes real practice to internalize
With the Ultimate on cooldown she loses the license to dive
Comps that instantly burst the temp HP break her trade math
No hard CC of her own — catching dedicated runners is on her team

playstyle.style: An honest fighter whose basic attacks adapt to range, throwing rebounding blades at distance. There is one trick — tapping basic attack just before the blade comes home sends it straight back out — but at heart she is a straightforward brawler, and the easy rating is accurate.
playstyle.suited: If you want one hero to learn the fighter role on, start here. The blade rebound is the only mechanic that needs drilling; once the return-timing tap feels automatic on jungle camps, take her into a real match.

synergy.reason: She can reset his cooldowns, allowing Heino to cast his powerful ultimate back-to-back.
Combining her teleports with Heino's time-reversal ultimate makes returning to fights and regenerating effortless.

counters.reason: She can instantly close the gap and burst down Heino before he has a chance to heal.
His strong CC can lock down Heino, setting up a kill before he can ever use his ultimate.

passive.description:
Heino engages in combat in either melee or ranged mode as fate dictates. His skills and melee Basic Attacks mark enemies for 7s on hit.
Ranged: He channels the Power of Fate to attack distant enemies, dealing 165 (100% physical attack) physical damage and (15% magical attack) magical damage.
Melee: He brandishes his scepter to attack all nearby enemies, dealing 165 (100% physical attack) physical damage and (45% magical attack) magical damage.
passive.name: Passive Skill: Fate's Guidance

skill1.description:
Heino reduces his cooldown by 0.2s for each marked enemy hit, up to 1s.
Ranged: He turns his scepter into energy and throws it, dealing 410 (410 + 75% magical attack) magical damage upon hit. He also throws 1 extra scepter at every marked enemy in front of him, dealing 75% damage.
Melee: He throws his scepter spinning, dealing 260 (260 + 45% magical attack) magical damage to enemies in its path and slowing them by 15% for 2s. He recovers 150 (150 + 5% extra Health) Health for each target hit.
Ranged: When extra scepters hit the same target multiple times, subsequent hits only deal 50% of the initial damage. Melee: Recovers Health up to 3 times.
skill1.name: Skill 1: Scepter of Fate

skill2.description:
Heino dashes forward. If there are no enemy heroes near the end of the dash, he goes into ranged mode. Otherwise, he goes into melee mode.
Ranged: Gains 15% Movement Speed for 2s. For each enemy hero near the starting point of the dash, his Movement Speed increases by 25%, up to 50%. If Skill 2 causes him to switch from melee to ranged mode, both the Movement Speed increase and its limit are doubled.
Melee: Gains 100 max Health and 100 max Mana, and recovers 450 (450 + 12% extra Health) Health while increasing max Health by the same amount. For each enemy hero near the endpoint of the dash, his Health recovery increases by 25%, up to 50%. If Skill 2 causes him to switch from ranged to melee mode, both the Health recovery and its limit are doubled.
skill2.name: Skill 2: Leap of Fate

skill3.description:
Heino leaves behind a memory whenever he changes to ranged mode. He creates a field that grants 15% damage reduction and recovers 400 (400 + 6% extra Health) Health. During this time, he has crowd control immunity but cannot move. After a 1.5s delay, the field deals 400 (400 + 100% magical attack) magical damage and he returns to the memory he left behind. If there is an allied tower within the field, that tower returns to its state from 5s earlier.
The lower his Health, the more Health he recovers, up to 2 times the base value.
skill3.name: Skill 3: Fate Rewind

strategy.earlyGame: Start with the lane decision. Heino runs mid as a ranged poke machine or the clash lane as a melee brawler with built-in healing and max HP growth — a genuinely dual-purpose hero. Either way, the through-line is mark management: skills and melee basic attacks apply a 7-second mark, and that mark is the precondition for Skill 1's healing and rapid recasts. Keep it running or your numbers fall apart. Until the Ultimate unlocks at level 4, skip the deep plays and use the time to get a feel for Skill 2's form swapping.
strategy.midGame: The moment the Ultimate clicks, Heino transforms. Switching to ranged form with Skill 2 records that spot, and the Ultimate returns you there after 1.5 seconds — which enables an almost unfair loop: record somewhere safe, wade in and brawl, then when you're at your limit, pop the domain, heal, and vanish home. Make it a habit before every objective fight from 8 to 10 minutes: record in the back, then commit in melee form. The lower your HP, the bigger the heal (up to double), so every second you stall makes the payoff larger.
strategy.lateGame: Past 15 minutes, form choice becomes your tactical dial. Thick frontline in front of you? Stay ranged and keep throwing Skill 1 with its phantom bolts. Thin frontline? Go melee, stack Skill 2's healing and max HP growth, and be the frontline yourself. In tower defenses, know this trick: if an allied tower stands inside the Ultimate's domain, the tower rewinds to its state 5 seconds earlier — a last-second save that decides siege after siege. Knowing that one interaction visibly changes your win rate in defensive games.
strategy.teamfight: Before every fight, without exception, record a ranged-form point somewhere safe. That single habit converts your melee dives from gambles into round trips. Once in, hold the brawl with Skill 2's healing and Skill 1, and when the focus fire arrives, cast the Ultimate: 15% damage reduction and super armor for 1.5 seconds, an AoE burst as the parting gift, and you're gone to the recorded point. From experience, the safest pattern is tanking the enemy's burst through the domain and then leaving — panic-casting it early wastes the low-HP healing bonus.

combos.title: Memory, Dive, Rewind
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (no enemies nearby → ranged mode, leaving a memory) → Skill 2 (near enemies → melee mode + heal) → melee Skill 1 (heals per marked enemy hit) → Skill 3 (returns to the memory after 1.5s)
combos.description: Only one memory is stored, so create it before you step forward. The mode Skill 2 lands in is decided by whether enemy heroes are near the end of the dash, not by your choice. During Skill 3 he has crowd control immunity but cannot move, so eat the burst on purpose: the lower his Health, the more he recovers, up to double.

combos.title: Marked Poke Loop
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (ranged throw applies a mark) → Basic Attack → Skill 1 again (extra scepter flies at the marked target)
combos.description: Marks come from his skills and melee Basic Attacks and last 7s. Each marked enemy hit refunds 0.2s of Skill 1's cooldown, up to 1s. The second cast throws an extra scepter at every marked enemy in front of him for 75% of the base damage.

strengths: Form swapping retunes his role to match the comp and the fight
The Ultimate's return converts aggression into guaranteed round trips
Healing scales up at low HP, giving him remarkable clutch survivability
Rewinding an allied tower 5 seconds is a defensive tool no one else has
weaknesses: Damage and healing both hinge on applying and maintaining marks
Rooted in place during the domain — bad casts invite focus fire
Dying before the return erases his entire gimmick; chained CC is lethal
Tracking forms and the record point at once keeps your hands busy

playstyle.style: A hybrid whose skills change between ranged and melee forms. His power source is always being the one who chooses the distance — the matchup is a duel over range control itself.
playstyle.suited: Players who want to cycle range decisions quickly, forever denying the opponent their favorite distance.

synergy.reason: He can easily follow up on Mayene's CC and knockups with his high burst damage to secure kills.
His long-range stuns are perfect for setting up Mayene's combos.

counters.reason: His reliable silence completely shuts down Mayene, who relies heavily on skill combos.
His unavoidable suppression can forcefully lock down the highly mobile Mayene.

passive.name: Passive Skill: Slack Off a Lil Bit
passive.description:
Mayene's skills consume Punch Strength or Kick Strength. When idle and not taking damage, she sits down to slack off, accelerating Strength recovery by 25%. While slacking, she snacks on treats, randomly recovering 110 (110 + 2% extra Health) × 1/1.5/2 Health.
Attacking, taking damage, or moving interrupts this effect. She won't slack off in Serious State.
Using a different skill combo within 3s of another boosts its effect by 25%.

skill3.name: Skill 3: Get Serious
skill3.description:
Mayene gets serious, dealing 360 (360 + 100% extra physical attack) physical damage to nearby enemies.

strategy.earlyGame: In a clash-lane 1v1, Mayene is about as scary as it gets. From level 2, with Skill 1 and Skill 2 online, the derivation combos put your opponent in a guessing game they cannot win. Default to Skill 1 → Skill 2 for the punch flurry and its healing to win repeated trades; when they back off, switch to Skill 2 → Skill 1, teleporting behind them for bonus damage equal to 15% of their missing HP. Fist and Leg charges refill one every 8.5 seconds, so the one house rule is: after dumping both, take half a step back and don't eat the counter-swing. In quiet moments, let the Passive kick in — she sits down, snacks, and heals.
strategy.midGame: Once the lane is broken, spend minutes 8 to 13 split-pushing a side lane as bait. Whoever comes to collect you eats Skill 2 → Skill 2: the flying kick's super armor, damage reduction, and healing let you tank the attempt outright, and against two or fewer pursuers it often flips into a kill. One player bending multiple enemies around her while the team takes the Tyrant or towers — that is the Mayene win condition. She is helpless if jumped at zero charges, so make checking for two full gauges before every fight a reflex.
strategy.lateGame: In late-game teamfights, cast the Ultimate first, not last. Its serious mode instantly refunds one Fist and one Leg charge and raises the cap to three, letting you chain derivations without pausing for breath. Hunt the backline: flank, lift them with Skill 1 → Skill 1, then finish with Skill 2 → Skill 1's missing-HP bonus. Takedowns with that finisher refund 50% energy (doubled for hero kills), so every kill reloads the next combo. When the 10-second window closes, your output falls off a cliff — overstaying is the one unforgivable sin.
strategy.teamfight: Hold the flank and wait for the enemy's CC to be aimed at someone else. Enter with Skill 2 → Skill 2 — super armor carries you straight through their counters. On landing, refill with the Ultimate and pick the derivation the moment demands: Skill 1 → Skill 1 to lift, Skill 1 → Skill 2 to sustain, Skill 2 → Skill 1 to execute. And honestly, the moment you stop running fixed sequences — reading "they're retreating: 2 into 1" and "they're standing their ground: 1 into 2" on reaction — is the moment Mayene actually begins.

combos.title: Pull and Launch (1 → 1)

The second adds physical damage equal to 10% of the target's max Health at Lvl 1, and enemies caught dead center take another 50%. She also takes 25% less damage during the strike at Lvl 1, so you can push through the counterattack.

combos.title: Blink Behind Finisher (2 → 1)

combos.description: The kick adds physical damage equal to 15% of the target's lost Health, so it scales with how much you have already chipped off. A takedown restores 300 Health at Lvl 1 plus 50% Strength, doubled when the target is an enemy hero. That refund is what reloads the next combo.

combos.title: Serious State Chain
combos.sequence: Skill 3 (Serious State + nearby damage) → Skill 2 → Skill 2 (flying kick) → Skill 1 → Skill 1 (1s launch)
combos.description: Entering the Serious State refunds 1 bar each of Punch and Kick Strength and raises the cap to 3. Using a different combo within 3s of the previous one boosts its effect by 25%, so closing with 2 → 2 and then launching with 1 → 1 lines up cleanly. It runs 10s, and once it ends her output thins out fast, so watch the timer before overextending.

strengths: Four derivations cover engages, sustain, defense, and executions

Takedown energy refunds let momentum turn her nearly unstoppable
weaknesses: Useless with empty gauges — charge accounting never stops

playstyle.style: An eccentric brawler juggling two stamina gauges — slack off and she literally sits down to snack. Weave her cartwheel dodge and pull correctly and her flurries take over the fight.
playstyle.suited: Players who see resource management as a puzzle, not a chore — and read 'very hard' as an invitation.

strategy.earlyGame: Dyadia opens the game glued to her jungler, not to a lane. Tag enemies with Skill 2 as you roam: the curse ticks damage, taxes gold off them every second, and shuts off stealth for 5 seconds, exposing bush ambushes as you walk in. Recast it and she dashes to the target for a 0.75-second root — sync that with your jungler's gank and you're manufacturing kills from level 2 or 3. Add the Passive's gold bonuses on top and this is a support who out-earns laners simply by staying in motion.
strategy.midGame: From 8 to 12 minutes the job is vision around objectives and catching strays. Land the Skill 2 recast root, then follow with Skill 3: enemies already carrying the curse eat an extra 1-second root, for 1.75 seconds of total lockdown — long enough for your team's damage to arrive. When an ally gets chunked, double-tap Skill 1. Dyadia runs to them mid-cast and delivers 600 base healing across the two stages. The taxed gold is only held, never owned: the marked target reclaims 100% of it by killing her, 50% by assisting. It also goes back if two cursed enemies meet and trigger Bitter Reconciliation. Protecting your income comes down to one rule — don't die to the person you taxed.
strategy.lateGame: Late game, your address is next to the carry. When an assassin dives, answer with the Passive's empowered basic: the swing knocks them back while its momentum carries you backward — peel (bodyguarding your carry) and self-peel in a single input. Thread Skill 3 down the middle of a forming brawl and one line delivers ally healing, enemy damage, and the bonus 1-second root on cursed targets all at once. The Skill 2 recast root is not a ranged tool — she dashes to the target to trigger it, so only reach for it while your team's damage still covers that ground. Stop one key enemy from there and the whole fight redraws.
strategy.teamfight: Stand half a step ahead of your backline. Job one is meeting the enemy engage with the Skill 2 recast root — you take 25% reduced damage during it (doubled against the rooted target), so you can play braver than her stats suggest. From there, cycle Skill 1's two-stage healing into wounded allies and keep flicking divers away with the empowered basic. A survival note from real games: if your team doesn't turn onto the enemy you rooted, don't force it — take the backward hop and reset the distance instead.

combos.title: Double Root Catch

combos.description: Recasting Skill 2 on a bitter-bonded enemy moves her onto them and immobilizes them for 0.75s. Through that window she takes 25% less damage, and the reduction is doubled against the target she pinned. Skill 3's 1s immobilize only applies to enemies already carrying the bond, so reversing the order breaks the chain.

combos.title: Two-Stage Bond Heal
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (fated bond + 200 Health) → Skill 1 recast (move to the ally + Blessing of Fate)
combos.description: The recast window is 5s. Skip the recast and the cooldown resets, so a speculative first cast costs nothing. The blessing restores 400 Health to the ally and grants 30% Movement Speed at Lvl 1, while Dyadia recovers 400 herself. Both of you leave the fight still carrying the speed boost, and that is what the two stages are really for.

combos.title: Swing Peel
combos.sequence: Passive enhanced Basic Attack (knockback + backward jump) → Skill 2 (apply bitter bond) → Skill 2 recast (0.75s immobilize)
combos.description: The enhanced Basic Attack swings her in front of the enemy, knocks them back, and carries her backward on the momentum. It peels the diver off your carry and opens her own spacing in the same motion. Every Blessing of Fate on an ally and every Bitter Reconciliation on an enemy cuts the wait for the next enhanced attack by 50%, so it comes back fast.

strengths: Taxes gold off enemies — staying in motion converts into an economy lead
Two roots plus the knockback basic add up to serious lockdown and peel
The curse's stealth shutdown exposes ambushes and invisible heroes
Recast dashes stretch her healing and catch range surprisingly far
weaknesses: The taxed target reclaims 100% of the gold by killing her, 50% by assisting
The recast-centric kit makes split-second reactions awkward
Near-zero personal damage — roots go to waste if allies don't respond
The bond system takes real time to internalize

playstyle.style: A matchmaker who ties fates — blessing allies who stay close and cursing enemies who stray near. Her swing keeps her safe while her bonds teach the team that proximity is power.
playstyle.suited: Players charmed by managing the distance between people — gently steering the whole formation from backstage.

synergy.reason: Hou Yi has no dash or blink; Skill 1 only enhances his Basic Attacks for 4s, so he has to stand still and keep firing. Flowborn's Skill 1 knockback and the charge of Power From Within shove divers off him, and those 4s get spent. That also leaves room to line up Burning Sun Arrow, which stuns for up to 3.5s.

Kongming locks onto a target and channels his Spirit Bomb before it fires. The 0.75s launch from Flowborn's All In covers that channel. The bomb also gains 2% extra damage for every 1% of max Health the target has already lost, so it bites hardest on an enemy who has been worn down.

counters.reason: Marco Polo stacks Destruction fast: Skill 1 alone fires 5 bullets. Once 10 stacks convert into Destroyed Defense, every Basic Attack and skill that lands adds another 100 true damage on top. The 50 defense Flowborn takes from Vitality does nothing against that portion.

Lu Bu ignores crowd control while descending with Skill 3, so Flowborn's launch cannot interrupt the dive. Inside the ring of slaughter he gains 150 physical and 150 magical defense, and an enchanted halberd adds a set amount of true damage on top of his Basic Attacks and skills. The longer the brawl runs, the worse it gets.

skill3.name: Skill 3: All In

strategy.earlyGame: The game starts before the gates open: pick your Flow enhancement at base, and if you're frontlining, the dual-defense option is the safe default. The early rule that matters most: cast Skill 1 near allies or minions. Flow stacks scale with the bodies around you (up to 9) and the healing climbs with them, so the same button is a different skill depending on where you press it. Roam or clash lane both work. When the Ultimate unlocks at level 4, syncing its knock-up with your jungler's gank is your first highlight moment.
strategy.midGame: Through the 8-to-12-minute objective fights, your Flow bank is your voice in the game. Skill 2 recasts free of cooldown for 4 stacks and the Ultimate for 5, so at full stacks you're effectively a tank with double the spellbook. Engage with the Ultimate's center hit (50% bonus damage plus a 0.75-second knock-up), then chain Skill 2 into the same target: the second and third strikes add escalating knock-ups on top. Land the full chain and the average carry simply does not walk away.
strategy.lateGame: When the game settles into 5v5 set pieces, your edge is initiating twice by yourself: once with the normal rotation, once more with stack-funded recasts. The most lethal Ultimate of the night is the second one — cast right as the enemy steps forward believing you're out of cooldowns. Hold the frontline with Flow-empowered basic attacks: each one heals, so as long as you keep swinging you're genuinely hard to bring down. Just remember Skill 1's stack income depends on nearby bodies — never drift into isolated fights.
strategy.teamfight: You take the front, but top off with Skill 1 before committing — a full Flow bank changes how brave you're allowed to be. Enter on the Ultimate's center hit, then run Skill 2 three times into one target: the chained knock-ups juggle them while your team pours in damage. If the backline gets dived, Skill 2's charging knockback carves the assassin off your carry while the shield absorbs the exchange. A habit worth building: keep at least 4 stacks in reserve at all times, so a surprise engage can always be answered with an instant recast.

combos.title: Bank the Flow First

Spending 4 stacks keeps Skill 2 off cooldown, and reaching Clearing and Rifting Slash means three casts on the same target inside 1.5s — that costs 8 stacks.

combos.title: Five Stacks, Two Leaps

combos.description: A cast paid for with 5 stacks does not enter cooldown afterwards. The second leap follows with no gap at all. The payment is only available while Skill 3 is off cooldown, so casting the first one normally kills the double. Skill 2 works the same way for 4 stacks.

combos.title: Backline Interpose
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (charge knockback + 350 shield for 3s) → enhanced Basic Attack (spend 1 Flow, restore 125 Health) → Skill 1 (knockback + refill Flow)
combos.description: Charge through the diver glued to your carry and absorb the trade behind a 350 shield at Lvl 1. The enhanced Basic Attack costs 1 Flow stack but restores 125 Health at Lvl 1, so he can hold the spot and hit back. Skill 1's knockback is explicitly not a crowd control effect — it shoves them off, and locking them down is your team's job.

strengths: Flow stacks buy cooldown-free recasts of Skill 2 and the Ultimate

playstyle.suited: Players learning the tank role who want to focus purely on the engage decision, with nothing else in the way.

counters.reason: Closes the gap with overwhelming mobility and bursts them down before they can even cast a skill.
Possesses undodgeable point-and-click hard CC that completely neutralizes all mobility.
