The cooldown option (5% CDR) is the default for combo uptime, while the magic-pierce boon punishes opponents who stack magic defense. In mid lane, clear waves with Skill 2's formation and place its far edge so it clips your lane opponent — waveclear and harass in a single cast. Treat Skill 1 less as a weapon and more as fuel: it cuts your other cooldowns by 50% and restocks Flow stacks, so fire it during safe windows while the wave sits on your side and you will never run dry at the 4-minute Tyrant fight. Until your Ultimate arrives at Level 4, winning the chip war is the whole job — don't force kills.
strategy.midGame: Around eight minutes, once cooldown boots and a magic-pierce staff are finished, a single formation starts taking frightening chunks out of people. Your job now is placement in tight spaces. Lay Skill 2 across river entrances and the corridors around the Tyrant pit, then stack the second cast's knock-up onto anyone who steps in — landing it on the first formation also raises its damage over time by 50%, holding enemies inside a zone that hurts more every tick. Flow caps at nine stacks, so the iron rule is topping off with Skill 1 before every fight. Walk in empty and your bonus casts vanish, along with half your output.
strategy.lateGame: Past 15 minutes, holding your full combo in reserve becomes the win condition. With your magic attack scaled through your final core items, the third cast's stun into Skill 3's beam drops anyone with marksman-grade durability. Skill 3 lets you cast other skills mid-channel, so the ideal picture is sweeping the beam while laying fresh formations at your feet. If someone dives you, you are not empty-handed: Skill 1 knocks them back, Skill 2 slows, and its follow-up casts launch and then stun. Four Flow stacks keep Skill 2 off cooldown entirely, so how many times you can shove a diver away comes down to your stack count. What you don't have is a dash or a blink — the moment you stand ahead of your frontline is the moment you die. When setting up before Overlord, always keep a wall and your teammates at your back.
strategy.teamfight: Open every fight from the absolute backline. Skip the enemy tank; drop Skill 2 under the fighter pushing into your carries, then chain the second cast's knock-up into the third cast's stun to freeze their front. Once you see an enemy blink go down, commit the Ultimate — its homing energy bolts chase runners down without your help. A Flow Formation paid for with four Flow stacks never touches its cooldown, so you can keep re-laying zones as long as stacks remain; that loop is the whole point of this hero. When you're spent, don't chase — fall back and let Skill 1's healing patch you up.

combos.title: Three-Circle Lockdown
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (Restock Flow, 50% Cooldown Cut) → Skill 2 (Slow) → Skill 2 (0.5s Knock-up) → Skill 2 (0.5s Stun)
combos.description: Recast Skill 2 within 1.5s and the circle becomes Launching Flow, then Stunning Flow. That hands Flowborn a 0.5s knock-up and a 0.5s stun without waiting on a teammate's crowd control. Land the second and third casts inside the first circle and its duration refreshes while its damage over time rises 50%. Skill 1 is the refill: casts paid with 4 Flow stacks never enter cooldown.

combos.title: Layering Under the Beam
combos.sequence: Skill 3 (Beam, Other Skills Usable) → Skill 2 (Slow) → Skill 2 (0.5s Knock-up)
combos.description: Other skills stay available while the beam channels. Keep it burning, drop the circle at their feet, and recast within 1.5s for the knock-up. The beam picks its own victim — the nearest enemy hero in range. Never fire from an angle where a frontliner stands closer than the target.

strengths: Spending Flow stacks lets Skill 2 and the Ultimate ignore cooldowns entirely
Skill 2's consecutive casts supply knock-up and stun with no outside help
Casting other skills during the Ultimate's beam packs absurd damage density
Skill 1's healing and cooldown cut give far more staying power than expected
weaknesses: No mobility skill — once Skill 1's small knockback is baited, nothing else peels
Damage ceiling depends heavily on precise nine-stack Flow management
Skill 1's stack income and healing shrink without teammates nearby
Ground-placed formations let blink users simply step out of the damage

playstyle.style: A turret mage who chooses her own stat upgrades through Flow selection. The beam and magic circle kit is simple area control — a polished template of the mage role.
playstyle.suited: Players who like tweaking their build direction game to game, wrapped in a kit that stays easy to pilot.

synergy.reason: Boosts backline survivability with shields, keeping them safe until their late-game damage scaling kicks in.
Stabilizes the laning phase with high sustain and protection, allowing the marksman to scale and shine.

counters.reason: Instantly deletes squishy marksmen with stealth engages and high burst damage.
Dives the backline with overwhelming mobility, bursting them down before there's any time to react.

passive.skill_name: Passive Skill: Flow of the World
passive.description:
Flowborn can draw the Flow into their body at the Base, increasing Attack Speed by 10%-20% (increases with hero level) and enhancing one of four other stats.
Vitality: Increases max Health by 300.
Piercing Heart: Increases Physical Attack by 30.
Haste: Increases Movement Speed by 3.5%.
Focus: Increases Cooldown Reduction by 5%.
Enhanced Basic Attack: Fires a piercing projectile, dealing 80 (80 + 20% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies in its path. Hitting an enemy extends its travel distance while reducing damage by 30%.
Each enhanced Basic Attack consumes 1 stack of Flow.
passive.name: Passive Skill: Flow of the World

skill1.description:
Flowborn channels the Flow, dealing 100 (100 + 25% extra physical attack) physical damage to nearby enemies and knocking them back (without applying crowd control). Also recovers 150 (150 + 4% extra Health) Health, gains 5 stacks of Flow, and reduces the cooldown of Arrow of No Retreat and Arrowstorm by 50%.
Nearby teammates and minions increase the recovery (up to 100%) and stacks of Flow (up to 9 stacks).
skill1.name: Skill 1: Convergence

skill2.description:
Flowborn shoots an enormous projectile at the target (can be blocked by enemy heroes), dealing 450 (450 + 120% extra physical attack) physical damage and knocking back non-hero units.
Flowborn can dash a short distance upon use (use it again within 1.5s to become enhanced).
Second Use: Enhances projectile damage by 25%.
Third Use: Levitates and enhances projectile damage by 50%.
Can spend 4 stacks of Flow to use this skill again.
Casting speed increases with Attack Speed.
skill2.name: Skill 2: Arrow of No Retreat

skill3.description:
Flowborn shoots 7 volleys of light projectiles at the target location (casting speed increases with Attack Speed), dealing 90 (50 + 24% physical attack) physical damage (every 3 projectiles counts as 1 Basic Attack). Projectiles lock on to targets within range. Also gains a 10% Movement Speed increase. Use this skill again to levitate.
Can spend 5 stacks of Flow to use this skill again.
skill3.name: Skill 3: Arrowstorm

strategy.earlyGame: Pick your Flow boon at base, then head for the farm lane. Take the max-HP option (300 HP) into aggressive matchups, and borrow damage with the physical attack boon when the lane looks safe. Until Level 4 your base damage is genuinely poor, so this is not a trading window — quietly collect last hits and experience and nothing else. If an enemy closes the gap, Skill 1's knockback and healing reset the exchange more often than not. It also halves the cooldowns of Skill 2 and the Ultimate, so spending it defensively never feels like a waste.
strategy.midGame: From 8 to 10 minutes, once attack-speed boots and your first damage item are online, Flowborn's signature mechanic starts spinning: attack speed accelerates your skill animations too. You're still not the main character of teamfights, so shove the lane, sweep open jungle camps, and rush your second core item. When called to Tyrant, join from the very back — planting Skill 2's giant arrow into the closest enemy is a full shift on its own. Each cast tacks on a short move afterward, so build the habit of stepping back half a pace every time you fire. It quietly prevents most deaths.
strategy.lateGame: Past 15 minutes, at four items and up, the lead role changes hands. Weaving bonus casts of Skill 2 and the Ultimate between basic attacks — paid for with Flow stacks — creates the damage spikes that define this hero's endgame. Fire Skill 2 three times within 1.5 seconds and the third becomes an aerial attack at 50% bonus damage, so the moment your frontline pins someone is the moment to unload the triple. Skill 1 restocks five stacks, more with allies or minions nearby; never let the tank run empty between fights. And never walk anywhere alone — stay close enough to see a teammate's back at all times.
strategy.teamfight: Your position is locked to the very back, and your target is whoever stands closest. When chased, Skill 1's knockback peels them off while the heal and the 50% cooldown refund on Skill 2 and the Ultimate set up your next burst. Arrowstorm's volley also grants 10% move speed, tailor-made for kiting backward. Once the enemy front cracks, spend your saved Flow stacks on the Skill 2 triple volley into whatever remains of their backline. You are softest right after dumping everything — at zero stacks, sit at max range and refuse to get greedy. That's how this hero grows old.

combos.title: Triple No-Retreat Volley
combos.sequence: Skill 2 → Skill 2 (+25% Damage) → Skill 2 (Levitate, +50% Damage)
combos.description: Chaining casts within 1.5s raises the damage by 25% and then 50%, and the third shot levitates Flowborn. The raw cooldown cannot deliver three in time, so the 4-Flow-stack bonus cast fills the gap. The projectile stops on the first enemy hero it hits, so an angle that puts their frontline in the way will never reach the back.

combos.title: Push Off and Fire Back
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (Knock Back, Heal) → Enhanced Basic Attack (Piercing Shot) → Skill 2
combos.description: When someone closes the gap, Skill 1 is the answer: it knocks them back without applying crowd control, restores Health, and banks 5 stacks of Flow. Skill 2 and Skill 3 both return at half cooldown, turning the retreat into return fire. More teammates and minions nearby means more healing and more stacks.

combos.title: Arrowstorm Pursuit
combos.sequence: Skill 3 (+10% Movement Speed) → Skill 3 (Levitate) → Enhanced Basic Attack
combos.description: The volley locks on to targets inside the marked area — 7 projectiles at Level 1, with every 3 counting as one Basic Attack. Flowborn also gains 10% Movement Speed, which is what keeps a fleeing target in range. Using the skill again levitates. Hold 5 stacks of Flow and one more cast comes without waiting on the cooldown.

strengths: Attack speed uniquely accelerates skill animations, double-dipping every point
Skill 1's knockback, healing, and cooldown refund make elite self-peel
Flow-stack bonus casts create burst windows that ignore cooldowns
Post-cast movement and aerial attacks on Skill 2 and the Ultimate make kiting exceptional
weaknesses: Weak base damage before Level 4 — early trades are nearly always losses
The piercing arrow loses 30% damage after passing through a target, so long-range poke rarely finishes anyone
Sloppy stack management removes the bonus casts and flattens the damage spikes
Targeted CC is lethal once Skill 1 is down, with no second escape

playstyle.style: A clean, honest marksman whose individuality lives in Flow selection — choose your own stat growth, then fight with a big arrow and an arrow storm anyone can understand.
playstyle.suited: Players learning the marksman fundamentals who still want build choices to call their own.

synergy.reason: His AoE cleanse and CC immunity allow Florentino to continuously output damage and pick up flowers without his combos being interrupted.
By clumping enemies up, he massively increases the hit rate of Florentino's flower toss (Skill 1), letting him wipe out multiple targets at once.

counters.reason: His uncleansable suppression ultimate completely stops Florentino's fancy footwork and combos, leaving him vulnerable to getting burst down by the team.
His long-duration suppression ultimate forcefully interrupts Florentino's combo mechanics, completely neutralizing him.

passive.name: Passive Skill: Shuffle
passive.description:
When Florentino leaves combat or touches a bouquet, his next Basic Attack is enhanced for 5s to include a dash and deal 160 (160 + 50% extra physical attack) extra physical damage. If it hits an enemy hero, he recovers 140 (140 + 2% extra Health) Health (halved against non-hero units).
After the dash ends, he can dash a certain distance again.

skill1.name: Skill 1: Blossom
skill1.description:
Florentino tosses a bouquet forward, dealing 300 (300 + 95% extra physical attack) physical damage, stunning the first enemy hit for 0.75s, and scattering 3 bouquets around the target that last 3.5s.
If Florentino touches a bouquet, he gains the enhanced Basic Attack Shuffle and refreshes Triple Threat's cooldown.

skill2.name: Skill 2: Triple Threat
skill2.description:
Florentino attacks the target 3 times with his sword.
1st Attack: Deals 130 (130 + 40% extra physical attack) physical damage and inflicts extreme slow for 1s.
2nd Attack: Deals 130 (130 + 40% extra physical attack) physical damage.
3rd Attack: Deals 130 (130 + 40% extra physical attack) physical damage over 2 hits.
Each hit deals an additional 130 (130 + 40% extra physical attack) true damage to the target and reduces Blossom's cooldown by 1s.
There is a 1.5s cooldown between the first 2 attacks. After the third attack, the skill goes on cooldown. After each attack, Florentino can dash a certain distance.

skill3.name: Skill 3: Gentlemen's Duel
skill3.description:
Florentino dashes in the target direction, marking the first enemy hero hit and increasing their damage taken by 10% for 5s while scattering 3 bouquets around them.
During the skill's duration, the recovery effect of Shuffle's enhanced Basic Attack is doubled, and Florentino gains crowd control immunity for 3s, extended by a further 1s for every bouquet he touches.
Touching a bouquet grants Shuffle's enhanced Basic Attack and refreshes Triple Threat's cooldown.
After the dash ends, he can dash a certain distance again.

strategy.earlyGame: In the clash lane, Level 1 starts with Skill 1. The 0.75-second stun sprouts three flowers around your target, so collect them mid-stun, then chain enhanced basic attack into Skill 2 for a trade loaded with true damage that your opponent simply cannot match. The enhanced basic heals 140 HP when it strikes a hero, which means the longer the slugfest runs, the wider the HP gap grows — that's the Florentino experience. Once the Ultimate arrives at Level 4, the mark's 10% bonus damage taken plus super armor makes your duels nearly unloseable. Just pick flower routes on the side ganks can't reach.
strategy.midGame: Around nine minutes, with your first two core items finished, it's time to move. Chip the enemy tower down, then show up mid: Skill 3's dash into the flower loop makes you a one-man gank engine. In the standoffs before Tyrant or Overlord, one Skill 1 threaded from a river bush is enough to take a pick. When nothing is happening, splitting side towers is genuinely one of your best uses of time. Watch your sustain, though — the enhanced basic's healing is halved against minions, so don't loiter in a lane at low HP expecting to heal it back.
strategy.lateGame: With a frost gauntlet and a sustain piece rounding out your build, the late game rewards duels over head-on 5v5s. Pressure a side lane, then catch whoever comes to answer with Skill 3 and finish them — that's the golden pattern. At rank 3 the mark raises their damage taken by 20%, and cycling Skill 2's true damage through flower pickups on a target like that kills even tanks on a timer. The only real threat is getting surrounded. Crowd control immunity runs 3 seconds and extends 1 second per bouquet you touch, but that ceiling is real — CC timed for the moment it drops will still put you down.
strategy.teamfight: You are not the frontal engage. Wait in a side bush, let the enemy's CC land on your frontline, then commit the Ultimate onto their backline. The dash blooms three flowers on arrival, so once you land, dance the loop — flower, Skill 2, flower, Skill 2 — and your damage never pauses. While the Ultimate runs, enhanced basic healing doubles, letting you shrug off a surprising amount of focus mid-combo. Your one losing script is getting burst before the first flower pickup. In the instant before you dive, check what skills the enemy still has up — every time.

combos.title: Bouquet Pickup Loop
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (0.75s Stun, 3 Bouquets) → Touch a Bouquet (Enhanced Basic Attack, Skill 2 Reset) → Enhanced Basic Attack (Dash) → Skill 2 → Touch a Bouquet → Skill 2
combos.description: A landed Skill 1 scatters 3 bouquets around the target for 3.5s. Every bouquet Florentino steps on empowers his next Basic Attack and refreshes Skill 2's cooldown. Each of Skill 2's three strikes adds true damage and trims 1s from Skill 1's cooldown. The bouquets last 3.5s: if the route to all three is not clean, take one and get out.

combos.title: Marked Duel
combos.sequence: Skill 3 (Mark, 3s Crowd Control Immunity) → Touch a Bouquet (Enhanced Basic Attack, Skill 2 Reset) → Enhanced Basic Attack → Skill 2 → Touch a Bouquet → Skill 2
combos.description: The dash marks the first enemy hero it hits and raises their damage taken for 5s. Three bouquets bloom around that target. Crowd control immunity starts at 3s and gains 1s for every bouquet touched. Enhanced Basic Attacks heal double while the skill runs, and each pickup hands Skill 2 back. The duel comes down to how much true damage fits inside those 5 marked seconds.

combos.title: Hit and Step Away
combos.sequence: Enhanced Basic Attack (Dash) → Skill 2 (1st Strike, 1s Extreme Slow) → Skill 2 (2nd Strike) → Disengage
combos.description: Simply leaving combat empowers the next Basic Attack. In lane, cash that in for the dash hit and the first two strikes of Skill 2, then walk out. The opening strike carries a 1s extreme slow, so the chase loses ground. Skill 2 enters its real cooldown only after the third strike: stop at two, and that strike plus the quick move behind it becomes the exit.

strengths: Flower pickups reset Skill 2 endlessly, cycling true damage nonstop
Enhanced-basic healing — doubled during the Ultimate — wins any slugfest
The super armor dash forces 1v1s on his terms
Constant dashes and bonus moves make roams and split pushes fast
weaknesses: Miss Skill 1 and no flowers bloom — the combo loses its front door
Flower spots are predictable; CC placed on the pickup path shreds him
Few answers to long-range poke and disciplined kiting
Flower tracking and micro-movement demand real practice time

playstyle.style: A fencer who scatters bouquets and weaves between them, each pickup refreshing his empowered strikes. He duels by designing routes through his own flowers — elegant to watch, demanding to pilot.
playstyle.suited: Players who choreograph their movement paths mid-fight, and care about winning beautifully.

synergy.reason: While Lorion's massive AoE knockup ultimate locks down multiple enemies, Marco Polo can safely unleash his full ultimate.
Chaining Lian Po's strong engage into Lorion's orb placement and ultimate creates a CC chain that devastates the enemy backline.

counters.reason: Zhuangzi's ultimate (team-wide CC immunity) completely negates Lorion's biggest strength: his massive AoE knockup ultimate.
Her umbrella-swap blinks let her easily dodge Lorion's Skill 1 orb placement and his ultimate's AoE.

passive.name: Passive Skill: Eternal
passive.description:
Lorion's skills detonate when they hit a target, dealing damage and activating his projectile.
While the projectile is outside him, the activated projectile deals 59 (59 + 12% magical attack) magical damage to the unit with the lowest Health within range every 0.75s for 4s.
While the projectile is inside him, the activated projectile deals damage to all units within range at double the frequency, and he recovers 25 (25 + 0.4% extra Health) Health (halved for non-hero units).

skill1.name: Skill 1: Here's What I Think
skill1.description:
Lorion moves his projectile to the target location, dealing 220 (220 + 44% magical attack) magical damage to units in its path. Upon reaching the destination, it detonates, dealing an extra 150 (150 + 30% magical attack) magical damage. When the skill is used, if the projectile is outside him, it deals 250 (250 + 50% magical attack) magical damage and inflicts 20% slow for 1.5s to units between its start and end points.
The projectile is recalled to Lorion when too far away.

skill2.name: Skill 2: Abyssal Pact
skill2.description:
When the projectile is outside him, Lorion recalls and then detonates it, dealing 150 (150 + 30% magical attack) magical damage and gaining 20% Movement Speed for 2s.
When the projectile is inside him, 30% of the cooldown is refunded.

skill3.name: Skill 3: Darkness Falls
skill3.description:
When the projectile is outside him, Lorion flies to it and detonates it, dealing 150 (150 + 30% magical attack) magical damage. During this period, he gains 25% damage reduction for 2s after he lands and crowd control immunity.
When the projectile is inside him, 30% of the cooldown is refunded.

skill4.name: Skill 4: Starry Night
skill4.description:
After a 2s delay, the projectile detonates, dealing 600 (600 + 120% magical attack) magical damage to nearby enemies and launching them for 1.25s.
When using his Ultimate, he immediately gains 1 Skill 1 charge.
If the Ultimate does not hit a hero, 50% of its cooldown is refunded.

strategy.earlyGame: In mid lane, clear waves with the orb held inside your body. Activated there, it strikes everything around you at double frequency and even heals you, which makes Lorion shockingly durable in lane scraps. When you want to harass, send the orb out with Skill 1 — and the moment it connects, don't leave it lying there. Recall it with Skill 2 and collect the 20% move speed. Repeat that send-and-recall rhythm patiently until Level 4 and you'll walk into the 4-minute Tyrant contest with a visible HP lead over your lane opponent.
strategy.midGame: From about eight minutes, once cooldown boots and a magic-pierce staff are complete, orb placement starts deciding fights. In the standoffs before Tyrant, your job is shipping the orb into enemy escape routes and narrow corridors with Skill 1, booking the Ultimate's detonation in advance. After a 2-second charge it erupts for heavy damage and a 1.25-second knock-up, so enemies simply cannot stand in that zone. Time the blast with your team's engage — detonating early is just an expensive scare. And since the activated orb auto-targets the lowest-HP enemy in range, parking it near someone chipped forces a recall all by itself.
strategy.lateGame: Your late-game role is zone control from the backline. With your magic attack fully built, a rank-3 Skill 4 detonation lands 1,200 base damage — enough to take a huge bite out of anything squishy. The discipline that matters here: never spend Skill 3 offensively. Flying to your orb carries 25% damage reduction and crowd control immunity, and the reduction lingers for 2 seconds after you land. In practice that flight is your last lifeline. When the enemy assassin is missing from vision, pre-place the orb toward your escape side before stepping up; if they jump you, you fly straight out of their reach. Let the orb project the threat while your body stays safe. That's the iron rule of late-game Lorion.
strategy.teamfight: Teamfight prep starts 30 seconds before the fight. At Overlord or Shadow Tyrant, set the orb at the pit entrance, then rake Skill 1's start-to-end line damage and slow through their formation. The moment they clump, detonate for the knock-up and let your team's follow-up turn it into a numbers win. If the brawl swallows you, recalling the orb into your body with Skill 2 is a real option — the double-frequency damage around you plus the self-healing makes you far harder to kill than you look. Lorion's teamfight is one continuous choice: which do you show the enemy, the orb or yourself?

combos.title: Plant and Detonate
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (Send the Projectile Out) → Skill 1 (Sweep from Start to End, 1.5s Slow) → Skill 4 (2s Delay, 1.25s Knock-up)
combos.description: The first cast drops the projectile at their feet or across the escape route. With it already outside him, the second cast damages every unit between its start and end points and leaves a 1.5s slow. Skill 4 detonates after a 2s delay. Book it to land with an ally's crowd control, not after it. Using it returns 1 Skill 1 charge, and a blast that hits no hero refunds 50% of its cooldown.

combos.title: Recall and Brawl
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (Projectile Outside) → Skill 2 (Recall and Activate) → Basic Attack
combos.description: Outside him, the activated projectile only strikes the lowest-Health unit in range. In a scrum that aim goes nowhere useful. Recall it with Skill 2 and it covers every unit in range at double the attack frequency. Each trigger returns 25 Health at Level 1, halved against non-hero units.

combos.title: Flight to the Projectile
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (Send It Down the Escape Route) → Skill 3 (Flight, 25% Damage Reduction, Crowd Control Immunity) → Skill 2 (Recall, 2s Movement Speed Bonus)
combos.description: Skill 3 flies Lorion to a projectile that sits outside him. Send it toward the way out, not toward the fight. The flight carries crowd control immunity and 25% damage reduction, and that reduction lingers 2s after he lands. Recall with Skill 2 on arrival and carry the 2s Movement Speed bonus out with him. Stray too far and the projectile returns automatically, so park it just past the escape route.

strengths: The orb swaps whole playstyles inside versus outside his body, covering any range
Planted detonation knock-ups own every chokepoint on the map
Damage-reduced, super-armor flight is elite escape for a mage
The outside orb hunts the lowest-HP enemy, projecting free closing pressure
weaknesses: Everything hinges on orb placement — one bad spot stalls the entire kit
The 2-second detonation delay gives mobile enemies time to dodge
Spending the flight offensively leaves him with no way out afterward
Straying too far force-recalls the orb and erases its zone threat

playstyle.style: A mage defined by where his projectile is: outside him it's a placed turret, inside him it fuels his own casts. One orb, two identities — and his wide launch ultimate opens teamfights.
playstyle.suited: Players who enjoy a game of 'where does my one resource live right now' hiding inside a clean-looking kit.

synergy.reason: Annette's ultimate (wind wall) completely shuts out enemy assassin dives, allowing the marksman to attack freely from the safety of the backline.
The wind wall keeps melee heroes at bay, allowing her to safely output damage from out of range.

counters.reason: They dish out heavy poke damage from far beyond the wind wall's range, easily overwhelming Annette's squishy health pool.
His high burst damage can potentially delete Annette before she even has time to deploy her ultimate.

passive.name: Passive Skill: Whisperwind
passive.description: While Annette is moving, her skill cooldowns are faster and she gains Mana. While there are teammates nearby, she also gains 25 Movement Speed.

skill1.name: Skill 1: Gust Force
skill1.description:
Annette conjures a magic circle at the target location that activates every 0.5s for 4s.
The magic circle deals 160 (160 + 28% magical attack) magical damage and inflicts 5% slow on enemy units for 1s, for up to 5 stacks.
The magic circle grants teammates 5% Movement Speed for 1s, for up to 5 stacks.

skill2.name: Skill 2: Wind Cuffs
skill2.description:
Annette fires an orb in the target direction, flying back from the recoil, gaining a shield that negates 400 (400 + 6% extra Health) damage for 3s, and gaining 75 Movement Speed for 2s.
The orb deals 300 (300 + 50% magical attack) magical damage to enemies it hits.
The orb grants a shield that negates 400 (400 + 6% extra Health) damage to all teammates it hits.
If the orb passes through a Gust Force magic circle, it pushes the magic circle to its destination.

skill3.name: Skill 3: Hurricane Wall
skill3.description:
Annette conjures a barrier around herself for 4s (requires channeling), knocking back enemies within range and dealing 300 (300 + 50% magical attack) magical damage. Enemies that touch the barrier will take equal damage and be stunned for 1.25s. Teammates within the barrier gain crowd control immunity.
While channeling, Annette becomes untargetable and is slowed by 50%.

strategy.earlyGame: Shadow your marksman from the start and support the farm-lane scraps with Skill 2's orb. Hit an ally and it shields; hit an enemy and it damages; and you bounce backward on every cast — one aiming decision covers offense and defense at once. Before the 4-minute Tyrant, your job is tagging along on ganks: Skill 1's formation stacks slows on enemies who cross it and speeds up allies who do, a ready-made chase engine. Since the Passive refunds cooldowns and restores mana as you move, walking the river beats standing still in lane — Annette performs best in motion.
strategy.midGame: Once your support item upgrade and cooldown boots are in, skirmishes start brewing around mid. Annette's spot is half a step ahead of her carry. The instant an enemy fighter telegraphs a dive, open Skill 3: every enemy inside the radius at that moment is knocked back. Anyone who walks into the barrier afterwards is not pushed away — they take damage and a 1.25-second stun instead. Teammates standing inside gain crowd control immunity. Because the knockback fires on cast, you can wait and watch their engage before committing. The trick of pushing your formation forward with the orb is also worth practicing for chipping enemies who hide under tower.
strategy.lateGame: The late game is an exercise in patience: hold the Ultimate for the one enemy who decides fights. With your defensive capes stacked, you won't fall over even standing forward. The ideal sequence at a fight's entrance is Skill 1 first to control the ground, then catching the enemy assassin mid-leap with the barrier as they jump your marksman. While it's active you become untargetable but your move speed is halved, so opening in the wrong spot strands you away from your team while the fight is decided. Open it right beside the person you're protecting — no exceptions.
strategy.teamfight: Stand next to your carry. The job is three tasks: lay Skill 1 across the enemy frontline's path to blunt the charge; thread Skill 2's orb through your most-focused teammate to keep shields flowing; and when the real dive arrives, meet it with the Ultimate — knockback, stun, and super armor for everyone inside. Keep that order and you'll tilt teamfights while dealing almost no damage yourself. The one hazard is the orb's recoil: bounce backward into a flanker and the story ends badly. Glance behind you before every cast — make it a reflex.

combos.title: Dive Breaker
combos.sequence: Skill 3 (Knock Back, 1.25s Stun, Crowd Control Immunity for Allies) → Skill 1 (Slowing Magic Circle) → Skill 2 (Shield an Ally)
combos.description: Open the barrier the instant someone jumps your carry. Enemies in range are knocked back, anyone who touches the wall is stunned for 1.25s, and allies inside gain crowd control immunity. Once they are off, Skill 1 slows the retreat and the orb hands a shield to the teammate it passes through. Channeling makes Annette untargetable but cuts her Movement Speed by 50% at Level 1, so open it right beside the ally she is protecting.

combos.title: Circle Delivery
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (Place the Magic Circle) → Skill 2 (Orb Pushes the Circle)
combos.description: An orb that touches the magic circle carries the whole circle to the orb's destination. That reaches enemies kiting at max range or sitting under tower. The circle activates every 0.5s and lasts 4s. Push it immediately after it lands.

combos.title: Recoil Retreat
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (Fire at the Chaser, Recoil Backward) → Skill 1 (On the Landing Spot)
combos.description: Firing the orb throws Annette in the opposite direction. The 3s shield and the 2s Movement Speed bonus are locked in by the cast itself. A hit is not required for them; landing one only adds magical damage to the chaser. Drop the magic circle where she lands and the pursuit has to walk through the slow. The one thing to check at the moment of firing is what sits behind her.

strengths: The Ultimate's knockback, stun, and super armor erase entire dives
Skill 2 is damage, shielding, and a reposition in a single button
Movement refunds her cooldowns, so skills keep cycling as long as she moves
Layered speed-ups and slows control the tempo of chases and retreats
weaknesses: Minimal personal damage — she can't convert her setups into kills alone
No healing, so teammates who are already chunked stay chunked
The barrier halves her move speed; a bad opening spot means instant separation
Forget the orb's recoil and it bounces you straight into trouble

playstyle.style: A support who literally cannot stand still — movement refunds her cooldowns. She accelerates allies through her circles, hands out shields, and her barrier ultimate bounces entire engages back.
playstyle.suited: Players who want to support at full sprint, using defensive skills as the signal to attack.

synergy.reason: He grants CC immunity and damage reduction, allowing her to chain resets and secure kills uninterrupted.
His long-range stun can lock down enemies, creating a safe opening for Butterfly to dive.

counters.reason: His AoE CC and high sustain can easily break the chain of Butterfly's skill resets.
Her repeated blinks and passive sustain let her dodge Butterfly's burst and easily turn the fight.

passive.description: Butterfly gains 2 marks from defeating heroes and 1 mark from assists and from killing monsters/minions. At 3 stacks, the next skill used will not enter cooldown.
passive.name: Passive Skill: Assassination

skill1.description: Butterfly deals 362 (240 + 70% physical attack) physical damage to nearby enemies. Each extra enemy hit increases damage by 25%. Also gains a shield that negates 381 (250 + 75% physical attack) damage lasting 2s, and gains 50% Movement Speed that diminishes over time.
skill1.name: Skill 1: Whirlwind

skill2.description:
Butterfly deals 333 (220 + 65% physical attack) physical damage to enemies in her path. The first enemy hit takes 1.5 times this damage and is slowed by 50% for 1.5s.
Hitting an enemy increases her Attack Speed by 25% and Critical Rate by 10% for 4s, for up to 2 stacks.
skill2.name: Skill 2: Sword Propel

skill3.description:
Butterfly jumps to a target enemy, dealing 557 (400 + 90% physical attack) physical damage (if the target is marked, deals extra true damage equal to 12% lost Health) and marking them for 4s. For 4s after hitting the target, she takes 50% less damage from all Basic Attacks.
While the mark is active, she recovers Health equal to 35% of damage dealt to the target. If the target is defeated, it will immediately reset her Ultimate's Cooldown.
Hitting marked targets with Basic Attacks will also reduce the Cooldown of Skills 1 and 2 by 1s.
skill3.name: Skill 3: Death Dealer

strategy.earlyGame: You're the jungler. Skill 1 gains 25% bonus damage for every additional enemy it hits, so casting from the center of each camp is free clear speed. The opening route is both buffs plus the river camps, aiming for Level 4 around the 3-minute mark. Passive stacks build from monster kills too, and at three stacks your next skill costs no cooldown — bank them before a gank and you walk in with an extra cast. As for the 4-minute Tyrant: touch it only when you've reached Level 4 before the enemy jungler has. Otherwise it's bait.
strategy.midGame: Once your jungle item and first damage item are finished, the real work begins: erasing chipped enemies. The ideal prey is a backliner under half HP. Death Dealer's leap applies the mark, converts 35% of your damage into healing, and — the headline — resets its own cooldown instantly on a takedown. Open ganks with Skill 2: the first enemy hit takes 1.5x damage and a 50% slow, and the attack speed and crit buffs it grants let your basics finish the job. The one rule that never changes, even in this window: do not walk into a healthy enemy team from the front.
strategy.lateGame: Late-game Butterfly is the cleanup crew, not the opening act. Even when the 5v5 starts, hold your side bush until the enemy's CC and attention are committed to your frontline. The Ultimate adds true damage equal to 12% of a marked target's lost HP, so anyone already chipped dies — armor stacked or not. One kill refunds the Ultimate on the spot, a hero takedown banks two passive stacks, and the chain reaction begins. The flip side: without that first kill, nothing starts. Whatever else you compromise on, never compromise on your entry timing.
strategy.teamfight: Your brawl loop is enter, kill, reset, next. Lead with Skill 2 before committing — the slow keeps them in reach, the attack speed buff quickens your swings, and each basic on a marked target shaves a second off both Skill 1 and Skill 2. When focus piles up, Skill 1's shield and decaying 50% speed boost carry you back to the edge of the fight. While your mark is active you take half damage from basic attacks, so a chasing marksman often can't actually finish you. One nuance: enemy support shields can rob your takedown reset, so start with the softest unshielded target — that's the correct kill order.

combos.title: Soften First, Then Leap
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (1.5x Damage, 50% Slow) → Skill 3 (Leap, Mark) → Basic Attack → Skill 1 (Shield, Haste)
combos.description: The first enemy Skill 2 hits takes 1.5 times the damage plus a 50% slow for 1.5s. Landing it also stacks the Attack Speed and Critical Rate buff, which is why it belongs before the leap rather than after. Basic Attacks on the marked target cut 1s from Skill 1 and Skill 2 cooldowns and return 35% of the damage dealt as Health. Skill 1 closes the pattern with a shield and a speed burst that covers either the chase or the exit.

combos.title: Takedown Reset Chain
combos.sequence: Skill 3 (Mark) → Basic Attack (Takedown) → Skill 3 (Cooldown Reset, Next Target) → Skill 2 → Skill 1
combos.description: Killing the marked target resets Skill 3's cooldown on the spot. A hero takedown also banks 2 passive marks, and at 3 the next skill used skips its cooldown entirely. Marked targets take extra true damage equal to 12% of their lost Health, so start with wounded enemies. Leap onto a healthy one and no reset comes — the chain ends right there.

combos.title: Jungle Clear Rotation
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (Catch Several Targets) → Skill 2 (Attack Speed and Critical Rate) → Basic Attack
combos.description: Skill 1 gains 25% damage for each extra enemy caught, so it belongs in the middle of a camp, not at its edge. Skill 2's hit grants the Attack Speed and Critical Rate buff, up to 2 stacks (25% and 10% at Level 1). Every monster killed banks 1 passive mark; reach 3 before you leave for a gank and the next skill costs no cooldown.

strengths: Takedown-triggered Ultimate resets give unmatched chain-kill power in brawls
35% damage-to-healing plus halved basic-attack damage while the mark runs
Lost-HP true damage finishes chipped targets through any amount of armor
Skill 1's shield and speed burst keep her entries and exits cheap
weaknesses: Without a first kill the resets never spin up and she fades hard
No CC of her own to start fights — she depends on teammates' lockdown
Hard CC exposes pure assassin fragility the moment it lands
Lacks a decisive answer to full-HP targets and healthy frontlines

playstyle.style: A snowballing assassin: takedowns build marks, and at three stacks her next skill has no cooldown. Every kill fuels the next — once she's rolling, nobody stops the chain.
playstyle.suited: Players chasing momentum itself — patient early, then ruthless the instant the window opens.
